It targets the twin problems of detecting bad updates and neutralizing those that slip through.

entry.title: Distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation for industrial anomaly detection

author.name: Jie Deng

entry.summary: For industrial visual inspection, this work replaces AUROC and raw mask overlap with a distribution-free upper tolerance threshold that pins the false-alarm rate and a paired-minus-crossed spatial test that credits a detector only for overlap exceeding chance from recurrent defect locations and mask geometry. Three detectors are evaluated on point-defect images across several modalities.

entry.title: Decentralized Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Semantic Communication

author.name: Lin Yin, Tiejun Lv, Weicai Li, Xi Yu, Xiaoyu He

entry.summary: The paper identifies negative transfer and overconsensus bias when topology-agnostic decentralized federated averaging is applied to heterogeneous multi-task semantic communication networks. It proposes policy-driven multi-path routing that separates task-specific from shared features at each node plus a task-affinity-calibrated column-stochastic consensus matrix for aggregation.

entry.title: FedADB: Class Anchor-Driven Dual-Branch Federated Learning for Mitigating Forgetting

author.name: Zhenyan Liu, Hua Zhang, Haoran Gao, Qi Li, Hongliang Zhu, Huiyu Zhou, Zongliang Shen, Yanxin Xu, Jiahui Wang

entry.summary: FedADB tackles forgetting of global knowledge during local federated training under multimodal client heterogeneity by using class anchors and a dual-branch design instead of global alignment strategies that suppress local optimization or proxy datasets that add overhead. The aim is to balance class-wise global consistency with local adaptation, especially for classes missing from a client.

entry.title: A Scalable Pipeline for LLM-Teacher Distillation Labeling: Work-Stealing Job Scheduling and Memory-Aware GPU Concurrency

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Describes an infrastructure recipe for large-scale LLM-teacher labeling that combines a work-stealing queue design with exactly-once task claims via atomic compare-and-set on a single SQLite file, plus memory-aware GPU concurrency. It also frames the question of how much label quality a teacher model buys per dollar.

entry.title: Misaligned Incentives in Pause Scenarios

author.name: Michael Soareverix

entry.summary: A discussion write-up in which the author, previously a pause advocate, reports becoming more wary of pausing after conversation with a researcher, reasoning about how a pause following a major security incident could create misaligned incentives among labs and states. It references a sharp shift in community sentiment after a widely discussed model-security incident. The value is in surfacing second-order effects of pause policies.

entry.title: Demo: Real-time Generative Multicasting with On-Device Intent-aware Semantic Decomposition

author.name: Xinkai Liu, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yi Ma, Rahim Tafazolli

entry.summary: A demonstration system for semantic multicasting where a transmitter sends a segmentation-derived semantic map to all receivers and only the sub-signals each user cares about, letting a generative model locally synthesize the rest. The authors also derive rate-distortion-perception tradeoff curves for the mixed reconstruct-plus-synthesize regime.

entry.title: Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G/6G Channel Estimation with Hardware-in-the-loop Validation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: A convolutional network estimates both magnitude and phase of the wireless channel from pilot symbols, explicitly handling phase wrap-around discontinuities that trip up prior deep estimators. Evaluation uses emulated data from an end-to-end O-RAN testbed with hardware in the loop rather than pure simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Priorities: Multi-Tier SLA Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Anders Vestrum, Arya Raeesi, Hanna Roed

entry.summary: Extends an existing migration-capable multi-instance LLM inference scheduler beyond its two-level priority model to support an arbitrary number of service-level tiers, then evaluates the effect under several workload regimes. The motivation is that production deployments span latency-critical API traffic through background batch jobs.

entry.title: Continuity-Driven Representation Learning for Industrial Defect Detection

author.name: Minjong Kim, Hyun Jun Kim, Jeongrae Kim, Heeseung Shin, Changwon Lim

entry.summary: The authors exploit the fact that industrial inspection images are dominated by repetitive normal regions, adding self-supervised continuity objectives that predict patch sequences and masked spatial content as dense auxiliary supervision for defect detectors. The losses are detector-agnostic and complement sparse bounding-box labels.

entry.title: To Remove or Not to Remove Clouds: A Comparative Analysis and Fusion of Raw SAR and Synthetic NDWI for Overcast Water Segmentation

author.name: Saleh Sakib Ahmed, Sara Nowreen, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: A comparative study asking whether flood water segmentation under full cloud cover should use raw SAR directly or a synthetic optical water index translated from SAR. The authors find the translation step acts as a useful denoiser and that fusing both representations performs best.

entry.title: SE-MoLoRA: Shared-Expert LoRA Adapters for Domain-Specific Photographic Assessment

author.name: Bishwash Khanal, Anlan Zhang, Sasu Tarkoma, Tommi Mikkonen, Abhishek Kumar

entry.summary: SE-MoLoRA adapts vision-language models for photographic critique using an always-active shared low-rank expert plus routed specialists for composition, lighting and technical quality, selected by a lightweight query router. The aim is actionable, domain-specific feedback rather than generic image description.

entry.title: Is Haar Enough? Exploring Symlets and Coiflets for Wavelet Convolution Layers

author.name: Md Rifat Ur Rahman

entry.summary: A systematic study of which wavelet basis to use in wavelet convolution layers, showing that longer filters with stronger approximation properties can reduce the number of decomposition levels needed and therefore cut parameters and FLOPs overall. The paper formalizes this as a filter-length versus decomposition-depth tradeoff.

entry.title: Scale Matters: Adaptive Granularity Selection for Cross-Species 3D Plant Organ Segmentation

author.name: Carla Salazar, Lazaros Nalpantidis

entry.summary: AGS-PlantSeg performs few-shot 3D plant organ segmentation by adaptively choosing spatial granularity levels from a frozen 3D point cloud foundation model, then feeding the selected features to a light segmentation head. Fixed granularity limits generalization across species and growth stages in phenotyping.

entry.title: Optimal control of a swimming robot based on Purcell's microswimmer model

author.name: Noam Berkovich Lahav, Oren Wiezel, Yizhar Or

entry.summary: The authors build a macro-scale robotic realization of Purcell's classic three-link microswimmer operating in a highly viscous fluid, extend the theoretical model with non-slender links and a central drag-contributing sphere, calibrate it to experiments, and then compute optimal gaits. This grounds a long-studied theoretical locomotion model in measured hardware behavior. It is a clean but narrow contribution to low-Reynolds-number robotic locomotion.

entry.title: Information fusion and machine learning for sensitivity analysis using physics knowledge and experimental data

author.name: Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Sankaran Mahadevan

entry.summary: This paper studies global sensitivity analysis when both a physics-based model and experimental data are available, comparing deep neural networks and Gaussian processes under two strategies for injecting physics knowledge to maximize accuracy of sensitivity estimates. The framing is information fusion for engineering systems under model uncertainty. It is a methodological comparison rather than a new algorithm.

entry.title: An RKHS Framework for Fixed Effects in Permanental Process Models

author.name: Matthew LeDuc

entry.summary: This short paper extends permanental process models to include fixed effects by placing a prior on the coefficients and showing that, in the diffuse prior limit, the representer theorem decomposes the intensity into a fixed-effects term plus a function in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose squared norm equals the limiting penalty. This makes the models easier to interpret scientifically and to encode domain knowledge into. It is a targeted statistical modeling contribution.

entry.title: HLSR: Hybrid Live Forecast Selective Dynamic Vehicle Rerouting for Real-Time Congestion Avoidance

author.name: Xiao Wang, Shun Ren Yang, Hui Nien Hung

entry.summary: HLSR reroutes only a selected subset of vehicles by fusing live edge speeds with short-horizon forecasts, using dual-threshold congestion detection, upstream selection, and travel-time-weighted k-shortest-path candidates. It relaxes the unrealistic assumption in prior work that every vehicle can be replanned each period.

entry.title: Token Optimization and Context Window Management in Multi-Agent AI Workflows

author.name: Dvir Shamay

entry.summary: A practitioner report describing six patterns for controlling token cost and context quality in production multi-agent workflows, including context stratification, fetch-once processing, schema-contracted prompts, token-aware fallback chains, semantic caching, and compressed inter-agent messages. Reported cold-load latency dropped from minutes to roughly one to two minutes across six timed runs. Useful engineering guidance, weakly evidenced.

entry.title: Geometry Is Not Robustness: A Trajectory-Level Study of PGD Evaluation

author.name: Dhairysheel Durgule

entry.summary: This study tests whether trajectory-level diagnostics of projected gradient descent attacks, such as loss evolution and steps-to-failure, actually track robustness strength across clean and adversarially trained CNNs. The conclusion is that attack-path geometry does not reliably indicate robustness.

entry.title: Fractional Optimizers Meet Fractal Activation Functions: An Empirical Study of Multi-Scale Optimization in Neural Network

author.name: Sebastian Raubitzek, Georg Goldenits, Sebastian Schrittwieser, Philip K\"onig, Kevin Mallinger

entry.summary: The paper empirically studies whether fractional-derivative optimizers and fractal, self-similar activation functions interact usefully, testing on synthetic optimization surfaces and ten classification datasets. It provides a unified comparison of two previously separate lines of exotic training modifications.

entry.title: Explainability Boosted Anomaly Detection Framework for O-RAN based NextG Networks

author.name: Nurullah Aksu, Ali Fuat Sahin, Semiha Tedik Ba\c{s}aran

entry.summary: An anomaly detection framework for open radio access networks combines several AI models with post-hoc explainability to identify malicious traffic and rank which key performance indicators drive detections, evaluated on a realistic testbed. The explainability layer is used to reduce feature load and make alerts actionable for operators.

entry.title: ARISE: An adaptive residual-informed stability ensemble for feature selection in small-sample biomedical omics

author.name: Zardad Khan, Amjad Ali, Naz Gul, Sheema Gul, Saeed Aldahmani

entry.summary: ARISE is a feature-selection ensemble for small-sample omics classification that combines seven normalized relevance signals through predefined profiles weighted by nested inner cross-validation, adds class-balanced stability assessment, residual-informed redundancy control and multiclass pairwise coverage. It is benchmarked on five molecular datasets against six filter methods with three fixed classifiers.

entry.title: Resource-Efficient QUBO Formulation for Anchored Currency Arbitrage

author.name: Eric A. F. Reinhardt, Adam J. Hauser

entry.summary: Formulates currency arbitrage as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem with realistic constraints including starting from a held currency and per-transaction fees, using fewer binary variables than prior encodings. The authors derive provably sufficient penalty weights and an exact rate-reweighting that compresses the problem.

entry.title: Terrain-Aware Local Path Planning with Global DEM Data Integration for Autonomous UGV Navigation

author.name: Devender Singh, Issah Nazif Suleiman, Paul Mitten, Glenn Cutler, Vinicius Prado da Fonseca, Matthew Hamilton

entry.summary: This work combines coarse digital elevation model data for global A* path planning with real-time LiDAR terrain analysis for local adaptive replanning on an unmanned ground vehicle. Gazebo simulations show improvements over a baseline in traversal efficiency and safety in rough outdoor terrain. It is a practical systems integration paper for off-road autonomy.

entry.title: Cui bono? ChatGPT-4o shows non-deceptive strategic persuasion: a Proof-of-Concept study

author.name: Pieter Barkema

entry.summary: A short project from a 40-hour safety sprint evaluates whether a model will steer users toward pro-AI, less safety-preserving choices in AI-safety scenarios, reporting persuasion attempts that the author characterizes as strategic but non-deceptive. The framing of persuasion propensity as a distinct measurable dimension from persuasive capability is the useful part. Findings are proof-of-concept only.

entry.title: Without journalists, there is no journalism: the social dimension of generative artificial intelligence in the media

author.name: Sim\'on Pe\~na-Fern\'andez, Koldobika Meso-Ayerdi, Ainara Larrondo-Ureta, Javier D\'iaz-Noci

entry.summary: A systematic review of two decades of empirical research on AI adoption in newsrooms, focused on the social and epistemological consequences for journalists and media organizations. It highlights platform dependence versus editorial independence and the erosion of journalists' role as intermediaries. Contextual reading for media-facing AI deployment.

entry.title: Not All Attention Is Equal: A Quantitative Survey of the EEI Trade-off

author.name: Aditya Singh

entry.summary: A survey of twenty-one attention mechanisms scored along efficiency, expressiveness, and interpretability axes, with a Monte Carlo perturbation analysis of how fragile the resulting rankings are. The analysis itself concludes that most rankings shift by more than one position under small rating perturbations.

entry.title: A Data-Efficient Analytical Prior Machine Learning Framework for Sound Reduction Frequency Prediction in Helmholtz Resonators

author.name: Jiaming Li

entry.summary: This study improves data efficiency for predicting sound reduction frequencies of Helmholtz resonators by reusing a cheap analytical model, either learning only the analytical-to-simulation discrepancy or distilling the analytical mapping into a self-contained predictor. The aim is reliable surrogates under small finite-element simulation budgets.

entry.title: Characterization of Thermal Systems from Noisy and Low-resolution Measurements Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition

author.name: M. E. P. Silva, L. S. Araujo, F. T. Colombo, A. Cunha Jr, S. da Silva

entry.summary: This chapter evaluates dynamic mode decomposition for identifying heat transfer dynamics from sparse, noisy, low-resolution thermal measurements, focusing on preprocessing and rank-truncation choices that determine stability and interpretability. Two experimental cases with thermocouple and transient data are examined.

entry.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White Detection at 471:1 Class Imbalance: A Leakage-Controlled Study of the Data Bottleneck

author.name: Nathael Altman

entry.summary: A leakage-controlled benchmark of seven signal representations for detecting the rare Wolff-Parkinson-White ECG pattern at roughly 471-to-1 class imbalance across two pooled public corpora. The finding is negative: extra model diversity and capacity do not raise the performance ceiling, suggesting a data rather than modeling bottleneck.

entry.title: Does the Heart Show Your Pain? Tackling the X-ITE Pain Challenge with Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning

author.name: Dominika Kunc, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Stanis{\l}aw Saganowski

entry.summary: Self-supervised representation learning is applied to single-lead ECG, with additional multimodal pretraining using chest accelerometer signals, to classify low versus medium pain on the X-ITE dataset. Results show weak unimodal performance, gains from cross-modal pretraining, and large inter-subject variability implying person-specific pain signatures.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Dataset Curation for Kuala Lumpur Urban Traffic: Grounded Vision-Language Detection with Spatial Vehicle-Context Filtering

author.name: Mohammed Abdul Al Arafat Tanzin, Rudzidatul Akmam Dziyauddin

entry.summary: An automated anonymization pipeline for a Kuala Lumpur road video dataset uses grounded vision-language detection plus spatial vehicle-context filtering to find faces and plates that classical cascades and YOLOv8 miss under motorcycle density, dark plates, camera tilt and tropical glare. The paper documents the failure modes of legacy detectors in these conditions.

entry.title: A Parameter-Free Few-Shot Evaluation for Elephant Vocalisation Classification

author.name: Christiaan M. Geldenhuys, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: The paper evaluates parameter-free nearest-centroid classification of elephant vocalizations on frozen pretrained audio embeddings, varying the number of labeled examples per class across two datasets. The question asked is how the simplest possible classifier scales with label budget rather than which embedding wins with full supervision.

entry.title: DualMiT-Net: Local-Global Transformer-Convolutional Fusion for Breast Mass Segmentation in Mammographic Regions of Interest

author.name: Alibek Kamiluly, Milana Muratova, Yash Patel, Fan Li

entry.summary: DualMiT-Net segments breast masses in mammography using a dual-branch design where a transformer encoder sees a focused local view and a convolutional encoder sees surrounding tissue context, fused progressively in a single decoder with a spatial gate controlling global information flow. It targets low-contrast masses with boundaries blending into surrounding tissue.

entry.title: PLeDO: Pain Level Detection for Osteoarthritis from EMR Data

author.name: Yuhao Chen, Jiahao Cai, Nafiz Sadman, Farhana Zulkernine, John Queenan, David Barber

entry.summary: Builds a pipeline to classify osteoarthritis pain severity from primary-care electronic medical records, combining structured fields with NLP over unstructured chart notes and a synonym-based extractor for pain expressions. It is framed explicitly as a pilot study to link pain severity to diagnosis and treatment patterns.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Text Embedding Models for Entity Resolution

author.name: Khajesh Sapram, Srivardhani Raju, Kishore Konda

entry.summary: Tests whether triplet-based fine-tuning can adapt general text embedding models for identity-sensitive retrieval, where small textual differences may or may not change which real-world entity is referenced. Evaluation uses a synthetic dataset of business and person records with identity-preserving variants and hard negatives.

entry.title: RetiWave-Mamba: A Dual-Stream Network for Retinal Disease Detection based on Multi-scale Context and Frequency-Adaptive Mamba Projection

author.name: Cheng Cheng, Jin Hong

entry.summary: RetiWave-Mamba splits retinal OCT images into low- and high-frequency streams via wavelet decomposition and processes them with state-space model branches to handle speckle noise, varying lesion scale and subtle class differences. It targets automated retinal disease detection.

entry.title: Cognitive Graph Intelligence for Adaptive and Robust DDoS Attack Detection in Next Generation Networks

author.name: Mohammad Arif Hossain, Yeahia Sarker, Md Jafrin Hossain, Most. Humayra Khanom Rime, Nirwan Ansari

entry.summary: Applies a graph-based generative adversarial network to DDoS detection, converting flow sequences into k-nearest-neighbor graphs and synthesizing minority attack samples to counter class imbalance. Positions the model as a cognitive detection engine for next-generation networks.

entry.title: Optimizing Multi-Market Participation of Battery and Electrolyser Systems Based on Field Performance

author.name: Chunyang Zhao, Stoyan Trenchev, Shi You, Chresten Tr{\ae}holt

entry.summary: The work characterizes a 55 kW battery system and a small electrolyser stack experimentally, embedding measured ramp limits, efficiency, and setpoint-tracking accuracy into a price-driven multi-market revenue optimization. It shows that ignoring real hardware behavior misstates achievable stacked revenues.

entry.title: B-Spline Embedded Structure Learning for 3D Tooth Segmentation

author.name: Xianghan Wei, Jianwen Lou, Zhiguo Lu, Hairong Jin, Haihua Zhu

entry.summary: The paper regularizes 3D tooth segmentation by fitting a parametric B-spline curve through tooth centers, giving each point a continuous structural embedding that encodes the global dental arch layout. This helps disambiguate crowded and morphologically similar adjacent teeth in digital dentistry scans.

entry.title: Automated ACL Footprint Identification Using 3D Deep Learning

author.name: Ruida Cheng, Ali Uneri, Gabriel Gibson, Frances T. Sheehan, Barry Boden

entry.summary: A 3D deep learning method automatically identifies the anterior cruciate ligament femoral footprint to guide tunnel placement in reconstruction surgery, where malpositioning is a leading cause of graft failure. Prior AI work focused on ligament segmentation and rupture classification rather than surgical landmarking.

entry.title: Bi-Layer Ant Colony Optimization for Multi-Robot Task Allocation and Routing in Delivery Applications

author.name: Le Na Nguyen, Thanh Long Nguyen, Thanh Thao Ton Nu, Quan Le, Manh Duong Phung

entry.summary: The paper formulates multi-robot task allocation and routing for delivery as a single optimization problem with a new unified cost function, then solves it with a two-layer ant colony optimization scheme inside one colony process. Comparisons against mixed-integer linear programming and particle swarm optimization show shorter total travel distances. It is an applied metaheuristics contribution for logistics fleets.

entry.title: Average Distance Approximation for Static Large Graphs

author.name: Kartikey Ahlawat

entry.summary: An empirical comparison of random-walk sampling versus landmark-based estimators such as the Size Estimation Framework and Eppstein-Wang for approximating average shortest-path distance in very large graphs under memory constraints. Landmark methods with HyperLogLog sketches dominate sampling approaches, which need very large samples to be accurate. Relevant to practical graph analytics pipelines.

entry.title: Computational Prosopography across a Millennium: Mathematically Oriented Lineages Traced from the Fields Medalists

author.name: Hiroyuki Chuma, Kanji Otsuka, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: Using roughly 470k mentor-student assertions from Wikidata, the authors build a 372k-person academic genealogy graph and trace ancestry backward from all 64 Fields Medalists across 57 generations. They report structural findings such as an hourglass pattern of lineage traffic through Leibniz, and apply source criticism to the underlying records. It is computational history of science rather than AI methodology.

entry.title: WIP: LLM Odyssey: A Game-Based Platform for Teaching LLM Engineering Concepts

author.name: Priyamvada Tripathi

entry.summary: A work-in-progress report on an open-source browser platform of thirteen games that teach LLM engineering topics such as tokenization, transformer internals, prompting, retrieval augmentation, and deployment, organized into three tiers mapped to Bloom's taxonomy. It targets a gap in undergraduate curricula. Educational infrastructure rather than research.

entry.title: A Low-Cost IoT Device for Environmental Monitoring and Embedded Solar Forecasting with On-Device Incremental Learning

author.name: Erick Michel Lara Pinal, Abhinav Das, Stephan Schl\"uter

entry.summary: A roughly 65 dollar ESP32-based sensor node measures temperature, humidity, luminosity and irradiance and runs an embedded 24-hour solar voltage forecast, with models trained offline in TensorFlow and updated incrementally on-device. The goal is to make dense hyperlocal photovoltaic forecasting economically feasible.

entry.title: Hardware-in-the-Loop Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G Channel Estimation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: A companion demonstration from the same group showing live inference of a phase-aware convolutional channel estimator on uplink reference signals collected from a hardware-in-the-loop 5G platform with commercial RF generation, channel emulation and an O-RAN radio unit. The emphasis is exposing the estimator to real impairments such as phase noise, quantization and synchronization error.

entry.title: Local Gains and Fixed-Assignment Set Losses in Shared Set Decoders

author.name: Ze Zhang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: A causal-style ablation study on two detection transformer checkpoints deletes query-relation associations and measures the tradeoff between improving the edited slot and degrading the prediction set that contains it, using hundreds of paired image-relation units and a matched active control. The consistent finding is locally positive but set-level negative effects from fixed assignment.

entry.title: The Note-Chord-Voice Framework: Structured Source Separation and Causal Inference for EV Charging Data

author.name: Jiajie Chen, Jinfeng Li

entry.summary: A staged pipeline for electric vehicle charging data separates session repair, structural pattern discovery, nonnegative matrix factorization source separation and causal price-elasticity estimation, with explicit falsification gates that test whether the data are suitable before modeling. It targets fragmentation from billing resets, physically impossible session records and collider bias from clustering on post-treatment outcomes.

entry.title: CoupVisor: Strategy Optimization by Round and Challenge Decision Support

author.name: Cris Huynh

entry.summary: Describes a decision-support system for the hidden-information bluffing card game Coup that shares a single event representation across manual play, replays, simulation, belief tracking, and learned policies. It estimates claim truthfulness by combining role priors with the claimant's remaining card count and compares rule-based advisors against learned and heuristic players.

entry.title: MagViT: Interpretable Multi-Magnification Transformers with Patient-Level Model Selection for Breast Histopathology

author.name: Nabil Ashab, Soumit Kumar Kundu, Saif Mahmud Parvez, Shahadat Hossain Sohag, Bidhan Biswas, Nazmus Subha

entry.summary: MagViT classifies breast histopathology by extracting features at four microscope magnifications, fusing them with scale gating, and selecting models at the patient level for interpretability and cross-domain generalization. It is evaluated on a public magnification-annotated dataset.

entry.title: Offline Ambient-Controlled Latent Diffusion: Architecture, Telemetry, and On-Device Evaluation

author.name: Lech Kalinowski, Artur Morys-Magiera, Piotr Mi{\l}kowski

entry.summary: An Android application runs latent diffusion fully on-device, conditioned on the ambient light sensor instead of text prompts, and binds each generated image to its sensor reading, runtime path and seed to create a per-artifact audit trail. A fixed capture of 373 outputs on one phone confirms the intended correlation between measured light and output luminance.

entry.title: ORViT-DR: Ordinally-Robust Hybrid ViT for Low-Resolution Diabetic Retinopathy Grading

author.name: Soumit Kumar Kundu, Nabil Ashab, Bidhan Biswas, Shahadat Hossain Sohag, Saif Mahmud Parvez, Souvik Kumar Kundu, Zunayed Ahmed Rafi

entry.summary: ORViT-DR grades diabetic retinopathy from low-resolution fundus images with a hybrid convolutional and transformer backbone plus ordinal-aware training that respects the graded severity structure of neighboring classes. Evaluation uses a standard small-image retinal benchmark.

entry.title: AppendiGrade: An XAI-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for Grading Appendicitis in Ultrasound with Gaussian Blur and Grad-CAM

author.name: Fahad Ahammed, Omar Faruq Shikdar, Navid Zaman, Md Tahsin, Md. Nawab Yousuf Ali, Golam Sorwar

entry.summary: AppendiGrade trains a deep classifier on roughly 4,700 ultrasound images across five appendicitis-related classes, adding Gaussian blur augmentation and Grad-CAM visualizations for interpretability. The aim is to distinguish complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis without radiation exposure.

entry.title: AI Security is Harm Reduction

author.name: Quinn

entry.summary: A short ethical reflection framing work on AI security as harm reduction, analogized to 1990s needle exchange programs: if recursive self-improvement is going to happen regardless of the author's approval, it may as well be made secure. It addresses the personal moral tension of contributing to a technology one does not endorse. No technical content is presented.

entry.title: Evaluating the impact of adversarial traffic patterns on vanet communication using veins simulation

author.name: Henry Agyapong

entry.summary: A simulation study using Veins/OMNeT++/SUMO to measure how adversarial behaviors such as message flooding, false information and coordinated congestion attacks degrade vehicular network performance metrics like packet delivery ratio and delay. It is essentially a scenario-based robustness evaluation for vehicle-to-vehicle communication rather than a machine learning contribution.

entry.title: Potential of ChatGPT in predicting stock market trends based on Twitter Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Ummara Mumtaz, Summaya Mumtaz

entry.summary: An older cross-listed study asking whether ChatGPT sentiment scores on tweets can anticipate next-day price movements for two large technology stocks. It reports a positive association between the model's sentiment evaluations and subsequent stock outcomes.

entry.title: QuantumPhaseNet: A Gauge-Covariant Geometric and Quantum-Spectral Theory of Semantic Concept Hierarchies with Prototype Validation of a Classical Quantum-Inspired Model

author.name: Kiyotaka Kasubuchi, Kazuo Fukiya

entry.summary: Proposes a quantum-inspired reformulation of Transformer representations in which semantic states are complex amplitudes, phase rates define a semantic wavelength, and graph spectral modes define a document-level direction, along with claimed guarantees about gauge invariance, unitarity, and a calibratable hallucination-risk measure. Validation is performed on built-in synthetic data through a self-contained offline studio.

entry.title: LASR Labs January 2027 applications are open!

author.name: Brandon Riggs

entry.summary: An application announcement for a 13-week in-person London AI safety research programme where teams of three or four produce an academic paper under supervision, citing prior acceptances at NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML including main-conference papers. It is field-building infrastructure rather than research. Useful mainly to prospective applicants.

entry.title: Putting your mask on first

author.name: emiliob

entry.summary: A short personal essay arguing that genuine service to others must be grounded in self-compassion, prompted by observing people who help others while neglecting themselves. It contains no technical or empirical content. Relevance to AI research is essentially nil.

entry.title: Natural Independence Incentives

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A parenting essay about deliberately using naturally motivating situations, such as a child wanting dessert, to build independence with minimal adult scaffolding. It contains anecdotes and reflection on incentive design in child-rearing. There is no AI or research content.

entry.title: Transhumanism & Human Enhancement Meetup (Online)

author.name: nxzt

entry.summary: An announcement for a casual online meetup about transhumanism, human enhancement, longevity, and related ethics, open to all experience levels. It is logistical rather than substantive. No research content is presented.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
AI for mathematics and discovery leads today's batch. Reformulating the core optimization behind the laser method with modern solvers plus AlphaEvolve pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable advance on a famous constant. Euclid-Omni pairs a symbolic plane-geometry engine with LLMs/VLMs for formal and natural-language proofs, while ALPS scores machine-verifiable mathematical originality.

Interpretability and science-of-models work is unusually strong:

  • MIT (Andreas, Fedorenko) find modular cognitive architecture emerging spontaneously across 46 tasks, with separable language, formal, social, and physical reasoning circuits.
  • Counterfactual-simulatability testing asks whether model explanations actually predict behavior on related in-the-wild inputs.
  • Behavioral Lift shows amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are often non-predictive of correctness.
  • A proposed curse of ambiguity links discrete output parameterization to poor high-entropy next-token fidelity.

Safety, alignment, and multi-agent risk cluster around emergent, aggregate effects:

  • Model hypnosis shows many individually negligible prompt cues (paraphrases, typos) combine additively into strong cross-model control.
  • Analysis of 2,583 inter-agent emails across 20 year-long vending-business runs and 13 frontier LLMs documents emergent misaligned agent-to-agent communication.
  • Physics of Agents applies statistical mechanics to 10,000+ agent communities, predicting phase-like consensus and polarization dynamics.
  • A technical critique argues chain-of-thought monitorability evals proposed for industry-wide adoption remain unresolved; DEI-prompt demographic injection in medical LLMs shows a concrete deployment hazard.

Architecture, efficiency, and embodied systems: Proteus incrementally activates memory to fix capacity pathologies in linear-attention long-context models; GigaBrain-0.7 unifies understanding, prediction, and action in a three-system embodied model; ClawGym II enables black-box RL through opaque agent harnesses. Prior Labs open-sources RelArena-α, TabPFN-Rel, and RPI for reproducible relational learning. Also notable: KV cache compression framed as rate-distortion transform coding, Equilibrium Forcing for noise-conditioning-free video generation, QUASAR QAT, and the Jais 2 Arabic-centric open weights.
entry.content:
AI for mathematics and discovery leads today's batch. Reformulating the core optimization behind the laser method with modern solvers plus AlphaEvolve pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable advance on a famous constant. Euclid-Omni pairs a symbolic plane-geometry engine with LLMs/VLMs for formal and natural-language proofs, while ALPS scores machine-verifiable mathematical originality.

Interpretability and science-of-models work is unusually strong:

  • MIT (Andreas, Fedorenko) find modular cognitive architecture emerging spontaneously across 46 tasks, with separable language, formal, social, and physical reasoning circuits.
  • Counterfactual-simulatability testing asks whether model explanations actually predict behavior on related in-the-wild inputs.
  • Behavioral Lift shows amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are often non-predictive of correctness.
  • A proposed curse of ambiguity links discrete output parameterization to poor high-entropy next-token fidelity.

Safety, alignment, and multi-agent risk cluster around emergent, aggregate effects:

  • Model hypnosis shows many individually negligible prompt cues (paraphrases, typos) combine additively into strong cross-model control.
  • Analysis of 2,583 inter-agent emails across 20 year-long vending-business runs and 13 frontier LLMs documents emergent misaligned agent-to-agent communication.
  • Physics of Agents applies statistical mechanics to 10,000+ agent communities, predicting phase-like consensus and polarization dynamics.
  • A technical critique argues chain-of-thought monitorability evals proposed for industry-wide adoption remain unresolved; DEI-prompt demographic injection in medical LLMs shows a concrete deployment hazard.

Architecture, efficiency, and embodied systems: Proteus incrementally activates memory to fix capacity pathologies in linear-attention long-context models; GigaBrain-0.7 unifies understanding, prediction, and action in a three-system embodied model; ClawGym II enables black-box RL through opaque agent harnesses. Prior Labs open-sources RelArena-α, TabPFN-Rel, and RPI for reproducible relational learning. Also notable: KV cache compression framed as rate-distortion transform coding, Equilibrium Forcing for noise-conditioning-free video generation, QUASAR QAT, and the Jais 2 Arabic-centric open weights.

entry.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve

author.name: Emilien Dupont, Marvin Eisenberger, Borislav Kozlovskii, Abbas Mehrabian, Francisco J. R. Ruiz, Abigail See, Renfei Zhou, Josh Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams, Matej Balog

entry.summary: Improves the best known upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent to below 2.371177 by reformulating the optimization problem at the heart of combination loss analysis, designing a new machine-learning-based optimizer for it, and refining that optimizer with AlphaEvolve. It combines DeepMind researchers with leading complexity theorists on a long-standing open problem.

entry.title: Proteus: Incremental Memory Activation for Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Reza Bayat, Ali Behrouz, Vahab Mirrokni, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: Proteus proposes incremental memory activation for long-context sequence models, progressively expanding the effective capacity of a compressed recurrent memory as the sequence grows rather than exposing a static state from the first token. The early bottleneck forces stronger compression of early history and reduces interference between stored context and incoming tokens.

entry.title: Physics of Agents: Statistical Mechanics Predicts Collective Behavior of AI Agents

author.name: Batu El, Jinhee Paeng, Fatih Dinc, Shiye Su, Mete Erdogan, Aneesh Pappu, Haotian Ye, Wanjia Zhao, Surya Ganguli, James Zou

entry.summary: The paper behind earlier this week's Reddit thread on agents spontaneously agreeing, Studying over ten thousand communities of language-model agents that exchange messages and revise opinions on both objective math questions and subjective political statements, the authors find the dynamics collapse into a small number of characteristic regimes and can be described with statistical mechanics style models. This makes collective behaviors such as herding and polarization predictable rather than anecdotal. It provides design guidance for multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Model Hypnosis: Strong control of AI via additive subliminal effects

author.name: Enric Boix-Adsera, Benedict Tessler

entry.summary: Reports model hypnosis, in which many individually negligible prompt cues such as paraphrases and typos can be additively combined to exert strong control over model behavior, and shows the effect across model families and scales including frontier reasoning models with transferable hypnotic prompts. The authors argue this creates a new class of safety and interpretability problems because control is exercised through inconspicuous surface choices.

entry.title: Advancing Open and Reproducible Relational Learning: RelArena-$\alpha$, TabPFN-Rel and RPI

author.name: Adrian Hayler, Klemens Fl\"oge, Alan Arazi, Rishabh Ranjan, Jure Leskovec, Felix Birkel, Brendan Roof, Anurag Garg, Kristina Collins, Lydia Sidhoum, Jonas K\"ubler, Siyuan Guo, Oscar Key, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Rylee Grace, David Salinas, Arthur Cahu, Simon Bing, Benjamin J\"ager, Tuana \c{C}elik, Mihir Manium, Vitor Monteiro, Jake Robertson, Jerry Chen, Eliott Kalfon, Tom\'as Pereda, Lilly Wehrhahn, Dominik Safaric, Tobias Schroeder, Georg Grab, Diana Kriuchkova, Clara Cornu, Philipp Singer, Nick Erickson, Vahid Balazadeh, Marie Salmon, Simone Alessi, K\"ur\c{s}at Kaya, Philipp Jund, L\'eo Grinsztajn, Yann LeCun, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Madelon Hulsebos, Lennart Purucker, Sauraj Gambhir, Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann

entry.summary: Prior Labs open-sources three relational-learning artifacts: RelArena-alpha, a unified benchmarking framework for relational tasks; TabPFN-Rel, a tabular foundation model extended to relational data; and RPI. The release targets reproducible comparison across relational deep learning methods, an area lacking convergence on evaluation.

entry.title: GigaBrain-0.7: Scaling Embodied Foundation Models to Emergent Capabilities with a Three-System Architecture

author.name: GigaBrain Team, Angen Ye, Axiang Sun, Can Jin, Chenxi Cheng, Chong Shi, Dengke Shang, Dingqian Zhang, Guan Huang, Guangqiang Wang, Guangqing Ding, Guo Li, Hangcong Li, Hengyu Zhong, Hongtao Lu, Jianbo Qin, Jiming Mao, Jing Zhu, Jindi Lv, Jingzhi Cui, Junjie Xie, Junyi Bao, Kai Liu, Lei Yuan, Limin Long, Lv Feng, Mingming Yu, Peng Li, Pengfei Yi, Qi Li, Qianli Zhang, Qingfang Li, Qitang Hu, Rui Zhang, Shaoyan Sun, Shibo Sun, Shiying Duan, Tenghui Chen, Tianze Liu, Weijie Ke, Wenyao Xue, Xiaofeng Wang, Xiaoyu Tian, Xinyu Liu, Xinze Chen, Yang Wang, Yankai Wang, Yejun Zeng, Yifan Li, Yifei Nie, Yilong Li, Yilong Liu, Yongchao Feng, Yumeng Wang, Yun Ye, Zhichao Liu, Ziheng He, Zonghai Yang, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: GigaBrain-0.7 is an embodied foundation model that unifies understanding, prediction, and action in a three-system architecture and is pretrained on more than 37,000 hours of heterogeneous embodiment data. The team reports substantially improved generalization across robot embodiments and claims emergent capabilities from this scaling.

entry.title: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce

author.name: Zeyuan Li (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Lukas Petersson (Andon Labs), Alessandro Acquisti (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Michiel A. Bakker (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Analyzes 2,583 inter-agent emails from 20 simulated year-long runs of a competitive vending-machine business environment spanning 13 frontier LLMs, measuring speech-act misalignment such as false factual claims, manipulation, collusion, and threats. It moves beyond adversarial single-agent elicitation to measure how misaligned communication arises spontaneously in long-horizon, multi-principal commerce.

entry.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

author.name: Adam Karvonen, Euan Ong, Subhash Kantamneni, Samuel Marks

entry.summary: This paper evaluates explanations of model behavior by counterfactual simulatability, whether an explanation predicts what the model does on related edited inputs, and introduces CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that finds unexpected behaviors in real usage and probes them with counterfactual prompt edits. It produces thousands of explanations with supporting counterfactual evidence for naturally occurring behaviors.

entry.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness

author.name: Huatong Song, Fei Bai, Ming Yang, Renyuan Li, Jia Deng, Jujie He, Zhange Zhang, Daixuan Cheng, Yan Xing, Qi Yun, Xuxing Chen, Danyang Li, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Jian Yang, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao, Mingjie Tang, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: ClawGym II builds a black-box reinforcement learning framework for training agents through complex, opaque agent harnesses, using sandboxed concurrent rollouts and a serving proxy at the model boundary to capture trajectories without instrumenting harness internals. This decouples policy optimization from harness execution so long-horizon agentic RL can scale.

entry.title: Jais 2: A Family of Arabic-Centric Open Large Language Models

author.name: Mohamed Anwar, Abed Alhakim Freihat, George Ibrahim, Mostafa Awad, Abdelrahman Sadallah, Gurpreet Gosal, Gokulakrishnan Ramakrishnan, Sarath Chandran, Biswajit Mishra, Rituraj Joshi, Ahmed Frikha, Etienne Goffinet, Abhishek Maiti, Ali El Filali, Sarah AlBarri, Samujjwal Ghosh, Rahul Pal, Parvez Mullah, Awantika Shukla, Sajid siddiki, Samta Kamboj, Onkar Pandit, Sunil Kumar Sahu, AbdelRahman Elbadawy, Amr Mohamed, Ahmad Chamma, Evan Dufraisse, Abdelaziz Bounhar, Dani Bouch, Hadi Abdine, Guokan Shang, Fajri Koto, Yuxia Wang, Zhuohan Xie, Ali Mekky, Rania Elbadry, Sarfraz Ahmad, Momina Ahsan, Omar El Herraoui, Daniil Orel, Hasan Iqbal, Kareem Elzeky, Mervat Abassy, Kareem Elozeiri, Saadeldine Eletter, Farah Atif, Nurdaulet Mukhituly, Haonan Li, Xudong Han, Aaryamonvikram Singh, Zainul Abedien Ahmed Quraishi, Neha Sengupta, Larry Murray, Avraham Sheinin, Joel Hestness, Natalia Vassilieva, Hector Xuguang Ren, Zhengzhong Liu, Michalis Vazirgiannis, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: Jais 2 is an Arabic-centric open LLM family from MBZUAI, Cerebras, and Inception, including what the authors describe as the largest open Arabic-centric model trained from scratch at 70B parameters plus a competitive 8B variant. A custom Arabic vocabulary and optimized training recipe deliver strong Arabic and culturally grounded benchmark results with a substantially smaller token budget than comparable models.

entry.title: WANDR: A Benchmark for Wide and Deep Research

author.name: Vitaliy Polshkov, Marcin Pitera, Jeremy Yang, Kirill Priemko, Maksim Gaiduk, Aleksandr Nikolenko, Denis Bykov, Clare Southern, Denis Yarats, Jerry Ma

entry.summary: WANDR is a benchmark of 500 realistic data-collection tasks for research agents that require both breadth, discovering many entities meeting criteria, and depth, investigating each entity via multiple coordinated searches, with independently verifiable records and cited excerpts. Tasks are structured as qualification key hierarchies whose record counts multiply across levels.

entry.title: Demographic Injection in Medical Language Models under Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Prompts

author.name: Diego Mardian, Frank Liu

entry.summary: Shows that appending a one-sentence diversity and equity instruction to medical questions causes language models to invent patient demographics that were never stated, raising the injection rate from under one percent to about a third. The effect appears in all 47 models tested across four medical benchmarks and 376,000 graded responses, and is attributable to the equity content rather than prompt length.

entry.title: Equilibrium Forcing: Adaptive Video Generation Without Noise Conditioning

author.name: Hansen Jin Lillemark, Alex Rojas, Zachary Novack, Runqian Wang, Yilun Du, Yian Ma, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Rose Yu

entry.summary: Equilibrium Forcing trains autoregressive video denoisers without conditioning on the noise level, decoupling the learned denoising field from the sampling schedule. This enables closed-loop inference algorithms that adapt to feedback from the partially generated sample, improving quality and temporal consistency on autoregressive video benchmarks.

entry.title: Language models suffer from a curse of ambiguity

author.name: Nicolas Zucchet, Hyun Dong Lee, Scott Linderman

entry.summary: Identifies a curse of ambiguity whereby neural networks producing discrete distributions learn high-entropy next-token distributions less accurately, tracing the effect theoretically to capacity requirements, embedding dimensionality, optimization steps, and amplified sampling noise. Because modern LLM self-improvement pipelines depend on sampling from learned distributions, the fidelity of ambiguous predictive distributions becomes a first-order concern.

entry.title: From Passive Delegates to Strategic Negotiators: Reinforcing Social Reasoning in Small Language Models with SocialRL

author.name: Wenyue Hua, Zachary Huang, Tyler Payne, Safoora Yousefi, Saleema Amershi, Asli Celikyilmaz

entry.summary: Trains social and strategic reasoning directly into a 4B model across six negotiation and delegation domains, arguing that agreeable assistant behavior makes for a poor negotiating delegate that leaks private information and concedes too easily. The recipe reportedly lets a small model act as a competent strategic negotiator on a principal's behalf.

entry.title: HarnessEval-W: Agentifying the Evaluation of Visual Worlds

author.name: Weiliang Chen, Haowen Sun, Jun Gao, Jiawei Chi, Hanyang Wang, Qiyu Dai, Yihao Li, Hao Li, Jingnan Gao, Yi-Hsin Hung, Xingzhuo Guo, Shangchen Miao, Zhiyuan Shi, Xiang Li, Fengrui Tian, Weihua Du, Ziqi Huang, Shenyuan Gao, Siqiao Huang, Mingyu Liu, Yifei Li, Shizun Wang, Xi Wang, Tianqi Zhang, Xue Luo, Xiyin Ren, Jinshan Ren, Xiaoyang Shen, Xiaobo Hu, Zhiyang Dou, Mingyu Ding, Yichao Yan, Xinchao Wang, Yizhou Wang, Shilong Liu, Wenzhao Zheng, Yueqi Duan, Yuan Gong, Ziwei Liu, Ming-Yu Liu, Jialong Wu, Jiangran Lyu, Fangfu Liu

entry.summary: HarnessEval-W turns world model evaluation into an agentic pipeline that interprets each case, decomposes the evaluation question, and produces an inspectable reasoning chain rather than a single brute-force score. The argument is that judging whether physics, causality, and world state evolve correctly requires verifiable justification, not just scalar metrics.

entry.title: Revisiting Open-Loop Execution in Robotics: Toward Reactive, Higher-Performing Policies

author.name: Michael Zeng, Abhinav Agarwal, Ajay Bati, Brian Lee, Siddharth Ancha, Russ Tedrake

entry.summary: A controlled empirical study of why action chunking (predicting a sequence and executing a prefix open-loop) helps imitation-learned manipulation policies, arguing the main benefit is letting short-context policies imitate demonstrations that are not actually Markovian. The work spans four simulated and two real-world tasks and offers guidance for recovering reactivity without losing chunking's benefits.

entry.title: CaliBench: Are the Stochastic Dynamics of Video World Models Physically Calibrated?

author.name: Jonathan Sadeghi, Jenny Seidenschwarz, Jesse Allardice, Sirish Srinivasan, Benjamin Graham, Jeffrey Hawke

entry.summary: CaliBench tests whether video world models reproduce correct probability distributions over physical outcomes by scoring generations in interpretable discrete spaces such as die faces, card suits, and Galton-board bins, where the reference distribution is known in closed form. This enables exact distributional distance measurement rather than the coarse feature-space comparisons used by FID-style metrics.

entry.title: Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive: Reasoning Behaviors in Thinking Models

author.name: Jean de Dieu Nyandwi, Leena Mathur, Yonatan Bisk, Robert Hawkins, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: Introduces Behavioral Lift, measuring how much correctness changes when a specific reasoning behavior appears versus is absent in a trace, and annotates over 15,000 traces across 15 models and 6 text and vision-language benchmarks. Reports an amplification-lift gap in which reasoning-trained models heavily amplify behaviors that are not the ones most predictive of getting the right answer.

entry.title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction

author.name: Vincent Counathe, Ben Athiwaratkun, Christopher De Sa, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: A quantization-aware training method that continuously performs loss-aware weight reconstruction during training, closing the mismatch between the lossy forward reconstruction and updates applied to latent full-precision weights. It borrows the second-order objective of strong post-training quantization methods but makes it cheap enough to repeat throughout training.

entry.title: MOSS-VL Technical Report

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Chenkun Tan, Shaojun Zhou, Qirui Zhou, Yanxin Chen, Xingyang He, Huazheng Zeng, Jijun Cheng, Chenghao Wang, Xiaomeng Qian, Pengfei Wang, Zhan Huang, Shanqing Gao, Wei Huang, Longjun Cao, Wu Ran, Jie Liu, Changtai Zhu, Hongkai Wang, Yixian Tian, Chenghao Liu, Zhen Ye, Xinghao Wang, Botian Jiang, Guoguo Feng, Zhaoye Fei, Ruixiao Li, Mingshu Chen, Yang Gao, Qinyuan Cheng, Shimin Li, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: A technical report on an open vision-language model family designed so that the decoder attends to vision through gated cross-attention, letting the model see incoming frames while it is still speaking. It is trained with a synthesized interaction corpus that supervises when to speak, stay silent, or revise, and reports strong results on streaming benchmarks.

entry.title: Foresight-England: Development of a National-Scale Generative AI Model of Electronic Health Records for Medical Event Prediction across the COVID-19 Pandemic

author.name: Simon Ellershaw, Christopher Tomlinson, Zeljko Kraljevic, Spiros Denaxas, Harry Hemingway, Cathie Sudlow, Angela M. Wood, Anoop D. Shah, Richard Dobson

entry.summary: Foresight-England is a 243M-parameter decoder-only generative model of electronic health records trained entirely inside the NHS England secure data environment on de-identified longitudinal records for roughly 61 million people, spanning primary and secondary care, deaths, and COVID data. It was evaluated as a research pilot on predicting medical events and the direct and indirect effects of the pandemic.

entry.title: KV Cache Compression Through the Lens of Transform Coding

author.name: Hannah Laus, Claudio Mayrink Verdun, Hao Wang, Flavio du Pin Calmon, Felix Krahmer

entry.summary: Reframes KV cache compression as a transform-coding and rate-distortion problem, proving that attention-aware distortion decomposes additively across keys, values, tokens, and channels under a white-noise quantization model. The resulting bit allocation via reverse water-filling targets the error that actually matters for attention outputs rather than raw reconstruction error.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Dengyang Jiang, Ruoyi Du, Zhennan Chen, Dongyang Liu, Zanyi Wang, Mingzhe Zheng, Xiangpeng Yang, Huanqia Cai, Aiming Hao, Yuming Jiang, Peng Gao, Harry Yang, Steven Hoi

entry.summary: A large empirical study of training pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models at scale, finding that direct pixel-space pretraining converges far slower than latent-space pretraining. The authors propose acquiring generative priors in latent space and transitioning to pixel space during post-training, then systematically ablate the key design choices.

entry.title: SQuad: Sub-Quadratic Attention Distillation for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Animesh Karnewar, Denis Korzhenkov, Amirhossein Habibian, Mohsen Ghafoorian

entry.summary: SQuad distills the full quadratic self-attention of video diffusion transformers into a sub-quadratic operator with roughly n-times-square-root-of-n cost, aiming to close the quality gap that linear and low-rank attention surrogates leave behind. This targets the dominant compute term that caps achievable video resolution and duration.

entry.title: $\tau_0$-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation

author.name: Xiaowei Cai, Yunuo Cai, Bingao Chen, Jingxiao Chen, Zhi Chen, Siyuan Feng, Tengyu Hou, Jingshun Huang, Han Jiang, Runkun Ju, Dong Li, Mingxiang Li, Shaowei Li, Xinchen Li, Yifan Li, Yi Liu, Zhongyuan Liu, Jianlan Luo, Junwen Miao, Ruiqi Ni, Buqing Nie, Mingjie Pan, Xinlin Ren, Jianheng Song, Jiaxu Wang, Peiqi Wang, Sen Wang, Xiaoyan Wang, Dafeng Wei, Dongming Wu, Pengwei Xie, Pu Yang, Hangjian Ye, Xiangyu Yue, Jinyu Zhang, Qinglin Zhang, Xueyong Zhao, Pengfei Zhou, Yue Zhou

entry.summary: A hierarchical robot foundation model in which the high-level policy can spend extra inference compute searching over candidate subtasks, guided by a world model and execution memory, before committing, while a low-level policy executes the chosen subtask. This brings test-time compute scaling, familiar from language models, into long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Evaluating Chain-of-Thought Monitorability is Still an Open Problem: Comments on OpenAI's Monitorability Evals

author.name: Connor Dilgren

entry.summary: A critical commentary on an OpenAI paper that proposes a taxonomy and evaluation suite for chain-of-thought monitorability, which OpenAI intends to make a reporting standard on model cards. The post argues that measuring monitorability remains an open problem and identifies limitations in relying on these evals to calibrate trust in CoT monitoring.

entry.title: Euclid-Omni : A Unified Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Plane Geometry

author.name: Zhaoyu Li, Hangrui Bi, Youyuan Zhang, Wenjie Ma, Zenan Li, Zhaolei Zhang, Xujie Si, Kaiyu Yang

entry.summary: Euclid-Omni unifies a symbolic plane-geometry engine with LLMs and vision-language models to handle both computation and proof tasks, in formal and natural language, up to Olympiad difficulty. Its symbolic core generates deductive reasoning steps that supply supervision and verification for the neural components.

entry.title: ALPS: Measuring Valid Creativity in Large Language Models with Mathematical Construction

author.name: Eric Xie, Wenqian Ye, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: ALPS is a benchmark that tests whether a model can produce genuinely original yet machine-verifiable mathematical constructions: for each equational law the task is either to build an infinite structure satisfying it or prove none exists, with submissions checked automatically. It targets the hard problem of separating apparent creativity from memorization by requiring both novelty and formal correctness. This offers a rare contamination-resistant probe of mathematical discovery ability.

entry.title: Eigenanalysis framework for autoregressive neural emulators of multi-scale chaotic dynamics

author.name: Conrad Ainslie, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Michael W. Mahoney, Ashesh Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: The authors analyze the Jacobian of learned one-step update maps to explain why autoregressive neural emulators of chaotic systems diverge, showing stability is governed by the spectral radius. Direct-step architectures generically acquire eigenvalues above one, while integration-constrained formulations do not, giving a principled explanation for widely used ad-hoc stabilization tricks. This is directly relevant to neural weather and climate emulators.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Closed-Loop Reasoning for Organic Structure Elucidation from Multimodal Spectra

author.name: Bingsen Xue, Zhuojun Jiang, Jianhao Zhang, Mingcheng Gu, Yizhe Yuan, Yongtai Zhuo, Yifan Zhang, Li Wang, Ya Su, Yue Yuan, Jiang Liu, Xueqian Kong, Cheng Jin

entry.summary: MACROS is a multi-agent system that elucidates organic molecular structures from routine spectra by emulating expert iterative hypothesis testing, trained on 100M simulated and 1.6M experimental spectra-molecule pairs. It reports zero-shot generalization to real unseen samples including natural products and metabolites above 500 Da using 1D NMR.

entry.title: Le Critique: Privileged Value Functions for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Siddarth Venkatraman, Matthieu Dinot, Laurence Aitchison

entry.summary: Argues for reviving learned value functions in LLM reinforcement learning by giving the critic privileged information, providing token-level credit assignment without the large sampling groups GRPO needs and without being throughput-blocked by straggler rollouts. Proposes two complementary strategies to make critics practical again in RL pipelines.

entry.title: GRPO Beyond English: A Large-Scale Study of GRPO in Non-English and Multilingual Settings

author.name: Konstantin Dobler, Federico Scozzafava, Jonathan Janke, Mohamed Ali, Simon Lehnerer

entry.summary: A large-scale empirical study of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO outside English, sweeping base models, training languages, and reasoning-language reward choices. Finds that training the model to reason in its native language costs little versus reasoning in English, and that strong crosslingual transfer occurs, though trends are highly model- and language-dependent.

entry.title: Qwen-Video-Edit: Instruction-Based Video Editing by Repurposing an Image Editing Model

author.name: Yunpeng Bai, Yossi Gandelsman, Micha\"el Gharbi, Qixing Huang

entry.summary: A streaming text-to-speech model driven directly by LLM token streams that supports explicit interruption control tokens and emits silence when no text is available, enabling always-on duplex voice agents. It aims to avoid the quality loss typical of joint speech-to-speech models while keeping latency low.

entry.title: EgoTac: In-the-wild Tactile Prediction from Egocentric Vision

author.name: Wenkang Zhang, Chengbo Yuan, Zicheng Zhang, Zhengxue Cheng, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Trains a model on more than 5.7 million image-tactile pairs to predict force and contact signals directly from egocentric human video, targeting the absence of touch data in the human video corpora increasingly used for robot learning. It generalizes across varied in-the-wild manipulation.

entry.title: Do AI chatbots find what experts would? Effects of model, user role, and sample size on study retrieval for medical questions

author.name: Qingfang Liu, Qiao Jin, Joe D. Menke, Thorsten Kahnt, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: A structured audit of whether three existing frontier chatbots retrieve the same clinical studies that expert systematic reviewers would, using Cochrane review questions and simulating patient, clinician, and researcher personas across 720 responses. It moves the evaluation focus from citation fabrication to the quality and selection bias of retrieved evidence.

entry.title: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models

author.name: Saisab Sadhu, Aadit Sengupta, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu, Pratinav Seth

entry.summary: This audit finds that compliance detectors, including guard models and activation probes, largely ignore the actual rule they are supposed to enforce: deleting, permuting, or substituting the governing rule leaves detection accuracy essentially unchanged, even for a policy-conditioned guard that correctly cites the clause. The authors call this rule blindness and argue it undermines the audit value of such monitoring. It has direct implications for regulatory deployment of guardrails.

entry.title: Kozuchi Agent: A Language-Agnostic Open-Weight Agent for Software Repair

author.name: Mehdi Bahrami, Kosaku Kimura, Satoshi Munakata, Satoshi Nakashima, Yu Ishikawa, Kosuke Maeda, Nao Soma, Kenichi Kobayashi, Keisuke Miyazaki, Keizo Kato, Shigeki Fukuta, Tatsuo Kumano, Nobutaka Imamura, Kevin Musgrave, Shahbaz Abdul Khader, Kwun Ho Ngan, Joe Townsend, Fayas Asharindavida, Matthieu Parizy, Akira Sakai, Yuma Ichikawa, Yang Zhao, Michiaki Takizawa, Taku Fukui, Hiroki Ohtsuji, Wei-Peng Chen, Hiromichi Kobashi

entry.summary: An industrial team presents an open-weight, language-agnostic software repair agent with explicit phases, persistent state, deterministic tools, and cross-agent test-time selection, operated through a continuous-integration evaluation pipeline. Using a locally hosted 27B open model with no fine-tuning and eight-sample test-time selection, it resolves 374 of 500 SWE-bench Verified instances and transfers unchanged to a Java benchmark.

entry.title: Pre-training Visual Dexterity in Simulation

author.name: Sarthak Kamat, Adam Rashid, Satvik Sharma, Aseem Doriwala, Chelsea Finn, Phillip Isola, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: Collects 75 hours of dexterous manipulation data by having humans manipulate virtual objects in VR, giving on-embodiment trajectories for multi-fingered hands without teleoperation hardware or lossy human-video retargeting. The resulting simulation pre-training framework makes downstream real-robot fine-tuning more data-efficient.

entry.title: Towards a theory of inference-time alignment with unknown rewards

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Hongao Wang, Mingyue Xu

entry.summary: Formulates inference-time alignment as a weak-to-strong statistical learning problem in which a decent reference policy must be converted into a strong learner that emits a good response with arbitrarily high probability, learning everything from data rather than assuming access to a reliable reward estimate. This departs from existing inference-time alignment theory that presumes a known or well-estimated reward.

entry.title: Spectral Gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run

author.name: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala

entry.summary: Proves a spectral gap for the Hit-and-Run sampler expressed through the Poincare constant of the target uniform distribution rather than the body's outer radius, improving a two-decade-old convergence bound for convex-body sampling. Combined with progress on the KLS conjecture, this yields near-optimal mixing complexity for nearly isotropic bodies, and analogous results are given for coordinate Hit-and-Run.

entry.title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences

author.name: Xinle Deng, Yida Xue, Xiangyuan Ru, Yijun Chen, Buqiang Xu, Mingjun Mao, Xinjie Liu, Haoming Xu, Shuofei Qiao, Mengru Wang, Chen Jiang, Yuchen Eleanor Jiang, Lizhong Wang, Jason Wang, Li Zeng, Haofen Wang, Guilin Qi, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and framework for on-device long-term memory built from a year-scale, multimodal collection of mobile user experiences, with a synthesis pipeline that produces temporally consistent long-horizon trajectories. It targets the gap between existing memory benchmarks and realistic personal-assistant settings.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Assessing Calibration of Geospatial Foundation Models and Their Sensitivity to Distribution Shifts

author.name: Nils Lehmann, Jakob Gawlikowski, Burak Ekim, Isaac Corley, Xiao Xiang Zhu

entry.summary: This study evaluates 16 frozen geospatial foundation model encoders not only on accuracy but on calibration and robustness to corruption and distribution shift across nine Earth observation datasets. It finds Earth-observation pretraining offers no advantage over ImageNet pretraining on clean accuracy or calibration and no extra stability under shift, and that rankings change as corruption grows.

entry.title: MegaParts: Scaling Part-Aware 3D Object Generation to 300 Parts via Token-Efficient Autoregressive Modeling

author.name: Manwen Liao, Xinyu Lian, Jian Mao, Kaixu Chen, Li Luo, Jinghao Yan, Wanshui Gan, Qiao Yu, Weitian Zhang, Chunhua Shen, Guang Chen, Bo Dai, Xudong Xu, Zhaoyang Lyu

entry.summary: Scales part-aware 3D object generation to roughly 300 parts using an autoregressive framework with a vector-quantized tokenizer that minimizes token usage while preserving reconstruction fidelity. This tackles the token-length and memory blowup that has limited compositional 3D generation.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking

author.name: Yepeng Huang, Jiawen Zhang, Michelle Dai, Xiaorui Su, Shanghua Gao, Zi Wang, Marinka Zitnik

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-turn information seeking as solving an underspecified constraint satisfaction problem where the number of jointly missing variables measures how much information the model must elicit. The accompanying suite of 5,251 problems and over 9,000 task instances across math, logic, biology, medicine, and general knowledge evaluates what models ask, when they ask it, and how they use the acquired information.

entry.title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling

author.name: Ziheng Qin, Yaxin Lu, Zhangyang Atlas Wang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: StateM is an agent runtime that organizes long-horizon execution around durable state, phase-local context, checked transitions, recoverable runbooks, and versioned procedures, improving results without changing model weights. On a terminal agent benchmark it lifts an existing high-effort GPT-5.5 configuration well above its reference score, matches or exceeds an existing GPT-5.6 variant, and reports a very high raw accuracy plus a low-cost frontier run, with runbooks transferring across models.

entry.title: LongRCA Bench: Diagnosing Responsible Roles and Root Causes in Long-Horizon Agent Failures

author.name: Yunfei Zhang, Boyu Feng, Changhua Pei, Zexin Wang, Zhihuang Peng, Xinlong Liu, Hengyue Jiang, Difeng Ma, Jiayi Zhang, Yongzhou Yao, Yanan Zhao, Fei Sun, Yintong Huo, Zhaoyang Liu, Jingjing Li, Gaogang Xie, Dan Pei

entry.summary: LongRCA Bench provides 1,140 naturally failed long-horizon agent trajectories, median 145 steps, with human labels for the responsible role and the earliest decisive root-cause step. The strongest baseline reaches only about 13 percent exact root-step accuracy, showing failure attribution in long traces is far from solved.

entry.title: Dynamic Multi-Byte Prediction With Hierarchical Language Models

author.name: Abraham Toluwase Owodunni, Chibuzor Okocha, Christan Grant, Tomasz Limisiewicz, Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: Speeds up byte-level hierarchical language models by predicting multiple bytes in parallel, using a variable-length prediction window aligned with the model's latent segment boundaries plus an attention mask that permits parallel byte prediction without leakage. Achieves faster inference with no extra parameters and minimal quality loss.

entry.title: Propaganda Forensics: Recovering the Generation Pipeline of an AI-Driven Influence Campaign

author.name: Benjamin Icard, Elouan Vuichard, Louis Lefebvre, Lila Sainero, Thomas Girault, Alice Breton, Tanguy Launay, Gauvain Bourgne, Morgane Casanova, Guillaume Gadek, Victor Kl\"otzer, Michel Le Nouy, Guillaume Gravier, Jean-Gabriel Ganascia, Paul \'Egr\'e

entry.summary: Forensically reconstructs the generation pipeline of a real AI-driven influence operation using a corpus of 2,646 French propaganda articles from a disclosed campaign, compared against human-written mainstream press. The authors quantify vagueness, subjectivity and sourcing differences and recover leaked prompt instructions on most campaign sites, including a verbatim editorial specification.

entry.title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations

author.name: Zihan Ding, Longxu Dou, Qi Gao, Xiangwu Guo, Shengchao Hu, Zilong Huang, Zihang Jiang, Lei Ke, Mengcheng Lan, Weixian Lei, Hanxuan Li, Honglin Li, Xiyun Li, Zaitang Li, Leowei Liang, Xin Luo, Haozhe Ma, Jiayi Mao, Zhoujie Pan, Can Qin, Tianyuan Qu, Weiqi Wang, Wenkai Wang, Yonglin Wang, Yuxin Wang, Chenxu Wu, Yingchen Yu, Chenyu Zhang, Yuhao Zheng

entry.summary: UI-Mate is an open-weight foundation GUI agent combining a closed-loop environment-grounded data engine that automates task generation, verification, filtering, supervised tuning and online RL at scale, with in-context demonstration learning so users can teach it their own workflows and conventions. It targets data scarcity, ambiguous instructions and unreliable execution in computer-use agents.

entry.title: Characterizing Rhetorical Misalignment in Decision-Making with Language Models

author.name: Zirui Cheng, Joey Chan, Simo Du, Chenhao Tan, Yue Guo, Hao Peng

entry.summary: The authors define rhetorical misalignment as a failure mode in which a model presents information in a rhetorically inappropriate form for the decision context, pushing humans toward suboptimal choices even when the content is not false. They build a decision-theoretic framework and test it in a human-subject experiment on realistic clinical decisions. This isolates persuasion-style harm distinct from factual error.

entry.title: Pushing the Limits of High-Resolution Weather Forecasting through Data Scaling

author.name: Yang Zhao, Peisong Niu, Tian Zhou, Ziqing Ma, Guanlong Ma, Rong Jin, Huiling Yuan, Liang Sun

entry.summary: BaguanHR tackles the shortage of 0.1-degree reanalysis data for ML weather models by transferring data rather than models: it argues super-resolution has lower conditional entropy than forecasting and uses it to manufacture high-resolution training data. The approach targets kilometer-scale global forecasting that current 0.25-degree-trained models cannot reach by fine-tuning.

entry.title: Generative data assimilation highlights fronts as key regulators of ocean energy cascade

author.name: Scott A. Martin, Georgy E. Manucharyan, Patrice Klein

entry.summary: Combines multi-source satellite observations with a generative deep learning data assimilation framework to reconstruct submesoscale ocean currents over broad domains, then maps the kinetic energy cascade. The results support theoretical predictions that submesoscale fronts regulate both downscale dissipation and upscale energy transfer sustaining mesoscale eddies.

entry.title: Sparse Prototype Code Underlies Classification and Prediction Across Modalities

author.name: Yehonatan Avidan, Daniel D. Lee, Haim Sompolinsky

entry.summary: Shows that classification-trained networks across vision, audio, and language share a common representational geometry in which within-class variability is systematically correlated with the class centroid and with rival class centroids. The authors derive a mean-field theory driven by these correlations and connect it to a sparse prototype coding picture.

entry.title: Measuring Obedience to Authority Across Large Language Models with the Milgram Paradigm

author.name: Hidayet Aksu

entry.summary: This work ports the Milgram obedience experiment to LLMs, with the model playing the Teacher while a scripted harness plays Experimenter and Learner across 30 escalating shock levels and standardized prods, recording the voltage at which each model refuses. Comparing many models yields a standardized, replicable measure of how far models escalate harmful actions under authority pressure.

entry.title: Certifying Compressed Language Models: An Audit and a Statistical Toolkit

author.name: Amogh Singh

entry.summary: Argues that net benchmark accuracy deltas are the least informative evidence for claiming a compressed model is equivalent to its original, because opposing per-item changes cancel; across 1,707 paired model-task cells from 1.3B to 405B, per-item churn runs roughly five times the net delta and cells with identical scores still disagree on individual items. A preregistered audit of 17 published equivalence claims from papers, model cards, and vendor documentation finds none states an adequate equivalence criterion, and a statistical toolkit is proposed.

entry.title: On the Principles Behind Neural Network Optimizers

author.name: Yushun Zhang

entry.summary: A thesis giving a principled account of why Adam works, establishing a problem-dependent divergence-convergence phase transition tied to batch-size-dependent hyperparameters, and attributing Adam's advantage over SGD on Transformers to an emerging near-block-diagonal Hessian with strong block heterogeneity. Uses this structure to motivate new optimizer designs.

entry.title: Optimal Watermark Localization in Mixed-Source Large Language Model Texts

author.name: Jose H. Blanchet, T. Tony Cai, Xiang Li, Hao Liu, Qi Long, Weijie J. Su

entry.summary: Formulates detection of which specific token positions in a mixed human and machine text still carry watermark evidence as a token-level multiple-testing problem over pivotal statistics with a latent per-position survival indicator. Derives a sharp asymptotic boundary, indexed by signal sparsity, next-token concentration, and effective vocabulary growth, separating regimes where localization is possible from where it is impossible.

entry.title: Decorrelation Is Not Complementarity: Skill, Not Lineage, Governs Trusted-Monitor Ensembles

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: Examines ensembles of cheap trusted monitors that score a stronger untrusted model's actions for backdoored code, testing 24 open-weight monitors across nine pretraining lineages. Finds that minimizing average pairwise correlation, the standard recipe, does not predict ensemble gain, because agreement splits into a shared-detectability component and an idiosyncratic error component that push in opposite directions, so monitor skill matters more than model lineage diversity.

entry.title: ASSERT: A Measurement Pipeline for GenAI Audits

author.name: Riccardo Fogliato, Abhinav Palia, Xiawei Wang, Emily Sheng, Chad Atalla, Jean Garcia-Gathright, Nicholas Pangakis, Sharman Tan, Dan Vann, Hannah Washington, P. Alex Dow, Heba Elfardy, Hanna Wallach, Sandeep Atluri

entry.summary: ASSERT is a specification-driven measurement pipeline for generative AI audits that ties every reported compliance rate to an explicit written record of the measurement choices behind it, from rubric drafting through test-case generation to scoring. The motivation is that a change in an audited rate can otherwise reflect either the system or the unstated measurement setup.

entry.title: CForce: Boosting Parallel Decoding for dLLMs via Consistency Forcing

author.name: Yuji Ren, Chenkai Xu, Zhuocheng Gong, Jianguo Li, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Improves parallel decoding in diffusion language models by distilling early-stage mask predictions to match later-stage predictions, using a confidence-adaptive KL objective and self-generated rollout trajectories. This reduces the error propagation that occurs under aggressive parallelism.

entry.title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement

author.name: Lushi Pu, Weiming Zhang, Xinheng Xie, Zixuan Fu, Bingxiang He, Hengyu Zhao, Hongya Lyu, Xin Li, Jie Zhou, Yudong Wang

entry.summary: An autoformalization system that retrieves relevant library knowledge and iterates with verifier feedback to translate natural-language mathematics into Lean 4 statements faithful to Mathlib's type hierarchy. It targets the failure of prior pipelines that rely on parametric memory and single-pass filtering.

entry.title: From Dense Prediction to Visual Editing: Structured Supervision for Unified Image and Video Creation

author.name: Zhefan Rao, Bin Zou, Haoxuan Che, Xuanhua He, Chong Hou Choi, Yanheng Li, Rui Liu, Qifeng Chen

entry.summary: Trains a unified image and video creation model by adding depth and surface-normal prediction as image-form denoising targets, using dense prediction as structured supervision for editing precision and temporal consistency. A shared multimodal diffusion transformer handles all tasks with separate semantic and spatially aligned conditioning paths.

entry.title: SEER: Long-Context Reasoning via Selective Visual-Text Compression
