entry.summary: DeepOHeat-v2 extends physics-trained operator surrogates for 3D-IC thermal simulation to high-contrast multi-die stacks, replacing the ill-defined continuous physics loss at material interfaces with a discretized loss and addressing severe ill-conditioning that defeats first-order optimizers. Enables fast, label-free thermal optimization in chip design.

entry.title: A Privacy Study of Sparse Collaborative Inference

author.name: Maximilian Andreas Hoefler, Karsten Mueller, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: Tests the common claim that sparsifying transmitted activations improves privacy in split edge-server inference by separately reconstructing inputs from the retained values and from the sparsity pattern (positions) alone. Finds that the position mask itself leaks substantial input information, undermining sparsity-as-privacy arguments.

entry.title: SCALE: State-Calibrated Latent Embeddings for JEPA Planning in the Right Geometry

author.name: Jiaming Hu, Yan Zheng, Tian Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes why joint-embedding world models plan differently depending on whether the latent space is inherited from a pretrained encoder (DINO-WM) or learned end-to-end with anti-collapse regularization, showing that Euclidean planning costs are dominated by high-variance principal directions. SCALE calibrates latent embeddings so that planning happens in a geometry aligned with task-relevant state.

entry.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification

author.name: Aman Singh Thakur, Rayan Khoury

entry.summary: Studies data-free white-box lineage verification, asking whether weights alone reveal shared ancestry between two compatible checkpoints, and shows that the identity-aligned component induced by residual training must be removed before comparison. The resulting centered residual signature score separates fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned, and quantized descendants from independent and distilled models with perfect AUROC on residual-MLP and GPT-2 benchmarks.

entry.title: RecurrentGPT: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation in Transformers

author.name: Amr Hegazy, Amr Alanwar, Mostafa Elhoushi

entry.summary: RecurrentGPT is a recurrent-depth transformer where fixed prelude and coda blocks bracket a single shared core iterated multiple times, with a lightweight gated update inspired by gated recurrent networks conditioned on the hidden state, the prelude output, and resampled noise. The aim is to recover the representational diversity that naive layer sharing destroys while keeping the memory savings of weight tying.

entry.title: The Distributional View of Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Gordei Verbii, Juho Lee

entry.summary: Reframes token-level knowledge distillation as matching distributions rather than comparing them pointwise, representing the teacher by a family of multi-temperature views along its logit annealing path and training the student against a geometry-aware aggregate under an embedding-based ground cost. Explores mixtures, log-linear pooling, entropic Wasserstein barycenters, and a debiased Sinkhorn flagship, with a collapse theorem characterizing when the design degenerates.

entry.title: The Null Token Knows: Reducing Message-Free Hallucination in ASR and NMT

author.name: Kirill Borodin, Vasiliy Kudryavtsev, Ivan Viakhirev

entry.summary: Studies whether the reserved end-of-generation or null token in speech recognizers and translation models already encodes an abstention signal that could suppress fluent output when the input contains no message. Finds a usable signal exists in models such as Whisper but that standard decoding ignores it, and that aggressive null-token boosting deletes legitimate speech.

entry.title: Architecture-Dependent Causal Transfer of Activation States Across Large Language Models

author.name: Fernando Cardenas Piepereit

entry.summary: Tests whether internal activation states can be transferred between architecturally different LLMs through a learned projection, evaluating representational similarity, cross-model retrieval, and end-to-end causal effects from activation injection during generation. Uses four small open-weight models and finds alignment above a random-initialization baseline, with transfer success depending strongly on architecture.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Niche Multilingual Code Translation via Reinforcement Learning with Execution-Based Verifiable Supervision

author.name: Kouki Yuki, Jie Zeng, Kyoko Ogawa, Ryunosuke Ikeda, Yohei Kobashi, Takeshi Kojima, Ikuya Yamada, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Bootstraps many-to-many code translation for less common programming languages by expanding verifiable Python seeds into an execution-validated multilingual pool, labeling model-generated translations by execution outcome, and training a reward model for preference-based reinforcement learning. Addresses the scarcity of parallel supervision that otherwise yields plausible but non-executable translations.

entry.title: How Much Do Legal RAG Systems Still Hallucinate?

author.name: Souvick Das, Sallam Abualhaija, Domenico Bianculli

entry.summary: Conducts a fine-grained audit of hallucination in eight legal retrieval-augmented generation systems across GDPR text in English and a French national civil code, scoring at both claim and answer level. Hallucination rates range from under ten percent for the best systems to much higher elsewhere, with validation on 142 expert-authored questions.

entry.title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model

author.name: Ziyang Luo, Zhongyao Chu, Xinjie He, Youting Wang, Xukui Qin, Runxiong Wu, Yan-Syuan Chen

entry.summary: Combines two activation-space interventions on a frozen LLM: a steering probe that improves reasoning by writing to the residual stream, and a direction that reads the stream to decide when to abstain. The paper shows the two interfere when run together and proposes a way to answer and abstain in a single forward pass.

entry.title: Xemo-Talker: Unlock Emotions Explicitly for Audio-Driven Talking Portrait Synthesis

author.name: Chaolong Yang, Yinuo Guo, Kai Yao, Yuyao Yan, Jie Sun, Guangliang Cheng, Shibin Wu, Bin Dong, Kaizhu Huang

entry.summary: An audio-driven talking-head system that gains finer emotion control by concentrating explicit emotion supervision on lower-variance components of the motion space, leaving principal components to handle articulation and pose. This resolves part of the usual tradeoff between lip sync accuracy and expressive control.

entry.title: Do Visual Grounding Decoders Need Feed-Forward Networks? A Controlled Study over Frozen Vision-Language Features

author.name: Tarun Tomar

entry.summary: A controlled ablation asking whether feed-forward layers are needed in visual grounding decoders built on frozen vision-language features, comparing attention-only, attention-plus-FFN, and deeper attention-only variants. Attention-only decoders match or nearly match while cutting trainable parameters by 44 percent and latency by 10 percent.

entry.title: Scalable Black-Box Model Attribution for Images

author.name: Asaf Livne, Amir Jevnisek, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: RPA shows that attributing an image to the generative model that produced it can be done in the strict black-box setting with a small CNN on raw patches, reaching around 98 percent on a 25-class benchmark and 93 percent on a 27-class one. It is data-efficient, robust to compression, blur and resizing, and its cost does not grow with the number of candidate models.

entry.title: Beyond Uncertainty: Generalizable Failure Monitoring for Surgical Segmentation under Acquisition Degradation

author.name: Hieu D. Pham, Dang P. M. Cao, Thanh Trung Huynh

entry.summary: TCSR-Monitor is a post-hoc failure monitor for surgical segmentation that supplements confidence with shape, temporal consistency, and image-quality cues, so it can catch confidently wrong masks under image degradation. It wraps a frozen model, needs no internals or ground truth at deployment, and is validated with a leave-one-corruption-out protocol.

entry.title: SingDance: Compositional Zero-Shot Singing-and-Dancing Video Generation with Role-Aware Audio Conditioning

author.name: Tao Feng, Xu Li, Xiangyang Luo, Ming Wen, Huadai Liu, Chen Zhang, Wei Xue

entry.summary: SingDance is a video diffusion framework for generating singing-and-dancing videos where the visible subject must both move to the music and articulate the vocals, treating the subject as either the vocal source or a listener. Role-aware conditioning and hard-compact routing select task-relevant pathways for this combined setting.

entry.title: Detachable Wire Drive : Reconfigurable Robot Architecture with Shared Actuators

author.name: Takahiro Hattori, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: The Detachable Wire Drive lets a reconfigurable robot share heavy, expensive actuators across morphologies by physically splitting and reconnecting wire drive paths through a Wire Detach Unit. The authors demonstrate a rigid 2-DOF arm, a continuum arm, and additional configurations from a common actuator base.

entry.title: Co-design of Neural and Muscle Network based on Embodied Perceptron Representation

author.name: Siyuan Tao, Yoichi Masuda, Hiroyuki Nabae, Masato Ishikawa

entry.summary: Introduces the Embodied Perceptron, a framework that treats a robot's physical body as a computational layer analogous to a neural network layer, enabling joint theoretical optimization of morphology and controller. It aims to replace expert intuition in body design with a systematic co-design method.

entry.title: Position: Evaluations of AI Moral Reasoning Still Miss Half of the Picture

author.name: Aidan Kierans, Ritam Dutt, Kaley Rittichier, Shiri Dori-Hacohen, Avijit Ghosh

entry.summary: Argues that evaluations of LLM moral competence overwhelmingly test whether outputs match human values while neglecting whether models can identify and apply context-sensitive moral norms. The authors trace this imbalance to reliance on descriptive ethics frameworks and call for benchmarks grounded in normative ethics.

entry.title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP

author.name: Wael Albayaydh, Rui Zhao

entry.summary: Encodes classical negotiation mechanisms such as alternating-offers bargaining and Vickrey-Clarke-Groves auctions as constraints over agent-to-agent message schemas, adds a runtime verification and repair layer, and benchmarks whether LLM agents negotiate rationally. The point is that current agent protocols standardize transport and discovery but guarantee nothing about strategic correctness.

entry.title: From Errors to Proofs: Minimal-Core-Guided Repair for Neuro-Symbolic Constraint Solving

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: Improves LLM translation of natural-language constraint problems into formal specifications by returning a minimal unsatisfiable core when the generated program is unsatisfiable, instead of a raw solver error message. The core pinpoints the exact conflicting constraints, giving a leakage-free repair signal that also covers programs that run but encode the wrong problem.

entry.title: Gathered, Not Admitted: How Attention Brings a Latent Variable into Verbalizable Form

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri

entry.summary: Investigates what causes a latent quantity inside a language model to become reportable, testing the intuitive idea that a gate admits representations into a global workspace. Using Jacobian-based lenses on open-weight models with five task arms sharing identical context, the authors find no gate where the workspace account predicts one, but do find that task demand for flexible reuse raises a concept visibility.

entry.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion

author.name: Yu He, Weikai Yang

entry.summary: SkillCommit builds a hierarchical, growing skill library for LLM agents by first storing each experience as an instance-specific patch and only abstracting skills once several share validated behavior. This avoids merging superficially similar but behaviorally incompatible strategies, a known failure of similarity-based experience consolidation.

entry.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints

author.name: Ao Zhou, Bo Dai, Le Yu, Xingyu Liu, Zeyu Hao, Lingkun Long, Chunming Hu, Jianlei Yang

entry.summary: EcoVLA splits vision-language-action model inference between robot hardware and an edge server to jointly meet real-time control deadlines and energy budgets, adapting to fluctuating network and system conditions. It targets the gap between on-device compute limits and unpredictable offloading latency.

entry.title: Large Models for Small Devices: Recent Advances and Empirical Analysis of Edge AI Deployment

author.name: Subhransu Das, Jiaming Cheng, Arnav Kumar, Sadia Afrose, Mingzhe Han, Michael Silagy, Shreya Palande, Brijesh Soni, Rajiv Ramnath

entry.summary: Surveys recent edge-deployment results for compressed models and then empirically deploys compact language and vision models on GPU, CPU and Raspberry Pi for question answering and segmentation. Finds no single compression technique dominates, with quantization and structured pruning trading places depending on the task.

entry.title: HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation

author.name: XinQi Wang, Jinwei Xiao, Sijia Cui, Hongming Zhang, Yanna Wang, Qingyang Zhang, Bo Xu

entry.summary: HyMem organizes a long-horizon agent's context into distinct functional layers so that high-level plans are isolated from verbose execution traces and intermediate tool outputs, rather than compressing one flat context. The goal is to prevent planning information from being drowned out as interactions accumulate.

entry.title: RLCascadeRouter: Quality-Estimator-Free Cascade Routing via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shihong Huang, Shengjie Wang, Hong Ma, Zhou Xu

entry.summary: Learns cascade routing policies with reinforcement learning directly on routing decisions, avoiding the usual predict-then-optimize pipeline where a quality estimator's prediction error does not align with routing loss. The router decides after each observed response whether to stop or escalate to another model.

entry.title: Augmenting Text to Increase Translation Difficulty

author.name: William Kalikman, \v{S}imon Sukup, Michal Te\v{s}nar, Vil\'em Zouhar

entry.summary: Proposes adversarially rewriting translation benchmark sentences to be harder, using gradients from a differentiable difficulty estimator combined with a fluency objective and beam search over candidate token substitutions. Offers a prompting-free alternative to LLM-based or human benchmark construction as machine translation saturates existing test sets.

entry.title: Navigation-Informed Embeddings: Dense-Retriever Adaptation from Agent Search Traces

author.name: Shrey Shah, Levent Ozgur

entry.summary: Turns the byproduct traces of agentic retrieval, namely queries, retrieved documents and stopping points, into training signal for adapting a deployed dense retriever without new relevance labels or LLM judgments. The stopping document becomes a soft positive and path documents provide ordinal hard comparisons, improving recall on an independent target benchmark.

entry.title: Defake-o3: From Speculative Rationales to Verifiable Evidence for Explainable AIGI Detection

author.name: Bowen Deng, Jiahui Zhan, Yikun Ji, Haozhen Yan, Jianfu Zhang

entry.summary: Defake-o3 detects AI-generated images while producing visually verifiable evidence, combining interactive zoom-in visual search with an evidence verifier that penalizes speculative or hallucinated artifact claims. The aim is to move multimodal detectors from plausible-sounding rationales toward auditable localized evidence.

entry.title: Contrastive Energy Fields for Inference-Time Procedure Planning in Instructional Videos

author.name: Mohamed Afham, Christoph Reich, Oliver Hahn, Daniel Cremers, Stefan Roth

entry.summary: CEFITO learns an action-conditioned representation space and casts procedure planning in instructional videos as a task-constrained optimization at inference time using contrastive energy fields, instead of directly regressing action sequences with feed-forward or diffusion models. This lets the planner reject actions that are implausible for the task rather than treating all actions as viable.

entry.title: Graph Machine Learning: An Opportunity for Power Systems

author.name: Martin Sadric, Sebastian P\"utz, Christian Nauck, Veit Hagenmeyer, Frank Hellmann, Dirk Witthaut, Benjamin Sch\"afer

entry.summary: This survey reviews nearly 800 papers at the intersection of graph machine learning and power systems, spanning forecasting, state estimation, optimization, and control, and argues that grid topology makes graph inductive biases a natural fit where physics-based solvers are too slow for real-time operation. It maps opportunities and open challenges for grid applications.

entry.title: Matched Outcomes, Divergent Gaze: How Foveated MLLMs Search Compared to Humans

author.name: Mohamed Amine Kerkouri, Marouane Tliba, Aladine Chetouani, Ulas Bagci, Alessandro Bruno

entry.summary: The authors drive three general-purpose multimodal LLMs fixation by fixation through human-matched foveated views on a goal-directed search benchmark and compare outcomes with human eye-movement scanpaths. Models match or exceed humans on target-presence decisions and acquisition efficiency, yet their gaze trajectories diverge from human scanpaths, dissociating outcome from process.

entry.title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization

author.name: Tony Alex, Wish Suharitdamrong, Sara Atito, Armin Mustafa, Muhammad Awais, Philip J. B. Jackson, Jiankang Deng, Ismail Elezi

entry.summary: AudioChaps is a post-training framework that aligns large audio language models with editorial judgment for segmenting long audio into thematically coherent chapters, a task where boundaries reflect subjective creator decisions rather than acoustic events. It targets a commercially relevant media workflow gap that standardized audio benchmarks do not expose.

entry.title: Learning to Unlearn: Machine Unlearning via Learning the Unlearning Behaviors

author.name: Hang Zhang, Kaifeng Zhang, Yixiao Ma, Weijie Xu, Ye Zhu, Kai Ming Ting

entry.summary: Instead of designing an increasingly intricate unlearning function, this paper learns to imitate unlearning behavior, treating the mapping toward a retrained model as something a model can learn, so that removal does not require expensive bespoke procedures on massive training sets. The goal is to approximate retrained-model behavior at lower computational cost.

entry.title: GoalEvolve: From Handcrafted Algorithm Priors to Goal-Driven Evolution of Physical Design Algorithms

author.name: Haixu Liu, Lei Zhou, Yuhao Ren, Yumao Wu, Zhiang Wang

entry.summary: GoalEvolve makes LLM-driven evolution of chip physical design algorithms accountable to end-of-flow quality of results rather than stage-local objectives, converting unmet multi-objective targets into normalized gaps, identifying the dominant bottleneck, and using stage-resolved checkpoint evidence to direct the next iteration. This addresses cases where stage-local gains vanish or hurt downstream stages.

entry.title: LUNG-KGMM: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Learning for Lung Cancer Incidence Prediction

author.name: Chunlei Yang, Shuyan Li, Zhong Cao

entry.summary: LUNG-KGMM predicts one-to-six-year incident lung cancer by combining longitudinal electronic health records, radiology reports, chest radiograph features, and guideline-derived knowledge graphs, with a leakage-sanitized report pipeline and a horizon-masked cumulative training objective for censored follow-up. The design targets both modality heterogeneity and label leakage risks.

entry.title: Spectral Rank Certification for Foundation Model Adapters

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: Develops a finite-sample statistical framework for inferring the effective rank of public foundation-model LoRA adapters, distinguishing nominal rank as a design choice from calibrated spectral evidence. It derives an exact chi-square divergence for a rank-one Gaussian reference experiment, a computable Le Cam bound at realistic layer sizes, remainder bounds for truncation, and connects to the rectangular BBP transition.

entry.title: FAST-DeepONet: Factor-Augmented Branch Representations for High-Dimensional PDE Inputs in the Small-Sample Regime

author.name: Jiyong Kwon, Bongseok Kim, Guang Lin

entry.summary: FAST-DeepONet stabilizes deep operator networks when PDE inputs are sampled at thousands of highly correlated sensors but few operator samples exist, combining a fixed spectral branch path with a regularized projection of the orthogonal residual under row-normalized directional penalties. On Navier-Stokes flow it holds error near 0.04 as branch dimension grows from 129 to 8193, where a plain DeepONet degrades from 0.0394 to 0.1556.

entry.title: Second-Moment Memory in Coordinatewise Adam

author.name: Jeonseong Kim

entry.summary: Shows theoretically that the long memory in Adam's second-moment denominator can itself slow progress, deriving an order-M2 to the minus one half bound on expected positive normalized updates and converting it into an average-stationarity lower bound on a smooth convex problem. Suggests long second-moment memory hurts even with well-behaved gradient noise.

entry.title: When Tool-Backed Skill Retrieval Fails: Source-Style Collapse in Executable Capability Retrieval

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Joseph James, Yang Wang, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: Documents source-style collapse, where a tool-retrieval model fine-tuned on one slice of the ToolRet benchmark fails badly on another slice of the same benchmark even with higher lexical overlap with the gold tools. Shows simple query-side TF-IDF fingerprints predict where the fine-tuned retriever will fail better than semantic or length proxies.

entry.title: DeltaLog: Deferred Materialization of Recurrent States for Linear Attention Decoding

author.name: Junqing Lin, Jingwei Sun, Guangzhong Sun

entry.summary: DeltaLog reduces the memory-traffic cost of decoding in linear-attention models by keeping the recurrent state as a dense base plus a bounded log of compact recent updates, so most decode steps append small factors instead of writing back the full state. The scheme is semantics-preserving and targets models with large states and many heads.

entry.title: Provenance, Not Behaviour: A Serialisation Artifact in Edge-IIoTset and a Leakage-Free Benchmark for Precision-Agriculture Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mostafa M. Galal

entry.summary: Shows that near-perfect published results on the widely used Edge-IIoTset intrusion detection benchmark largely reflect a serialization artifact rather than network behavior: the dataset's own recommended one-hot preprocessing exposes categorical columns whose placeholder spelling, the string zero in the normal branch versus zero point zero in the attack branch, separates classes with perfect accuracy. The authors then offer a leakage-free benchmark for precision-agriculture intrusion detection.

entry.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit

author.name: Fengming Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes six million Reddit comments from cross-partisan forums to show an ideologically asymmetric interruption of political discourse diversification starting around late 2022, affecting conservative users. Permutation testing over thousands of candidate dates finds no sharp break at the ChatGPT launch, suggesting gradual rather than discrete change.

entry.title: Spatial Attention Noise Masking for Causally Sufficient Interpretability

author.name: Benjamin Formby, Kuang-Ching Wang, D Hudson Smith

entry.summary: Proposes a vision interpretability method that actively masks the input image with learned spatial attention noise before classification, so that explanations are causally sufficient rather than merely correlational. It contrasts with post hoc saliency methods that cannot make strong causal claims.

entry.title: SA-GEM: Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning for Efficient Remote Sensing Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kexin Ma, Jing Xiao, Bowen Xing, Liang Liao, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: A plug-in token pruning framework for remote sensing vision-language models that adapts token granularity to task scale and modulates importance using geospatial evidence cues, targeting the quadratic growth of visual tokens with resolution. It addresses the dilution of sparse but critical evidence in very high-resolution imagery.

entry.title: Perspective-Invariant Attack with Enhanced Transferability of Adversarial Examples

author.name: Kaisheng Liang, Yiming Cao, Bin Xiao

entry.summary: Improves black-box transferability of adversarial examples by adding global perspective transformations, sampling image-corner vertices with multiple degrees of freedom to simulate viewpoint changes during attack generation. Prior input-transformation attacks used only local operations like shuffling and resizing.

entry.title: Boundary-Aligned Contribution Routing for Robust Optical--SAR Object Detection

author.name: Haifa Zhang, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: Learns task-conditioned routing that regulates how much each of optical and SAR modalities contributes before cross-modal fusion, using only detection supervision. The motivation is that misaligned or mismatched modalities can be conditionally harmful and cause negative cross-modal transfer.

entry.title: FMReward: Aligning and Evaluating Audio-Driven 3D Facial Animation with Human Preferences

author.name: Sijing Wu, Yunhao Li, Zhilin Gao, Huiyu Duan, Yucheng Zhu, Guangtao Zhai, Patrick Le Callet

entry.summary: Introduces FMPair, described as the first human preference dataset for audio-driven 3D facial animation, and trains a perceptual reward model that is used both to evaluate and to fine-tune animation systems. It moves the field away from ground-truth reconstruction error toward preference-aligned optimization.

entry.title: WorldRover: A Scalable Synthetic Video Data Engine for World Exploration with Rich Annotations

author.name: Xiaojie Xu, Zhengyuan Lin, Runyi Li, Yihao Liu, Kaipeng Zhang, Yongtao Ge

entry.summary: WorldRover is an Unreal Engine data engine producing long-range exploration videos of artist-built environments with paired camera trajectories, dense geometry, temporal correspondence and control signals on the same frames. It targets training and evaluating generative or reconstructive world models where real capture cannot supply all these annotations.

entry.title: StreamOPD: A Post-Training Recipe with Spatio-Temporal Cue Gating for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Keming Wu, Baoyi Wang, Kaichen Zhang, Xiang An, Zuhao Yang, Sudong Wang, Haowei Zhu, Tingxuan Huang, Hongcheng Gao, Bin Wang

entry.summary: StreamOPD is a post-training recipe for streaming video understanding that fixes a memory-free recent-window protocol and shows a training-free sliding window already matches systems with elaborate inference-time memory and retrieval. It combines verifiable streaming data with thinking-mode on-policy distillation, arguing that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards fits the low-latency streaming regime poorly.

entry.title: Interactive Whole Slide Images for RL-based Tumour Segmentation

author.name: Mohamad Mohamad, Francesco Ponzio, Maxime Gassier, Nicolas Pote, Xavier Descombes

entry.summary: This work formulates gigapixel whole-slide tumour segmentation as a reinforcement learning navigation problem, where a PPO-trained agent moves, zooms, and selects tumour regions in a multi-resolution slide environment. It combines local views with a global thumbnail in an actor-critic architecture instead of exhaustively scoring all patches.

entry.title: OccamView: Object-Conditioned View Selection for Frame-Budgeted Active 3D Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Gao, Wei Zhang, Zeyu Ni, Dihao Zhu, Ruifeng Li, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: OccamView selects next-best views for active 3D Gaussian reconstruction under tight frame budgets by conditioning on objects, maintaining an online object memory rather than treating object-occluded regions as generic unexplored space. This prevents budget-limited planners from covering the scene broadly while leaving objects half-reconstructed.

entry.title: Reliable Piezoresistive Strain Sensing Through Physical Limits and Uncertainty Monitoring

author.name: Carmen Ballester, V\'ictor Mu\~noz, Dorin Copaci, Dolores Blanco

entry.summary: This paper argues that probabilistic regressors for soft piezoresistive strain sensors can look confident while operating outside their calibrated range or while internally failing, so confidence alone is not trustworthiness. It pairs a physics-informed probabilistic inverse model with explicit admissibility limits and uncertainty monitoring for control loops.

entry.title: RAPAC-DP: Response-Aligned Pending-Action Compensation for Diffusion Policies under Delayed Execution

author.name: Tao Wang, Wei Wang, Jianhui Wang, Qi Wang, Weidi Huang, Bing Xu

entry.summary: RAPAC-DP compensates for network and compute delays when diffusion or flow-based imitation policies run on remote servers, by conditioning a lightweight adapter on the actions already queued for execution. Training uses delay-conditioned samples synthesized from delay-free demonstrations, and disabling the adapter exactly recovers the base policy.

entry.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems

author.name: Xabier Muruaga

entry.summary: Argues that agent security is fundamentally an authorization architecture problem and introduces an agentic principal chain that tracks delegated authority across principals and sub-agents, evaluating each request against accumulated context rather than in isolation. This bounds harm from prompt injection by limiting what authority an agent can exercise or pass on.

entry.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix

author.name: Jinhyun Jeon, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: Observes that multi-agent LLM workloads have two opposite KV-cache needs, a long shared prefix wanting contiguity and per-request suffixes wanting fine-grained allocation, and proposes asymmetric paging with separate hot and cold pools plus a per-step backend dispatcher. It is presented as the first asymmetric-granularity KV cache in a production paged serving engine.

entry.title: PL-Guard: Probabilistic Logic Reasoning for LLM Guardrails

author.name: Satchit Chatterji, Shihan Wang, Giovanni Sileno, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Separates the two jobs that safety classifiers usually conflate by having a local model ground policy-relevant predicates from a prompt-response pair, then reasoning over those facts with probabilistic logic rules. The neurosymbolic split is intended to reduce both unsafe compliance and over-refusal while making policies auditable and editable.

entry.title: Robo-Dopamine 2.0: History-Conditioned and OOD-Aware Process Reward Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yijie Xu, Haopeng Jin, Run Zhou, Shengbang Liu, Sixiang Chen, Hongyang Cheng, Sicheng Hu, Peterson Co, Jinwen Luo, Huajie Tan, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a process reward model for reinforcement-learning refinement of robot manipulation policies that conditions on execution history and explicitly handles out-of-distribution states, using pairwise comparisons rather than static before-and-after snapshots. This aims to distinguish harmless variations from genuine task failures during off-trajectory execution.

entry.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity

author.name: Armin Steinhauser

entry.summary: Introduces an attention-free zero-shot time series forecaster with roughly 147 thousand parameters that computes dominant periods with a zero-parameter spectral detector, folds the context on phase, and decodes quantiles autoregressively. It claims to define the size-versus-probabilistic-accuracy frontier on a public forecasting leaderboard among entries declaring no test leakage.

entry.title: Routing Divergence Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Influence in Same-Weight MoE Self-Distillation

author.name: Cedric Caruzzo, Donggeun Yoo, Tae Soo Kim

entry.summary: Investigates whether differing expert routing between two forward passes of the same mixture-of-experts weights meaningfully changes behavior during self-distillation, using an exact blockwise decomposition to separate routing effects from content effects. The conclusion is that routing divergence is a weak signal of behavioral influence, a negative result across seven open checkpoints.

entry.title: Scaling Manual-Grounded Appliance Manipulation with Data Synthesis and Unified Planning

author.name: Yuxing Long, Lei Kang, Ziyan Yu, Yuzheng Gao, Bin Cheng, Jiyao Zhang, Xiaoqi Li, Haolin Yang, Dongjiang Li, Hui Shen, Hao Dong

entry.summary: Builds a scalable pipeline that converts appliance manuals into a hierarchical appliance graph and synthesizes part grounding, long-horizon plans, and closed-loop recovery data, yielding a large dataset spanning 22 appliance categories with tens of thousands of tasks. A unified planner trained on it handles state-dependent household appliance operation.

entry.title: Measuring Fairness in Large Audio Language Models via Semantic-Aware Bias Estimation

author.name: Zhe Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a mixed-effects regression framework for auditing demographic bias in large audio language models that controls for spoken content via sentence-level semantic embeddings and treats speaker identity as a random effect. Argues that ignoring these confounders yields misleading conclusions about model fairness in spoken-input settings.

entry.title: Repair, Not Improvement: Decomposing Constrained Decoding in Tool-Call Abstention

author.name: Janghoon Lee (Redrob)

entry.summary: Isolates the effect of grammar-constrained decoding on a case prior work explicitly excluded, namely tool-call abstention where declining to call any function is the option an enum most easily removes. Using three conditions over a byte-identical prompt in English and Korean with small open models, it separates the grammar's role in controlling where generation stops from which tokens may be emitted.

entry.title: Batch-wise Adaptive Pruning: Periodic Neuron Activation-Aware Weight Pruning for Language Reasoning Model

author.name: Yongmin Kim, Shota Takashiro, Yusuke Iwasawa, Takeshi Kojima, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Shows that training-free adaptive pruning methods for reasoning models break down under batched inference because a shared mask forces activation aggregation whose distribution no longer matches the offline-calibrated threshold, causing sparsity drift and accuracy collapse. Proposes a batch-aware periodic activation-aware pruning scheme to restore accuracy at high throughput.

entry.title: Zero-MELO: Test-Time Evidence Calibration with Multimodal LLMs for Zero-Shot Micro-Gesture Recognition

author.name: Chengyan Wang, Hanliang Xie, Yueyi Yang, Haoyu Chen

entry.summary: Improves zero-shot recognition of subtle micro-gestures by having a multimodal LLM calibrate evidence at test time rather than relying on a single forward pass, addressing the poor motion sensitivity of standard prompting. It targets implicit affective analysis from brief, spatially localized movements.

entry.title: ProjFormer: Point Cloud Completion via Geometric-Projective Transformer and Cross-Modal Semantic Constraints

author.name: Sheng Liu, Meng Wang, Ruihui Li, Huilong Pi, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: A point cloud completion method that enforces geometry-consistent 2D-3D interaction through deterministic projection of 3D points onto multi-view features, plus adaptive routing between structural and observation-driven features. It replaces learned attention and fixed fusion in prior multi-view completion methods.

entry.title: GLaQ: Grounding Latent Queries in Visual Evidence for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Zesheng Yang, Lingling Zhang, Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Zhang, Pengyu Li, Heng Wang, Lin Wu

entry.summary: GLaQ improves multimodal chain-of-thought by grounding continuous latent reasoning queries in visual evidence, avoiding both external image-manipulation tools and the redundancy of autoregressive latent states that depend only on their predecessors. It aims to preserve fine-grained visual information across text reasoning steps without inference-time tool calls.

entry.title: How Sampling Strategy Affects Imbalance Mitigation in LiDAR Segmentation: A Study of Structured vs. Random Point-Based Architectures

author.name: Antonis Savva, Christos Kyrkou, Theocharis Theocharides

entry.summary: A systematic benchmark of six reweighting schemes and five imbalance-aware losses across three LiDAR datasets and two point-cloud architectures, finding that inverse-frequency weighting can degrade performance by up to 12 percent versus uniform weighting. The effect of imbalance mitigation depends strongly on whether sampling is structured or random.

entry.title: Test-Time Instance Selection for Improved Whole Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Quoc Anh Nguyen, Sunhong Park, Jin Tae Kwak

entry.summary: Test-Time Instance Selection is a training-free, plug-and-play method that picks a compact representative subset of whole-slide patches during inference, combined with a multi-view ensemble. It avoids the extra training required by existing learned instance-selection modules.

entry.title: US-VLA: An Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Abdomina

author.name: Cheng Zhang, Xingzheng Wu, Guihao Yan, Xifeng Hu, Zhi Liu, Mei Wu, Qing Cai

entry.summary: US-VLA is a vision-language-action model for autonomous abdominal ultrasound that encodes clinical semantic goals and outputs sequential probe manipulation actions, avoiding hand-designed reward functions or large interaction datasets. The claim is better generalization across devices, patients, and clinical scenarios than reinforcement learning approaches.

entry.title: Closing the Affective Loop: Multimodal Speaker-Listener Emotion-Dynamics-Aware Empathetic Social Robots

author.name: Zi Haur Pang, Casey Kennington, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: AffectLoop is a spoken dialogue system on a social robot that tracks the speaker's verbal and facial affect while also modeling the robot listener's own evolving affective state, conditioning LLM response generation on both streams. It aims to move empathetic dialogue from one-way emotion mapping to a bidirectional affective exchange.

entry.title: The Hallucination Snowball: Modeling Error Propagation as State Transitions in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines

author.name: Prabhjot Singh, Bhushan Pawar

entry.summary: Models error propagation in sequential multi-agent LLM pipelines as a Markov chain over four states in which an injected false fact mutates from raw number to derived computation to narrative to invisible conclusion. Across hundreds of injected hallucinations in a four-agent financial pipeline, detectability collapses at each handoff, with escape probability rising to roughly ninety percent at the final boundary.

entry.title: Task- and Session-Level Model Routing: A Common-Interface Hybrid Evaluation of Four Open-Source Routers Across Four Benchmarks

author.name: Kiran N. Kumar, Santhosh K. Saminathan

entry.summary: Compares four open-source model routers under a single common protocol across RouterBench, BFCL v4, tau2-bench, and WebArena with a locked matrix of candidate outcomes. Three of the routers effectively emit near-constant tier assignments, and a trivial always-mid baseline matches one router almost exactly, undermining claimed routing gains.

entry.title: When Uncertainty Isn't Enough: An Empirical Study of Self-Correction in Code Generation

author.name: Pranav Rakasi, Maanas Lalwani, Arnav Srivastava, Arya Palanivel, Tinuade Adeleke, Ruizhe Li, Sean Wu

entry.summary: Tests whether uncertainty estimators developed for natural language transfer to code generation, comparing token entropy, verbalized confidence, probability of correctness, entropy ensembles, and semantic entropy probes on HumanEval and BigCodeBench. Multi-sample probability of correctness correlates best with actual correctness, while other signals including semantic entropy probes correlate weakly, and the signals are then used to trigger selective self-correction.

entry.title: Beyond Correctness: Toward Automated Novelty Verification with Lean 4

author.name: Ayrton Porto

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline that formalizes statements from a LaTeX paper into Lean 4 and then issues a novelty verdict using prior existence in formal and informal corpora, non-triviality checks via automatic tactics, and structural proof distance measured by overlap of premise sets. It is evaluated on arXiv papers withdrawn for duplication.

entry.title: Semantic Uncertainty-Guided Orchestration in Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: John Knowlton, Aritra Guha, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: HASSUM orchestrates hierarchical multi-agent LLM systems using semantic entropy and semantic density to estimate trust at the level of answer meaning rather than token probabilities. These uncertainty signals drive adaptive coordination so unreliable intermediate reasoning is not propagated.

entry.title: T-LLM Compiler: Trusted LLM-based Code Optimization and Verification Framework

author.name: Zahra Fazel, Sunanda Gamage, Shayan Shirahmad Gale Bagi, Amir H. Ashouri, Tomasz S. Czajkowski, Bryan Chan, Reza Azimi, Yaoqing Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a trusted compiler framework in which LLMs perform high-level code transformations while traditional compilers and verification tools check correctness before the transformations are accepted. Reported results indicate substantial improvements in the correctness of LLM-driven code optimization.

entry.title: Bias-Corrected Ceilings of Emotion Predictability from Human Label Variation Based on Instance-Level Fano Bounds

author.name: Keito Inoshita

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for estimating a bias-corrected upper bound on text emotion recognition accuracy given genuine human label variation, using an anchored Dirichlet-mixture empirical Bayes estimator with instance-level information-theoretic bounds. It separates irreducible from reducible error so claims that a benchmark is saturated can be made or refuted with discipline.

entry.title: Breaking and Defending LLM-Powered Social Media Bot Detection Systems

author.name: Nof Orenstein, Yoni Birman

entry.summary: Studies attacks against LLM-powered social media bot detectors, showing adversaries can target the reasoning and generation mechanisms of the detector itself rather than only mimicking human behavior, and proposes corresponding defenses. Frames the arms race between bots and LLM-based moderation.

entry.title: DriveCache: Action-Aware Caching for Driving World Model Inference

author.name: Jianchun Yang, Jian Liang, Xianda Guo, Pinhan Fu, Yanlun Peng, Conglang Zhang, Wenke Huang, Mang Ye

entry.summary: DriveCache is a training-free caching controller for diffusion-based driving world models that allocates feature reuse using driving signals available before generation, such as ego speed and planned trajectory. The authors show empirically that cache tolerance varies with ego translation and rotation, denoising progress, and reuse length, and exploit this to increase throughput. It is a domain-specific improvement over generic diffusion acceleration.

entry.title: Time to Reason: Scalable Neurosymbolic Learning for LTLf via Fuzzy Semantics

author.name: Riccardo Andreoni, Andrei Buliga, Alessandro Daniele, Paolo Felli, Chiara Ghidini, Marco Montali, Massimiliano Ronzani

entry.summary: The authors systematize differentiable fuzzy semantics for finite-trace linear temporal logic within a unified framework and pursue scalable neurosymbolic learning under temporal constraints. They fill theoretical gaps left by earlier temporal neurosymbolic work while targeting practical scalability. This supports learning models that must respect temporal specifications.

entry.title: Probabilistic Circuits as Reasoning Machines in Artificial Intelligence (Part I)

author.name: Robert Peharz

entry.summary: This cumulative habilitation thesis presents probabilistic circuits as a tractable framework for reasoning and learning under uncertainty, arguing for probability as a core AI language and explaining how structural constraints make otherwise NP-hard inference tractable. It consolidates a body of work on structure, learning, and inference for these models. It serves as a reference for tractable probabilistic modeling.

entry.title: PDDLCoder: Agentic PDDL Generation for LLM-Assisted Symbolic Planning

author.name: Veit Laule, Jiangtao Shuai, Manfred Hauswirth, Sonja Schimmler

entry.summary: PDDLCoder is an agentic framework that iteratively generates, analyzes, and refines full planning domain and problem specifications from natural language so that a symbolic planner can produce verifiable plans, and NL-pddlgym provides a benchmark with automated verification. It avoids the rigid pipelines, partial specifications, and human-in-the-loop feedback of prior hybrid methods. The pairing of framework and benchmark addresses an evaluation gap.

entry.title: BRA-Audit: Budgeted Runtime Auditing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Cumulative-Exposure Audit-Point Placement

author.name: Kaixiang Wang, Yidan Lin, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: BRA-Audit places auditor checkpoints inside LLM multi-agent systems by modeling execution as a dynamic dependency graph and choosing audit points under a token budget using cumulative exposure. The goal is to catch propagating hallucinated or malicious agent outputs without the cost of auditing every agent every round.

entry.title: Writing Style Similarity Reflects Academic Genealogy

author.name: Cameron Manzo

entry.summary: Builds a corpus of 5,803 arXiv authors linked through the Mathematics Genealogy Project and shows that advisors sit about 40 percent closer in style embedding space to their own students than to random same-field authors, with the effect replicated by two open encoders. This complicates authorship attribution and AI-text detection systems that assume each author's style is idiosyncratic.

entry.title: RamseyGadgets: A Graph Construction Dataset for LLMs

author.name: Zohair Raza Hassan, Deepak Pandita

entry.summary: RamseyGadgets is a dataset of graph construction tasks designed so that solutions cannot be recalled from training data, in contrast to famous Ramsey-type constructions already documented in the literature. It tests whether LLMs can genuinely reason toward graphs satisfying specified extremal properties.

entry.title: MetaReason: Precise Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning via Editing Meta Information for Solving Geometry Problems

author.name: Penghao Yin, Haomin Wang, Qihong Tang, Xiaoye Qu, Hongjie Zhang, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: MetaReason improves multimodal geometry problem solving by parsing diagrams into structured meta-information, editing that structure with predefined tools to render high-fidelity intermediate visual states, and then reasoning over the interleaved text and images. This avoids the low rendering fidelity and geometric inaccuracy that plague prior visual-state reasoning approaches.

entry.title: MotionGS-SLAM: Event-Modulated Gaussian Splatting for Motion-Blur Robust SLAM

author.name: Zhiqiang Hu, Shouren Huang, Masatoshi Ishikawa

entry.summary: MotionGS-SLAM handles motion blur in Gaussian splatting SLAM by modeling blur formation forward within the rendering pipeline instead of trying to deblur inputs, using event camera data to modulate each Gaussian's rasterization. The dual-modulation mechanism exploits microsecond event timing to constrain an otherwise ill-posed problem.

entry.title: WeSCE: A Benchmark for Measuring Security Drift in LLM-Driven Code Editing

author.name: Zhiyu Zhang, Tingyue Wen, Senke Sun, Dengxiang Liang, Enhao Huang

entry.summary: WeSCE measures security drift when LLMs edit code under prompts that specify only functional goals, using 400 executable programs covering feature addition, removal, bug fixing, and refactoring. It defines a continuous risk aggregation over heterogeneous vulnerability signals and tracks changes in average risk, worst-case severity, and vulnerability distribution.

entry.title: Optimal Lower Bounds for Networked Information Aggregation

author.name: Ambar Pal

entry.summary: Provides matching lower bounds for a recently formulated problem in which learners arranged on a directed acyclic graph must aggregate their parents' predictions plus local features, sharpening prior upper bounds on aggregation error. The result closes a theoretical gap in networked learning under information-flow constraints.

entry.title: FluxBin: Flexible LUT-based Ultra-low-bit LLM Inference by Algorithm-Kernel Synergy

author.name: Qingyao Yang, Runming Yang, He Xiao, Wendong Xu, Junyu Chen, Haobo Liu, Chenchen Ding, Ruihan Hu, Yik-Chung Wu, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: Co-designs a binary-basis post-training quantization scheme with an optimized lookup-table CUDA kernel so that ultra-low-bit LLM inference actually delivers speedups rather than being lost to dequantization overhead. A decoupled row-column binary decomposition raises representational capacity while staying hardware-friendly.

entry.title: LLMs Get Smarter from Targeted Synthetic Multilingual Data

author.name: Ishika Agarwal, Arkajyoti Charaborty, Tanner Sorensen, Neha Gupta, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: Takes a data-centric approach to the problem that language models answer the same question differently depending on the prompt language, using targeted synthetic multilingual data instead of English pivoting or fully language-balanced training. The claim is that this raises overall capability rather than merely equalizing it downward.

entry.title: QUMem: Personalized Memory for Query-Conditioned User-State Inference in LLM Agents

author.name: Heng Wang, Yifei Li, Lingling Zhang, Pengyu Li, Xinyu Che, Xinyu Zhang, Zesheng Yang

entry.summary: QUMem is a memory architecture for LLM agents that segments interaction histories by event coherence rather than fixed turns or tokens, stores functionally distinct user facts as separately retrievable units, and infers query-conditioned user state instead of relying on a single top-k retrieval. It targets personalization where preferences shift and conflict over time.

entry.title: MUSE: An Interactive Meta-Agent for Understanding and Steering LLM-powered Data Science Systems

author.name: Wei-Hao Chen, Weixi Tong, Yuan Tian, Chenglong Wang, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: MUSE is an interactive meta-agent that restructures raw execution traces of LLM-powered data science systems into navigable semantic levels, lets users ask grounded questions about specific workflow steps, and steer the agent's reasoning. It targets the difficulty of diagnosing and correcting agentic data-science failures.

entry.title: Static Pruning Across Sparse Retrieval Regimes: What Transfers, What Breaks, and What Still Helps

author.name: Zirui Song, Yuye Zhu, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The authors run the first cross-engine study of static pruning for sparse neural retrieval, testing pruning strategies across an exhaustive inverted index, block-max pruning, and clustered indexes on two benchmarks with encoders at opposite query-density extremes, totaling over a thousand configurations. They report which prior conclusions transfer, which break under dynamic pruning, and which still help.

entry.title: Coverage-Maximizing Multinomial Subset Routing under Operational Constraints

author.name: Quan Zhou, Yiyan Huang

entry.summary: Multinomial Subset Routing is an online learning framework where the learner maintains a multinomial policy over experts, samples several per round, and receives reward determined only by the best expert in the sampled subset, subject to long-term two-sided operational constraints. This max-style, non-additive reward structure matches routing across specialized models but is not captured by standard combinatorial bandits.

entry.title: MLLM-Guided Semantic Correction for Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Junhao Chen, Zheqi Lv, Keting Yin, Shengyu Zhang, Zhou Zhao, Feiyang Chen, Xinyu Duan, Baoxing Huai, Fei Wu

entry.summary: This training-free framework injects multimodal LLM feedback into the diffusion sampling loop to detect and repair semantic errors such as missing objects or mismatched actions during text-to-video generation, rather than only optimizing prompts beforehand or refining afterward. Semantic evidence is used to steer the diffusion trajectory mid-generation.

entry.title: When Context Misleads: Intent-Guided Decoding for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Haolin Jin, Pengyue Yang, Huaming Chen

entry.summary: Intent-Guided Decoding arbitrates between retrieved context and parametric memory based on user intent, using answer-level filtering plus token-level correction to steer decoding rather than applying a fixed trust policy toward retrieved evidence. This targets both over-trusting misleading context and under-using context when the user explicitly wants context-following.

entry.title: TDD-Agent: Test-Driven Reasoning for Code Generation

author.name: Hongyue Yu, Kefan Li, Jiakun Li, Hongzheng Chai, Yuan Yuan, Rui He, Junyi Wei

entry.summary: TDD-Agent operationalizes test-driven development for code generation: the model first writes executable tests to clarify expected behavior, then iteratively refines both code and tests using execution feedback, rather than treating generated tests as static post-hoc validators. This mitigates misleading feedback when generated tests are themselves wrong.

entry.title: TRACE-Bench: Decomposing and Diagnosing Multi-Reference Image Generation

author.name: Haoran Wang, Chaofan Ma, Ran Yi, Lizhuang Ma

entry.summary: TRACE-Bench replaces predefined task categories in multi-reference image generation evaluation with four atomic operators (anchor, disentangle, apply, compose), so any prompt becomes a compositional formula whose complexity is measured by operator slot count. This yields controlled difficulty scaling and diagnostic attribution of failures to specific capabilities.

entry.title: Steering the Flow: Inverting Face Recognition Models via Gradient-Guided Flow Matching

author.name: Ye Lu, Shen Wang, Zhaoyang Zhang, Yihan Yan, Li Liu, Runze Liu, Fanghui Sun

entry.summary: Proposes SFMI, a two-stage white-box model inversion attack that first pretrains an unconditional flow-matching prior over face manifolds and then steers sampling trajectories with progressive gradient guidance toward a target identity. The framing of inversion as trajectory steering aims to make reconstruction of training identities from face recognition models more stable than prior stochastic-guidance approaches.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Resolution Diffusion Models for Trajectory Generation in Urban Systems

author.name: Wen Ye, Muyan Weng, Chuizheng Meng, Hao Niu, Yizhou Zhang, Yan Liu

entry.summary: MR-Traj is a multi-resolution diffusion framework for synthetic human mobility trajectory generation that explicitly composes coarse and fine spatial-temporal structure instead of only matching global distribution similarity. The goal is privacy-preserving synthetic data that remains useful for traffic management, epidemic modeling, and urban planning.

entry.title: A Reproducibility Study of Partial Residual Ablations in Pre-LN Transformers

author.name: Pratikkumar Babariya

entry.summary: A reproducibility study ablating attention and feed-forward residual pathways separately in Pre-LN GPT-style transformers at 10M and 124M parameters, finding that removing the attention residual reliably collapses performance to the no-residual floor while removing the feed-forward residual shows a reproducible partial recovery. The result implies the two residual pathways play asymmetric roles.

entry.title: Generative Learning of Separatrices

author.name: Ellis R. Crabtree, Dimitris G. Giovanis, Anastasia Georgiou, George Datseris, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis

entry.summary: Uses generative modeling to identify and reconstruct separatrices, the boundaries between basins of attraction in multistable high-dimensional dynamical systems, which are chronically undersampled because trajectories rarely visit their neighborhoods. The approach avoids requiring closed-form knowledge of the governing equations.

entry.title: Degeneracy Counting Quantum Algorithm using Decoherence

author.name: Malay Marut Das, Mark A. Novotny, Yaroslav Koshka

entry.summary: Develops a quantum algorithm that counts the global optima of a classical optimization problem by measuring decoherence in a small probe coupled to the problem within a canonical thermal pure quantum state, avoiding enumeration of individual minima. It provides the first numerical demonstration of the perturbative decoherence-degeneracy relation on random-energy Hamiltonians.

entry.title: Structuring Semantic Embeddings for Principle Evaluation: A Prototype-Guided Contrastive Learning Approach

author.name: Che Shen, Junwei Su, Lingpeng Kong, Chuan Wu

entry.summary: Prototype-Guided Contrastive Learning adds a geometric regularization module on top of frozen text embeddings, combining a semantic stream, prototype-anchor attention, and supervised contrastive objectives, to separate examples that are semantically similar but task-distinct. It is evaluated on post-hoc principle-evaluation proxies such as toxicity detection, fine-grained emotion, and ordinal review rating.

entry.title: Beyond Field Accuracy: Two-Axis Diagnosis of Inverse-PINN Parameter Error

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Qian Tao

entry.summary: Provides a two-axis post-training diagnosis for inverse physics-informed neural networks, which can fit a field accurately yet return the wrong physical parameter, separating finite-sample resolution under a stated observation protocol from the signed parameter preference encoded in the final learned field and residual metric. Endpoint consistency checks whether joint training actually delivers that preference.

entry.title: SAGA: Structure-Attended Generative Action Embedding Model that encodes Multi-Surface User Action Sequences

author.name: Tsz Fung Pang, Po Jen Chen, Nimish Ronghe, Farhad Farahani, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: SAGA is a generative action embedding model that encodes multi-surface user interaction sequences across a financial services ecosystem, spanning checkout, peer-to-peer payments, in-app engagement, email, and account actions, into a unified user representation. A per-field tokenization schema decomposes each event into product, interaction, and surface tokens to enable field-level attention and per-field training objectives.

entry.title: Measuring Structured Predictability in Neural Training Dynamics: A Cross-Regime Study

author.name: Fanqi Wang, Weisheng Tang, Hairong Qi

entry.summary: Introduces probes that measure how much recent parameter updates predict near-future updates, calibrated against null baselines, and applies them to CIFAR vision training and public Pythia pretraining checkpoints. Finds that auxiliary vector parameters such as norms and biases carry systematically different short-horizon predictability than matrices.

entry.title: UniFed-VLM: Federated Instruction Tuning for Vision-Language Models with Multiple Heterogeneity

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Baochen Xiong, Xiaoshan Yang, Yifan Xu, Zhang Qimeng, Haifeng Chen, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: UniFed-VLM tackles federated instruction tuning of vision-language models when clients differ simultaneously in task, modality, and model architecture. It aims to allow privacy-preserving VLM adaptation in domains like healthcare where centralizing data is not permitted.

entry.title: Demystifying Oversmoothing in Sheaf Neural Networks: An Index-Theoretic Criterion

author.name: Junwen Dong, Yuhan Peng, Hao Li, Huitao Feng, Kelin Xia

entry.summary: Shows that the absolute dimension of a sheaf Laplacian kernel is a misleading indicator of anti-oversmoothing power, since some sheaf configurations inflate that dimension with uninformative constant harmonic sections. Introduces a relative, index-theoretic geometric criterion characterizing genuine anti-oversmoothing capacity.

entry.title: Evolving Executable Pipeline Programs for AutoML with Language Models

author.name: Sofoklis Kitharidis, Cor J. Veenman, Jan N. van Rijn, Thomas B\"ack, Niki van Stein

entry.summary: Presents an AutoML framework where an LLM acts as the variation operator in an evolutionary loop over complete executable scikit-learn-compatible pipeline programs, rather than searching a predefined operator space. Evaluated on standardized OpenML tasks under a leakage-controlled protocol that hides dataset identity from the generator.

entry.title: A Vision Transformer for ECG-Based Detection of Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction Across Multiple Clinical Sites

author.name: Burcu Ozek, Aruna Mohan, David Vorchheimer, Daniel Weiss, Eyal Kedar, Tamar Sobol, Or Zilbershot, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: Trains an ensemble of vision transformers from scratch on individual heartbeats from 12-lead ECGs to detect reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, using over ten thousand patients across seven sites and validating externally on four thousand patients from three geographically independent sites. Reports AUROC around 0.88 with balanced sensitivity and specificity at realistic 8.7 percent prevalence.

entry.title: AMPLIFAI: A Multiphase CT Dataset for Benchmarking Clinical Reasoning in LI-RADS Assessment of Liver Lesions

author.name: Pranav Kulkarni, Nikhil Shah, Amritansh Suryavanshi, Jana Delfino, James Tonascia, Jade Wong-You-Cheong, Barton Lane, Joseph Chirico, Jeffrey D. Hirsch, Ang Li, Heng Huang, Florence X. Doo

entry.summary: Releases AMPLIFAI, described as the first public multiphase abdominal CT dataset annotated with LI-RADS categories and segmentations for three key features, arterial phase hyperenhancement, washout, and enhancing capsule. Aimed at enabling AI systems that follow the standardized, biopsy-free radiological reasoning pathway for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis.

entry.title: Spinning Conformal Correlators from Neural Networks

author.name: Manas Dogra, James Halverson, Joydeep Naskar

entry.summary: Extends the neural-network field theory correspondence to spinning fields by combining random neural network ensembles with the conformal embedding formalism, computing two-, three-, and four-point correlation functions in examples. For a particular ensemble of independent identically distributed neurons the construction recovers four-dimensional Maxwell conformal field theory in the infinite-width limit.

entry.title: On Stopping Rules and Spatial Adaptation for CART

author.name: Zineng Xu, Yuchao Cai, Yan Shuo Tan

entry.summary: Provides theory for the statistical role of stopping rules in the CART regression tree algorithm, an aspect far less studied than the splitting rule, proving that CART with a minimum impurity decrease criterion and a suitable threshold attains pointwise adaptation under spatially heterogeneous and anisotropic smoothness. This shows the greedy, practically deployed algorithm can match adaptation properties previously established only for Bayesian trees or empirical risk minimization.

entry.title: How Many Samples Are Needed to Determine Causal Direction? Sharp Minimax Bounds for Bivariate LiNGAM

author.name: Jikai Jin

entry.summary: Quantifies the sample complexity of determining causal direction between two linearly related variables, going beyond classical LiNGAM identifiability to characterize difficulty when the structural coefficient is weak or the disturbances are nearly Gaussian. Proves a sharp local minimax rate whose denominator combines a coefficient-driven term with the product of coefficient strength and distance from Gaussianity.

entry.title: $S^3$: A Smooth Simulation Surrogate for Optimizing Discrete Abstractions of Dynamical Systems

author.name: Jordan Peper, James Mathias Gast, Vignesh Nanduri, Tanmayee Maram, Ethan Howes, Ivan Ruchkin

entry.summary: Introduces a differentiable objective that approximates bi-simulation-style relations so that finite abstractions of black-box or neural-network-controlled dynamical systems can be optimized directly for soundness with minimal conservatism. Aimed at verification of safety-critical autonomous systems.

entry.title: EMS Coreset: An Efficient Expectation-Maximization Algorithm for Sinkhorn Coreset

author.name: Haoyun Yin, Chuanhui Liu, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a Sinkhorn-based coreset method that allows non-uniform coreset weights so the entropically regularized transport coupling admits closed-form expectation-maximization updates, generalizing k-means with soft assignments. Provides asymptotic consistency and Lipschitz stability guarantees with competitive empirical approximation at lower cost.

entry.title: Improved Regret Analysis for Parallel Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization

author.name: Shion Takeno, Shogo Iwazaki

entry.summary: Shows that batched Gaussian process Thompson sampling can achieve regret bounds without the multiplicative batch-size penalty and without the impractical initial uncertainty-sampling phase required by prior analyses. Also derives substantially better bounds in the noiseless setting.

entry.title: Scaling Creative Writing Beyond Story-Centric Data with Attribute-Guided Genre Expansion

author.name: Hwan Chang, Yongil Kim, Heuiyeen Yeen, Yireun Kim, Jinsik Lee, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: Proposes separating thematic breadth from genre-form control when synthesizing creative writing training data, pairing human-authored story prompts as seeds with manually curated genre attributes that enforce structural and formatting conventions. The resulting multi-genre dataset aims to move models beyond story-centric creative writing.

entry.title: Information Satisfaction: A Reader-Centered Axis for Summarization Evaluation

author.name: Isabel Cachola, William Walden, Reno Kriz, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating summaries by how well they satisfy the information needs of a specific reader persona (role and expertise) rather than by generic quality metrics or a single query. The argument is that personas are more stable and informative than queries for judging summary utility.

entry.title: Geometry-Calibrated Closed-Form Shrinkage for SAR Despeckling

author.name: Xuran Hu, Mingzhe Zhu, Djordje Stankovi\'c, Yujie Zhu, Zhenpeng Feng, Yifang Ban, Ljubi\v{s}a Stankovi\'c

entry.summary: Revisits nonlocal sparse SAR despeckling and shows that three quantities usually treated as tunable hyperparameters are actually determined by the construction, yielding an exact closed-form soft-threshold solution instead of iterative inner optimization. This simplifies and speeds up the estimator.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Spatio-Temporal Context Modeling for 4D Occupancy Forecasting

author.name: Sitao Chen, Zhuangwei Zhuang, Hui Luo, Qingyao Wu, Mingkui Tan

entry.summary: GAST forecasts future 3D occupancy grids for driving scenes using progressive explicit-implicit generation with pose-driven warping plus dual-path spatio-temporal modeling, instead of discrete tokenization with autoregressive prediction. The goal is better geometric fidelity for static structures and temporal coherence over longer horizons, useful for corner-case simulation in autonomous driving.

entry.title: PixelControl: Fine-Grained Condition Fidelity in Text-to-Image Diffusion

author.name: Xin Lin, Haodong Li, Zhifei Zhang, Yutong Yang, Haitian Zheng, Juanxi Tian, Zhe Lin, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: PixelControl performs controllable text-to-image diffusion directly in pixel space on a pixel diffusion transformer backbone, avoiding the latent VAE bottleneck that weakens thin contours and small conditioned regions. Structure-aware control injection strengthens residuals around fine spatial structures for better condition fidelity.

entry.title: ChainSpace: A Chained-Reasoning Paradigm for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Xiaohan Zhang, Feng Gu, Xudong Rao, Xuhao Pan, Tao Wei, Zhou Pan, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: ChainSpace structures spatial reasoning as multi-round chains where later questions depend on constraints established earlier, so models must maintain persistent spatial state instead of answering independent questions with shortcuts. The authors instantiate a benchmark following this paradigm to measure state-preserving spatial understanding.

entry.title: Emergent 3D Instance Segmentation from Self-Supervised Point Transformers

author.name: Ted Lentsch, Santiago Montiel-Mar\'in, Holger Caesar, Julian F. P. Kooij

entry.summary: Probes a frozen self-supervised point transformer to test whether object instance information is already present without handcrafted geometric priors, across SemanticKITTI, nuScenes and Waymo. The analysis finds the instance signal concentrated in attention queries and keys rather than in values or output features, enabling unsupervised 3D instance segmentation.

entry.title: GaussianDWM++: Language-Grounded 3D Gaussian Driving World Model for Unified Scene Understanding, Editing, and Multi-Modal Generation

author.name: Tianchen Deng, Xuefeng Chen, Shuang Wu, Qu Chen, Jiajun Zhu, Bo Dai, Jianfei Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: GaussianDWM++ builds a driving world model on foundation-feature Gaussian tokens to unify 3D scene understanding, language-grounded reasoning, controllable 4D editing and multi-modal generation in one framework. The Gaussian representation is argued to align text with 3D structure better than point cloud, occupancy or BEV alternatives.

entry.title: GeoPose: Patient-agnostic CTA-to-DSA registration through projection-space calibration

author.name: Rudolf L. M. van Herten, Robert Graf, Paula Feldman, Johannes C. Paetzold

entry.summary: GeoPose performs 3D-to-2D registration of preoperative CT angiography to intraoperative biplanar angiography without patient-specific training, by predicting C-arm pose in a learned canonical frame and transferring it via projection-space calibration. A residual network plus optional short optimization refines the pose for unseen patients.

entry.title: From Continuous Design to Delay-Aware Discrete Synthesis: Guaranteed High-Bandwidth Joint Control for PMSM Drives

author.name: Edmundo Pozo Fortuni\'c, Mehmet C. Yildirim, Sami Haddadin

entry.summary: This paper introduces a delay-extended discrete-time model of a robot joint drive that explicitly accounts for communication and computation delays, enabling direct synthesis of a discrete PI current controller with guaranteed bandwidth. It replaces the usual heuristic choice of sampling frequency followed by iterative validation.

entry.title: Grouping Auction-Consensus Algorithm for Decentralized Task Allocation in Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Jose Rodriguez, Sven Koenig, Wenjie Dong, Qi Lu

entry.summary: Proposes GACA, a decentralized multi-robot task allocation method that keeps the two-phase auction-plus-consensus structure of the widely used CBBA baseline but bids over spatially clustered groups of tasks rather than individual tasks. This better matches the objective of minimizing total team travel distance in spatially spread environments.

entry.title: Semantic- and Density-Aware Planning for Accessibility-Preserving Multi-Object Placement

author.name: Benno Wingender, Nils Dengler, Nicolas Busch, Sicong Pan, Maren Bennewitz

entry.summary: SDPP plans where to place a stream of arriving objects on a partially filled shelf, jointly optimizing semantic grouping, dense space use, and continued manipulator accessibility for future placements, without knowing future arrivals. It formalizes an online organization problem relevant to household service robots.

entry.title: FlexWorm: Primitive-augmented Hybrid Contact-motion Planning for Suction-based Multi-segment Deformable Robots

author.name: Zili Tang, Tiecheng Guo, Qinyue Zhang, Meng Guo

entry.summary: FlexWorm plans full 3D motion for multi-segment suction-based soft robots that must jointly decide discrete adhesion switching and continuous body deformation under collision and quasi-static constraints. A block-wise inverse-kinematics hybrid search replaces hand-designed gaits and environment-specific scripts.

entry.title: Physiological World Models for Human State Transitions

author.name: Chongyang Zhang, Rendong Wang, Hao Zheng, Hanwen Zhang, Yang Liu, Xiaolong Wei, Bin Chong

entry.summary: Introduces a physiological world model that learns how a person's physiological state transitions in response to events, behaviors and interventions, using a structured, quality-scored state-transition token linking before-state, event, context and after-state. It shifts health AI from state recognition toward counterfactual and predictive modeling of the whole person.

entry.title: MoE Router-Guided Clustering for Heterogeneous Federated Instruction Tuning

author.name: Ankita Sharma, Bahar Farahani, Sanaz Rahimi Moosavi, Amir Rrahmani, Farshad Firouzi, Krishnendu Chakrabarty

entry.summary: Uses the routing behavior of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs as a similarity signal to cluster federated clients before aggregation, so that clients with compatible instruction distributions collaborate and negative transfer is reduced. Targets privacy-preserving instruction tuning under heterogeneous data.

entry.title: FedPA-LoRA: Product-Aligned Framework for Mitigating Aggregation and Initialization Errors in Heterogeneous Federated LoRA

author.name: Juseok Jeon, Ramy E. Ali, Doyun Kwon, Myungbeom Her, Jinhwi Kim, Jinhyun So

entry.summary: FedPA-LoRA resolves the tension in federated LoRA between accurate aggregation in product space and continuity of each client's local factors, by aligning local factors to the aggregated product each round. It provides convergence guarantees under both matched and heterogeneous client ranks.

entry.title: Schema-Agnostic Graph Reasoning Agent for Hybrid Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Marius Dragic, Ruben Ifrah, Alexandre Rio

entry.summary: GRA treats a hybrid knowledge graph like an unfamiliar filesystem, giving an LLM agent seven generic tools for listing neighbours, reading node content and searching descriptions, with all domain specifics discovered at run time. On an industrial benchmark of 258 analytical questions with SQL-derived gold answers it beats full-context baselines.

entry.title: Adding Voice Cloning to Text-to-Audio-Video Models with a Single Zero-Initialised Layer

author.name: Ivan Mikheev, Viacheslav Vasilev, Anna Dmitrienko, Alexey Letunovskiy, Ivan Kirillov, Kirill Chernyshev, Denis Dimitrov

entry.summary: Shows that a text-to-audio-video generator can be given voice cloning capability by adding one zero-initialized linear layer to its audio backbone plus a short fine-tune, conditioning on a brief reference recording through prepended latents and a global speaker embedding. It is benchmarked against five text-to-speech cloning systems on hundreds of speaker-text pairs.

entry.title: ALKEMIE Agent: an autonomous platform for computational materials design

author.name: Hongfu Huang, Yuzhe Li, Ao Xu, Bo Liu, Changrui Wang, Kan Tang, Ning Yang, Shengxian Liu, Hanyu Liu, Pengpeng Zhang, Linggang Zhu, Fengkai Liu, Yichen Lu, Tong Zhao, Naihua Miao, Jian Zhou, Zhimei Sun

entry.summary: Presents an agentic platform for computational materials design that couples retrieval-augmented generation with a materials knowledge base, registered simulation skills, provenance-tracked databases, and AI-assisted structure handling. The aim is to automate fragmented, manual multi-scale materials workflows end to end.

entry.title: Layers Matter: Why Continual Learning Regularization Should Be Layer-Adaptive

author.name: Brian B. Moser, Ahmed Anwar, Tobias Christian Nauen, Shishir Muralidhara, Federico Raue, Ren\'e Schuster, Stanislav Frolov, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: Proves under a block-diagonal curvature assumption that catastrophic forgetting decomposes into per-layer terms weighted by each layer's top Hessian eigenvalue, which diagonal Fisher-based regularizers fail to capture. The conclusion is that continual learning penalties should be layer-adaptive rather than purely per-parameter.

entry.title: LiD-GLM: Lipschitz-constrained Deep Generalized Linear Models

author.name: Tom Splittgerber, Niklas Koenen, Marvin N. Wright, Werner Brannath

entry.summary: Combines generalized linear models with invertible residual networks so the neural component adds flexibility while its Lipschitz constraint keeps the interpretable statistical part from being dominated. Positioned between rigid structural constraints and weak indirect constraints in semi-structured hybrid modeling.

entry.title: Non-Crossing Deep Quantile Regression for Distributional Survival Prediction

author.name: Shuai Huang, Zhe Qu, Zhaowei Hua, Guohao Shen, Rui Tang, Hongtu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a censored non-crossing quantile framework that jointly estimates multiple conditional survival quantiles with ordering guaranteed by construction, using Kolmogorov-Arnold and Transformer backbones. Establishes a finite-sample excess-risk bound for the estimator on right-censored data.

entry.title: Does a Language Server Save Tokens for Coding Agents? A Measurement Methodology and Preliminary Study

author.name: Pengcheng Xu

entry.summary: Asks whether Language Server Protocol based semantic retrieval actually saves tokens for coding agents compared with plain lexical search, noting the claim is widely asserted but rarely measured. Proposes tokens-to-success as the metric plus a five-arm ablation isolating semantic retrieval from confounds, with pre-registered failure modes and preliminary results.

entry.title: StreamHear: Domain-Adapted Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Streaming Speech Recognition

author.name: Zefang Liu, Chenyang Zhu, Sangwoo Cho, Xujun Peng, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Sambit Sahu

entry.summary: StreamHear adapts streaming speech recognition to shifted domains by fine-tuning an offline transducer teacher on limited labeled data, pseudo-labeling abundant unlabeled audio, and retraining the streaming student on the mixture. Adds a prior-regularized dynamic-programming realignment step to fix chunk-level word placement, improving over supervised fine-tuning across four domains.

entry.title: GALA: Generation-Aware Cross-Modal Alignment for Text-to-Time-Series Synthesis

author.name: Haochen Zhang, Gengwei Zhang, Laura Yao, Nicholas Konz, Tianlong Chen
