Added components include online probability updates, workspace limits, support-plane filtering, and a grasp-feasibility mode, with intent correctly bracketed in all 20 tested steps.

entry.title: Design Optimization for Large High-Force Soft Robot Manipulators Under Gravitational Loads

author.name: Isara Cholaseuk, Penelope Llibre, Alexa Kyriacou, Audrey Wang, Akua K. Dickson, Ran Jing, Juan C. Pacheco Garcia, Andrew P. Sabelhaus

entry.summary: Develops a geometry optimization method for large pneumatic soft robot limbs that maximizes blocking force under an anti-buckling constraint while supporting their own weight, with an explicit closed-form solution under stated assumptions. Three fabricated geometries validate the predictions.

entry.title: Position: Certified Correctness in Neural Constraint Reasoning Requires Symbolic Integration

author.name: Shufeng Kong, Xiaochuan Zhang, Caihua Liu

entry.summary: Argues that neural constraint solvers systematically violate hard constraints under distribution shift even when confident, and that symbolic verification should be integrated whenever checking is cheap relative to solving. Sudoku serves as the representative NP-complete testbed given its polynomial-time verification and exponential search.

entry.title: TAHB: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Text-Attributed Hypergraph Learning

author.name: David Yoon Suk Kang, JungHyun Kim, Juhyun Jeon, Sang-Wook Kim

entry.summary: Releases the first public benchmark pairing hypergraph structure with raw textual node and edge attributes, containing ten real-world datasets from e-commerce, academic, movie, and political networks. It enables systematic study of how pretrained and large language models combine with higher-order graph learning.

entry.title: GraphLoom: Reliability-Calibrated Graph Evidence Routing for Multimodal KG-RAG

author.name: Zafar Ali, Asad Khan, Aalia Malik, Pavlos Kefalas

entry.summary: GraphLoom builds an instance-level multimodal knowledge graph from grounded scene descriptions, extracted triples, and external commonsense, then performs reliability-calibrated subgraph retrieval with bounded expansion instead of dumping all retrieved evidence into the generator. The goal is compact, faithful evidence that supports multi-hop reasoning without unsupported generation.

entry.title: ReasonCast: Agentic Demand Forecasting with Selective Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Ziyue Yang, Chaolin Xu, Yijing Wang, Tiankai Gu, Hui Yang, Yanhong Lin, Kaiyuan Liu, Fei Xiao

entry.summary: ReasonCast has an agent inspect event context, a text-free baseline forecast and its uncertainty, then emit explicit structured interventions (such as level shifts around promotions or holidays) rather than fusing text embeddings uniformly with time series. The aim is selective, interpretable semantic adjustment of demand forecasts.

entry.title: Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: Framework, Metrics, and a Cardiovascular Pilot

author.name: Ummara Mumtaz, Aimen Noor, Awais Ahmed

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating healthcare LLMs against a provenance-preserving causal knowledge graph in which assertions are first-class nodes, extracting scenario-relevant subgraphs and varying how much grounding the model receives. A cardiovascular pilot tests reasoning about interventions, mechanisms, harms and uncertainty rather than single-answer accuracy.

entry.title: Invariant Pretraining for Robust Code Representations

author.name: Yifeng He, Yundi Xu, Christopher Castro Gaw Gonzalo, Zili Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Documents how encoder-based code models degrade when programs are rewritten into semantically equivalent but syntactically different forms, then shows a lightweight continued-pretraining recipe using semantics-preserving transformations that recovers much of the lost robustness. Evaluation spans four encoders, two tasks, and four datasets.

entry.title: EgoGazeLite: On-Device Egocentric Gaze Prediction for Token-Efficient Multimodal LLM Video Input

author.name: Matteo Stoiber, Niels Buus Lassen

entry.summary: Replaces dedicated eye-tracking hardware with an on-device gaze predictor so that egocentric video can be cropped around the likely fixation point before being sent to a multimodal LLM, cutting visual token counts roughly tenfold. The work analyzes the joint accuracy and latency constraints needed to preserve downstream description quality.

entry.title: Temporal Graph Prototype-conditioned Conformal Prediction for Fraud Detection

author.name: Xudong Chen, Shengbo Gong, Lu Cheng, Wei Jin

entry.summary: Adapts conformal prediction to edge-level fraud detection on temporal interaction graphs, where fraud is rare and embedded in benign neighborhoods, causing standard graph conformal methods to produce needlessly large prediction sets. The proposed prototype-conditioned calibration tightens sets while retaining coverage guarantees.

entry.title: RetroMPA: A Molecular Property-Aware Auxiliary Framework for Enhancing Retrosynthesis Prediction

author.name: Mianzhi Liu, Fan Xiao, Zhiliang Yu, Huayang Huang, Yuke Li, Yi Yang, Wenbo Liu, Yu Wu

entry.summary: RetroMPA is a model-agnostic post-hoc module that injects molecular property knowledge into existing retrosynthesis predictors, acting as a chemical filter that recalibrates candidate reactant predictions rather than generating SMILES itself. It plugs into a range of data-driven retrosynthesis models to improve top-k accuracy.

entry.title: Picking the Right Image to Classify: Reliable-Input Selection in Teledermatology

author.name: Fabian Gr\"oger, Marco Weishaupt, Philippe Gottfrois, Simone Lionetti, Linda Wermelinger, Nipun Ranasekara, Ludovic Amruthalingam, Alexander A. Navarini, Marc Pouly

entry.summary: The paper introduces reliable-input selection for teledermatology: when several photos of one lesion exist, choose the image the classifier is most likely to get right rather than trying to make the classifier robust to all of them. An oracle selector raises weighted F1 substantially, quantifying the headroom available from input triage.

entry.title: MELD: A Protocol for Merging Knowledge Across Distributed Agentic Memories

author.name: Lauri Lov\'en, Jaakko Sauvola, Jukka Riekki, Sasu Tarkoma

entry.summary: MELD is a protocol for merging knowledge across federated agent memories, admitting each incoming claim through a five-way decision (insert, merge, relate, conflict, or reject) based on claim-key identity, embedding similarity, and a natural-language-inference verdict under context and freshness gates. Contradictions are recorded rather than silently discarded, with auditable authenticated updates.

entry.title: Bounded Semantic Planning and Deterministic Compilation for Reliable Enterprise Text-to-SQL

author.name: Yi Ai

entry.summary: This work moves the stochastic boundary in enterprise text-to-SQL: a multi-turn planner grounds business phrases and chooses among governed options, while graph traversal, role predicates, grain lowering, SQL construction, and validity checks are deterministic code. On an adjudicated 38-question insurance benchmark with three runs each, the compiled semantic path outperformed direct schema-to-SQL generation.

entry.title: A Physiology-Informed Digital Twin Framework for Simulating Liver Health Progression

author.name: Sumaiya Afroz Mila, Sandip Ray

entry.summary: HEPATWIN is a physiology-informed digital twin of the human liver that simulates carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism, bilirubin conjugation, bile production, and detoxification to generate longitudinal biomarker trajectories under patient-specific diet and activity inputs. A stage-transition mechanism keeps simulated progression consistent with clinical disease patterns.

entry.title: L3Cube-IndicQuest v2: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Factual Knowledge of Large Language Models Across Indic Languages

author.name: Rinit Jain, Tirthraj Mahajan, Advait Joshi, Raviraj Joshi

entry.summary: Releases a multilingual question-answering benchmark of 3,471 curriculum-grounded English pairs across nine domains, drawn from Indian educational curricula, competitive exam material, and reference books, then translated into 19 Indic languages. Construction combines context-grounded LLM generation and validation with semantic deduplication and human verification to keep quality while scaling.

entry.title: Generalized Linear Bandits with Memory

author.name: Heesang Ann, Hyunjun Choi, Taehyun Hwang, Younghoon Shin, Haeju Cheong, Min-hwan Oh

entry.summary: Theoretical work on bandit problems where rewards depend on a finite window of past actions, showing that an earlier T^(3/4) regret bound was an artifact of loose analysis and that root-T regret is achievable. The authors extend the sharpened analysis to generalized linear reward models with a block-wise algorithm using shrunken confidence bounds.

entry.title: Structured Prediction for Scalable Spreadsheet Table Understanding: From Cell Types to Table Ranges (Extended Version)

author.name: Antoine Gauquier, Ioana Manolescu, Pierre Senellart

entry.summary: A two-stage pipeline for spreadsheet understanding that classifies cell roles using gradient-boosted trees over structured features plus a pairwise CRF for spatial consistency, then deterministically derives table bounding boxes. Emphasizes efficiency and scalability over large-model approaches.

entry.title: Predicting, Evaluating, and Explaining Top Misinformation Spreaders via Archetypal User Behavior

author.name: Enrico Verdolotti, Luca Luceri, Silvia Giordano

entry.summary: Builds predictive and explainable models to rank social media users by their contribution to misinformation spread, using three overlapping behavioral archetypes: amplifiers, super-spreaders, and coordinated accounts. Aims to support proactive platform interventions rather than post-hoc content removal.

entry.title: SAGE-OR: Semi-supervised Adaptive Scene Graph Generation for Operating Rooms

author.name: Brandon Leblanc, Charalambos Poullis

entry.summary: SAGE-OR generates surgical scene graphs from operating-room video without localization supervision by deriving object grounding implicitly from frozen foundation-model features and running a lightweight graph transformer over cached embeddings. A semi-supervised formulation with generic segmentation prompts removes the need for depth rigs and dense multi-modal labels.

entry.title: Decomposing Whole Slide Image Report Generation with Graph-Constrained Multiple Instance Learning Workflows

author.name: Antony Gitau, Martyna Borak, Bj{\o}rn-Jostein Singstad, Martin Paulson, Karl Thomas Hjelmervik, Ola Marius Lysaker, Veralia Gabriela Sanchez

entry.summary: Decomposes whole-slide pathology report generation into frozen tile embeddings, multiple-instance learning heads answering organ-specific diagnostic questions, an organ-conditioned graph that assembles answers into a reasoning chain, and a language model that renders the report. The decomposition makes visual recognition, structured reasoning and generation failures separately auditable, evaluated on over two thousand held-out slides.

entry.title: What You Ask is What You Ground: Bridging Question Intent to Temporal Evidence for Grounded VideoQA

author.name: Jinhwan Seo, Kyubeom Han, Jumin Lee, Junhyug Noh, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: Identifies question-invariant grounding as a failure mode in grounded video question answering, where models return nearly the same temporal window regardless of the question asked. GroundFormer fixes this by conditioning video features on question intent before localization through learnable communication tokens plus a factorized multiple-instance cross-attention that couples answering and grounding.

entry.title: BagShift: Measuring How Patch Selection Changes the Evidence Seen by Whole-Slide MIL

author.name: Ruicheng Yuan, Zhenxuan Zhang, Liwei Hu, Anbang Wang, Haijie Xu, Jiawei Luo, Guang Yang

entry.summary: BagShift is a paired protocol that isolates how the patch selector, rather than case mix, changes what evidence whole-slide multiple-instance learning models actually see, holding features and predictor fixed. With equal patch budgets, spatially dispersed versus locally concentrated sampling drops agreement metrics by roughly 1.6 versus 18 points on a prostate grading dataset, showing severe deployment sensitivity.

entry.title: Depth-guided Multi-view Exposure Bracketing for HDR Robot Vision

author.name: Jinnyeong Kim, Juhyung Choi, Woohyeok Kim, Sunghyun Cho, Seung-Hwan Baek

entry.summary: Releases a large HDR robot vision benchmark with 121 real scenes spanning modest to extreme dynamic range plus 20 synthetic CARLA sequences, and proposes distributing very different exposures across multiple low-bit-depth cameras and fusing them with depth guidance. This enables single-shot HDR perception evaluation for multi-sensor robotic systems.

entry.title: HiFi-BRep: High-Fidelity Latent Representation for Robust B-Rep Generation

author.name: Junhao Hou, Chenqi Luo, Pufan Wang, Jiaying Lu, Yusheng Liu, Feiwei Qin, Meie Fang, Kun Zhou

entry.summary: HiFi-BRep addresses two brittleness sources in generating CAD boundary representations: padding noise and feature contamination in the latent space, and sequential error propagation with train-inference mismatch from non-differentiable validity checks. It uses a topology-aware encoder with learnable queries to build a cleaner latent representation for robust generation.

entry.title: A Unified DINOv2-Based Framework for LVEF Estimation, GLS Dysfunction Classification, and Early Cardiotoxicity Prediction

author.name: Xiaotong Zhang, Mingyue Cui, Qing Cao, Jingming Xia

entry.summary: A frozen DINOv2 encoder with task-specific adapters and heads is used for three cardio-oncology echocardiography tasks: ejection fraction regression, strain-based dysfunction classification, and baseline prediction of future cardiotoxicity. The framing is that these tasks provide complementary early-warning signals.

entry.title: Benchmarking Identity-Sensitive LLM Outputs for Surveillance and Security Robots

author.name: Nneka Hyman, Jasmine Khan, Raj Korpan

entry.summary: Evaluates whether prompting LLMs with 236 different demographic identity labels changes the surveillance and security robot design specifications they generate, using readability metrics as an initial proxy. Reported significant differences suggest identity-conditioned variation in text that may seed real robot design documents.

entry.title: Robot-Body-Aware Traversal Risk Graph Planning for Wheeled-Legged Robots in Complex Terrain

author.name: Zhiqiao Guo, Bichi Zhang, S\"oren Schwertfeger

entry.summary: Extends traversal risk graph navigation for wheeled-legged robots by evaluating risk over the robot's oriented rectangular footprint along edges and yaw sweeps, rather than over circular node neighborhoods. This captures partial support loss and body-terrain interference that appear especially during turns.

entry.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Strict-Feedback Nonlinear Systems with Asymmetric Actuator Constraints

author.name: Saurabh Kumar, Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Abhinav Sinha

entry.summary: Proposes a safety-critical control architecture for strict-feedback nonlinear systems that embeds asymmetric actuator limits, rate limits, and time-varying output constraints directly into a differentiable dynamic input realization, instead of clipping commands after design. This renders the admissible actuator set forward invariant by construction.

entry.title: Adaptive Bridge: A Proxy-Based Decoupling Layer for Mitigating DDS Backpressure in ROS 2

author.name: Kaushalraj Puwar

entry.summary: Adaptive Bridge is a ROS 2 middleware proxy that prevents one slow subscriber on a reliable DDS topic from throttling all other subscribers, by republishing to separate reliable and best-effort writers and adaptively rate-limiting noncritical consumers based on health probes. This protects safety-critical local nodes from backpressure.

entry.title: FLOPs vs Real Work: The Importance of Replication in AI Efficiency Assessment

author.name: Enrique Barba Roque, Lu\'is Cruz

entry.summary: A replication study of the alpha-FLOPs estimator, which was proposed to correct the mismatch between reported floating point operations and actual execution time. The authors re-run the original experiments on newer hardware, surface methodological limitations in the original work, and question how well the correction generalizes.

entry.title: RETRACE: Resilience-Guided Trait-Conditioned Craving Estimation from Wearable Physiology in Opioid Use Disorder

author.name: Yi Xiao, Harshit Sharma, Dessa Bergen-Cico, Asif Salekin

entry.summary: RETRACE estimates opioid craving from wearable physiology under subject-independent evaluation, where craving signals are weak and largely entangled with stress responses. The method conditions on trait-level psychological resilience, which is not observable in short wearable windows but shapes stress regulation and craving vulnerability.

entry.title: UC-PSRO: Utility-Conditioned Policy-Space Response Oracles with a Communication-Dropout Curriculum for Game-Theoretic Course-of-Action Generation in Adversarial Swarms

author.name: Phillip Jiang

entry.summary: Trains UAV swarm courses of action using policy-space response oracles self-play, FiLM conditioning on a commander intent weight vector so a single policy is re-steerable at execution, and a curriculum of increasing communication dropout. Targets adversarial, communication-degraded multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Implementation of a Metacognition Framework for Self-Awareness and Self-Regulation in Ensembles of LLMs

author.name: Charles Courchaine, Ricky J. Sethi, Hefei Qiu

entry.summary: Implements a metacognitive controller for LLM ensembles that computes a five-dimensional state vector covering signals such as correctness evaluation, experiential match, conflicting information and problem importance, and uses it to regulate ensemble behavior. Targets known weaknesses in self-assessed uncertainty and knowledge-conflict detection.

entry.title: From Contexts to Values: Context-Dependent Defeat in Abstract Argumentation

author.name: Albert Sadowski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: Studies context-dependent argumentation frameworks, where a defeat function switches each attack on or off per context such as a procedural stage or applicable regulation, and asks whether such frameworks reduce to value-based ones with per-context value orderings. The result clarifies whether context is a genuinely new primitive in abstract argumentation.

entry.title: Adaptive Mixing of Policies from Searching and Policies from Learning

author.name: Gavin B. Rens

entry.summary: Flexer adaptively mixes a learned policy network with Monte Carlo tree search output, shortening search depth when the network's priors are reliable and the environment model's variance is low. It reports gains over an AlphaZero variant, DQN and approximate dynamic programming on small symbolic problems.

entry.title: Assessing LLMs' mathematical abilities requires understanding the various mechanisms of mathematical creativity

author.name: Silv\`ere Gangloff

entry.summary: A conceptual position paper arguing that mathematical creativity is not a single capacity but several mechanistically distinct modes, including reflexive introspection, analogical import, problem-driven construction, and bridging distant domains, plus a distinction between pattern-triggered and strategically motivated conjecture formation. The claim is that these modes are non-substitutable, so benchmarks measuring one say little about the others. It argues current evaluations of LLM mathematical invention are underspecified.

entry.title: When Single-Dataset Conclusions Fail: A 45-Task Study of Threshold Tuning and Resampling for Imbalanced Classification

author.name: Diyorbek Musaev

entry.summary: Using a leakage-free nested cross-validation protocol, the paper shows that conclusions about class-imbalance methods drawn from a single popular fraud dataset do not generalize: threshold tuning gives no benefit there but the identical protocol over 45 tasks spanning imbalance ratios up to roughly 1 to 178 tells a different story. The contribution is a methodological warning about single-dataset generalization in applied ML. It supports more careful empirical practice.

entry.title: Process-Constituted Intelligence: A Shared Criterion for Humans and Machines

author.name: Michael J. Richardson, Ayeh Alhasan, Cassandra Crone, M. Paula Diaz Monfort, Patrick Nalepka, Mark Dras, Rachel W. Kallen, David M. Kaplan

entry.summary: This position paper argues intelligence is constituted by process rather than output, and that generative models trained on traces of human cognition achieve only weak equivalence to the cognition they imitate. The authors define strong equivalence across seven process features assessable against human data. It offers a criterion for comparing human and machine intelligence beyond output benchmarks.

entry.title: AstronOS: A Unified Execution Model and Runtime for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems

author.name: Zhenhang Nie (iFLYTEK Co., Ltd., Hefei, China), Gui Zheng (iFLYTEK Co., Ltd., Hefei, China), Xudong Sun (iFLYTEK Co., Ltd., Hefei, China), Tailong Zhu (iFLYTEK Co., Ltd., Hefei, China), Bin Zhang (iFLYTEK Co., Ltd., Hefei, China)

entry.summary: AstronOS proposes an execution model in which a unit of work keeps persistent identity and versioned authoritative state across many model calls, with results advancing state only after validation and recording. The authors compare five strategies for carrying an established plan into a fresh model session, including rereading source material, replaying full history, and state handoff. It reframes agent infrastructure around work items rather than conversations.

entry.title: A Policy Algebra for Trust-Preserving Agentic AI Execution

author.name: Bhaskar Tripathi, Anurag Kumar, Ramendra Kumar, Bhavesh Gadhe

entry.summary: The paper defines reliable capability for agents as a path property rather than an outcome property: a task counts as successfully done only if every action event stayed admissible under identity, tool, data, memory, budget, approval, and audit constraints. It proposes a policy algebra describing this reliability envelope for enterprise agent execution. The framing separates capability from trustworthy execution.

entry.title: CACSurv: Concordance-Aligned Comparative Learning with Large Language Models for Cancer Survival Prediction

author.name: Tianqi Xiang, Qixiang Zhang, Xinpeng Ding, Yi Li, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: CACSurv reformulates LLM-based cancer survival prediction from independent per-patient time regression to concordance-aligned comparative learning, matching how survival models are actually evaluated by ranking and handling censored observations properly. It focuses on clinical reports as the primary input rather than images or genomics. The result is better alignment between objective and evaluation metric.

entry.title: Chronocooked: A Benchmark for Implicit Interval Timing in Reinforcement Learning Agents

author.name: Amrapali Pednekar, Alvaro Garrido-Perez, Yara Khaluf, Pieter Simoens

entry.summary: Chronocooked is a reinforcement learning benchmark of cooking-style tasks where timing information is unobserved but essential for optimal reward, designed to expose whether agents can learn implicit interval timing. Baselines cover non-recurrent, recurrent, and biologically plausible models. It argues time perception deserves explicit attention in RL agent design.

entry.title: Policy Iteration with Human Feedback: Bringing Post-Training RL to In-context Learning

author.name: Minh-Ha Nguyen, Cathy Shyr

entry.summary: Policy Iteration with Human Feedback keeps the base model fixed and instead maintains a versioned natural-language policy and tool set that is revised through an evaluate-and-improve loop, with a model critic proposing revisions and a clinical expert retaining authority over evidence interpretation. It ports the generalized policy iteration pattern to in-context learning. The application is clinical reasoning and tool-use trajectories.

entry.title: Orbital AI Computing: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Satellite Scale

author.name: Nisha Sarwar, Lei Jiang, Fan Chen

entry.summary: This work extends a lifecycle carbon model for orbital AI datacenters with accelerator-aware modeling, comparing a lightweight edge module suitable for small satellites against a high-performance rack system requiring heavy-lift launch. Because launch emissions scale with system mass, hardware choice dominates sustainability outcomes. It questions blanket claims about low-carbon space compute.

entry.title: WARA: Toward Automated Wireless Optimization Research with Closed-Loop LLM Agents

author.name: Yuan Guo, Yilong Chen, Chao Hu, Xianghao Yu, Liang Hong, Jie Xu

entry.summary: WARA is a closed-loop multi-agent system that, from only a topic, identifies research gaps, formulates wireless resource allocation problems, designs and runs algorithms, and assembles deliverables. The authors present it as the first end-to-end autoresearch framework for the wireless domain. It illustrates domain-specialized automated research pipelines.

entry.title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Decisions in Self-adaptive Systems

author.name: Jasmina Gajcin, Juan C. Rosero, Ivana Dusparic

entry.summary: EARL is a Python library that generates counterfactual, what-if explanations for reinforcement learning policies in self-adaptive systems, letting users compare alternative outcomes to understand agent behavior. It targets the transparency and verification difficulties of deep RL policies. Counterfactual explanations are chosen for their demonstrated intuitiveness to humans.

entry.title: BDIP-Net: Dual-Interaction Graph Learning for Property Prediction of Bilayer Materials

author.name: An Vuong, Chen Zhao, Jin Hu, Shui-Qing Yu, Xintao Wu

entry.summary: BDIP-Net predicts properties of stacked bilayer materials with a dual-interaction graph model that explicitly separates strong intra-layer bonding from weak inter-layer van der Waals coupling, paired with a machine-learning-driven workflow that produces near-first-principles-quality bilayer structures from monolayer inputs. This avoids expensive quantum-chemistry optimization in the discovery loop. It targets stacking-dependent materials design.

entry.title: P2E-VQ: ECG-linked representation augmentation for PPG via discrete patch retrieval

author.name: Zhongli Wu, Zhuangzhi Gao, He Zhao, Feixiang Zhou, Fu Wang, Jinru Ding, Yuankai Wang, Hongyi Qin, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Bil Kirmani, Yalin Zheng

entry.summary: P2E-VQ improves cardiac prediction from wearable PPG by retrieving discrete ECG-linked representation patches instead of trying to reconstruct ECG waveforms, which the authors argue is an ill-posed inverse problem. The retrieval-augmented design targets downstream diagnostic performance rather than waveform fidelity.

entry.title: pico-type: A 1.5M-Parameter Byte-Level Multi-Head Content Classifier

author.name: Gautam Kishore

entry.summary: pico-type is a 1.5M-parameter byte-level classifier that predicts seven content attributes at once from raw UTF-8, including modality, code language, MIME type, and secret-leak risk flags. It uses convolutions plus small bidirectional attention layers with rotary encodings and no tokenizer or pretrained embeddings.

entry.title: Path2ST: Hierarchical Cell-Tissue Grounded Cross-Modal Translation for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Wei Lou

entry.summary: Path2ST predicts spatial gene expression from H and E histology by treating it as hierarchical cross-modal translation, conditioning autoregressive generation on both cell-type and tissue-microenvironment structure. This targets the cost gap between routine pathology imaging and spatial transcriptomics assays.

entry.title: Unraveling the Size Determination Mechanism of Nanocrystal Synthesis via Interpretable Neural Networks

author.name: Kai Gu, Haizheng Zhong

entry.summary: NanoEQL is a fully white-box equation-learning network that replaces activation functions with chemistry-motivated operators, including smoothed variants to avoid gradient explosion at singularities, to recover interpretable size-determination laws in nanocrystal synthesis. It also introduces a temperature-aware scheme for weighting precursor contributions.

entry.title: Synthesizing Post-Acetazolamide Cerebral Blood Flow Maps from Baseline MRI in Moyamoya Using 3D Generative AI

author.name: Julia Huang, Camila Gonzalez, Rydham Goyal, Aja Zou, Sasha Alexander, Michael Moseley, Moss Y. Zhao, Gary K. Steinberg

entry.summary: CAE3D is a deterministic 3D conditional autoencoder that synthesizes post-acetazolamide cerebral blood flow maps from baseline ASL MRI in Moyamoya patients, for cases where the drug challenge cannot be performed. It is compared against ten baselines including diffusion-style 3D models and frozen foundation-model adapters.

entry.title: The Open-Strategy Dictator Game: Cooperation Under Mutual Transparency

author.name: Michael Glass

entry.summary: Proposes a dictator game variant where each player's strategy is a natural-language document visible to all and an LLM adjudicates the interaction, enabling conditional cooperation based on reading the counterparty's declared policy. Round-robin tournaments show conditionally cooperative strategies dominate under softmax equilibrium analysis.

entry.title: PaSTel: Anchoring Histology in Spatial Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Hierarchical Bio-Prior Contrastive Pretraining

author.name: Azim Dehghani Amirabad, Junchao Zhu, Pushpak Pati, Walid Abdelmoula, Tommaso Mansi, Rui Liao

entry.summary: PaSTel pretrains histology-transcriptomics alignment with biological priors at spot, functional, and tissue levels, using TF-IDF reweighting to avoid housekeeping genes dominating gene selection and modeling spatial dependencies rather than independent spot-patch pairs. The aim is more discriminative multimodal representations for spatial transcriptomics tasks.

entry.title: Looks Can be Deceiving: Annotator and Reviewer Performance Across Imagery Sources in Crowd-Sourced Aerial Damage Assessment

author.name: Thomas Manzini, Priyankari Perali, Raisa Karnik, Stephen Johnson, Robin R. Murphy

entry.summary: Empirically compares human annotator and reviewer performance across drone, crewed aviation, and satellite imagery in a post-disaster building damage dataset covering nine disasters and tens of thousands of buildings. It provides the first evidence base for allocating human labeling effort across imagery sources in multi-source aerial datasets.

entry.title: Fast Test-Time Refinement for Robust Learned Image Compression

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Chi-Man Pun, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: Studies test-time refinement as an adversarial defense for learned image compression codecs, seeking to cut its prohibitive iteration cost and extend evaluation to white-box attacks and objectives beyond L2-bounded rate and untargeted distortion. The work also tries to give theoretical grounding to why refinement confers robustness.

entry.title: VGGT-Align: Bridging Local Reconstruction and Global Consistency for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Wei Zhang, Yihang Wu, Songhua Li, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Addresses scale drift in chunked long-sequence 3D reconstruction built on feed-forward reconstruction backbones by exploiting geometric invariants that persist across temporal segments in structured driving scenes. The invariants expose per-chunk scale inconsistencies, which are then corrected during global alignment.

entry.title: Integrating Persuasion Theory into the Epidemiological Modelling of Health Misinformation Spread on Social Media

author.name: Mkululi Sikosana, Sean Maudsley-Barton, Oluwaseun Ajao

entry.summary: A speculative design paper arguing that blockchain-resident agents whose human principals die or lose keys become ownerless entities better understood through analogies to feralized animals and wildlife law. It proposes an inheritance protocol framing for governing agents that cannot be shut down.

entry.title: NICE: Scale-Stable Perturbations for Graph Neural Network Explanations via Noise Corruption

author.name: Ziluowen Luo, Jun Yin, Ruochen Liu, Ming Cheng, Shirui Pan, Chengqi Zhang, Senzhang Wang

entry.summary: Identifies that the standard element-wise masking used by post-hoc graph explainers deterministically shrinks message magnitudes, compounding across layers into a distribution shift the authors call scale drift, which corrupts the predictions used to infer importance. The proposed alternative uses noise corruption to build scale-stable perturbations.

entry.title: Towards Computational Provenance: Carrying Causal-State Evidence in Generated Text

author.name: Benjamin Belay

entry.summary: Explores computational provenance, asking whether generated text can carry detectable statistical evidence of which internal causal state produced it, tested in a modular feed-forward network and a small transformer trained on an arithmetic task with two discrete intermediate pathways. The verified internal state is made to determine a subtle statistical signature in the output.

entry.title: Early Cycle Charge Trajectory Generative Prediction and Full Life Cycle Health Management of Iron-Chromium Flow Batteries Based on FlowBD-E1

author.name: Suyang Zhuang, Zekun Jiang, Tianhang Zhou

entry.summary: FlowBD-E1 forecasts full charge voltage and current trajectories in an industrial 33 kW iron-chromium redox flow battery from early cycles, aiming to detect degradation before substantial capacity loss and to support full lifecycle health management. It argues that compressing aging into scalar capacity or state-of-health labels discards diagnostic signal.

entry.title: Paired Exact-Reset Evaluation of a Prediction-Derived Medium-to-Full World-Model Cascade

author.name: Malo de Pastor

entry.summary: Proposes a paired exact-reset audit protocol for deciding when a cheap medium-capacity world model should escalate to a frozen full predictor, executing all candidate actions from identical reset states so the paired physical-loss difference defines the routing target. It is evaluated on a PushT bank of 1,600 states and 39 tasks.

entry.title: Real-Time State-of-Health Estimation and Online Degradation Prognosis from Partial Battery Discharge Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Bego\~na Ispizua, Serio Gil-L\'opez, Leire Arrizabalaga, Ibai La\~na

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed deep learning method for lithium-ion state-of-health estimation from incomplete discharge curves taken from arbitrary voltage windows, reporting mean absolute percentage error below four percent, together with a real-time degradation trend estimator. The setting reflects heterogeneous field operating conditions rather than controlled full cycles.

entry.title: PERO: Efficient Robust Post-Training Foundation Models for Encrypted Traffic Classification

author.name: Wumei Du, Jiarong Wen, Kaiyu Zhang, Zi Yang, Yiqin Lv, Longfei Zhang, Dong Liang, Zheng Xie

entry.summary: PERO post-trains encrypted-traffic foundation models with a computationally tractable approximation of risk-sensitive objectives so that rare, high-loss misclassifications of malicious traffic are penalized. It targets the gap between average-case accuracy metrics and tail robustness needed in security deployments.

entry.title: Learning Auditable Classifier Models: Source-Disjoint Tree Ensembles

author.name: Srikumar Krishnamoorthy

entry.summary: RPTE builds tree ensembles under a bounded feature budget with source-disjoint patterns and separate coefficient estimation so that each prediction can be audited compactly. It is aimed at clinical and regulated tabular settings where boosting is accurate but hard to explain per prediction.

entry.title: Geometry of Forgetting: Representation Flux in Continual Learning

author.name: Maksim A. Kazanskii

entry.summary: Introduces representation flux, a geometric measure of per-sample latent displacement across sequential training, and shows it correlates with catastrophic forgetting and can rise before observable performance drops. Frames forgetting as a representation-space dynamics problem rather than only a parameter-regularization one.

entry.title: Operator-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Multitask Deep Learning

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari, Thomas Borsani, Giuseppe Di Fatta

entry.summary: Derives Rademacher-complexity generalization bounds for deep multi-output networks by treating layers as Koopman composition operators on vector-valued RKHSs, separating task-coupling from layerwise operator norms. Also analyzes a one-dimensional Brownian/Cameron-Martin regime with exact derivative-norm characterizations.

entry.title: Retrieval-guided Twin Fusion with Similarity-aware Contrast for Molecule-Text Alignment

author.name: Shunshun Gu, Shengqi Qiu, Hang Zhou, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: RISEN aligns molecules and text by constructing latent twin molecules for substructures and using similarity-aware contrastive objectives to capture fine-grained substructure-to-text correspondences. Targets molecule search and property prediction in a joint embedding space.

entry.title: Efficient Coreset Selection via K-Nearest Neighbor Graphs

author.name: Yingfan Liu, Leiyu Zhang, Jiadong Xie, Mingzhe Wang, Jeffrey Xu Yu, Jiangtao Cui

entry.summary: KNNG-CS selects training coresets using a k-nearest-neighbor graph to estimate per-item importance and greedily choose representatives, avoiding the quadratic distance matrices required by CRAIG-style gradient-approximation methods. Requires only linear storage in dataset size.

entry.title: Task-Anchored Representation Shaping for Pre-Trained Model-Based Continual Learning

author.name: Zhiming Xu, Huiyu Yi, Zhen-Hao Xie, Baile Xu, Furao Shen, Jian Zhao, Suorong Yang

entry.summary: TAILS is a lightweight module for pre-trained-model-based continual learning that maintains fixed task anchors as persistent references and reshapes latent representations so that inputs from unknown tasks can be resolved at inference. It targets cross-task prediction, the main bottleneck once per-task adaptation is easy with strong pretrained features.

entry.title: BRAID: Learning Equilibrium Maps in Interdependent Security Games via Weight-Tied Iterative Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Elnaz Nowrouzi, Zhiqun Zuo, Xueru Zhang, Mohammad Mahdi Khalili

entry.summary: BRAID amortizes Nash equilibrium computation for interdependent security games on networks by training a weight-tied iterative graph neural network that maps game parameters directly to equilibrium effort profiles in one forward pass, reported as up to 43 times faster per instance than best-response iteration. The architecture is derived from the fixed-point structure of the games, with sum aggregation reflecting the underlying externality form.

entry.title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training

author.name: Jia Quan Loh (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Vincent Crocher (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Marlena Klaic (Melbourne School of Health Sciences, The University of Melbourne), Denny Oetomo (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne), Ying Tan (Human Robotics Laboratory, Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Melbourne)

entry.summary: Proposes a learning-from-demonstration framework so rehabilitation robots reproduce personalized physical therapist-patient interaction patterns across varying practice conditions during upper-limb task-specific training. Motivated by the failure of existing rehab robots to beat conventional therapy.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Priorities: Multi-Tier SLA Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Anders Vestrum, Arya Raeesi, Hanna Roed

entry.summary: Extends the Llumnix LLM serving scheduler from two priority levels to arbitrarily many SLA tiers and evaluates the effect on heterogeneous service-level objectives under several regimes. Targets production deployments mixing latency-critical calls with background batch jobs.

entry.title: Where the Cost Falls: A Deployment-Aware Adoption Order for Stability Enhancements to Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks

author.name: Rowan Hussein, Mohamed Ouf

entry.summary: Compares four common stability enhancements for cycle-consistent GAN training not only by output quality but by where their computational cost falls, deriving a recommended adoption order for teams under compute or latency budgets. The argument is that the cost profile follows from architecture rather than from any specific run.

entry.title: Remote-Sensing City Layout Extraction with MLLM

author.name: Zigan Zhou, Kai Li, Yupeng Deng

entry.summary: Casts urban layout extraction from a single top-down satellite image as constrained code generation with a multimodal LLM, producing an executable city graph with object identities, typed relations, topology and regeneration rules rather than boxes or masks. An image model supplies a semantic prior and three ordered MLLM passes recover roads, land cover regions and buildings before deterministic normalization.

entry.title: Real-time Estimator of Actuator Control and Health (REACH) on an Eel-Inspired Soft Robot

author.name: Zhangjingyi Jiang, Myungsun Park, Michael T. Tolley, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: REACH estimates actuator health on an eel-inspired soft swimming robot in real time using a soft-body model, a sigma-point filter, and a formal statistical hypothesis test. It is evaluated with GPS, IMU, and bend sensors so a degraded robot can still complete or abort its mission safely.

entry.title: Pluralistic Human-Robot Interaction: Designing for Robot Interaction with Diverse Communities

author.name: Raj Korpan

entry.summary: A conceptual framework arguing that social robot design should treat human diversity as a first-class constraint, drawing on pluralism, civic dialogue, perspective-taking, cultural humility, and moral imagination rather than optimizing only for engagement and task success. It sketches implications for design and evaluation practice.

entry.title: Generated Context versus Governed State: Functional Conditions for Accountable Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Augusto Bernardo Pissarra, Victor Lorena de Farias Souza

entry.summary: Argues that longitudinal clinical reasoning is a state-estimation problem under partial observability and that current LLM interfaces maintain no persistent governed representation of what is currently true about a patient. It distinguishes generated context from governed state and separates true state, observations, evidence, belief, and simulated state as objects clinical AI routinely conflates.

entry.title: Agent Gym: A Framework for Continuous Evaluation and Evolution of LLM Agents Through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback

author.name: Pouya Ghiasnezhad Omran, Michael Zimmermann, Duncan Cambridge, Ashmita Kapoor, Tanya Dixit

entry.summary: Agent Gym wraps an existing deployed LLM agent so that domain experts can correct its behavior continuously through human-in-the-loop feedback, without editing source code or running heavy log-and-retrace engineering cycles. It targets the gap between an agent frozen at deployment and business rules that keep changing.

entry.title: When Stories Evolve: Benchmarking LLM Storytelling Across Agent Architectures in Open-Ended World Simulations

author.name: Yuqi Chen, Sixuan Li, Yunfeng Cai, Xueai Li, Ka Man Yan, Ying Li

entry.summary: Introduces a process-level benchmark for long-form LLM storytelling in evolving world simulations, separately measuring how much of a planned narrative gets produced, when canon consistency breaks, and how meaningfully branches develop. Across frontier models the consistency and richness axes do not trade off smoothly, suggesting architecture choices matter more than raw model quality.

entry.title: FirstDiff: One-Step Diffusion-Based Anomaly Detection for Multivariate Time Series via Initial Noise Prediction

author.name: Ali Boudaghi, Alireza Nemati, Hadi Zare

entry.summary: Observes that the noise predicted at the very first reverse-diffusion step already carries most of the anomaly signal for multivariate time series, enabling detection in a single evaluation instead of a full denoising trajectory. This yields large computational savings over iterative diffusion-based detectors.

entry.title: Behaviour Is an Incomplete Measure of Reasoning Development: Cross-surface pre-arrival accessibility and the limits of developmental inference in a recurrent-depth reasoner

author.name: Simon Lam-Muir

entry.summary: A single-author study of a 30M-parameter recurrent-depth relational reasoner argues that behavioral thresholds, final checkpoints, and probe readouts identify different moments of capability acquisition. Using preregistered pre-arrival hidden-state probes and controls, it finds vastly different acquisition costs across symbolic versus verbal training surfaces, cautioning against inferring internal development from behavior alone.

entry.title: TokenSTFormer: A Tokenized Spatial-temporal Attention Model for Holistic Motion Analysis in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Screening

author.name: Dong Chen, Kenneth M. C. Cheung

entry.summary: The authors release ScoliGait, a dataset of about 1,500 gait video clips paired with X-ray records, and TokenSTFormer, a spatial-temporal tokenized attention model for screening adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from motion video. Reported accuracy around 0.79 beats a vanilla ViT encoder baseline.

entry.title: Agent-Native Telemetry: Verifiable State-Delta Evidence for Autonomous Operations

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes agent-native telemetry: instead of verbose human-readable logs, systems emit compact verifiable state deltas via an Agent Telemetry Protocol and a State-Delta Evidence Ledger with cryptographic provenance and completeness guarantees. The motivation is that autonomous agents waste context parsing prose rather than reasoning about state change.

entry.title: Decoupled Temporal Encoding for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Pengfei Jia, Jingjian Wang, Jingmao Li, Ge Zhang, Feng Shi

entry.summary: This work replaces NLP-inherited positional encodings in transformer-based generative recommenders with decoupled temporal encoding that separately represents discrete item order and multi-level real-time effects such as recency, meal-time peaks, weekday shifts, and promotion bursts. It is motivated by a production food-delivery and instant-retail recommendation system.

entry.title: Revisiting the Performance of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Introductory Object-Oriented Programming Assessments: Insights from 2026

author.name: Marina Lepp, Joosep Kaimre

entry.summary: This education study grades solutions from five deployed assistants, including GPT-5.2, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Microsoft Copilot, on authentic introductory object-oriented programming tests using the same rubric applied to students, and compares against historical student results and last year's findings. It also categorizes recurring error types on real exam tasks.

entry.title: SIGMA-Lane: Scale-pyramId Gated MAmba for Temporally Consistent Video Lane Detection

author.name: Tiancheng Zhang, Mengmeng Wang, Yan Gao, Xiangjie Kong, Guojiang Shen, Jiaxin Du

entry.summary: SIGMA-Lane treats occlusion in streaming video lane detection as state contamination in state-space temporal models, placing occlusion-aware gates directly on the SSM write and residual-fusion paths rather than supplying obstacle masks as auxiliary inputs. This prevents corrupted observations from persisting in hidden state across frames.

entry.title: Adaptive Post-Processing Drives Instance-Level Detection in Stroke Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Qinghui Liu, Jon Andr\'e Ottesen, Atle Bj{\o}rnerud, Kyrre Eeg Emblem

entry.summary: For the ISLES'26 stroke lesion challenge, the authors find that volume-conditioned adaptive post-processing, which adjusts connected-component size thresholds to each case's predicted lesion burden, improves instance-level Lesion-F1 more than architectural changes. Small lesions are the main beneficiary because near-miss predictions currently score like complete misses.

entry.title: X$^2$Localizer: Cross-grained Alignment for Progressive Cross-view Video Geo-localization

author.name: Zichao Zeng, Weijia Fan, Yufan Chen, June Moh Goo, Junwei Zheng, Ruiping Liu, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Rainer Stiefelhagen, Jan Boehm

entry.summary: X2Localizer targets progressive cross-view video geo-localization, where ground-view video must be matched to geo-tagged aerial imagery under varying temporal budgets, prefix-based inference, random starts, and interruptions rather than fixed-length clips. It uses cross-grained alignment supervising both global prefix-to-aerial retrieval and token-aggregated matching.

entry.title: Beyond Effective Sample Size: Effective Number of Proposals for Adaptive Importance Sampling

author.name: Ali Mousavi, Victor Elvira

entry.summary: Argues that effective sample size, the standard diagnostic for adaptive importance sampling, only measures weight concentration and says nothing about how proposal components are spatially arranged, so several proposals collapsing onto the same target region can look healthy. Introduces an effective number of proposals diagnostic to capture proposal diversity in population-based schemes.

entry.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Decoding Topological Quantum Codes

author.name: Changwon Lee, Tak Hur, Jeongwoo Jae, Daniel K. Park

entry.summary: A review of machine learning approaches to decoding topological quantum error-correcting codes, framing decoding as high-throughput classical inference over spatiotemporally correlated stabilizer measurement data and surveying accuracy, scalability, and real-time deployability trade-offs. Motivated by the tightening decoder requirements as code distance grows in fault-tolerant architectures.

entry.title: Inferential Evaluation of Surrogate-Derived Models under Covariate Shift

author.name: Longtian Shi, Molei Liu, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: Studies how to evaluate a model trained on abundant surrogate labels when it is deployed in a target population where gold-standard outcomes are unobserved, using a three-sample setup of a small gold-labeled source, a large surrogate-labeled source, and an unlabeled target. Proposes cross-fitted estimators that transport information across sources under conditional transportability to give inference on target performance.

entry.title: Domain-Agnostic Neural Topic Modeling with Contextual Token-Level Semantic Graph Representation

author.name: Seung-Won Seo, Won Ik Cho, Yongmin Yoo

entry.summary: Argues that neural topic models degrade on specialized corpora because domain-specific terms collapse in the frozen encoder's embedding geometry, which retraining or parameter-efficient tuning cannot fix. Adds a learnable graph layer over token-level embeddings to acquire corpus-specific semantic structure for more interpretable topics.

entry.title: Self-Routed Tensor Adapters for Parameter-Efficient Universal Visual Adaptation

author.name: Suraj Yadav

entry.summary: Self-Routed Tensor Adapters perform multi-domain visual adaptation by projecting each input into a low-rank space and routing within the adapter itself, avoiding external routers and large expert banks used by mixture-of-experts adapters. Aims for compact parameter-efficient tuning of frozen vision foundation models across heterogeneous domains.

entry.title: S2Dialog: Multimodal Dialogue Retrieval with Semantic and Acoustic-Style Modeling

author.name: Xueqi Wang, Zhigang Wang, Runqing Zhang, Zhenqi Jia, Junfeng Zhao

entry.summary: S2Dialog performs retrieval at the level of whole dialogues, matching both textual semantics and acoustic conversational style rather than isolated utterances or a single modality. The retrieved dialogue examples are meant to serve as references for emotion recognition in conversation, spoken dialogue systems, and conversational speech synthesis.

entry.title: A Calibrated Test of Internal Action Maps: State Signals Without Global Affine Closure

author.name: Dekun Yang

entry.summary: Investigates whether hidden-state directions that encode state changes also support reusable, composable affine action maps, using a synthetic permutation-group carrier and a small Qwen model. The conclusion is that decodable or causally usable signals do not imply global affine closure.

entry.title: Generation of Synthetic Fingerphotos with GANs

author.name: Conor Miller-Lynch, Sandip Purnapatra, Syed Konain Abbas, Lambert Igene, Faraz Hussain, Soumyabrata Dey, Stephanie Schuckers

entry.summary: Generates synthetic contactless fingerphotos with StyleGAN2-ADA and StyleGAN3 and evaluates them for realism, privacy preservation, and diversity using biometric comparison scores. The goal is usable substitute data given the scarcity and sensitivity of real contactless fingerprint datasets.

entry.title: LightLoc++: Sensor-Robust Representation Learning for Efficient Outdoor LiDAR Localization

author.name: Wen Li, Shangshu Yu, Dunqiang Liu, Qiming Xia, Sheng Ao, Siqi Shen, Chenglu Wen, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: LightLoc++ tackles the sensor-transfer weakness of decoupled scene coordinate regression for outdoor LiDAR localization, where a frozen pretrained backbone degrades when new scans come from different LiDAR configurations. It learns sensor-robust representations so that only lightweight scene-specific heads need training, cutting per-scene training from days.

entry.title: Feed-Forward Hierarchical Gaussian Diffusion for Extreme CT Reconstruction

author.name: Yuezhe Yang, Li Cheng

entry.summary: HiGDiff reconstructs 3D CT volumes from severely limited projections using a feed-forward hierarchical Gaussian diffusion model that separates global anatomy from local detail, with physics-conditioned anatomical anchors guiding where Gaussian primitives are allocated. It targets sparse-angle, limited-angle and low-photon degradations jointly rather than one at a time.

entry.title: PoseAdapter: Dual-Stream 2.5D Controllable Image Generation for Complex Multi-Object Scenes

author.name: Yufeng Chi, Huimin Ma, Fan Gao, Zhice Niu, Keqin Li, Jianmin Li

entry.summary: PoseAdapter adds orientation and spatial control to multi-object text-to-image generation using a lightweight condition layout of per-object captions, 2D boxes and 3D angles instead of dense 3D maps. A context-aware dual-stream design is used to trade off strict instance isolation against global scene coherence and to reduce attribute leakage.

entry.title: Bitstream Action Recognition is Byte Modeling

author.name: Fangcheng Li, Chaoran Huang, Tianyi Liu, Wenyang Liu, Kejun Wu, Qiong Liu, You Yang, Zhengguo Li

entry.summary: BRACE recognizes actions directly from compressed video bitstreams as a byte-modeling problem, using a dual-branch architecture that treats corrupted and intact bitstreams as two realizations of the same action to anchor robust embeddings. This removes dependence on successful pixel decoding when transmission or storage corrupts the stream.

entry.title: ES3D: Embedding Semantics into 3D Space for Component-Aware Editing

author.name: Xuancheng Jin, Rengan Xie, Jiayuan Lu, Wenting Zheng, Rui Wang, Yuchi Huo, Lincheng Li, Yingfeng Chen

entry.summary: ES3D embeds semantic features directly into 3D space so that individual components of a 3D asset can be retrieved and edited using local reference images rather than text prompts or manually supplied 3D masks. This is aimed at fine-grained edits that do not disturb regions meant to stay unchanged.

entry.title: KeyID: Decoupled Drafting and Keyframe Editing for Identity-Preserving Video Generation

author.name: Jianjie Luo, Yiming Zhong, Haoming Shen, Yupeng Xiao, Zhenguo Yang

entry.summary: KeyID is a training-free framework for identity-preserving video generation that first drafts identity-agnostic video dynamics aligned with references, then injects the target identity through sparse keyframe corrections. This avoids tuning costs while maintaining identity consistency through long and complex actions.

entry.title: TransAnyText: Translating Arbitrary Text in E-commerce Images via Structured Visual Generation

author.name: Xiaoan Liu, Lichen Ma, Zipeng Guo, Yu He, Xiaoyan Su, Shaojie Guo, Hao Yang, Jingling Fu, Xiaolong Fu, Zhen Chen, Yu Guo, Fei Wang, Xinyi Liu, Yongjun Zhang, Ke Zhang, Junshi Huang

entry.summary: TransAnyText reframes translating text inside e-commerce images as generating renderable HTML patches, letting a vision-language model handle understanding, translation and structured layout while a diffusion model inpaints backgrounds. The decoupling of semantic generation from pixel rendering yields editable outputs that preserve visual identity.

entry.title: Calibration-Free Vehicle Speed Estimation: A Monocular Keypoint-Template Approach

author.name: Gaofeng Su, Keya Li, Raja Sengupta, Kara M. Kockelman

entry.summary: This work estimates vehicle speed from monocular video without camera calibration by fitting a 36-keypoint vehicle template and updating a homography every frame. It compares keypoint-only tracking against warped optical flow across more than 400 clips from roadside and overhead views.

entry.title: Evidence of Absence: Cross-Modal Abductive Risk Perception to Sustain World Models When Vision Fails

author.name: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

entry.summary: This paper proposes sustaining a structured world state when vision fails by treating the absence of expected corroborating evidence as evidence for a hidden cause, instantiated with a microphone array that estimates engine and tire bearings and approach rate. The abductive framework is presented as modality-agnostic.

entry.title: Dual-Branch State-Displacement Network for Sea Surface Temperature Super-Resolution

author.name: Wankun Chen, Feng Gao, Yanhai Gan, Chuanzheng Gong, Xun Gong, Junyu Dong, Qian Du

entry.summary: DBSD-Net super-resolves satellite sea surface temperature fields using a wavelet frequency branch with a structural state-space module plus a branch extracting semantic features from a frozen VGG backbone. The goal is recovering fine thermal structures such as ocean fronts.

entry.title: Rotate Disks to Reach Farther: Design and Modeling of a Novel Reconfigurable Tendon Driven Manipulator

author.name: Sabyasachi Dash, Yangkun Liu, Will Hunter, John Golden, Girish Krishnan

entry.summary: Presents a tendon-driven continuum manipulator whose spacer disks can rotate to locally reroute tendons, producing richer spatial deformations, in both manually locked and continuously rotating variants. A piecewise-constant-strain static model within an energy-minimization framework predicts the resulting shapes.

entry.title: Deep Probabilistic Indoor Gas Source Localization via Physical Dependency-Guided Sequential Inference

author.name: Seunghwan Kim, Hyungjin Kim, Junhee Lee, Hyondong Oh

entry.summary: A deep probabilistic method for locating indoor gas sources from sparse mobile-robot measurements, structured to respect the physical dependency chain in which wind and source position jointly determine concentration fields rather than regressing the source end-to-end. It aims for CFD-informed accuracy at online-usable cost.

entry.title: H-PAC Hand: Control-Oriented Modeling and Tendon-Elasticity Compensation for an Underactuated Robotic Hand

author.name: Teng Yan, Jiongxu Chen, Teng Wang, Yue Yu, Qixiang Hua, Zihang Wang, Yongru Chen, Bingzhuo Zhong

entry.summary: H-PAC is a 15-DoF, 6-actuator underactuated tendon hand with an analytical actuator-to-joint model and a mechanics-based compensation scheme for joint errors caused by tendon stretch under spring loading. It is implemented in a host-plus-microcontroller hierarchy driving six position-controlled servos.

entry.title: Convergence Analysis of Statistical Inverse Problems on Reproducing Kernel Banach Spaces

author.name: Darrel K Joseph, M P Rajan

entry.summary: Analyzes Tikhonov regularization for linear statistical inverse problems posed in reproducing kernel Banach spaces, deriving convergence guarantees when the data are noisy independent samples from an unknown distribution. It extends classical Hilbert-space learning theory results to the Banach setting.

entry.title: When to Communicate: Belief Distributions and KL Divergence for Principled Gating in Multi-Agent RL

author.name: Teoman Kaman

entry.summary: Proposes gating inter-agent communication in multi-agent RL by the KL divergence between agents learned belief distributions over a latent world state, triggering messages only when belief disagreement exceeds a threshold. This replaces high-variance REINFORCE-learned binary gates with an interpretable, information-theoretic criterion.

entry.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs across Text and Audio Modalities for Accessible Disaster Assistance

author.name: Anuridhi Gupta, Samara Mansoor, Hemant Purohit

entry.summary: Evaluates whether multimodal LLMs give consistent and actionable disaster guidance across text and audio inputs for users with access and functional needs, including hard-of-hearing people, caregivers, and elderly individuals with dementia. Modality consistency is treated as a deployment prerequisite for emergency chatbots.

entry.title: Agentic Data Cleaning Without a Clean Reference: An Experimental Study of Capabilities and Trade-offs

author.name: Hadi Fadlallah

entry.summary: Studies reference-free data cleaning by LLM agents, where unusual values may be genuine or erroneous, using a framework combining profiling, executable checks, evidence retrieval with source ranking, conservative repairs, reversible scripts, and provenance logs. Seven agent configurations are compared over financial, clinical, and environmental datasets across 126 runs with controlled synthetic corruption.

entry.title: When Is an Agent Evaluation Over? Outcome Finality and Cross-Unit Separation

author.name: Avyay M. Casheekar

entry.summary: Argues that scoring an agent on the state visible when a run is stopped presupposes two independent conditions that the endpoint does not establish: that the outcome is final and that runs do not share state with each other. The paper specifies what evidence justifies declaring a final label, including resolving, bounding, or retaining uncertainty about anything that could still change the outcome.

entry.title: Andy: A Mathematical Agent for Rigorous Proof and Autonomous Research

author.name: Zi'an Wang

entry.summary: Describes an autonomous mathematical research agent that separates proof generation from correctness evaluation and supports knowledge acquisition, targeted revision, and multi-stage verification. The workflow is illustrated by extending a published control-theory result into a new synchronization problem for delayed heterogeneous networks with switching topologies.

entry.title: RAGas: Retrieval-Augmented Gas Optimization for Smart Contracts with Continuous Knowledge Integration

author.name: Yishun Wang, Wenjin Yi, Wenkai Li, Zongwei Li, Xiaoqi Li

entry.summary: Catalogs twelve fine-grained gas-wasting antipatterns in Ethereum smart contracts into a curated knowledge base and uses retrieval-augmented generation to suggest functionality-preserving gas optimizations that improve as new patterns are added. Targets ongoing deployment cost reduction as usage patterns evolve.

entry.title: Unified Pedestrian Path Prediction Using Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: \v{S}imon Sukup, Ariyan Bighashdel, Pavol Jancura

entry.summary: Adapts a spatial-temporal graph attention network into a unified inverse reinforcement learning framework for pedestrian path prediction, defining states and actions so the same backbone supports deterministic and stochastic policies and sequential decision-making with REINFORCE or PPO. Extends prior shallow-network comparisons of task formulations to deep models.

entry.title: DeCo-MIL: Debiased Counterfactual Reasoning for Long-Tailed Whole Slide Image Analysis

author.name: Xiaoxiao Li, Xitong Ling, Jiawen Li, Weiming Chen, Zhenyang Cai, Xidong Wang, Tian Guan, Benyou Wang, Yonghong He

entry.summary: DeCo-MIL addresses a coupled dual long-tail problem in whole-slide image analysis, where rare classes have few slides and their diagnostic evidence is confined to a few patches. It combines frequency-debiased counterfactual reasoning with instance-level evidence selection to improve rare-class recognition.

entry.title: Catching Hallucinated Citations in Video-LLM Question Answering: A Self-Verification Pipeline and Verifier Ablation Study

author.name: Yogesh Kumar

entry.summary: Tackles hallucinated timestamp citations in video question answering by re-examining each cited frame with an independent verifier before showing answers to users, and ablates three verifier designs across two hardware stacks. A key negative finding is that simply asking the vision model whether a frame supports a claim performs poorly.

entry.title: Visualizing Uncertainty-to-Action Composition for Human Oversight

author.name: Chisom Anyabolu, Akshat Dubey, Georges Hattab

entry.summary: This work argues that uncertainty visualizations typically encode uncertainty in outputs while leaving unclear what oversight action should follow, and proposes a framework that composes multiple uncertainty conditions into a single oversight response under a precedence policy with a contextual safety modifier. It pairs the framework with visual designs binding uncertainty to action.

entry.title: A Regulatory Placebo? The Systemic Failure of Mandatory GenAI Labeling

author.name: Jingyi Chen, Chaofan Bu, Shibo Yan, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: This policy analysis characterizes global mandatory generative AI labeling requirements as reactive symbolic legislation, arguing they create implementation dilemmas and may impede technical progress. It critiques three theoretical justifications for labeling regimes as reflecting regulators' misunderstanding of how modern generative systems work.

entry.title: NRCD: An Open Database of Collegiate Running with Unified Performance Standardization

author.name: Jonathan A. Karr Jr., Ryan M. Fryer, Ben Darden, Nicholas Pell, Kayla Ambrose, Evan Hall, Ramzi K. Bualuan, Nitesh V. Chawla

entry.summary: Releases the National Running Club Database with 128,963 approved performances from 28,913 collegiate athletes across 1,336 meets and four sports spanning 2004 to 2026, with unified cross-event performance standardization. Existing results sites block bulk download, which had confined prior studies to roughly 500 performances and skewed them toward male athletes.

entry.title: KOALA: Koopman Operator Learning for WiFi-Based Anticipatory Hum

author.name: Quang-Anh N. D., Duc Pham Minh, Thao Phuong Pham, Minh Anh Nguyen, Huan X. Nguyen, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: KOALA predicts future human motion from WiFi channel state information by lifting noisy CSI-derived poses into a Koopman latent space where dynamics are linear, enabling multi-horizon forecasts without error-amplifying autoregressive rollouts. Positioned as a privacy-preserving camera alternative.

entry.title: Breaking the Compression Barrier: Cross-Architecture Compression Boundary Learning via Reverse Regrowth

author.name: Zhaocen Liu, Satvik Praveen, Yi Sheng

entry.summary: BRIDGE reframes model compression as boundary search: it first over-sparsifies a network to expose the collapse region, then hierarchically regrows critical structure to recover accuracy, rather than pruning forward toward an unknown limit. Aimed at finding feasible compression limits for edge deployment.

entry.title: Group ICA 2.0: Closing the Gap Between Subjects and Group Latent Decomposition with Copula-Linked Group ICA (CoLiG-ICA)

author.name: Oktay Agcaoglu

entry.summary: CoLiG-ICA extends group independent component analysis for fMRI by jointly estimating template-shared, cohort-specific, and subject-only brain networks using copula-based dependence modeling with deep-learning optimization. Aims to preserve individual heterogeneity that conventional group ICA averages away.

entry.title: The Ethical Decision Head: Operationalizing Normative Ethics in Autonomous Vehicles via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

author.name: Thomas Mbrice, Ammar Ali, Sami Mian, Khai Hern Low, Eric Chen, Arshia Aghajani, Wolf Sch\"afer, Amin Shirangi

entry.summary: Encodes utilitarian and Kantian normative frameworks as differentiable reward signals for a policy-gradient agent trained in CARLA-aligned autonomous driving scenarios, then compares the resulting behaviors. Frames ethical reasoning as an explicit reward-shaping component in the vehicle decision stack.

entry.title: CFR without Unbiasedness: Deterministic Guarantees for Persistent Public-Chance Schedules

author.name: Jiaxing Guo, Lei Ye

entry.summary: Analyzes counterfactual regret minimization when a public-chance node is only partially sampled using a fixed without-replacement ordering, feedback that is conditionally biased because earlier batches shape later profiles. Proves a deterministic target-transfer theorem bounding full-cut exploitability by observed regret plus a public-debit term coupling coverage discrepancy with strategy motion.

entry.title: Prototype-Rectified Iterative Self-supervised Manifold Denoising under Severe Acoustic Shift

author.name: Ashish Anand Shukla, Rini Smita Thakur, Aryan Das, Vinod K. Kurmi

entry.summary: PRISM is a training-free, source-free test-time adaptation method for audio-text foundation models under severe acoustic noise, built on the hypothesis that such noise induces a low-rank affine shift in the multimodal latent space with over 90 percent of distortion energy in the leading 60 principal components. It estimates and reverses this shift from an unlabeled target batch using prototype rectification and iterative manifold denoising, avoiding gradient-based adaptation that tends to reinforce noise.

entry.title: A Unified Geometric Framework for Developmental Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Data

author.name: Mary Chriselda Antony Oliver, Kaitlyn Hohmeier, Tuyen Tran, Alejandra Castillo, Caroline Moosm\"uller, Shiying Li

entry.summary: Proposes an optimal transport based geometric framework for reconstructing developmental trajectories from destructively sampled single-cell and spatial transcriptomic snapshots, moving beyond aligning distributions in gene expression space to comparing the relational structure of gene expression networks. Aims to recover temporal and spatial dynamics from unaligned independently sampled populations.

entry.title: GOD: Enhancing Generalization via Deep Grafting for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: WooJoo Kim, JunYoung Kim, JaeHyung Lim, HwanJo Yu

entry.summary: Graft-Oriented Distillation improves sequential recommenders by replacing individual frozen teacher components with student components during training, isolating which part of the student causes weak generalization. This component-level grafting is contrasted with conventional output or representation matching distillation.

entry.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge

author.name: Kexin Shi, Renhe Sun, Yuge Huang, Ximeng Wang, Jiayi Zhou, Jian Liu, Malu Zhang

entry.summary: A challenge system report for unsegmented multilingual conversation processing, fine-tuning a speech recognition model with random leading-silence cropping, timestamp correction, and exponential moving average for diarization plus recognition. For the understanding task with no provided training data, it builds synthetic question-answer pairs through multimodal candidate generation and distribution-matched augmentation before fine-tuning an omni-modal model.

entry.title: PE-CSNet: An equivariant network architecture with learnable patch-based sparse representation

author.name: Kai Li, Haitao Long, Bo Zhang, Haiwen Zhang, Zhi Zhou

entry.summary: An equivariant deep unrolling network for compressive sensing that learns a patch-based sparse transform instead of using a predefined one, embedding the learned sparsity into the optimization procedure. It targets medical imaging, remote sensing, and compression applications.

entry.title: TinyDETR-Pose: Towards End-to-End Real-Time Single-Stage 6DoF Object Pose Estimation with Lightweight Transformers

author.name: Paul Julius K\"uhn, Duc Anh Nguyen, Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Michael Weinmann, Arjan Kuijper

entry.summary: TinyDETR-Pose performs single-stage, end-to-end 6DoF object pose estimation on a lightweight DETR backbone with dedicated heads for rotation, monocular depth and projected object center, avoiding non-differentiable PnP or RANSAC stages. It targets real-time inference on resource-constrained edge hardware.

entry.title: A Multi-Annotator Study of Segmentation Noise and Uncertainty in Turbid Underwater Images

author.name: Galadrielle Humblot-Renaux, Vasiliki Ismiroglou, Malte Pedersen

entry.summary: Reports the first large multi-annotator study of segmentation in real turbid underwater scenes, with over one hundred participants annotating under controlled turbidity levels. It quantifies how visibility degradation drives annotator disagreement and what that implies for label noise and uncertainty estimation outside the medical domain.

entry.title: AlignJEPA: Predictive Vision-Language Alignment for Remote Sensing Foundation Models

author.name: Md Aminur Hossain, Omkumar Vaghasiya, Rajeev Ranjan Dwivedi, Vinod Kurmi, Biplab Banerjee

entry.summary: AlignJEPA aligns a frozen remote sensing visual encoder with a text encoder by training only a lightweight predictive network that reconstructs text embeddings from masked visual tokens, rather than relying on global contrastive alignment. The goal is natural-language archive search, image-text retrieval and question-conditioned Earth observation analysis.

entry.title: BASeg: Boundary-Aware Remote Sensing Segmentation with Structural Penalties

author.name: Yuexi Song, Kailai Sun, Zhuoyu Wang, Mingyi He, Paul Pu Liang, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: BASeg introduces a Mahalanobis-angle boundary loss that weights structural importance and penalizes boundary orientation error for remote sensing semantic segmentation, and can be dropped into existing architectures. The authors also raise the underexplored issue of city morphology diversity and segmentation performance on generated imagery.

entry.title: FlowDance: Music-Driven Dance Video Generation with Parallel Pose and RGB Streams

author.name: Genying Li, Boda Lin, Jiachen Li, Zijian Jia, Haojie Zheng, Yiming Wang, Shuchen Weng, Si Li

entry.summary: FlowDance generates music-driven dance videos of a reference person using parallel pose and RGB streams, with timestep-aware pose injection that adapts structural guidance across denoising steps and persistent identity injection for long clips. The authors also curate a high-quality dance video dataset for the task.

entry.title: MITE-Net: SWaP-Optimized 4K Video Tiny Target Perception for Embodied Edge SAR

author.name: Mingshuo Xu, Mu Hua, Jigen Peng, Qi Wang, Shigang Yue

entry.summary: MITE-Net targets real-time detection of tiny targets in 4K video on size, weight and power constrained UAV hardware by cascading a bio-inspired learning-free motion-based region proposal stage with a sub-0.14M parameter detection head. The work also contributes specialized 4K tiny-target datasets and hardware-level benchmarks for edge deployment.

entry.title: A Plug-and-Play 2D Motion Interface for Real-World Motion Language Models

author.name: Kaname Yokoyama, Norimichi Ukita

entry.summary: Introduces a plug-and-play interface that lets 3D-pretrained motion language models consume 2D motion inputs without any modification or fine-tuning, sidestepping the difficulty of recovering accurate 3D motion from monocular video. Results match 3D-input performance and beat training on 2D motions from scratch, with a new real-video evaluation set.

entry.title: TR-GS: High-Fidelity Sparse-View CT Volumetric Rendering via t-Distribution Gaussian Splatting and Ray-Confidence Modeling

author.name: Zedong Xiao, Yiren Wang, Zhou Liu, Xiaolin Liu, Zhangji Lu

entry.summary: TR-GS replaces standard Gaussian primitives with projectable Student t-distribution primitives and adds ray-confidence modeling for sparse-view CT volumetric rendering, aiming to be less sensitive to unreliable observations. This targets structural artifacts and reconstruction uncertainty when projections are limited to reduce radiation dose.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity Matching: Structured Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Referring Segmentation in 3DGS

author.name: Yizhao Wang, Xinfa Wang, Jingbo Wang, Jingbo Wang, Guantao Zhang, Yafeng Han, Guohong Gao, Yuhe Xia

entry.summary: QAGaussian performs open-vocabulary referring segmentation over 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes by learning query-conditioned multi-scale Gaussian slots and structured reasoning, instead of relying on global text-region similarity. This targets failures involving attributes, reference objects, spatial relations and part-whole granularity.

entry.title: PosterText: Towards Unified Visual Text Generation and Editing for E-commerce Poster

author.name: Xiaoan Liu, Lichen Ma, Zipeng Guo, Yu He, Xiaoyan Su, Shaojie Guo, Jingling Fu, Xiaolong Fu, Hao Yang, Tongxuan Liu, Yu Guo, Fei Wang, Xinyi Liu, Yongjun Zhang, Junshi Huang

entry.summary: PosterText unifies e-commerce poster generation and editing by treating text patches as atomic units supporting addition, deletion, modification and reference-guided style control, trained with a four-stage curriculum. It targets the gap where existing systems do either end-to-end generation or rigid multi-stage design but not flexible precise editing.

entry.title: Cross-View Urban Sensing: Mapping Subjective Streetscape Perception via AlphaEarth Embeddings and Urban Context

author.name: Peilin Li, Pengfei Chen, Jingyu Wang, Zhifeng Yang, Tiansheng Chen, Mengjie Gong, Xiao Cheng

entry.summary: CVLNet predicts subjective streetscape perception across five dimensions from satellite-derived AlphaEarth embeddings and multi-source urban context, removing the need for street view imagery at inference. It uses labels from a pretrained street-view perception model and is validated across four Southeast Asian cities.

entry.title: Can Unsupervised Methods Outperform Supervised Deep Learning When Ground Truth Is Sparse? A Case Study of Bronchovascular Bundle Segmentation in Low-Dose CT
