author.name: Riccardo Fogliato, Abhinav Palia, Xiawei Wang, Emily Sheng, Chad Atalla, Jean Garcia-Gathright, Nicholas Pangakis, Sharman Tan, Dan Vann, Hannah Washington, P. Alex Dow, Heba Elfardy, Hanna Wallach, Sandeep Atluri

entry.summary: ASSERT is a specification-driven pipeline that ties every reported compliance rate in a generative AI audit to a written record of the measurement choices that produced it, so a change in the number can be attributed either to the system or to the measurement. It helps draft behavioral rubrics and test cases and then runs the audit end to end. The authors, including established measurement-theory researchers, demonstrate it in a case study.

entry.title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Why Power Sampling Can Fail and How to Fix It

author.name: Haohui Yang, Jiaxing Sun, Xiujun Ma

entry.summary: Documents a paradox in power sampling, a verifier-free inference-time technique that sharpens a language model distribution over whole reasoning trajectories: it can shift more probability mass onto correct trajectories while reducing downstream self-consistency accuracy by as much as 18.5 points. The authors attribute this to a dose mismatch from fixed sharpening exponents and a second mismatch, and propose corrections.

entry.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

author.name: Ben Anson, Conor Houghton, Edward Milsom

entry.summary: Addresses the incompatibility between the Muon optimizer and LoRA, since a low-rank update cannot be exactly orthogonalized, by approximating a relaxed Muon objective through linearization plus least squares. The resulting sMuon method uses only matrix multiplications and performs well across supervised fine-tuning tasks.

entry.title: Q2.5 2026 Timelines Update: Uplift and Revenue

author.name: brendanhalstead

entry.summary: A quarterly update to a public AI timelines model, replacing reliance on coding time-horizon extrapolation with anchors based on measured research uplift and AI revenue. The authors report slightly shorter timelines but mainly greater confidence due to a stronger evidence base and better-documented modeling.

entry.title: An explainable biomedical foundation model via large-scale concept-enhanced vision–language pretraining

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Nature Biomedical Engineering paper presents a biomedical vision-language foundation model pretrained at scale with explicit clinical concept supervision, so that its predictions can be attributed to named medical concepts rather than only saliency heatmaps. Building interpretability into the pretraining objective, instead of bolting it on afterward, is a practically important direction for clinical deployment and regulatory acceptance of medical AI.

entry.title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Yu Zhuang, Kefei Chen, Yitong Duan, Shuxin Zheng, Jian Li, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: AgentRewind adds runtime recovery to long-horizon LLM agents by recording aligned checkpoints of both the agent context and a controlled environment, so an agent that makes an irreversible early mistake can roll back and retry with knowledge from the failed attempt. The authors also build MettleBench to measure recovery rather than only first-pass success. This targets one of the main practical failure modes of deployed agents: error propagation that later actions cannot undo.

entry.title: Rollplex: Cross-Phase GPU Spatial Sharing for Vision Language Model Post-Training

author.name: Hanfeng Lu, Tianyu Feng, Suyi Li, Yuheng Zhao, Wei Gao, Shaopan Xiong, Ju Huang, Siran Yang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Presents a runtime that overlaps prompt and video prefix processing with rollout decoding during on-policy RL post-training of vision-language models, exploiting idle GPU capacity without breaking synchronous semantics. It targets the phase-serial execution pattern inherited from text-only RL frameworks, which wastes compute when visual inputs dominate.

entry.title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement

author.name: Lushi Pu, Weiming Zhang, Xinheng Xie, Zixuan Fu, Bingxiang He, Hengyu Zhao, Hongya Lyu, Xin Li, Jie Zhou, Yudong Wang

entry.summary: MathForm improves autoformalization into Lean 4 by retrieving Mathlib library knowledge instead of relying on parametric memory and by using verification feedback to iteratively refine generated formal statements. It addresses the twin failures of wrong library typing and semantic drift from the natural-language source. Formal verification feedback loops are among the most credible routes to reliable mathematical AI.

entry.title: TimeSage-EV: A Live Benchmark for Agentic Time Series Analysis in Evolving Environments

author.name: Qingren Yao, Yaxuan Kong, Yuqi Nie, Yichen Li, Stefan Zohren, Anna Vettoruzzo, Qingsong Wen, Ming Jin, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: TimeSage-EV is a live, continuously updating benchmark for agentic time-series analysis in which LLM agents receive data and source reports up to a cutoff and are scored against withheld future releases, spanning 60 institutional scenarios and 1,485 QA pairs across varied release cadences. It targets contamination and staleness problems that plague fixed-snapshot time-series QA benchmarks. Live, cutoff-aware evaluation is an increasingly important evaluation design.

entry.title: Capacity-Dependent Effects of Data Selection for Reasoning

author.name: Cuong Dang, Hoang Anh Just, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: This paper tests the popular intuition that fine-tuning works best on teacher responses that already sit close to the student distribution, and finds that the benefit of likelihood-based data selection depends strongly on student capacity and training duration. Controlled math-reasoning experiments span 1.5B to 8B students with stronger teachers. The result cautions against treating high-likelihood selection as a universal recipe.

entry.title: Language-Specific Gaps in AI Safety Training Datasets

author.name: Chialuka Prisca-Mary Onuoha, Bright Etornam Sunu, Rashidat Sikiru

entry.summary: Audits 21 multilingual safety resources across Hausa, Swahili and French slices and finds that headline claims of coverage across a dozen or more languages routinely fail on inspection at the individual language level, with recurring gaps in provenance, annotation reliability, access and harm taxonomy. A controlled within-pipeline comparison supports the argument that per-language quality, not language count, should govern safety claims.

entry.title: ScienceFlow: A long-horizon agent for ML research, scientific discovery and beyond

author.name: Mingming Zhao, Jiqian Dong, Kangping Xu, Zadid Hasan, Chengrui Fan, Shan Jiang, Shuai Mao, Ting Lingya, Linyi Zou, Tailin Zhou, Yun Hin Chan, Wenkai Zhang, Zhanhong Zhou, Guowei Huang, Hongliang Li, Wenjing Cun, Zhitang Chen, Mingxuan Yuan, Yanhui Geng

entry.summary: ScienceFlow is a long-horizon autonomous research agent that decomposes ML research into executable research segments with mechanisms for state continuity, recovery from dead ends, and value-driven allocation of compute across exploration branches. It targets the failure of existing auto-research agents to sustain coherent goal-directed work over extended horizons. Automated ML research agents are a high-stakes capability frontier.

entry.title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel as LLM Agents Act and Observe

author.name: Zhensu Sun, Chengran Yang, Yunbo Lyu, Jieke Shi, David Lo

entry.summary: Observes that ReAct-style agents leave reasoning idle while an action executes and the environment responds, and proposes forking several auxiliary reasoning branches during that window, decoding them concurrently, then merging useful thoughts back when the observation arrives. The method is training-free and hides the extra reasoning cost inside existing latency.

entry.title: Coverage Aware Active Evaluation for Failure Discovery with Paired Systems

author.name: Anjali Parashar, Rachel Luo, Apoorva Sharma, Sushant Veer, Edward Schmerling, Carson Sobolewski, Mingxin Yu, Chuchu Fan, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive method for discovering rare failures in autonomous systems under tight testing budgets by combining plentiful cheap proxy evaluations (simulators or related policies) with a few expensive target-system tests, learning a local corrector of proxy risk to guide scenario selection. It explicitly manages coverage so that heterogeneous failure modes are not missed.

entry.title: Regime-Conditional Verification: Correctness Estimation for Adapting and Monitoring Safety Classifiers

author.name: Thiago Sandoval, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Regime-Conditional Verification wraps an off-the-shelf LLM safety classifier and, using the classifier's internal representations, estimates the probability that a given decision disagrees with the deployer's own policy, selectively flipping likely-wrong predictions without retraining. The same correctness estimates serve as a label-free distribution-shift detector for ongoing monitoring. It targets the practical gap between a vendor-trained moderation policy and each deployer's actual requirements.

entry.title: FreeBalance: Pre-Routing Online Moe Load Balancing via Residual Workload Prediction

author.name: Pengfei Chen, Yize Wu, Shouxu Kuang, Ke Gao, Ling Li

entry.summary: Tackles expert-parallel load imbalance in Mixture-of-Experts serving by predicting residual workload and rebalancing before routing decisions are available, so expert migration overhead leaves the inference critical path. Existing online balancers react to post-router statistics and therefore stall the slowest rank. This targets a concrete latency bottleneck in large MoE deployments.

entry.title: Clearing the Fog: Towards Installing and Refining Proactive Exploration Capabilities in LLM Agents

author.name: Zhizhao Guan, Chen Huang, Ziming Liu, Hongru Liang, Wenqiang Lei, See-Kiong Ng, Tat-Seng Chua, Anthony G Cohn

entry.summary: Studies proactive exploration in LLM agents, identifying that standard demonstrations suffer hindsight bias and that RL signals fail to separate productive exploration from aimless wandering. The method synthesizes exploration-rich trajectories and uses contrastive trajectory pairs during RL to reward informative information-gathering. It targets a capability gap that limits agents in partially observable environments.

entry.title: Tripwire: Triggering Aligned Refusal via Statistically Certified Safety Neurons

author.name: Wei Zhao, Zhe Li, Peixin Zhang, Jun Sun

entry.summary: Tripwire identifies a small set of statistically certified safety neurons whose activation triggers aligned refusal, and keeps the intervention dormant for benign inputs instead of perturbing every request. It aims to fix the utility tax of prior neuron-suppression and classifier-based safety-neuron defenses. The conditional, certified framing is a step toward fine-grained jailbreak defenses that do not degrade general capability.

entry.title: Do AI chatbots find what experts would? Effects of model, user role, and sample size on study retrieval for medical questions

author.name: Qingfang Liu, Qiao Jin, Joe D. Menke, Thorsten Kahnt, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: Researchers including NIH authors evaluated three widely used chatbots, an Anthropic Sonnet-class model, a Gemini Pro model, and a GPT-5.5-class model, on twenty clinical questions derived from recent Cochrane reviews, varying user role (patient, clinician, evidence synthesizer) and repeating queries for 720 responses total. They assess whether retrieved studies match what expert reviewers would select, going beyond the usual focus on fabricated citations. The findings speak to evidence quality in clinical LLM use.

entry.title: CForce: Boosting Parallel Decoding for dLLMs via Consistency Forcing

author.name: Yuji Ren, Chenkai Xu, Zhuocheng Gong, Jianguo Li, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: CForce is a distillation method for diffusion language models that forces early-denoising mask predictions to agree with later-stage predictions, using self-rollout trajectories and a confidence-adaptive KL objective blending forward and reverse divergence. This reduces the error propagation that limits aggressive parallel decoding. It targets the central speed-quality tradeoff of the diffusion LLM paradigm.

entry.title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models

author.name: Xinye Li, Lingshuai Lin, Lei Wang, Liuzhou Zhang, Jialin Cui, Qingshan Li, Guanchu Wang, Qingbin Liu, Xi Chen, Jiang Bian, Wai Lam

entry.summary: ForgeWM converts a bidirectional action-conditioned video generator into a few-step causal world model through domain adaptation, teacher-forced causal training, causal consistency distillation, and on-policy distribution matching against a bidirectional teacher. The goal is low-latency interactive generation that stays aligned with discrete keyboard and continuous mouse inputs across temporally compressed latent chunks. It advances playable video world models.

entry.title: AdvDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Joint-Aligned Actions and Adversarial Learning

author.name: Zhiyue Zhao, Jingyi Wu, Hairuo Liu, Mingyu Liu, Liyang Li, Hengdi Zhang, Tong He, Zhengxue Cheng

entry.summary: AdvDex is a vision-language-action framework for dexterous manipulation that learns from both human and robot demonstrations, introducing OmniShare, a large multimodal dataset of human demonstrations with kinematic supervision and tactile measurements, plus joint-aligned action representations and adversarial learning to disentangle task-relevant cues from embodiment appearance. It aims to reduce dependence on expensive teleoperation. Cross-embodiment generalization is the central claim.

entry.title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Shu Wan, Miles Ma, Hank Zhu, Guangqi Liu, Stephen Wang, Qingsong Wen, Huan Liu

entry.summary: The authors document forecast collapse, where time-series foundation models and deep forecasters produce nearly flat predictions with poor cross-sectional ranking for hourly equity returns while performing fine on trading volume, and trace it to low target predictability limiting calibrated point-forecast amplitude plus per-series objectives that leave cross-series structure unidentified. They verify the effect across many models and public benchmark configurations. It is a cautionary result for applying TSFMs to low signal-to-noise financial targets.

entry.title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination

author.name: Shuo Liang, Yixing Ma, Pengfei Zhou, Xingyan Chen, Zihan Mei, Manting Li, Feihan Chen, Zhiwen Wang, Bin Xu, Haotian Zhang, Jiajun Song, Shiya Su, Run Liu, Zhenghang Ni, Yifa Yu, Jintao Hong, Bolong Feng, Yifei Liu, Zirui Zhang, Jingxuan Zhang, Songlin Zhao, Yifan Bai, Kang Tan, Yizhe Liu, Junhao Du, Yongtao Ge, Zhaopan Xv, Xinyuan Zhang, Mengru Ma, Chunhua Shen, Wei Wang, Yang You, Zheng Zhu, Kaipeng Zhang, Wangbo Zhao

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark for detecting AI-generated crisis videos by anchoring nearly 1,800 real videos across ten social-risk categories against about 16k clips from nine open and closed generators, and evaluates detectors, human perception, and robustness under social-media dissemination. Provides evidence on how detectability varies with generation settings and survives re-encoding and sharing.

entry.title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction

author.name: Vincent Counathe, Ben Athiwaratkun, Christopher De Sa, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Points out that quantization-aware training computes gradients through a lossy weight reconstruction while updating latent full-precision weights, creating a mismatch that raises the achievable loss floor. Introduces a method that continuously performs cheap loss-aware reconstruction during training, borrowing from second-order post-training quantization but making it affordable to repeat.

entry.title: AgilePE: Autonomous UAV Pursuit-Evasion via Self-Play Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenhao Tang, Tianyang Chen, Zhejun Cui, Boyuan An, Jiayu Chen, Ruize Zhang, Huidong Liu, Tianyue Wu, Qingmin Liao, Fei Gao, Yu Wang, Chao Yu

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end self-play reinforcement learning system for aerial pursuit and evasion in which the policy maps onboard state directly to collective thrust and body rates, skipping intermediate trajectory generation. The work integrates agile low-level control, competitive policy optimization and sim-to-real transfer in one framework.

entry.title: ATLAS: Discovering Agent Strategies through LLM-Guided Abstraction and Automata Learning

author.name: Ignacio D. Lopez-Miguel, Andreas Happe, J\"urgen Cito, Ezio Bartocci, Bettina K\"onighofer, Martin Tappler

entry.summary: Recovers interpretable finite-state models of LLM agent behavior by combining trace abstraction with automata learning over recorded agent-environment trajectories. The goal is to move agent evaluation beyond pass rates and raw logs toward explicit, human-inspectable strategy models for tasks like software testing and penetration testing.

entry.title: Envs-FORGE: Frontier-Optimized Reward-Grounded Environment Synthesis for Agent RL

author.name: Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Honghao Liu, Xueyuan Lin, Zhichao Shi, Hao Zhou, Xuhui Jiang, Chengjin Xu, Jia Li, Jian Guo

entry.summary: Turns environment synthesis for terminal-agent reinforcement learning into an adaptive policy: seed pass rates are estimated, six generation actions are scored against a target learning frontier, and a per-seed mixed-integer program selects which action conditions the synthesis of instruction, fixtures and verifier. This replaces fixed prompting recipes that treat every seed identically.

entry.title: When Personal Memory Has No Single Answer: Evaluating LLM Agents under Irreducible Conflict

author.name: Lu Yang, Shusheng Xu, Zhuoran Li, Tongkai Yang, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Introduces TANGLE, a benchmark for cases where an agent's stored personal memories genuinely conflict and no single answer is recoverable because context, timing, or source authority is missing. Rather than scoring which memory an agent picks, it evaluates whether agents recognize underdetermination, preserve alternatives, seek missing information, and act appropriately.

entry.title: QuaSAR: Quantization Compensation via Stable Activation-Aware Rank Truncation

author.name: Lin-Fa Lee, Yi-Yu Chang, Kuo-Hei Yeh

entry.summary: Shows that popular training-free post-training quantization methods that gate layer compensation by goodness-of-fit misfire at 4-bit weights and activations, because rank-deficient activations make the closed-form solver numerically unstable and produce spuriously negative fit scores. The authors propose stable activation-aware rank truncation to separate genuine unpredictability from solver failure. This is a precise numerical diagnosis with direct implications for low-bit deployment quality.

entry.title: PACE-Bench: Benchmarking Physics Adaptation via Code Evolution in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Yuhao Zhan, Bingxiang He, Zecong Tang, Chaojun Xiao

entry.summary: PACE-Bench evaluates self-evolving agents on 144 source-to-target pairs across six simulated physics domains, where a code solution that works in the source environment breaks after a physics mutation and must be repaired using sandbox diagnostics within a limited attempt budget. Ten self-evolving methods from four families are compared. It probes adaptation and recovery rather than optimization under fixed conditions, which most agent evaluations assume.

entry.title: Participatory Moral AI Is Not Neutral: The Invisible Hand of Developers

author.name: Taenyun Kim, Edyta Bogucka, Daniele Quercia

entry.summary: The authors show that participatory moral preference elicitation is not value-neutral because developers pre-select which features get voted on, who votes, and how questions are framed, and they demonstrate empirically that each choice shifts the resulting aggregate policy. They call for documenting these decisions as normative rather than technical. This complicates the common proposal to democratically train value-aligned models via public preference polling.

entry.title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems

author.name: Zhaoyan Sun, Xiaoxiao Wang, Guoliang Li

entry.summary: This paper reinterprets database ACID guarantees for LLM agents operating on persistent environments, defining semantic atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability so multi-step agent workflows can be rolled back, kept consistent, and safely run concurrently. It proposes a framework for transactional agent execution over workspaces and tools. The framing imports decades of systems reliability thinking into agent design.

entry.title: The Query Knows What to Forget: A Second Erase Direction for Linear Attention

author.name: Dhruman Gupta, Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: Observes that delta-rule linear attention derives its erase vector from the current key while read interference is actually measured through the query, then adds a second query-derived erase direction orthogonal to the key. The change is argued to reduce state interference and improve long-context retrieval in gated linear attention models.

entry.title: KV Cache Compression Through the Lens of Transform Coding

author.name: Hannah Laus, Claudio Mayrink Verdun, Hao Wang, Flavio du Pin Calmon, Felix Krahmer

entry.summary: Analyzes key-value cache quantization through rate-distortion theory, proving that under a white-noise model the attention-aware distortion decomposes additively across keys, values, tokens, and channels, then allocates bits using transform coding and reverse water-filling. This replaces the usual objective of minimizing cache reconstruction error with one that accounts for how error propagates through attention.

entry.title: HERMES: a multi-agent framework for structured knowledge extraction from ultra-long documents in geoscience

author.name: Ziqi Song, Zongyuan Xiang, James G. Ogg, Bruce S. Lieberman, Gabi Ogg, Natalia L\'opez Carranza, Wen Du, Yufei Ye, Shuan Li, Zhong Peng, Shaoqi Yu, Juye Wei, Ying Zhou, Jieping Ye, Jiang Yang

entry.summary: A multi-agent LLM framework for extracting structured data from ultra-long scientific monographs, integrating domain constraints, validation rules and evidence tracing over parsed text, tables, figures and captions. Applied to a 55-volume paleontology treatise, it produced a public database of over 32,000 taxonomic entities and roughly 452,000 attributes.

entry.title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning

author.name: Anna Borisiuk, Andrey Savchenko, Alexander Panchenko, Elena Tutubalina

entry.summary: Observes that facts memorized more strongly during pretraining, proxied by popularity signals such as Wikidata sitelinks, resist unlearning more than rare facts, yet standard methods apply uniform gradient pressure. The proposed method scales per-fact forgetting strength by popularity and auto-balances forget and retain objectives with a dual-ascent controller, reportedly leaking far less under paraphrased and adversarial probes.

entry.title: Limitations of Synthetic Data Generation in Specialized Data-Scarce Domains

author.name: Edward Zhang, Marcel Hussing, Tanay Tandon, Shenbagaraj Kannapiran, Jason Hughes, Youkang Wang, Joshua Caswell, Agelos Kratimenos, Yi Fan Li, Milan Manoj, Ethan Sanchez, Sumukh Shrote, Camillo Jose Taylor, Daniel A. Hashimoto, Eric Eaton

entry.summary: Evaluates whether diffusion-based synthetic image generation actually helps in sparse, high-variance real-world domains, using five trauma classification tasks with subject-wise splits and comparing distribution-modeling and sample-perturbation approaches against non-generative augmentation baselines. The findings caution against extrapolating ImageNet-style synthetic data successes to specialized data-scarce settings.

entry.title: ARC: Fair Relative Advantage Comparison in Open-Ended Real-World Interaction

author.name: Yongqi Tong, Tan Li Hui Faith, Choy Zhen Wen Marcus, Zhou Jin, Kewei Fu, Jiang-Ming Yang, Jianshe Li, Xin Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies a fairness problem in group-based RL for open-ended interaction: when rollouts in a group adopt different valid strategies (answering directly, clarifying, confirming), reward-model style preferences distort relative advantages and push the policy toward reward-preferred rather than context-appropriate behavior. The proposed fix conditions rollout grouping on strategy so comparisons stay behaviorally matched.

entry.title: Evolve Vision-Language-Action Model into an Agent with On-the-fly Tool-use

author.name: Yi Ding, Yanzhao Yu, Xili Dai, Xianbiao Qi, Peiwen Sun, Xueqian Wang, Xiangyu Yue, Jianan Wang

entry.summary: ART tunes existing vision-language-action models to call off-the-shelf tool modules for low-level vision, affordance estimation, and embodiment support, shrinking the continuous action solution space the policy must cover directly. The authors build 30K tool-use trajectories and argue for better generalization with far less demonstration data. It merges agentic tool use with end-to-end robot policies.

entry.title: Reaction-Transformation-Aware Flow Matching for Generalizable Transition State Generation

author.name: Kaipeng Zeng, Wenxi Zhai, Shengrui Xu, Jie Zhao, Bowen Li, Shiyue Wang, Junchi Yan, Tong Zhu

entry.summary: TransTS generates chemical transition-state structures from atom-mapped reactant-product pairs using flow matching that explicitly represents the bond-level transformations of an elementary reaction, rather than only learning geometric correspondence between endpoints. The goal is generalizable prediction that avoids expensive quantum saddle-point searches. Faster transition-state prediction would accelerate mechanistic chemistry and catalyst design.

entry.title: BCIJelly: An integrated ecosystem for brain-computer interface research

author.name: Liyuan Han, Xinrui Yang, Tianyu Zheng, Qizhi Yang, Yitao Qin, Liang Chen, Qinglai Wei, Binjie Hong, Xinhe Zhang, Rui Xiong, Yong Gu, Mu-ming Poo, Bo Xu, Chengyu Li, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a unified brain-computer interface research ecosystem bundling 18 curated datasets, 15 benchmark decoders, 80 reusable modules, automated architecture search, and a hardware deployment pipeline in one Python framework. An LLM-guided closed-loop mode extends the architecture search to task-specific decoder design without manual engineering.

entry.title: hint$^2$: Hierarchical World Models for Inference-Time Temporal Logic Guidance

author.name: Moritz Zoellner, Anastasios Manganaris, Ahmed H. Qureshi, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical world-model method that steers short-horizon, chunk-based manipulation policies toward satisfying long-horizon linear temporal logic specifications at inference time. This bridges the mismatch between closed-loop replanning policies and LTL constraints evaluated over full trajectories.

entry.title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model

author.name: Ziyang Luo, Zhongyao Chu, Xinjie He, Youting Wang, Xukui Qin, Runxiong Wu, Yan-Syuan Chen

entry.summary: Combines two residual-stream interventions on a frozen language model: a conditional steering probe that writes at mid-stack layers to improve reasoning accuracy, and a zero-shot sufficiency direction that reads the stream and triggers abstention when evidence is insufficient. The paper shows the write disrupts the read, costing up to 8 AUROC points, and reconciles both in a single forward pass instead of two.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Niche Multilingual Code Translation via Reinforcement Learning with Execution-Based Verifiable Supervision

author.name: Kouki Yuki, Jie Zeng, Kyoko Ogawa, Ryunosuke Ikeda, Yohei Kobashi, Takeshi Kojima, Ikuya Yamada, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Bootstraps many-to-many code translation for less common programming languages using execution-verified supervision: seed Python programs are expanded into a validated multilingual pool, candidate translations are labeled by execution outcome, and preferences train a reward model for preference-based reinforcement learning. This targets the sparse-supervision regime where models produce plausible but non-executable code.

entry.title: Reward Machines for Signal Temporal Logic

author.name: Alper Kamil Bozkurt, Shangtong Zhang, Yuichi Motai

entry.summary: Develops reward machines for signal temporal logic so that history-dependent STL robustness can be turned into Markovian reward structures suitable for reinforcement learning. This addresses the intractability that arises when STL robustness scores, which depend on execution history, are used naively as RL rewards.

entry.title: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Tianyu Fan, Chao Huang

entry.summary: Argues that agent capability is jointly determined by the model and the runtime harness that mediates context, tools, control flow, and stopping, and proposes co-evolving both in a loop: build harnesses for a fixed model, train the model on verified trajectories, then rebuild harnesses as capability changes. HELIX provides a source-traceable substrate that decomposes agent systems into typed ports and reusable components so harness edits preserve intervention identity.

entry.title: APTER: Adaptive Post-Training with Expert-Grounded Rubrics

author.name: Xukai Wang, Liangqi Li, Zhiyue Xu, Jingang Zhou, Xiaoyu Shi, Jiansheng Cai, Bo Zhang, Zhe Li, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: APTER grounds rubric-based post-training in structured expert domain knowledge so that evaluation criteria are consistent across samples rather than generated independently per query, enabling diagnosis and targeted repair of recurring capability gaps. It combines fine-grained rubric scoring with optimization and a diagnostic loop for professional-domain models. The work sits in the fast-growing rubric-as-reward line of alignment research.

entry.title: Knowing When to Stop: Bayesian Optimal Stopping for LLM Evaluations

author.name: Toby D. Pilditch

entry.summary: The optstop framework treats LLM benchmarking as sequential measurement, using hierarchical Bayesian inference to keep sampling only where per-item uncertainty remains high and to stop early where estimates are already precise. It supports binary, ordinal, and continuous outcomes and adds a safeguard for near-zero performance regimes where rare successes dominate. It offers a principled way to cut evaluation compute without inflating error bars.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yijiang Li, Yijun Liang, Yunjie Tian, Bingyang Wang, Ke Zhang, Zhenfei Yin, Di Fu, Philip Torr, Nuno Vasconcelos

entry.summary: Argues that useful teacher-student asymmetry for on-policy distillation can be created by removing information from the student rather than giving the teacher privileged access, yielding a self-supervised distillation signal with no labels, rewards, or larger teacher. If it holds up, this reduces reliance on stronger models or annotated supervision for visual reasoning improvement.

entry.title: Reflex: Enabling Fast and Predictive Vision-Language-Action Models for Reaction-Critical Manipulation

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Wanruo Zhang, Xiao Li

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of six dynamic, reaction-critical robot manipulation tasks with an evaluation harness that decouples simulator stepping from control and supports configurable inference latency, plus an efficient vision-language-action model trained without large-scale robot pretraining. Highlights that existing VLA benchmarks mostly test quasi-static generalization and hide latency effects.

entry.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

author.name: Zian Meng, Zhen Li, Chuanhao Li, Qiang Li, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Builds an interactive game world model that explicitly predicts a compact interpretable 3D world state, delegates geometry to a fixed zero-parameter renderer, and uses the neural network only to paint appearance. The split is meant to stop long-horizon drift in pose, geometry, and occlusion that plagues purely pixel-space autoregressive world models.

entry.title: Boosting Data Augmentation with Stochastic Weight Averaging

author.name: Longde Huang, Axel Flinth, Jan E. Gerken

entry.summary: Studies stochastic weight averaging as a cheap substitute for deep ensembles when using data augmentation to impose task symmetries. The authors model the late-training trajectory as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and analyze symmetry properties in the infinite-width limit.

entry.title: VoiceDesigner: Text-to-Voice Generation and Editing via Unified Diffusion Modeling and Data Augmentation

author.name: Jiarui Hai, Karan Thakkar, Ke Chen, Yunyun Wang, Jiaqi Su, Rithesh Kumar, Mounya Elhilali, Zeyu Jin

entry.summary: Proposes a unified diffusion framework for generating and editing voices from text descriptions, targeting both diverse real and fictional speaker timbres and flexible editing such as cloning and emotion or tone modification. A hybrid data augmentation pipeline addresses the scarcity of description-voice pairs.

entry.title: What preferences can - and cannot - predict in multi-agent online learning

author.name: Omar Abbadi, Rida Laraki, Panayotis Mertikopoulos

entry.summary: Investigates how far the purely ordinal preference structure of a game determines the long-run behavior of no-regret dynamics such as follow-the-regularized-leader. The authors show every dynamically stable set has a preferentially stable skeleton, and characterize when preferences alone pin down asymptotic stability.

entry.title: Beyond Text Conditioning: A Systematic Study of MLLM-DiT Fusion for Video Generation

author.name: Yanbo Ding, Yijia Fan, Caihua Shan, Yifan Yang, Yifei Shen, Weijie Wang, Xirui Hu, Dongsheng Li, Lili Qiu, Yuqing Yang, Yali Wang

entry.summary: A systematic study of how to couple a multimodal LLM with a diffusion transformer for video generation, examining what intermediate representation should bridge them, how the LLM should produce it, and how the diffusion model should consume it. Moves beyond treating the MLLM as a frozen text encoder toward using it as a semantic planner.

entry.title: Omni-LiveAvatar: Minute-Level Real-Time Streaming Joint Audio-Visual Avatar Generation

author.name: Lunjie Zhu, Xingtong Ge, Fangyu Lin, Yi Zhang, Zhening Liu, Mengfei Li, Yumeng Zhang, Guanglu Song, Yu Liu, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Distills a large bidirectional joint audio-video diffusion model into a few-step autoregressive generator so talking avatars can be streamed live for minutes rather than short clips, with a synchronized long and short term memory to prevent drift. Claims a first for minute-scale real-time joint audio-visual avatar generation.

entry.title: Mandato: Protocol-Level Enforcement of Digitally Signed Mandates on AI Agent Actions with Cryptographically Chained Audit Trails

author.name: Giovanni Racioppi

entry.summary: Presents Mandato, a proxy that sits in front of tool-calling protocols such as MCP and enforces cryptographically signed mandates specifying which tools an agent may call, with what parameters, for how long, and on whose authority, producing chained tamper-evident audit logs. It moves agent authorization out of application code into a verifiable infrastructure layer. This is infrastructure for agent accountability and delegated authority.

entry.title: Engineering Reliable Coding Agents: Evaluating and Operating the System Around the Model

author.name: Stephanie Jarmak

entry.summary: This monograph argues that coding agents are evaluated as models but deployed as systems, and synthesizes 164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, and 17 system case records to show that many apparent model failures originate in the harness, execution state, retrieval, memory, permissions, or resource allocation. It proposes a framework for evaluating and operating agents at the system level. The systems framing complements benchmark-centric research.

entry.title: From Fixed Grids to Moving Particles:A Transferable Latent Operator for Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Meng Li, Chuqi Chen, Zhengqing Gao, Xi Zhou, Xiao Sun, Yang Xiang, Huaxi Huang

entry.summary: The Transferable Latent Operator learns a shared latent flow representation that allows a model trained only on Eulerian field data to perform zero-shot Lagrangian particle rollouts without any particle-level supervision or task-specific adaptation. This addresses the scarcity of Lagrangian trajectory data relative to gridded fields. Cross-representation transfer is an unusual and useful capability for neural PDE surrogates.

entry.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Haonan He, Haodi Lei, Yun Luo, Haoran Zhang, Shunkai Zhang, Yizhuo Li, Shengji Tang, Zhilin Wang, Runzhe Zhan, Lei Bai, Ganqu Cui, Fangchen Yu, Yafu Li, Peng Ye, Ning Ding, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Tackles the engineering obstacles of on-policy distillation when teacher and student differ in tokenizer and context length, aligning only tokens that span identical text and controlling response-length explosion and instability. Demonstrated by transferring proof-style reasoning from a long-context teacher into short-context students.

entry.title: Batch-wise Adaptive Pruning: Periodic Neuron Activation-Aware Weight Pruning for Language Reasoning Model

author.name: Yongmin Kim, Shota Takashiro, Yusuke Iwasawa, Takeshi Kojima, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Shows that training-free activation-aware pruning methods for reasoning models break under batched inference because a shared mask forces activation aggregation, which invalidates offline-calibrated thresholds and causes sparsity drift and accuracy collapse. The paper proposes a periodic, batch-aware adaptive pruning scheme that restores reasoning accuracy in the throughput-oriented regime.

entry.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations

author.name: Arwa Osman, Marco Baroni, Iuri Macocco

entry.summary: Shows that intrinsic dimensionality estimates of language model representations depend systematically on how many unique final tokens a probing dataset contains, with a reversal between low and high lexical diversity regimes. The authors derive an exact parameter-free formula for the crossover point, implying that many published ID comparisons may reflect dataset construction rather than linguistic properties.

entry.title: Evaluating Agentic Learning Harness Capabilities Without Labels via the Scaling Hypothesis

author.name: Aryan Luthra, Kshitij Jain, Siddharth Arya, Bobby Filar, Anna Bertiger

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating continual-learning agent harnesses (LLM plus retrieval or memory that improve from feedback without retraining) without labeled benchmarks, by leveraging scaling-hypothesis style reasoning instead of a judge model. Motivated by cybersecurity operations where labels are scarce, stale, and unrepresentative.

entry.title: BiasTrace: Linking Reasoning Behaviours to Biased Outputs in LLMs

author.name: Varsha Ramineni, Hossein A. Rahmani, Jerome Ramos, Karin Sevegnani, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: Introduces an annotation scheme for labeling reasoning behaviors inside model-generated chains of thought and linking those behaviors to biased final outputs, moving bias analysis from outputs to process. The aim is to identify which reasoning patterns, not just which words, drive discriminatory inferences. It connects reasoning-trace analysis with fairness evaluation.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Inflation-Aware Routing for Agentic LLM Systems

author.name: Heming Fu, Shan Lin, Qianqian Xie, Guojun Xiong

entry.summary: The authors define token inflation as the ratio between the true cost of an agentic workflow including retries and the naive single-call cost, measuring inflation up to roughly four times for a small model on multi-hop QA. Their InflationAgent router uses these measurements plus branch-aware chain-of-thought handling to route queries by real expected cost rather than per-token price. It corrects a systematic underestimation in cascade routers like FrugalGPT.

entry.title: Training-Free Knowledge Transfer Across Model Scales through Activation-Guided Pruning

author.name: Jiahe Fan, Si Chen, Yinghao Hou, Aiyuan Zhang, Hong Xie

entry.summary: Activation-Prune-Merge transfers capability from a large donor model into a smaller recipient without training, by building task-conditioned activation maps on the donor, selecting salient layers, hidden dimensions, and attention heads, and merging the pruned donor slice into the recipient. It explores cross-scale heterogeneous fusion where neuron-wise semantic alignment is impossible. The result would be a cheap alternative to distillation if it holds broadly.

entry.title: MedClaw: Heuristic Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Surgical Video Reasoning

author.name: Yingying Fan, Penghui Du, Leyan Zhu, Runze He, Zimeng Wu, Yuxuan Zhang, Liang Chen, Jiahao Xie, Jiangtang Wang, Shuai Shao, Anchao Yang, Yutong Bai, Yan Wang

entry.summary: MedClaw handles tens-of-minutes surgical videos by separating a text-only orchestrator that plans which evidence to collect from perception tools that answer localized visual queries, improving by evolving context instead of training weights. This avoids both context-window compression of the full procedure and the data hunger of trained video agents. It targets long-horizon temporal reasoning about before, after, and across-stage questions.

entry.title: Consistent Model Chasing Is Minimax Optimal: The Exact Value of Scalar Adversarial Adaptive Control under Large Parametric Uncertainty

author.name: Dimitar Ho

entry.summary: Solves exactly the minimax value of a scalar adaptive control game where the unknown pole can be arbitrarily large and disturbances are adversarial and bounded. The paper shows that consistent model chasing achieves the exact optimal worst-case peak deviation, giving a value where prior theory offered only stability certificates and regret rates.

entry.title: Pairton: Iterative Reconstruction of Short-Lived Particles

author.name: Andreas Hermansen, Chris Scheulen, Tobias Golling

entry.summary: Formulates reconstruction of short-lived particles at colliders as iterative masked prediction over a graph, predicting edges of an adjacency matrix that encodes decay relationships. Using a pairformer-style architecture with dynamically updated pairwise representations, it reports state-of-the-art results on fully hadronic top pair decays.

entry.title: Conditional Neural Optimal Transport for Predicting Cellular Phenotypes from Molecular Structure

author.name: Gauthier Avit\'e, Maxime Sanchez-Renauld, Nicolas Bourriez, Auguste Genovesio

entry.summary: Casts prediction of molecule-induced cellular phenotypes in high-content microscopy as an inductive conditional optimal transport problem from control-cell image representations to treated-cell distributions. Classical static optimal transport baselines fail at scale, motivating a conditional neural transport model that generalizes to unseen compounds.

entry.title: ChartProbe: A Diagnostic Study on Visual Reasoning through Perception, Grounding, and Simple Reasoning

author.name: Mahsa Khoshnoodi, Sarah Adel Bargal

entry.summary: A diagnostic benchmark that decomposes chart question answering into perception, grounding of elements to labels, and single-step computation, with probes generated automatically from the rendering code so gold answers are exact and require no human labeling. It tests whether vision-language model chart failures really stem from reasoning or from these more basic skills.

entry.title: AI Evaluation Should Work With Humans

author.name: Jan Kulveit, Gavin Leech, Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: A short position paper arguing that benchmarking superhuman autonomous performance implicitly steers development toward replacing humans, and that the field should instead evaluate human-AI team performance. The authors claim this reframing would push toward complementary systems and better societal outcomes.

entry.title: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In?

author.name: Alireza Kargarzadeh, Nariman Khaledian, Navid Parvini, Sid Ghatak, Arman Khaledian

entry.summary: Uses an LLM teacher distilled into a compact classifier via active learning to tag 4.57 million financial news articles with event types and attributes, clusters them into stories, and measures abnormal returns before, at, and after publication. The study tests the folk claims that news is already priced in and that traders buy rumor and sell news across roughly 3,000 US stocks. It is a large-scale empirical market-microstructure study enabled by LLM-based annotation.

entry.title: A Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning Framework for Structured Drift Diagnosis and Recovery in Autonomous LLM Agents

author.name: Ismail El Hamraoui, Sagar Jose, Nicolas Bureau, Robert Plana

entry.summary: Introduces a plug-and-play module for detecting and recovering from behavioral drift in autonomous LLM agents, where a small language model is RL-trained to specialize at each node of a recovery graph handling step-level detection, risk assessment, and recovery choice. The design assumes the main task agent is too large and expensive to retrain, so supervision is externalized. It is aimed at preventing irreversible side effects in deployed agent workflows.

entry.title: AnchorBench: A Multi-Pathway Benchmark for the Anchoring Effect in LLMs

author.name: Yiderigun Borjigin, Alexander Hermann, Christian Cyron, Roland Aydin

entry.summary: AnchorBench evaluates the anchoring cognitive bias in LLMs across multiple anchor delivery pathways and explicitly separates irrelevant anchors from plausible ones, testing ten open-weight and four frontier API models. It finds anchoring effects are strong and pathway-dependent rather than uniform. This gives a more discriminating picture than prior narrow anchoring studies.

entry.title: Concept Guidance: Precise, Training-Free Latent Control for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Nikolai R\"ohrich, Isabell Hans, Felix Krause, Bj\"orn Ommer

entry.summary: Introduces a concept-wise mutual information analysis showing that different diffusion network layers specialize in different generated structures, then exploits this with a training-free guidance method that amplifies concept-relevant layers. This enables continuous control of attributes like aesthetic quality and better local coherence for hard cases such as text and hands.

entry.title: Training Fair Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Patrik Kenfack, Jesse C. Cresswell, Anthony L. Caterini, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou, Ulrich A\"ivodji

entry.summary: Bakes group-fairness constraints directly into the pretraining of tabular foundation models so that fair predictions emerge from a single in-context forward pass, using synthetic fairness tasks and a fairness-aware architecture. Addresses the practical problem that sensitive attributes are often unavailable and that standard fairness post-processing does not fit in-context learning.

entry.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding

author.name: Zewen Jin, Shen Fu, Zeping Duan, Shannon Wang, Weihao Wu, Chengjie Tang, Congkun Ai, Ping Gong, Zijian Dai, Youhui Bai, Cheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts architecture optimized for small-batch decoding, where inference is memory-bound and dominated by loading expert weights rather than compute. Aims to cut latency for interactive assistants without the accuracy loss of aggressive weight compression or the overhead of very fine-grained expert designs.

entry.title: Detecting Contaminated Code-Generation Prompt Batches via Influence Functions

author.name: Francesco Quinzan, Noor Munir, Yishun Lu, Stephen Roberts

entry.summary: Proposes a threat-model-agnostic detector that uses influence functions to flag batches of coding prompts whose generated outputs exert anomalous parameter-space influence relative to a benign reference distribution, rather than matching known vulnerability signatures. Introduces benchmark datasets for evaluating detection of prompts that elicit insecure code.

entry.title: Catching the Imposter: Self-Supervised Learning of Physical Coherence with Cross-Entity Feature Permutations

author.name: Aleksei Rozanov, Arvind Renganathan, Vipin Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces a self-supervised pretext task in which some of an entity's features are swapped with real values donated by a different entity, forcing the encoder to detect physically incoherent combinations. Evaluated on ERA5-Land reanalysis with 21 environmental variables across seven downstream climate and carbon-flux tasks.

entry.title: No Universal Signal Predicts Sample-Level LLM Regression under Version Updates

author.name: Jia Sheng, Yiwei Lu

entry.summary: Tests whether any inference-time signal can predict sample-level regressions when a model is upgraded to a newer version, comparing single-model signals like confidence and logit margin against cross-version signals like output KL divergence and representation drift. Across six benchmarks the finding is negative: no signal reliably adds value over a plain confidence baseline.

entry.title: Attributing Preprocessing Invariance in Spectral Foundation Models

author.name: Dongjun Wei, Hongyi Wu, Yinuo Zou

entry.summary: Argues that apparent preprocessing invariance in spectral foundation models can be an artifact of input normalization rather than learned robustness, since self-statistic normalization can map differently preprocessed spectra to identical vectors before any learned parameter acts. Using a Raman foundation model as a case study, the authors give conditions under which invariance is trivially guaranteed. It is a methodological correction to how invariance claims are evaluated.

entry.title: Reading Between The Lines: Modeling and Evaluating Behavioral Realism in Legal Simulation

author.name: Divya Vetticaden, Arya Gupta, Julian Nyarko, Megan Ma

entry.summary: WitnessSim simulates deposition witnesses with controllable legal personas and evaluates them along two separate axes, behavioral realism (via adversarial probing, blinded attorney comparison, and longitudinal trajectories) and pedagogical usefulness for attorney training. Attorneys did not systematically prefer real over simulated testimony, and witness behavior shifted meaningfully with question form. It shows legal AI evaluation needs behavioral realism metrics beyond factual accuracy.

entry.title: PPAPlace: Differentiable Cross-Stage Objectives for Chip Placement Optimization

author.name: Ruogu Chen, Jie Han

entry.summary: PPAPlace attacks the observation that half-perimeter wirelength, the standard placement objective, correlates near-zero with post-route timing outcomes, and that evaluated AI placers therefore degraded performance, power, and area relative to hierarchical baselines. The authors study label fidelity across four design-flow stages and build differentiable cross-stage objectives that align optimization with post-route metrics. It addresses the objective-mismatch problem head-on in AI for chip design.

entry.title: Overcoming Shortcut Learning in Graph Neural Networks through Active Explanation Guidance

author.name: Taraneh Younesian, Steve Azzolin, Antonio Longa, Francesco Ferrini, Vincenzo Marco De Luca, Stefano Teso

entry.summary: XIGL is an architecture-agnostic human-in-the-loop procedure that detects graph neural network reliance on non-causal shortcuts by inspecting explanations, then collects targeted corrective feedback from expert users to deconfound the model, with query strategies designed to limit expensive annotation. It links explainability directly to model correction rather than passive inspection. The aim is better out-of-distribution reliability.

entry.title: Whose doctor does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in large language model-assisted physician choice

author.name: Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig

entry.summary: Runs a prespecified randomized audit of how seven language models pick among synthetic physician profiles, varying reputation signals and name-implied gender and ethnicity across thousands of choice sets and tens of thousands of scored responses. Frames assistants as infomediaries whose recommendations silently determine which professionals become visible.

entry.title: When Denoising Hurts: Rethinking the Terminal Step of Diffusion Time Series Forecasters -- Extended Version

author.name: Dat Nguyen-Cong, Luong Tran, Tung Kieu

entry.summary: Empirically finds that diffusion-based time-series forecasters recover useful temporal structure at relatively high noise levels while continued low-noise denoising can introduce drift and worsen forecasts, contradicting the assumption that more refinement is always better. Proposes a label-free criterion for stopping the reverse process early and argues this explains prior narrow architecture and schedule choices.

entry.title: Unknown Unknowns: Model Misspecification in Machine Learning for Physics

author.name: Juan Cruz-Martinez, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro, Alexander Held, Michael Kagan

entry.summary: A perspective piece on model misspecification when machine learning models trained on simulations are deployed on real particle physics and astronomy data. It frames the goal as absorbing nuisance misspecification while preserving sensitivity to the anomalies that would constitute discoveries.

entry.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit

author.name: Fengming Liu

entry.summary: Uses six million Reddit comments from cross-partisan forums between 2019 and 2025 to document an ideologically asymmetric interruption in the diversification of political discourse beginning around late 2022, affecting conservative but not progressive users. A permutation test over thousands of candidate cutoff dates shows the change builds gradually rather than breaking sharply at the chatbot launch date, and a continuous LLM exposure index is used instead.

entry.title: Algorithm Design and Physician Liability

author.name: Shujie Luan, Shubhranshu Singh, Tinglong Dai

entry.summary: An analytical economics model of how a new liability rule that holds providers responsible for relying on algorithms with disparate group accuracy changes both an AI vendor's design incentives and a physician's decision to use the tool. It explores whether liability pressure actually improves accuracy for disadvantaged groups given asymmetric improvement costs.

entry.title: Simulation-Aware In-Context Policy Improvement for LLM-Aided Analog Layout Refinement

author.name: Bingyang Liu, Ziming Wei, Xiaohan Gao, David Z. Pan

entry.summary: Uses an LLM to improve sample efficiency in analog integrated circuit layout parameter tuning, where each evaluation requires costly parasitic extraction and post-layout simulation that makes Bayesian optimization impractical. The approach performs simulation-aware in-context policy improvement so the model refines its tuning strategy from observed simulation feedback.

entry.title: Removing Temporal Note Redundancy Improves Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Medicine

author.name: Chenran Weng, Joo Seung Lee, Malini Mahendra, Anil Aswani

entry.summary: Shows that clinical free-text notes used in RL state representations for mechanical ventilation are dominated by copy-forward and templated redundancy, which dilutes genuinely new information, and proposes a redundancy-aware multimodal state representation to fix this. The approach combines structured EHR data with de-duplicated temporal note signals for sequential ventilator decisions. It addresses a specific and underappreciated data pathology in clinical RL.

entry.title: Measuring Fairness in Large Audio Language Models via Semantic-Aware Bias Estimation

author.name: Zhe Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semantic-aware mixed-effects regression framework for measuring demographic bias in large audio language models, incorporating sentence-level semantic embeddings of the reference text as covariates and treating speaker identity as a random effect. The goal is to prevent content and speaker confounds from being misread as demographic bias. It is a measurement-methodology contribution for spoken-input fairness audits.

entry.title: Engineering Signals of Human-AI Collaboration in the Agentic Coding Era: A Longitudinal Analysis of 33,228 Pull Requests from vLLM and SGLang with Implications for Biomedical AI Agents and Bioinformatics Pipeline Developmen

author.name: Jiada Li, Xuesong Ye, Olamide Olowoniyi

entry.summary: This longitudinal study computes seven engineering metrics across 33,228 merged pull requests in two high-velocity AI infrastructure repositories, segmenting development into eras aligned with major shifts in AI-assisted coding to describe changes in throughput, cycle time, review density, contributor diversity, and PR size. It offers empirical team-level evidence about how agentic coding is reshaping open-source workflows. Conclusions are descriptive rather than causal.

entry.title: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions

author.name: Xiaokai Yan, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and framework for proactive mobile GUI agents that must infer user intent from action histories, not just execute given instructions, with roughly 72k intentions and 700k actions across 52 apps. It shifts agent evaluation from reactive task completion toward understanding, prediction, and execution of latent user goals.

entry.title: Seeing Red, Thinking Bad: Color Bias in Vision Language Models

author.name: Kohsuke Ide, Ryousuke Yamada, Yoshihiro Fukuhara, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Yutaka Satoh

entry.summary: Shows that vision-language models reading text rendered as images can be swayed by purely cosmetic styling changes such as color and contrast, using stealth visual prompts that preserve semantics. Also probes how these perturbations shift vision-encoder representations, raising concerns for VLM use in screening and recommendation.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Discovery and Construction of a Counterexample to the Convergence of Three-Block ADMM with the Identity Matrix as its Third Constraint Block

author.name: Kenan Xu, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: Uses AI assistance to discover and then rigorously construct a counterexample showing that direct three-block ADMM can diverge even when the third constraint block is the identity matrix, closing a previously open subcase in optimization theory. The result is a negative answer with a human-verified construction.

entry.title: The Integer Alibi: Localizing Cross-Kernel Divergence in INT8-Quantized LLM Inference

author.name: Teng-Ruei Chen

entry.summary: Shows that swapping only the INT8 matrix-multiply kernel inside a serving stack, with checkpoint, prompts, hardware, and decoding held fixed, produces generations that never match between the two implementations, even though each is bitwise reproducible on its own. Because exact integer accumulation cannot explain the divergence, the paper localizes the cause elsewhere in the quantized pipeline.

entry.title: CytoBERT: A Foundation Model for Cytometry Data

author.name: Syed Abdul Haseeb Qadri, Bjarne C. Hiller, Felix Blanke, Vanja Sophie Cangalovic, Kutalm{\i}\c{s} Co\c{s}kun, Amin Mirzaei, Tom Siegl, Sebastian Bader, Thomas Kirste, Martin Becker

entry.summary: Presents an open-weight transformer foundation model for single-cell cytometry data, designed to handle the heterogeneous panels and unstandardized protocols that block transfer across studies. The release includes public weights and code for a domain with few existing foundation models.

entry.title: Emergent Models: Intelligence from Tiny Substrates

author.name: Giacomo Bocchese, Nicola Giacobbo, Etienne Guichard, James Wiles, Akshaj Devireddy

entry.summary: Proposes a paradigm in which models are simple open-ended substrates such as cellular automata that iterate a fixed local rule for an adaptive number of steps, trained by evolutionary search, with an interface mapping latent state to inputs and outputs. The hypothesis is that such substrates are biased toward learning the underlying generating rule and thus extrapolate beyond training ranges.

entry.title: Offline Deep Q* Estimation with Diffusion Models

author.name: Xiaohong Chen, Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Chen Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling operator estimation from value learning in offline reinforcement learning by first fitting conditional diffusion models for the reward law and transition kernel, then plugging these into the optimal Bellman equation to estimate the optimal action-value function. This yields a data-driven approximation of an operator that is otherwise unobservable from logged data.

entry.title: Generation-Powered Inference for Distribution-Valued Outcomes

author.name: Yijiao Zhang, Hongzhe Li

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for valid statistical inference on distribution-valued quantities such as Wasserstein barycenters when an imperfect generative model supplies auxiliary predictions, for example predicted single-cell responses to perturbations. Gains efficiency from the generative model without assuming it is correct.

entry.title: Program-space Diffusion for Morphology-to-Transcriptomics Prediction

author.name: Ruyter Swann, Dorent Reuben, Racoceanu Daniel

entry.summary: Reframes predicting spatial gene expression from histology images as conditional diffusion in the space of transcriptional programs rather than independent per-gene regression, exploiting coordinated expression structure. This also sidesteps inconsistent gene-selection protocols that make cross-method comparison unfair. It could reduce reliance on expensive spatial transcriptomics assays.

entry.title: SheetCompass: Hierarchical Relation Graphs for Agentic Spreadsheet Reasoning

author.name: Panjing He, Mingyue Cheng, Yucong Luo, Li Li, Xiaohan Zhang

entry.summary: SheetCompass builds explicit hierarchical relation graphs over workbooks so an agent can reason about cross-sheet associations, column dependencies, and spatial layout instead of flattening spreadsheets into token sequences. Memory-driven agentic execution then performs analysis and automation tasks. It targets a common enterprise use case where structure loss is the dominant failure cause.

entry.title: HAM-RAG: Hierarchy-Aware Multimodal RAG for Structure-Faithful Interleaved Generation

author.name: Yin Li, Ziyang Hu, Zhiyu Guo, Xiangyu Liu, Wenbin Li, Boo-Ho Yang, Rav Lawana, Ziyue Li, Wei Zeng, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: HAM-RAG preserves document hierarchy as a grounding signal through both retrieval and generation so that interleaved text-and-image outputs keep source organization and local text-image relations, instead of flattening documents into isolated units. The authors release HAM-Bench spanning game walkthroughs, web pages, scientific papers, and recipes. Gains are reported across multiple backbones.

entry.title: SPARGen: Unifying Spatial Perception and Reasoning through Native Multimodal Generation

author.name: Jinsheng Quan, Jianhua Li, Siyi Xie, Xuanke Shi, Kewang Deng, Zukai Chen, Feifei Shao, Lei Yang, Quan Wang, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: Presents a unified multimodal model that recasts 3D reconstruction, dense correspondence, and spatial reasoning as instruction-conditioned generation, mixing token sequences for structured or linguistic outputs with image-aligned dense geometric fields. The goal is shared spatial supervision so that geometry and language reasoning reinforce each other instead of living in separate task-specific modules.

entry.title: GALA: Generation-Aware Cross-Modal Alignment for Text-to-Time-Series Synthesis

author.name: Haochen Zhang, Gengwei Zhang, Laura Yao, Nicholas Knoz, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage method for generating time series from natural language that first contrastively aligns a pretrained text encoder with a time-series foundation model into a shared space, then uses the aligned conditioning for generation. The motivation is that existing text-conditioned generators never deliberately match the conditioning representation to the signal modality.

entry.title: Online Inference in Distributional Temporal-Difference Learning

author.name: Yang Peng, Liangyu Zhang

entry.summary: Develops online statistical inference for functionals of the return distribution estimated by nonparametric distributional temporal-difference learning from a single trajectory. The paper establishes a functional central limit theorem in Cramer space for the averaged estimator and validates bootstrap inference for smooth functionals such as variance, CVaR and expectiles.

entry.title: Information Satisfaction: A Reader-Centered Axis for Summarization Evaluation

author.name: Isabel Cachola, William Walden, Reno Kriz, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: Argues that summarization metrics measuring general quality or specific properties miss whether a summary is useful to a particular reader, and proposes a reader-centered evaluation axis based on stable personas such as role and expertise rather than one-off queries. A biomedical researcher and a family physician need different summaries of the same article.

entry.title: CAST: Closed-form Analytic Semantic Transfer for Zero-Shot Classifier Extension

author.name: William Heyden, Habib Ullah, Muhammad Salman Siddiqui, Fadi Al Machot

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free and image-free way to extend a pretrained classifier to unseen classes by injecting weights derived in closed form from semantic descriptions. The paper supplies a finite-sample error decomposition that isolates a semantic extrapolation residual quantifying when the transfer should succeed.

entry.title: Attention Capture Is Not Detection: A Two-Stage Account of How Humans Miss Localized AI Image Edits

author.name: Chiao-Chieh Deng

entry.summary: An eye-tracking study with 59 participants shows that noticing a localized AI image edit and correctly judging it as fake are separable stages driven by different factors: edit area governs whether the gaze is captured, while semantic plausibility governs judgment accuracy and look-but-fail-to-see errors. This challenges the platform assumption that detectability is a single property warranting a binary warning.

entry.title: OpenBelief-Nav: Evidence-Preserving Object Memory for Open-Vocabulary Language-Guided Navigation

author.name: Dinh Tuan Nguyen, Anh Dao, Phuong Nam Dang, Quan-Dung Pham, Tuyen P. Le, Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes an object memory for language-guided navigation that keeps observation-level phrases, reliability cues and frame-mask provenance instead of collapsing each mapped object into a single fused feature or committed label. Related phrases are consolidated into a vocabulary-independent belief supporting both fixed-vocabulary projection and free-form retrieval, evaluated on ScanNet200 and Replica scenes.

entry.title: Your Probabilistic JEPA Is Secretly a Hidden Markov Model: A State-Space Interpretation of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning

author.name: Yongchao Huang

entry.summary: Argues that a probabilistic, time-indexed version of video JEPA with a predictive information bottleneck has the same computational structure as a hidden Markov model, mapping the context encoder to filtering, the predictor to latent dynamics, and the decoder to emission. It defines four levels of correspondence with conditions for exact sequence-level equivalence and proposes a concrete Markov-chain variant.

entry.title: Learning to Assemble Novel Structures with Unfamiliar Parts under Semantic Constraints

author.name: Jonghyuk Park, Alex Lascarides, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: Presents a neurosymbolic agent that learns to assemble novel structures from unfamiliar parts when the relevant semantic constraints and part concepts were unavailable during training, acquiring them through embodied dialogue and demonstrations. Experiments use a simulated toy truck assembly domain combining natural-language symbolic evidence with dense visual input.

entry.title: MACS: A Hybrid Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable Conversational E-Commerce Recommendation

author.name: Juli Huang, Hannah Clay, Sajjad Beygi, Thomas Sarda, Negin Golrezaei, Amin Saberi

entry.summary: MACS is a hybrid multi-agent conversational recommender for merchants who require that suggestions come only from a fixed catalog with no web search or unsupported product claims, using LLMs for language-facing interpretation and preference elicitation while delegating constraint satisfaction and inventory grounding to non-LLM components. Multi-turn preference persistence is a core requirement. The design is aimed at reliability under hard commercial constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Model Merging

author.name: Utkarsh Agarwal, Vamshi Bonagiri, Raul Astudillo, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: Frames the choice of model-merging hyperparameters as an expensive black-box multi-objective problem and applies multi-objective Bayesian optimization to approximate the tradeoff frontier under a small evaluation budget. Tested with several merge operators on mid-size Qwen and Llama models across instruction, math, and code capabilities.

entry.title: Stochastic Control Policies for Robust Molecular Transition Path Sampling

author.name: Jingqian Liu, Yu-Hsiang Wang, Yanru Qu, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Reframes rollout-based learned control for molecular transition path sampling as learning a proposal distribution in path space, aiming to fix the instability and strong seed dependence reported for existing control-force methods. Keeps underlying molecular dynamics intact so sampled trajectories remain physically plausible.

entry.title: MedMix: Specialization-Consistent Federated Sparse MoEs under Modality Heterogeneity

author.name: Adiba Orzikulova, Dong Min Kim, Jaehong Yoon, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: Studies sparse mixture-of-experts models in federated medical learning where clients differ in which modalities they possess and individual records have different missing-modality subsets, showing that locally learned routing diverges and pushes experts toward incompatible specializations. Proposes a specialization-consistent scheme to keep expert roles aligned across clients.

entry.title: Quantum Multi-Armed Bandits and Linear Bandits: Lower Bounds and Algorithms

author.name: Maoli Liu, Zhuohua Li, John C. S. Lui

entry.summary: Establishes the first minimax regret lower bounds for quantum multi-armed and finite-action linear bandits under a quantum reward oracle model, showing logarithmic dependence on horizon is unavoidable and resolving an open question about horizon-independent regret. Also tightens dimension dependence relative to prior algorithms.

entry.title: SPEAR: Structure Property Explainability with Attention Regularization

author.name: Aditya Raghavan, Utkarsh Pratiush, Dalton A. Pearl, Jade Holliman Jr, Katharine Page, Philip D Rack, Sergei V Kalinin

entry.summary: Argues that unregularized attention gives unstable and intensity-driven attributions in models mapping spectroscopic or diffraction data to material properties, and adds a learnable regularization scheme that constrains attention distributions during training. The result is claimed to be more stable, selective and physically interpretable attribution.

entry.title: Scaling Creative Writing Beyond Story-Centric Data with Attribute-Guided Genre Expansion

author.name: Hwan Chang, Yongil Kim, Heuiyeen Yeen, Yireun Kim, Jinsik Lee, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: Builds creative writing training data beyond stories by separating thematic seeds, drawn from human-authored story prompts, from manually curated genre attributes that enforce structural, stylistic and formatting conventions. Strong LLMs then generate quality-filtered query and response pairs across multiple genres.

entry.title: Consensus-gated Multi-Agent Neural Architecture Search for Seismic Fault Segmentation

author.name: Shehram Baig, Ahmad Mustafa

entry.summary: Builds an agentic neural architecture search system in which a panel of three frontier LLMs debates each candidate architecture until unanimous consensus, writes the PyTorch implementation, cross-reviews it and submits it for training, applied to seismic fault segmentation under tight labeled data budgets. The referenced models are existing releases rather than new launches.

entry.title: MAGneT-3D: Monocular and Domain-Generalizable Temporal 3D Detection

author.name: Mohamed Kotb, Johannes Meier, Christoph Reich, Oussema Dhaouadi, Luis Denninger, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Shows that learned queries in query-based monocular 3D detectors overfit the training camera geometry, then replaces them with anchors adaptively generated at inference to enable cross-dataset generalization for temporal monocular 3D detection. Claims the first domain-generalized method for this setting.

entry.title: Spatial Message Passing in Language Space for Pathology Image Interpretation

author.name: Jing-Cheng Yang, Hao-Jung Wang, Jinhao Du, Yang Hu, Ming-shan Tsai, Jens Rittscher, Bin Li

entry.summary: Handles gigapixel pathology slides by turning tiles into text descriptions and doing spatial reasoning entirely in language space: tiles are graph nodes, edges encode adjacency, and an LLM iteratively refines each description using messages from neighbors. The resulting representation is human-readable by construction.

entry.title: Retrieval Grounding Latent Reasoning for Dense Retrieval

author.name: Gang Zhou, Xiongxi Yu, Hu Tian, Yang Wei, Lu Pan, Ke Zeng, Shibiao Xu, Xiaolong Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes a dense-retrieval framework in which intermediate latent reasoning steps are explicitly tied to retrieval-relevant supervision, rather than being trained only against the final retrieval objective. The authors argue that end-objective-only training lets latent reasoning collapse into shortcuts that add no real retrieval gain. The work targets reasoning-intensive retrieval where relevance depends on instruction-conditioned inference.

entry.title: Does a Language Server Save Tokens for Coding Agents? A Measurement Methodology and Preliminary Study

author.name: Pengcheng Xu

entry.summary: This preliminary study formalizes whether Language Server Protocol based semantic retrieval actually saves tokens for coding agents versus plain lexical search, introducing a tokens-to-success metric and a five-arm ablation to isolate the semantic-retrieval effect from confounds. The authors note the efficiency claim is widely asserted but essentially unmeasured in public work. It is a methodology contribution for evaluating agent context budgets.

entry.title: CutClean: Neural Network Pruning for Privacy-Preserving Inference

author.name: Leonardo Magliolo, Vito Paolo Pastore, Giuseppe Valenzise, Enzo Tartaglione

entry.summary: CutClean shows that networks can leak sensitive attributes even without representation imbalance, then prunes to reduce that leakage by attaching auxiliary linear privacy heads at each block to quantify information flow and increasing sparsity where private information concentrates. The method jointly improves privacy and sparsity. It links compression and privacy defense in a single procedure.

entry.title: P2Skill: Privacy Preserving Skill Distillation for Cloud-Local LLM Inference Systems

author.name: Myunghoon Ryu, Geunpyo Park, Sungjoon Lee, XinYu Piao, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: P2Skill keeps personally identifiable information on-device by having a local small model follow iteratively refined skill prompts to decompose requests, route only non-sensitive parts to the cloud model, paraphrase, and reconstruct the final answer, without fine-tuning or heavy perturbation. Skills improve from observed execution failures. It targets the privacy-utility loss of masking and perturbation approaches in hybrid inference.

entry.title: How Much Do Legal RAG Systems Still Hallucinate?

author.name: Souvick Das, Sallam Abualhaija, Domenico Bianculli

entry.summary: Empirically measures hallucination in eight legal retrieval-augmented generation systems across GDPR text in English and a French civil code, using claim-level and answer-level scoring plus a validation set of expert-written questions. Findings indicate hallucinations remain widespread, with the best systems still ungrounded on a nontrivial share of responses.

entry.title: Contrastive Learning for Interpretable Anomaly Detection at Collider Experiments

author.name: Haoyi Jia, Sagar Addepalli, Julia Gonski

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage anomaly detection method for collider physics that first learns a supervised contrastive embedding across many known physics processes and then runs an autoencoder in that space, so anomaly scores are more interpretable and less confounded by energy scale and object multiplicity. Reports broader and deeper sensitivity to new-physics signals than a baseline autoencoder on simulated high-luminosity LHC conditions.

entry.title: Post-training Quantization for Hybrid Iterative Generative Models

author.name: Jing Gao, Junyi Wu, Wei Wang, Yan Yan, Yao Zhao

entry.summary: Analyzes why naive post-training quantization collapses hybrid autoregressive-plus-diffusion image generators, attributing failure to extreme activation outliers and to small quantization errors that get amplified unpredictably across iterations. Proposes targeted fixes so these models can be accelerated without retraining.

entry.title: AutoSchema: Live Schema Grounding for Agentic Text-to-Sparql over Heterogeneous Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Koji Tsuda

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free agentic framework that grounds text-to-SPARQL query generation by inspecting live endpoint schemas at query time, mapping question entities to graph identifiers and exploring relation paths, rather than relying on curated and manually maintained metadata files. Targets heterogeneous life-science knowledge graphs with divergent schemas.

entry.title: Non-Parametric Spatiotemporal Trajectory Prediction via State-Conditioned Transition Sampling

author.name: Michael Fore, Akshay Jain, Justin Downes, Rohan Pradhan, Duncan Botti

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free, zero-parameter method for multi-modal vessel trajectory prediction that builds a lookup table of historical state-to-next-position transitions and retrieves neighbors with a product kernel over position, bearing, speed and time.
