author.name: Rachel Lawrence, Jacqueline Maasch

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the generative AI community lacks operational definitions of reasoning, which makes the construct validity of reasoning benchmarks unverifiable, and proposes grounding evaluation in rule-based and verifiable automated reasoning traditions. It offers definitional scaffolding to make progress measurable.

entry.title: Fast Length-Squared Sampling for Positive-Semidefinite Matrices

author.name: Rajarshi Bhattacharjee, Ethan N. Epperly, Cameron Musco, Aaron Tian

entry.summary: Gives a rejection-sampling algorithm that draws columns of a positive semidefinite matrix proportional to squared norm in expected linear time, which is sublinear in input size and provably optimal. This removes a standard preprocessing assumption underlying many sublinear matrix algorithms for low-rank and eigenvalue approximation.

entry.title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint

author.name: Fnu Pramono, John Cai, Sourabh Kulkarni

entry.summary: TRAPSBench is a procedurally generated video benchmark of 1,404 matched physics pairs in which one targeted change makes the outcome undeterminable, paired with a metric that rewards correct answers when knowable and abstention when not. Across sixteen vision-language models spontaneous restraint is poor, and probing suggests the models internally encode undeterminability but fail to express it.

entry.title: Better, Faster, Stronger: Programmatic Skill Learning Best Reduces Agent Cost

author.name: Zixi Huang, Xiheng Wang, Andrew Wang, William Jurayj, Bernal Jim\'enez Guti\'errez, Daniel Khashabi, Nicholas Andrews

entry.summary: Compares strategies for teaching LLM agents reusable skills and argues that representing skills as executable programs yields the largest cost reductions, since deterministic action sequences replace expensive trial-and-error exploration. Skills can be discovered incrementally at inference time.

entry.title: Hybrid Gated Attention

author.name: Zekun Zhou, Ruobing Xie, Lanrui Wang, Weixuan Sun

entry.summary: Extends gated attention with three complementary gating strategies drawn from different stages of the attention computation, combining element-wise and head-wise modulation to mitigate attention sinks. The claim is an improved effectiveness-efficiency tradeoff for attention layers.

entry.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing

author.name: Minhan Cho, Jimin Kweon

entry.summary: Independently reproduces and stress-tests two published methods for improving LLM reasoning reliability, one aggregating token probabilities at inference and one editing a logic subspace of hidden states, across new domains and multiple 7-8B models. One of the original methods shipped no public code, so the authors reimplemented it.

entry.title: UniTexture: Cross-Task Universal Adversarial Textures for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yukun Dai, Mingzhe Dai, Tianshi Wang, Fengling Li, Jingjing Li, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: UniTexture crafts a single adversarial 3D texture that, placed in the scene, reliably pushes vision-language-action robot policies toward attacker-chosen action deviations across many different tasks and instructions, rather than one task at a time. It demonstrates cross-task universal vulnerabilities in generalist manipulation policies. Raises concrete physical-safety concerns for deployed embodied agents.

entry.title: GS$^{2}$CI: Robust Gaussian Splatting For Snapshot Compressive Imaging via Large Vision Model Priors

author.name: Yanming Yang, Chenxi Song, Ping Wang, Xin Yuan, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: DreamX-Phi 1.0 is an action-conditioned video world model that predicts future robot observations from a current frame, a language instruction, and a commanded sequence of end-effector poses and gripper states. It injects per-arm rigid-motion geometric encodings into attention so rollouts respect each arm's commanded path and preserve arm identity, addressing the gap between visually convincing and physically faithful predictions. Targets scalable robot policy evaluation and data generation.

entry.title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts

author.name: Xu Cao, Houze Yang, Vipin Gunda, Zhongyi Zhou, Tianyu Xu, Adarsh Kowdle, Inki Kim, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: Introduces promptable gaze target estimation, replacing brittle multi-stage pipelines that need head boxes and pose with an end-to-end concept-driven model specified through natural language. Removes error cascading and adds the flexibility that prompting has brought to other vision tasks.

entry.title: Adversarial Resilience of Poisson-Process Submodular Maximization over Matroids: From Robust Offline Optimization to Full-Bandit Learning

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Proves an adversarial resilience theorem for a Poisson-process greedy swap algorithm for submodular maximization over matroids, showing the classic 1/e and 1-1/e limiting guarantees survive under bounded oracle corruption with an additive penalty. Extends the results toward full-bandit learning settings.

entry.title: Structural Silence: When AI Infrastructure Fails Speakers of Underrepresented Languages

author.name: Avijit Roy, Proma Roy

entry.summary: Analyzes how AI infrastructure disadvantages speakers of underrepresented languages before any model is trained, using Bengali as a case study and identifying interlocking failures in web presence, tokenization, benchmarks, and deployment. Notes Bengali holds under 0.5 percent of global web content despite representing a far larger share of speakers.

entry.title: SteerBench-Work: A Benchmark for Agent Steering at Action Boundaries

author.name: Oguz Serdar, Cuneyt Mertayak

entry.summary: SteerBench-Work evaluates whether workplace LLM agents correctly decide to proceed or hold for human review at consequential action boundaries such as sending mail, merging code or moving money. It contains 106 incident-anchored scenarios with evidence-reversed mirror pairs and near-balanced labels so both error directions are equally exposed.

entry.title: Language-Conditional Dequantization: Recovering What Quantization Steals from Non-English Languages

author.name: Nirmal Thomas

entry.summary: Shows that aggressive 3-bit quantization degrades non-English performance two to four times more than English, then attaches tiny per-language low-rank correction adapters to an already-quantized model. The method recovers most of the perplexity gap for non-Latin scripts at 0.12 percent parameter overhead and under twenty minutes of training per language.

entry.title: Total Recall at What Cost? Benchmarking the Serving Cost of Agentic Memory Systems

author.name: Natchanon Pollertlam, Witchayut Kornsuwannawit

entry.summary: Benchmarks the actual serving cost of three agentic memory systems against rolling-window and full-transcript baselines over conversations up to 400 turns, pairing cost with answer accuracy. Costs turn out to be poorly predicted by conversation length alone, with regressions missing memory system costs by wide margins.

entry.title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of SLMs: Pre-trained vs. Compressed

author.name: Haokun Lin, Kaijie Zhu, Haobo Xu, Yichen Wu, Zhichao Lu, Qingfu Zhang, Zhenan Sun

entry.summary: Compares the trustworthiness of small language models built from scratch against those obtained by pruning, quantizing, or distilling larger models, across fairness, robustness, privacy, and related dimensions. It asks whether compression silently erodes safety-relevant properties that accuracy benchmarks do not capture.

entry.title: SPARED: Reasoning-Based AI-Generated Image Detection via Adversarially Edited Data

author.name: Yicheng Bao, Xiahui Guo, Xuhong Wang, Xin Tan

entry.summary: Sets up an adversarial reinforcement learning loop in which a diffusion image editor learns to turn real photographs into fakes of the same photograph that fool the detector, while a reasoning multimodal model learns to expose them with an explained verdict. Editing the same source image removes the provenance shortcut that plagues detectors trained on real and fake images from different sources.

entry.title: HounsWorld: A Multimodal World Model for Hidden Patient-State Readout, Reconstruction, and Simulation

author.name: Yunhao Bai, Zhongwei Qiu, Guangyu Guo, Yiming Huang, Tony C. W. Mok, Qinji Yu, Ling Zhang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: Frames CT-centered clinical intelligence as inference over a shared latent patient state, so that answering questions, reconstructing images, and simulating disease progression all become predictions conditioned on that state. It ships both a patient-disjoint benchmark unifying the three task families and a 3D multimodal world model.

entry.title: Do LLMs Beat Nash? Testing Decentralized Coordination in Self-Play Multi-Agent Games

author.name: Deborah Sinishaw, Qile Zhu, Edwin Meriaux, Gregory Dudek

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of one-shot, no-communication matrix and coordination games where thirteen language models play against copies of themselves, scored against the Nash equilibrium baseline for uncoordinated play. Two frontier-hosted models consistently exceed their Nash baselines, suggesting some models can reason about identical counterparts well enough to coordinate without messaging.

entry.title: Detecting a Route Flip Is Easier Than Knowing Whether to Fix It: Causal Route-Mediated Damage in Quantized Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Parvel Gu

entry.summary: Studies how 4-bit KV-cache quantization perturbs top-k mixture-of-experts routing, flipping which experts fire, and builds a causal apparatus that prices the routing-mediated fraction of the resulting quality damage (roughly a third on OLMoE at 4-bit). It also argues that detecting a route flip is far easier than deciding whether that flip is harmful.

entry.title: InfraBench: Evaluating Infrastructure Agents Across Layers, Lifecycle, and Risk

author.name: Yuan Gao (Wanxiang), Zeren Yang (Wanxiang), Junnan Li (Wanxiang), Shawn (Wanxiang), Zhong, Ahmed Dajani, Mai Zheng, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau

entry.summary: InfraBench evaluates AI agents on realistic infrastructure management tasks spanning the full system stack and operational lifecycle, with fine-grained risk assessment of destructive actions. Across 15 agent-model configurations no agent achieves full marks, with mean effective scores from roughly 40 to 88 percent.

entry.title: Towards the Harness of Embodied Agents

author.name: Qi Wang, Tianyi Wang, Chengyang Li, Shikun Ban, Yurun Chen, Yizhong Ge, Jason Qin, Chengtai Li, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Thea transfers the coding-agent harness paradigm to embodied robotics, wrapping robot capabilities as callable tools inside an agentic loop and supplying the two things the physical world does not provide for free: a persistent symbolic scene graph as context, and action outcome judgments expressed as exit codes. The claim is that embodied performance depends on infrastructure around the model, not the model alone.

entry.title: Harness-IF: Evaluating Instruction Following Across Instruction Surfaces in Coding Agents

author.name: Zining Huang, Haoran Que, Hong Zeng, Ge Zhang, Zuo Wang, Jin Chen, Haodong Wang, Zhongfei Hou, Changxin Pu, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang

entry.summary: Harness-IF evaluates whether coding agents actually follow operational rules by scoring rules individually from execution evidence across the five configurable instruction surfaces a deployed agent reads. Its key metric, Against-Prior Accuracy, counts only rules that oppose the agent's unprompted default behavior, established by re-running tasks with each rule withheld.

entry.title: Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education

author.name: Tushar Udeshi, Anna Khazenzon, Kabir Khan, Nick Breen, RJ Corwin, Chris DiGiano, Kodi Weatherholtz, Marek Zaluski

entry.summary: Practitioners behind a large deployed K-12 AI tutor describe the quality and engagement metrics they use and the experiments, including model swaps, prompting changes, personalization, and agents, that actually moved those metrics. Valuable as a rare disclosure of live evaluation practice at educational scale.

entry.title: Self-evolving network verifiers

author.name: Ioannis Protogeros, Tibor Schneider, Laurent Vanbever

entry.summary: Argues that symbolic network verifiers should automatically derive their control-plane models from router software behavior instead of hand-encoded RFC interpretations, since vendor implementations drift from specifications. Aims to remove the ongoing expert maintenance burden that keeps formal verification out of most production networks.

entry.title: When the API Speaks the Wrong Language: Revisiting Post-Training for Multilingual Tool Use

author.name: Siddharth Chauhan, Thomas Butler, Abhishek Singhania, Pankaj Porwal, Honey Gupta

entry.summary: Names and measures argument language mismatch, where a model picks the right tool but emits argument values in the wrong language, producing outputs that pass semantic checks yet fail operationally and go unmeasured by standard function-calling metrics. Finds supervised fine-tuning is a surprisingly strong remedy, matching or beating more elaborate reinforcement learning approaches under matched model selection.

entry.title: TELLME: Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment

author.name: Minjun Kim, Inho Won, Hyeonseok Lim, MinKyu Kim, Junghun Yuk, Wooyoung Go, Jongyoul Park, Jungyeul Park, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: TELLME injects quiz-style test items into continual pre-training, borrowing the test-enhanced learning idea from cognitive science to improve domain knowledge retention with less data and compute. Reported to outperform standard continual pre-training baselines for domain adaptation.

entry.title: DreamFly: Causal Memory and Receding-Horizon Diffusion Planning for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yan Deng, Fei Xu

entry.summary: DreamFly adapts a diffusion-based vision-language-action model to aerial navigation with a causally aligned memory that uses only past observations, receding-horizon planning for longer lookahead, and a more reliable termination mechanism. Targets partial observability and premature or missed goal detection in drone VLN.

entry.title: Prof-K: Probabilistic One-Pass Filtering for Efficient Top-k Selection

author.name: Tadeusz Dziarmaga, Witold Sikora, {\L}ukasz Struski, Jacek Tabor, Marcin Mazur

entry.summary: Introduces Prof-K, a single-pass sampling-based top-k selection algorithm with probabilistic correctness guarantees that avoids the memory cost of exact methods and the fragility of heuristic approximations. Relevant to sparse attention, MoE routing, and retrieval workloads where top-k is a hot primitive.

entry.title: The Impact of Temporal Context Length and Encoding Strategies on Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning

author.name: Ahmed Sameh, Ramzi Al-Sharawi, Yogatheesan Varatharajah

entry.summary: A controlled ablation of self-supervised ECG modeling that varies input horizon from seconds to ten minutes and compares continuous convolutional patch embeddings against fixed vector-quantized tokens, holding the transformer and training protocol constant. It tests whether common short-window and tokenization choices discard information needed for rhythm inference and patient-level consistency.

entry.title: A Cloud-Edge System for Multimodal Clinical Screening in Resource-Constrained Rural Settings

author.name: Hei Ting (Una), Chan, Chenwei Wu, Xueshen Liu, Zesen Zhao, Boyuan Zheng, Luis Filipe Nakayama, Michael G. Morley, Liyue Shen, Jiasi Chen, Z. Morley Mao

entry.summary: Describes a cloud-edge architecture for rural clinical screening where lightweight edge models convert raw multimodal medical data into compact structured outputs and a cloud LLM synthesizes a clinical summary, with an LLM orchestrator choosing which diagnostic tools to invoke. It is evaluated on twenty multimodal clinical scenarios under bandwidth and compute constraints.

entry.title: Robust data-driven discovery of fractional differential equations via weak formulations and Pareto-based subset selection

author.name: Pongpisit Thanasutives, Yoshinobu Kawahara

entry.summary: Weak-Pareto discovers fractional partial differential equations from noisy data by moving fractional operators onto smooth test functions via an adjoint-consistent weak form and selecting among term subsets and continuous fractional orders with a Pareto criterion. It mitigates the noise amplification that plagues fractional derivative estimation.

entry.title: History-informed Lagrangian Neural Networks

author.name: Tianshuo Zhang, Xianglei Xing, Wenzhe Zhai, Jia Gao, He Cao

entry.summary: HiLNN extends Lagrangian neural networks to position-only observations by using a recurrent encoder to infer latent context from history, reconstructing unobserved velocities and adapting to trajectory-specific physical parameters. This enables long-horizon mechanical forecasting without full state access.

entry.title: Unifying Depth and Width Pruning for LLMs via Binary Knapsack Optimization

author.name: Palaash Goel, Ayan Sengupta, Akshay Nambi, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: SNIPER performs structured LLM pruning by solving a knapsack allocation over coarse components followed by fine-grained pruning to hit exact budgets, replacing greedy myopic heuristics. It introduces a budget-fidelity metric and reports that existing pruners miss target compression ratios by up to a third.

entry.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion

author.name: Xichen Ye, Yifan Wu, Zhikang Xie, Xiangyu Yue, Cheng Jin, Weizhong Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that common cache-reuse policies for accelerating diffusion inference rely on local similarity heuristics that correlate poorly with final output quality, because errors propagate non-uniformly along the denoising trajectory. GCache derives an error-propagation bound, reparameterizes it, and optimizes caching for global impact.

entry.title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning

author.name: Zirui Song, Huaxing Liu, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Xinye Li, Lang Gao, Jinghui Zhang, Zheng Lu, Fengxian Ji, Xiaojun Chang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Proposes an inference-time audit that projects intermediate representations into vocabulary space via a Jacobian lens to measure how accessible supposedly unlearned concepts remain inside a model. The key question is whether such residual internal signals predict future knowledge recovery under continued training, enabling proactive rather than post-hoc unlearning audits.

entry.title: CT-$\Delta$Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal 3D Medical Imaging Difference Reporting with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kegeng Tang, Jingbo Wang, Shaogang Ren, Zihao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for longitudinal difference reporting in 3D CT, where a vision-language model must compare two scans of the same patient over time and describe clinically meaningful change. It targets a gap left by medical foundation models that only reason about a single study.

entry.title: MuseCritic: Learning Multi-Aspect Song Rewards through Natural-Language Aesthetic Critiques

author.name: Jiabao Zhuang, Changhao Jiang, Hanchen Wang, Jiahao Chen, Zhixiong Yang, Zhenghao Xiang, Yifei Cao, Jiajun Sun, Hui Li, Ming Zhang, Tao Ji, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: Builds a reward model for full-length generated songs that first writes a natural-language critique across five aesthetic dimensions and then uses that critique as an intermediate representation to predict continuous scores. Training proceeds by distilling teacher critiques and then refining the scoring head.

entry.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention

author.name: Qi Zhao, Qirui Li, Hanlin Tang, Yiduo Li, Zhen Guo, Cuifeng Shen, Chao Xu, Zhaosheng Chi, Xiaojin Lu, Kan Liu, Tao Lan, Lin Qu, Xi Li

entry.summary: Speeds up diffusion transformer video generation with a training-free sparse attention scheme that clusters keys in a rotary-position-aligned subspace and estimates a per-head, per-input top-k budget online. This avoids both the coarseness of block-level proxy scores and the brittleness of a fixed sparsity threshold.

entry.title: A Controlled Study of Self-Supervised Image and Video Pretraining under Limited Resources

author.name: Brun\'o B. Englert, Gijs Dubbelman

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of self-supervised pretraining objectives for images and video, contrastive, reconstruction, feature-prediction, and diffusion, under matched data, architecture, and compute budgets, including jointly trained image-video variants. It asks whether the current enormous scale of visual foundation model pretraining is actually necessary. Provides practical guidance for groups without frontier-scale compute.

entry.title: HPSD: Hybrid-Policy Self-Distillation for Text-Image-to-Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiazi Bu, Pengyang Ling, Yujie Zhou, Yibin Wang, Yuhang Zang, Xuanlang Dai, Shengyuan Ding, Tianyi Wei, Xiaohang Zhan, Jiaqi Wang, Tong Wu, Dahua Lin, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: HPSD asks whether the extra quality a text-image-to-video model achieves when given a high-quality first frame can be internalized into its plain text-to-video mode, and argues supervised fine-tuning fails because it is off-policy. The proposed hybrid-policy self-distillation supervises states the student actually visits. A concrete recipe for self-improvement in video generative models.

entry.title: V-RAE: Rethinking Video Latent Spaces for Generation

author.name: Minghui Guo, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei

entry.summary: V-RAE builds compact video generative latents on top of frozen vision foundation model features, with lightweight temporal pooling to strip redundancy and a decoder to restore continuous motion, arguing that reconstruction-optimal latents are not necessarily good for generative modeling. This mirrors the broader move toward representation autoencoders in image generation. Could improve training efficiency and semantic structure for video diffusion.

entry.title: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark

author.name: Dairu Liu, Zekun Qi, Jiayu Zeng, Ruixi Yu, Yu Guan, Yintianrun Zhang, Xuchuan Chen, Sikai Liang, Zekai Li, Chenghuai Lin, Xinqiang Yu, Wenyao Zhang, He Wang, Li Yi

entry.summary: HumanTracker is a humanoid motion tracking benchmark with roughly 153 hours of optical motion capture from professional performers across four motion families, designed so evaluation aligns with what humans perceive rather than only averaging per-frame kinematic error. It emphasizes physical artifacts like foot skating, unstable support, and mistimed contacts that current metrics miss. Addresses a measurement problem holding back whole-body humanoid imitation.

entry.title: Temporal GRPO: Beyond Trajectory-Level Credit in Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yao Zhou, Hang Gao, Fengge Wu, Changwen Zheng, Wenwen Qiang

entry.summary: Temporal GRPO fixes credit aliasing in reinforcement learning post-training of vision-language-action policies, where a single trajectory-level advantage punishes the early actions of a rollout that made real progress before failing late. It detects task stages, aligns rollouts to stage-specific action intervals, and compares only rollouts that reached the same stage before applying stage-level advantages. Improves credit assignment for sparse-reward robot post-training.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Generated Detection Rules in Cybersecurity

author.name: Anna Bertiger, Bobby Filar, Aryan Luthra, Stefano Meschiari, Aiden Mitchell, Sam Scholten, Vivek Sharath

entry.summary: Introduces an open-source framework and three expert-inspired metrics for judging whether LLM-generated cybersecurity detection rules match the quality of human-authored ones, using a holdout methodology on a real detection corpus. Matters because security teams are already deploying LLM rule generators with almost no rigorous measurement.

entry.title: Causal inference for group-contaminated structured outcomes: observable quotients, lossless reduction and exact randomization inference

author.name: Usef Faghihi, Amir Saki

entry.summary: Develops theory for causal inference when structured outcomes such as images are observed only after unknown unit-specific group transformations, characterizing which targets are recoverable via invariants and when quotient reduction is statistically lossless. Provides exact randomization inference in this setting.

entry.title: Preference Tree Optimization: Enhancing Goal-Oriented Dialogue with Look-Ahead Simulations

author.name: Lior Baruch, Moshe Butman, Kfir Bar, Doron Friedman

entry.summary: Preference Tree Optimization builds preference data by expanding conversation trees with look-ahead rollouts against simulated patients and an oracle evaluator, then trains agents with DPO for motivational interviewing dialogue. Targets multi-turn goal-oriented conversation in low-data specialized domains.

entry.title: When Can You Trust Offline Evaluation of Equal-Cost Top-k Allocation? A Controlled, Reproducible Benchmark and Practitioner's Guide

author.name: Binshuang Li

entry.summary: Benchmarks six off-policy estimators across five datasets and two known-effect sweeps for deterministic top-k budget allocation, where no action randomization remains to smooth estimates. Finds that overlap is governed by alignment between logging and target actions rather than logging sharpness, and validates the mechanism against a non-simulated paired reference.

entry.title: Decentralized Multi-Player Q-Learning in Episodic Markov Decision Processes with Information Asymmetry

author.name: Larissa Xu, King Bi, William Chang

entry.summary: Studies decentralized multi-agent Q-learning in tabular episodic MDPs under three information-asymmetry regimes and provides algorithms with regret bounds scaling in the joint action space, plus exponential-weights methods for the hardest setting. Players cannot communicate during learning but may agree on a protocol beforehand.

entry.title: TANGCO: Learning Topology-Aware Capacity Allocation for Overload-driven Cascading Failures

author.name: Orkun Irsoy, Leman Akoglu, Osman Yagan

entry.summary: TANGCO trains a graph neural network policy through a cascade simulator to allocate a fixed capacity budget across network nodes so that overload-driven cascading failures are resisted. It handles a non-differentiable, piecewise-constant fail-or-survive objective that defeats gradient-based and exact methods.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Estimation of Causal Effect on CVR with Targeted Regularization

author.name: Jiayi Dan, Bo Li, Lu Deng, Yong Wang

entry.summary: Develops a doubly robust estimator with targeted regularization for causal effects on post-click conversion rate, arguing that an unbiased loss over the full sample does not guarantee an unbiased final estimator. It addresses selection bias and variance inflation from restricting to clicked samples.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution

author.name: Peidong Wang, Zhiming Ma, Ying Chang, Xufang Luo, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Yuqing Yang, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: SHAPER adapts embodied agents to new environments without any weight updates by co-evolving reusable skills and a context-plus-code execution harness against target-environment feedback. It targets fixed-interface robot settings where programmable APIs and additional training data or rewards are unavailable.

entry.title: LODESTAR: Trustworthy Entropy Is Navigated, Not Merely Measured -- Reinforced Polarizer Keeps a Frozen LLM from Being Confidently Misled by the Wrong Evidence

author.name: Po-Jen Ko, Che-Cheng Wu, Hung-Chun Hsu, Li-Yang Chang, Chuan-Ju Wang

entry.summary: Formulates training large models on constrained hardware as a mixed-integer scheduling problem over checkpoint selection, activation placement, recomputation, and CPU-GPU-NVMe transfer overlap, then executes the solved policy. It couples 8-bit optimizer states with the schedule to hide communication off the critical path.

entry.title: Mr3D-VL: A generalist vision language foundation model for Multiparametric 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging

author.name: Zhi Qiao, Xintong Wu, Yichu He, Feng Shi

entry.summary: Presents a generalist vision-language foundation model for multiparametric 3D brain MRI that reasons directly over volumetric data instead of stacked 2D slices, targeting tasks such as glioma grading. It aims to add natural language interaction and cross-modal interpretability to mpMRI analysis.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs

author.name: Beining Xu, Hairui Wang, Jiaxin Wang, Changsheng Chen, Anirban Chakraborty

entry.summary: Shows that document-understanding multimodal models fill in missing fields on identity documents by recalling memorized relationships among fields from training data, leaking multiple correlated pieces of personal information even without visual evidence. The authors propose a dynamic relational unlearning framework to break those memorized field associations.

entry.title: Comparing Congress's Two AI Emergency Shutdown Mechanisms

author.name: Philip Dowdell

entry.summary: A side-by-side explainer comparing two US bills introduced in July 2026 that would let the federal government order emergency suspension of frontier AI systems: the FRONTIER Act section 8 and the AI Kill Switch Act. It contrasts who issues orders, whether training or only deployment can be halted, the triggering standard (imminent catastrophic risk versus a covered incident), and duration.

entry.title: VAKRA: Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Across APIs and Retrieval Under Tool-Use Policies

author.name: Ankita Rajaram Naik, Anupama Murthi, Benjamin Elder, Siyu Huo, Raavi Gupta, Abhinav Jain, Praveen Venkateswaran, Abdulhamid Adebayo, Danish Contractor

entry.summary: VAKRA is an enterprise agent benchmark with over 8,000 executable APIs across 62 domains, covering diverse API interaction styles, multi-hop reasoning over structured APIs, and multi-source reasoning constrained by natural-language tool-use policies. Correctness is verified by re-executing predicted calls against live APIs so multiple valid solution paths are accepted.

entry.title: Chemically Meaningful Textualization Enables Explainable Validation of Metal-Organic Frameworks by Large Language Models

author.name: Guobin Zhao, Xiao-Yan Li

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs can act as interpretable validators of metal-organic framework crystal structures when crystallographic data is converted into chemically meaningful text, and identifies which descriptors matter. Finds that encoding local coordination environments, rather than sheer volume of structural detail, drives validation success.

entry.title: Strengthening Full Justified Representation: Efficient Verification and Computation

author.name: Nicholas Teh

entry.summary: Strengthens the full justified representation axiom for approval-based committee voting into a variant that is both satisfiable and verifiable in polynomial time, closing a coNP-hardness gap. Analyzes a residual-budget greedy algorithm whose partial committees admit priceable completions via sequential Phragmen.

entry.title: RoadWeaver: Large-Scale Lane-Level HD Map Generation from Scratch for Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Yueyuan Li, Zexi Chen, Weijie Xi, Mingyang Jiang, Songan Zhang, Hanyang Zhuang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: Generates large-scale lane-level HD maps from scratch in a coarse-to-fine manner, synthesizing a global road layout, expanding it into a connected network, then producing topologically consistent lane geometry. Reports high reachability and low endpoint alignment error for driving simulation at scale.

entry.title: Fingerprinting Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Collapsed Generation

author.name: Yuanmin Huang, Chen Chen, Geng Hong, Xiaoyu You, Hui Xue, Zhenxing Qian, Mi Zhang, Min Yang

entry.summary: Fingerprints proprietary text-to-image diffusion models by exploiting collapsed generation, where certain inputs produce nearly identical images across random seeds, treating these collapse-prone conditions as intrinsic behavioral signatures. Enables non-invasive ownership verification without watermarking or modifying the model.

entry.title: DexterSQL: Deep Schema Exploration and Rule-based Correction for Text-to-SQL Generation

author.name: Anik Pramanik, Murat Kantarcioglu, Vincent Oria, Shantanu Sharma

entry.summary: DexterSQL is a prompting-only text-to-SQL system adding deep schema exploration to disambiguate similar columns, a memory of recurring generation failures, and rule-based correction of missing or misplaced conditions. Targets the weaknesses of non-fine-tuned pipelines on complex queries.

entry.title: Confidence Calibration of Deep Learning Systems

author.name: Coby Penso

entry.summary: A thesis on confidence calibration that drops the usual assumption of clean validation data, developing methods that recover noise-free confidence estimates using an estimated label-noise model and addressing domain shift. Motivated by safe deployment where reliable probabilities matter as much as predictions.

entry.title: Which Site, and When: A Free-Satellite-Data Test of Himalayan Glacial Lake Bursts, Landslides, and Ice Floods

author.name: Matthew Kahn, Milan Arjel, Nirmala Adhikari, Mingmar Sherpa, James Pope

entry.summary: Builds predictive models for Himalayan glacial-lake outburst floods, rainfall-triggered landslides, and smaller glacier-pond floods using only free radar interferometry deformation data and satellite weather, separating which-site susceptibility from when-triggered timing. Extends a prior feasibility study that identified the signals but proposed no model.

entry.title: Knowledge-guided Pattern Discovery via Coupled Tensor Factorizations

author.name: Gaute Johannessen, Geert Roelof van der Ploeg, Evrim Acar

entry.summary: Proposes knowledge-guided coupled tensor factorization that jointly analyzes real multiway measurements with simulated data from computational mechanistic models, injecting domain priors into otherwise purely data-driven pattern discovery. Applications include metabolomics and neuroimaging.

entry.title: EU-ETS under attack? The impact of carbon price suppression on the decarbonization of the power sector

author.name: Javier Gonzalez-Ruiz, Carlos Rodriguez-Pardo, Alice Di Bella, Paolo Mastropietro, Jose Pablo Chavez-Avila, Massimo Tavoni

entry.summary: A systematic review of FDA AI/ML medical device summary reports from 2021 to 2025, checking whether public regulatory documentation contains enough evidence to independently assess trustworthiness dimensions such as fairness, robustness and explainability. The finding is that clearance documentation leaves large reporting gaps.

entry.title: Excess Separability: Nuisance-Controlled Residual-Stream Probing for Benchmark Contamination Detection

author.name: Florian Braun

entry.summary: Proposes detecting benchmark contamination by probing internal activations, but first shows the naive linear-probe approach fails, then specifies a protocol using a placebo-matched depth profile of probe accuracy tested against a label-permutation null. It requires neither the training corpus nor advance canary planting.

entry.title: Statistical Properties of Robust Learning under Distributional Shifts

author.name: Zhiyi Li, Xiaojie Mao, Yunbei Xu, Ruohan Zhan

entry.summary: Derives finite-sample generalization bounds for distributionally robust optimization and robust satisficing measured on the shifted target distribution rather than the source or adversarial worst case, and compares the two frameworks systematically. This clarifies when each robust formulation actually helps under real deployment shift.

entry.title: How Do VLMs Behave When Blind or Misled? Behavioral Evaluation of VLMs on Scientific Figures

author.name: Paul Osemudiame Oamen, Owusu-Banahene Osei, Ananya Mukherjee, Christian Greisinger, Steffen Eger, Pius Onobhayedo, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: SciFigBench evaluates vision-language models on scientific figures across perception, reasoning and behavioral reliability, using image transformations, resistance probes and caption-bias probes over 250 heavily annotated figures. It measures how models behave when visual evidence is removed or misleading rather than only when it is present.

entry.title: Foundation models for movement data: Are they ready for prime-time?

author.name: Alexander Br\"auer, Benjamin Cauchi, Nils Strodthoff

entry.summary: Benchmarks four open-source accelerometer foundation models against supervised baselines on nineteen tasks spanning activity recognition, clinical monitoring and physiological inference. Results are task-dependent: supervised models stay competitive on activity recognition while foundation models lead on fall and stress detection and are more robust to sensor placement changes.

entry.title: Causal Structure is Inducible but Functionally Decoupled: The Routing/Readout Boundary of a Typed Mechanism Library

author.name: Xining Xun

entry.summary: Uses a typed mechanism library of discrete slots on small transformers trained on a causal-world benchmark to show that type-level supervision induces slot-by-type internal organization for routing, yet this structure is functionally decoupled from how answers are read out. Findings are preregistered and tested at 22.6M and 125M scales.

entry.title: Asymptotic Risk Calibration for Selective Question Answering

author.name: Shufan Lin, Sijin Dong

entry.summary: Proposes a post-hoc calibration framework for selective question answering that reformulates error control among accepted answers as a linear expectation constraint and applies a conformal-risk-style monotonized calibration. This gives statistical guarantees on the error rate of answers the model chooses to give, unlike fixed uncertainty thresholds.

entry.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning

author.name: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang, Bingnan Li, Shuqi Gu, Kan Ren, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Hua

entry.summary: Proposes encoding a film into a knowledge-graph representation with typed edges and a linked asset layer of images, audio, and clips, then reconstructing video from it, so that agents can reason over and manipulate cinematic structure. The autoencoding objective is what forces the graph to remain faithful to the source video.

entry.title: MV2: Multi-View Multi-Vehicle Driving Dataset for Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Sanjay Bhargav Dharavath, Hanvitha Saraswathi Mukkamala, Faizan Farooq Khan, Ioannis Kakogeorgiou, Aditya Arun, C V Jawahar, Zakaria Laskar

entry.summary: Releases a driving dataset captured simultaneously by a car, a scooter, and a drone following distinct but synchronized trajectories, enabling novel view synthesis to be tested under much larger viewpoint changes than single-trajectory data allows. Training on one platform and testing on another creates a demanding generalization benchmark.

entry.title: StrAD: A Streaming Method and Benchmark for Audio Description Generation for Long-form Videos

author.name: Julian Spravil, Sebastian Houben, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and streaming method for generating audio descriptions over full-length videos, rather than captioning pre-cut clips with ground-truth timestamps and character databases. This reframes accessibility narration as an online decision about what to say and when.

entry.title: Vision-Language Models are Fragile Multilingual Associators

author.name: Ritabrata Chakraborty, Rajatsubhra Chakraborty, Shivakumara Palaiahnakote, Angelo Cangelosi, Umapada Pal

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark that varies the language of context and query to test whether vision-language models keep visual-attribute bindings stable across languages, evaluating both task performance and causal interventions on internals. Binding collapses across language families and scripts, with the internal binding computation shifting to later layers and weakening causally, while closely related languages hold up better. Combines multilingual evaluation with mechanistic analysis.

entry.title: BrainWAM: Action-Space Coordination of Semantic Priors and Predictive Dynamics for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Bing Zhan, Shuyao Shang, Jiahao Gu, Shuo Lu, Yuan Xu, Zhao Wang, Yida Wang, Xueyang Zhang, Kun Zhan, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: BrainWAM unifies the semantic priors of vision-language-action driving models with the predictive rollouts of generative world action models, after finding that naively merging them through shared token attention lets semantic shortcuts crowd out predictive dynamics. Inspired by complementary brain systems, it coordinates the two in action space instead. Addresses a real integration failure in end-to-end driving planners.

entry.title: FIRE-VLA: Failure-Informed Self-Evolution for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Hao Dou

entry.summary: FIRE-VLA tackles the case where all sampled rollouts in a GRPO group are failures, which leaves the relative reward signal uninformative. It triggers self-distillation from a frozen round-start copy of the model that is privileged with hidden future trajectory information, turning unresolved failures into supervised signal for driving vision-language-action policies.

entry.title: When Explanations Betray Backdoors: Black-Box Auditing for Language Model Classifiers

author.name: Yang Liu, Ran Zou

entry.summary: Studies black-box detection of backdoored language-model classifiers when the defender has only clean data but can request a rationale alongside the label. Their Groundedness Drift score, which measures whether the rationale stays anchored in the input, beats compared detectors on AUROC and residual attack success across two 7B backbones, five datasets and four attack families.

entry.title: Cutting AI Datacenter Energy with Reinforcement Learning: Measured Power Control of LLM Training from One GPU to the Fleet

author.name: Eliseo Curcio

entry.summary: Instruments GRPO reinforcement-learning post-training with half-second GPU power telemetry at 7B, 14B, and 72B scales and trains a PPO meta-controller that adapts generation parameters to measured power draw. Reports large reductions in power-limit violations alongside higher token throughput and energy efficiency.

entry.title: VQ-bench: A Composable Vector Quantization Framework

author.name: Ashwin Padaki, Amir Ingber, Edo Liberty

entry.summary: Provides a unified compositional framework for vector quantization, identifying seven conceptual primitives and re-expressing 25 published quantizers as pipelines over them, released as an open-source benchmark. Targets the resurgence of quantization as core AI retrieval and serving infrastructure.

entry.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs

author.name: Utkarsh Bahuguna

entry.summary: Shows that self-consistency majority voting reduces per-problem accuracy on most GPQA Diamond problems for two small instruction-tuned models, 56.6 percent of problems for one and 65.7 percent for the other, despite being a standard inference-time compute strategy. The effect was pre-registered on a confirmatory split after exploratory observation, and an oracle over sample counts shows large headroom for adaptive routing.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation

author.name: Ziqiang Wan, Li Gu, Zhixiang Chi, Zhi Liu, Seyed Mehdi Ayyoubzadeh, Yuanhao Yu, Yang Wang

entry.summary: MobileJudgeBench evaluates LLM-as-judge methods on 931 human-annotated mobile agent trajectories spanning six benchmarks, four agent models, and 68 apps, testing six judging approaches across multiple backends. A key finding is that a simple screenshot-sampling baseline judge matches or beats purpose-built judges.

entry.title: A Modular Agentic Framework for Synthetically Constrained Multi-Objective Hit-to-Lead Optimization

author.name: Kelvin P. Idanwekhai, Enes Kelestemur, Benjamin Strickland, Matthew Hart, Steini Davidsson, Angelos Angelopoulos, Ron Alterovitz, Marcello DeLuca, Alexander Tropsha

entry.summary: SABLE is an open-source agentic framework for hit-to-lead drug optimization where an LLM interprets goals and routes tasks to tools for reaction-templated analog enumeration, ADMET and physicochemical prediction, structure-based affinity scoring, and Bayesian optimization. It functions as a computational twin of the analysis and prioritization stages of the design-make-test-analyze cycle.

entry.title: Foresight Without Seeing: Latent Futures for World Action Models

author.name: Jiakai Huang, Zhongbo Wu, Zheng Zhang, Zihan Wang, Shan You, Tao Huang

entry.summary: ForeWAM is a world action model for robotics that conditions action generation on predicted future dynamics without decoding future video, avoiding the iterative denoising cost of explicit-future models while retaining a predictive interface that direct-policy models lack. It supplies latent foresight to the action transformer at inference time.

entry.title: Making AI-Generated Feedback Matter: From Provision to Student Enactment

author.name: Omar Alsaiari, Nilufar Baghaei, Jason M. Lodge, Dragan Ga\v{s}evi'c, Naomi Winstone, Hassan Khosravi

entry.summary: A large quasi-experimental cohort study across 13,037 students and over 51,000 authored resources compares three AI-mediated feedback workflows, distinguishing feedback provision from student uptake and enactment. It targets the finding that generative AI solves the scale problem for feedback but students still fail to act on it.

entry.title: XBridge: Entity-Grounded Latent Bridge for Heterogeneous LLM Communication

author.name: Wooseong Yang, Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Yu Wang, Philip S. Yu, Junhyun Lee

entry.summary: XBridge enables decode-free latent communication between LLMs from different families, identifying an entity grounding problem where cross-attention bridges suffer rare-token compression collapse and lose entity identity through the continuous bottleneck. It adds mechanisms to preserve entity grounding across architecture boundaries.

entry.title: FrontierFinance: A Challenging Benchmark for Measuring Frontier Intelligence of Finance Agents

author.name: Yuhao Zhang, O. Ozan Koyluoglu, Thejas Venkatesh, Richard Diehl Martinez, Vishank Bhatia, Arash Alidoust, Ashwin Paranjape

entry.summary: FrontierFinance is an open benchmark of 220 expert-crafted investment research queries with 11,543 source-attributed rubrics spanning six use cases across the full investor workflow, evaluated under a common agent harness. It targets long-form open-ended analyst tasks where extraction benchmarks are saturated and reference-based or generic judge scoring fails.

entry.title: Making Your LLMs More Objective: Stabilizing LLM Safety Behavior Across Traits with Trait-Invariant Safety Tuning

author.name: Lang Cao

entry.summary: Documents trait-induced safety variation, where assigning a persona or trait in the system prompt changes whether an aligned model refuses the identical request, and introduces deviation and flip-rate metrics to quantify it. Provides representation-level analysis of the mechanism and proposes trait-invariant safety tuning to stabilize refusal decisions across personas.

entry.title: Policy-as-logic for robust reasoning over rules

author.name: Rahul Nair, Bastian Lipka, Elizabeth Daly

entry.summary: Separates fact extraction from rule reasoning by using an LLM to ground predicates from natural-language input and an answer set solver to reason over policies expressed in formal logic. Reports better accuracy and robustness to input perturbations than policy-as-prompt and policy-as-code baselines, with roughly a tenfold reduction in token usage.

entry.title: Retry, Switch, or Abstain? Learning Strategy-Aware Tool-Use Policies via Controlled Error Injection

author.name: Chaoran Chen, Vy Nguyen, Ziji Zhang, Abhinav Gullapalli, Ziyi Wang, Yuxuan Lu, Dakuo Wang, Jing Huang, Zhou Yu, Jin Lai

entry.summary: BENCH2ROBUST converts failure-free tool-use benchmarks into controlled stochastic environments with transient, persistent, and silent tool failures, and with scenario-controlled solvability so episodes genuinely require retrying, switching, or abstaining. Studies two interventions: a Bayesian tool memory providing runtime recovery context, and training strategy-aware policies via controlled error injection.

entry.title: Who Thinks Best Depends on How Long You Let Them: Budget-Dependent Rankings in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Rodrigo Guedes de Souza, Alison R. Panisson

entry.summary: Varies the maximum token generation budget across seven levels for four models on three reasoning benchmarks over 56,476 inferences and finds that model rankings reverse across budgets on every benchmark. It also reports that 3 to 19 percent of items get worse with more budget even controlling for truncation, and oracle model complementarity of up to 27.8 points.

entry.title: Herding End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guards

author.name: Sim\'on Pati\~no Idarraga, Erick Silva, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker

entry.summary: Attaches a lightweight neuro-symbolic guard to the command interface of an already-trained end-to-end driving agent, checking each command against explicit traffic and physics rules and substituting the nearest safe alternative when violated. Every intervention is traceable to the rule that fired, adding auditability without retraining.

entry.title: Consolidator: Learning Persistent Routed Memory Across Context Boundaries

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: Tests whether copying short-term memory into a slower long-term store is sufficient for persistence across a context boundary, using a shared slot-local operator that transforms routed state before accumulation and then clearing the cache. Finds that retained long-term memory must also condition the router to influence which slots later inputs access, demonstrated on a two-segment modular arithmetic remapping task.

entry.title: Instruction Alignment for Binary Code Representation Learning

author.name: Huaijin Wang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using compiler debug information to supervise instruction-level correspondences when learning binary code embeddings, rather than only function-level similarity. The authors show that models fine-tuned for function similarity already implicitly improve instruction alignment, and exploit that signal explicitly for better and more interpretable representations.

entry.title: Co-constructing sociotechnical AI governance: participatory system mapping using algorithm registers

author.name: \'I\~nigo de Troya, Maurus Enbergs, Neelke Doorn, Roel Dobbe

entry.summary: Uses participatory system mapping with diverse stakeholders to examine what public-sector algorithm registers reveal and hide about the sociotechnical systems in which algorithms operate. Argues that entry-level transparency does not deliver system-level accountability and proposes a more pluralistic safety-oriented view.

entry.title: GENADA: efficient generative time series adversarial attack framework

author.name: Michael Baronov, Denis Vorobev, Margarita Rusanova, Petr Sokerin, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: GENADA trains a generator to produce adversarial perturbations for time series models in a single forward pass, replacing costly iterative gradient attacks that repeatedly backpropagate through the victim. Includes single-step and iterative variants for domains such as healthcare, finance, and energy.

entry.title: Training Under Challenge: Executable Certificates and Challenge-Closed Optimality for Neural Networks

author.name: Farhang Yeganegi, Arian Eamaz, Mojtaba Soltanalian

entry.summary: Proposes an executable-certificate framework in which predeclared procedures construct alternative networks in the same class and re-evaluate the objective, so any better candidate becomes a replayable witness bounding the checkpoint's optimality gap. It aims to distinguish genuine convergence from being trapped, representation-limited, or trainer-mismatched.

entry.title: Finding the Needle in a Haystack: Test-Time Analog Circuit Representation Adaptation for Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Fin Amin, Sounak Dutta, Paul D. Franzon

entry.summary: TTARO adapts pretrained analog-circuit embeddings online during Bayesian optimization so representations reorganize around the figure of merit being optimized rather than staying frozen after encoder pretraining. It addresses a mismatch between representation learning objectives and the search objective in expensive topology search.

entry.title: Momentum as Residual-Driven Multiplier Correction for Deep Learning Optimization

author.name: Zhixin Ren, Yau Lyu, Congrong Li, Liping Zhang, Shengbo Eben Li

entry.summary: Models each person's personal space as a radial Gaussian mixture derived from proxemics theory and turns the resulting robot-centric cost into a dense reward for deep RL crowd navigation. The aim is interpretable social compliance without sacrificing navigation efficiency.

entry.title: Can Spectral-Clipping Enable Better Learning While Forgetting Less for Low-Rank Adaptation?

author.name: Hyowon Wi, Noseong Park

entry.summary: Analyzes singular value structure in pretrained weights and LoRA adapters, arguing that principal components are reusable while minor components carry task-specific adaptation, and links unbounded adapter singular value growth to catastrophic forgetting. Proposes spectral clipping to improve learning while forgetting less.

entry.title: Online Inference for Quantile Temporal Difference Learning in Distributional Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijie Cheng, Yang Peng, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Establishes functional central limit theorems for synchronous and asynchronous quantile temporal difference learning, showing averaged iterates converge weakly to rescaled Brownian motion, and derives an online random-scaling inference procedure. The statistic can be computed without storing the full iterate trajectory.

entry.title: Located but Not Releasable: Silent Gate Inversion and Bounded Linear Release

author.name: Xining Xun

entry.summary: Runs a fully preregistered detect-localize-release pipeline on a small transformer known to encode latent causal structure it does not use behaviorally. Localization succeeds and interventions have measurable effects, but converting the located structure into correct behavior proves much harder than locating it.

entry.title: Spark-to-Paper: End-to-End Research Paper Generation as a Composable Skill

author.name: Zhuoyang Qian, Biao Wu, Yiran Wang, Chris D Yan, Desan Dai, Liangwei Zheng, Jin Jiang, Junsheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: Implements end-to-end research paper generation as thirteen composable skills inside an existing coding assistant, separating model judgment from deterministic checkable operations and fixing required evidence before experiments are run. It aims for consistency across a long generation process without a bespoke agent platform.

entry.title: Lifecycle-Optimal Tokenization: Vocabulary Size as a Deployment-Regime-Dependent Infrastructure Parameter

author.name: Rima Mittal, Ankit Gubrani, Satyanarayana Kakollu

entry.summary: Argues that optimal tokenizer vocabulary size is not a constant but depends on the serving regime, formalizing lifecycle cost as training plus inference cost weighted by volume and batch size. Controlled experiments on two GPU families show the inference-optimal vocabulary shifting by roughly sixteen times across batch sizes.

entry.title: Confucius4-TTS: Transcript-Free Cross-Lingual Zero-Shot TTS with a Learnable Speaker Encoder

author.name: Huaxuan Wang, Huimin Wang, Ruiyu Zhang, Yingjie Li, Yitao Duan

entry.summary: A technical report on a multilingual zero-shot text-to-speech system covering fourteen languages that clones voices from untranscribed reference audio using a learnable speaker encoder. Removing the audio-prompt transcript requirement is what enables practical cross-lingual cloning from in-the-wild recordings.

entry.title: Semantic Steering for Controllable Generation: Tuning-Free Concept Erasure in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Qiao Li, Xiaomeng Fu, Yuanshu Zhao, Qipeng Wang, Jiao Dai, Jizhong Han

entry.summary: Proposes a tuning-free way to suppress unsafe or unwanted concepts in multimodal diffusion transformers by steering semantics at inference, avoiding architecture-specific weight edits that are impractical for large deployed models. It targets the deeply entangled knowledge and context-dependent text encoders of modern large text-to-image systems.

entry.title: EgoPHI: Estimating Contact and Force from Egocentric Vision

author.name: Andela Ilic, Rachel Schuchert, Yijing Jiang, Christian Holz

entry.summary: EgoPHI estimates dense contact maps and 3D force distributions on hands and objects from a single first-person RGB image plus object geometry, using a physics-simulation pipeline to synthesize per-vertex force supervision that real datasets lack. Recovering forces, not just contact, moves egocentric perception toward physically grounded interaction understanding. Useful for robot imitation from human video and AR interaction.

entry.title: Spatially-Grounded Text-to-Video Generation via Inference-Time Gradient-Free Optimization

author.name: Guillaume Jeanneret, Mathis Koroglu, Hugo Caselles-Dupr\'e, Arnaud Dapogny, Matthieu Cord

entry.summary: GATO-Vid provides spatial control over where objects appear in text-to-video diffusion outputs without any training and without gradient backpropagation, replacing costly backward passes with an analytical trajectory optimization. This removes a major compute bottleneck in training-free layout guidance for large diffusion transformers. Practical for controllable video generation at scale.

entry.title: Geometry-Grounded Unified 3D Perception for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Longfei Xu, Xiaohui Wang, Zehao Huang, Han Li, Ya Yang, Naiyan Wang, Si Liu

entry.summary: GeoUP adapts the reconstruction-oriented latent representation of a 3D foundation model (VGGT) to calibrated streaming multi-camera driving inputs, factorizing attention into self, temporal, and view components so the shared representation preserves metric 3D structure. It argues semantic-pretrained backbones plus bolted-on geometry modules lose consistent scene geometry. Relevant to unifying detection, occupancy, and mapping in camera-only driving stacks.

entry.title: How Good are Foundation Models in Longitudinal MRI Disease Progression Reasoning?

author.name: Wafa Al Ghallabi, Ritesh Thawkar, Sara Ghaboura, Omkar Thawakar, Numan Saeed, Dana Al Nuaimi, Ajnas Alkatheeri, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan

entry.summary: Introduces a time-aware, multi-view MRI benchmark with about 3,900 expert-verified question-answer pairs from 890 patients and over 3,200 longitudinal scans, requiring models to compare timepoints, integrate anatomical planes, and localize interval change. Existing medical vision-language benchmarks are single-scan and single-view, missing the temporal reasoning central to radiology. Exposes a concrete capability gap in medical foundation models.

entry.title: A Unifying Perspective on Causal World Models: From Observations to Representations to Structure

author.name: Avinash Kori, Fabrizio Russo

entry.summary: A position and formalization paper arguing world models must go beyond generating plausible futures to capture entity properties, entity-entity interactions, and entity-environment interactions, and giving a formal definition of causal world models tied to the tasks they should support. It connects world modeling to existing causal representation learning theory across levels of abstraction. Conceptual scaffolding for a fast-moving but loosely defined area.

entry.title: HumanoidVLN: A Physics-Grounded Simulator and Benchmark for Vision-Language Navigation Across Diverse Humanoid Embodiments

author.name: Quan-Dung Pham, Anh Dao, The-Anh Nguyen, Minh Nguyen-Dinh, Phuong Nam Dang, Tri Pham, Hung Tran, Bach Dao, Tuyen P. Le, Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: HumanoidVLN is an Isaac Sim based simulator and benchmark for vision-language navigation on legged humanoids, spanning four robots with differing degrees of freedom and heights, and using a hierarchical stack combining a reinforcement-learned locomotion policy with higher-level navigation. It captures constraints wheeled-agent benchmarks ignore, including bipedal physical limits, morphology variation, and camera shake induced by walking. Fills a real gap as humanoid platforms proliferate.

entry.title: LLMs have the capacity for self-imposed steganography

author.name: Edward Cant

entry.summary: A safety project demonstrating that a language model can be trained to embed hidden information in its own plaintext outputs, first via prompted synonym substitution and then via an internalized red/green watermarking scheme that lets the model watermark itself based on system-prompt instructions rather than via the sampler. Motivated by the risk that a misaligned model could use steganography to evade control-protocol monitoring.

entry.title: How to Spend Your Oracle Budget: Practical Guidance for Protein Structure Prediction Models

author.name: Aleksandra Kalisz, Jack Simons, Krisztina Sinkovics, Noam Ghenassia, Shikha Surana, Henry Moss, Paul Duckworth

entry.summary: Benchmarks how to spend a limited biological oracle budget when guiding protein structure prediction models, comparing FK-steering, DPO, best K-of-N sampling, and an optimization-over-outputs method applied in the generative model's latent subspace. Provides the first systematic budget-aware comparison for this setting.

entry.title: An Agentic Workflow for Legacy HPC Modernization: Converting the Two-Electron-Integral Core of GAMESS

author.name: Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina, Peng Xu, Mark S. Gordon

entry.summary: Applies an agentic workflow with three prompt-specialized roles operating under an agent-authored version-controlled specification to modernize the two-electron-integral core of the GAMESS quantum chemistry package, with humans holding a small number of gates. Safety comes from an exact domain verification oracle, and the authors argue the boundary of safe delegation is exactly where that oracle loses visibility.

entry.title: JieZi: A Large-Scale Expert-Audited Dataset and Benchmark for Ancient Chinese Character Exegesis

author.name: Ran Li, Huiguo He, Jiahuan Cao, Junle Liu, Hiuyi Cheng, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Defines a four-level vision-language question answering task for scholarly exegesis of ancient Chinese characters, spanning identification, glyph-form analysis, meaning interpretation, and diachronic evolution, and releases a large expert-audited dataset and benchmark. Moves beyond narrow character recognition and retrieval toward modeling the full interpretive workflow.

entry.title: From Safety Documentation to Safety Knowledge Support: An Evidence-Grounded LLM Framework for Medical Devices

author.name: Tuhinangshu Gangopadhyay, Rasmus Adler, Peter Liggesmeyer, Jan Reich

entry.summary: Proposes an evidence-grounded LLM framework for medical device safety and risk-management documentation aligned with ISO 14971 and IEC 62304, emphasizing source links, traceability, uncertainty handling, and lifecycle support. Motivated by the document-heavy nature of regulated safety engineering and scarcity of expert reviewers.

entry.title: Large-scale Testing Global Optimization Methods with Black-box Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Wojciech Zarzecki, Jaros{\l}aw Arabas

entry.summary: Argues that black-box adversarial attack tasks should serve as high-dimensional benchmarks for global optimization, since existing suites rest on a handful of decades-old analytic functions that may bias algorithm development. It demonstrates several evolutionary algorithms and metaheuristics on such attack problems.

entry.title: Dead text or binding clause? Measuring and restoring constraint influence in black-box LLM dialogues

author.name: Haoyuan Zhu

entry.summary: Documents behavioral relapse in multi-turn dialogue, where models keep obeying constraints the user has explicitly revoked, and builds a black-box system that ledgers each constraint with an executable checker, records revocations, and compiles the net constraint state before generation. A sequential ablation probe measures per-clause adherence and enables targeted repair.

entry.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

author.name: Pan Wang, Yihao Hu, Hang Wang, Zirui Lv, Xin Zhang, Jianshe Li, Jiang-Ming Yang, Wei Wu, Yongqi Tong

entry.summary: Argues that generic self-correction playbooks hurt agents when only a coarse failure signal is available, and proposes a diagnosis-first approach that uses development-set failure analysis to decide which repair interventions are permissible at test time. The aim is a narrower, better-matched recovery interface for language agents.

entry.title: RT-SEMamba: Real-Time Speech Enhancement Mamba via Progressive Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Rong Chao, Sung-Feng Huang, Moreno La Quatra, Sabato Marco Siniscalchi, Wen-Huang Cheng, Szu-Wei Fu, Yu Tsao

entry.summary: Presents a fully causal speech enhancement model built on state-space blocks that keeps a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing attention cache, plus a progressive distillation scheme that compresses an eight-layer teacher into a one-layer student. The distilled model recovers much of the quality gap under a 25 millisecond latency budget.

entry.title: Towards Physics-Faithful Generation of Scientific Diagrams

author.name: Minghui Zhang, Jinxin Shi, Yifan Chang, Liangliang Zhao, Yuandong Pu, Qian Yu, Ming Hu, Hanxiao Zhang, Yun Gu, Yirong Chen, Yu Qiao, Bo Zhang, Xiangchao Yan, Bin Fu, Yihao Liu

entry.summary: Princigram is a text-to-image system for physics diagrams that must be physically correct, not merely photorealistic, using a structured physical chain-of-thought schema per subdiscipline to decompose the diagram before generation. It targets the failure of web-trained generators to get force directions, coordinate systems, and thermodynamic states right. Matters for education and scientific communication where plausible-but-wrong figures are harmful.

entry.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design

author.name: Yaxin Luo, Haobin Jiang, Jialv Zou, Xu Huang, Wenhao Yan, Haodong Li, Zhengrong Yue, Jing Li, Xiaofu Chen, Xiaohan Zhao, Jiacheng Liu, Jiacheng Cui, Zhiqiang Shen, Xiaotong Li

entry.summary: AutoDesign frames turning multimodal sources into structured media artifacts as a long-horizon agentic process and has a meta-harness optimizer guide a code agent to recursively improve its own scaffolding from rollout feedback, aligned with human design priors. It is instantiated on academic paper-to-poster generation with a new benchmark. Contributes to the self-improving agent harness literature.

entry.title: EnterpriseRAG: Benchmarking LLM Instruction Adherence and Robustness under Non-Ideal Enterprise Retrieval

author.name: Huiqi Miao, Xinbao Sun, Bo Wang, Fanyu Meng, Lijun Mei, Na Wu, Di Jin, Chao Deng, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: EnterpriseRAG is a 983-sample expert-validated benchmark simulating retrieval noise, knowledge gaps, and factual conflicts alongside complex multi-constraint instructions across six domains. Across 13 leading LLMs it exposes a 57-point orchestration gap: about 80 percent of individual constraints are satisfied but only 26.8 percent of responses satisfy all of them at once.

entry.title: Governing Agentic AI in FinTech

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: Defines a verifiability gap for financial agentic AI as the shortfall between the verification that delegated authority demands and the explainability plus reproducibility actually retained, indexed to a verifier and audit lag. Tests the resulting governance theory empirically across nine model versions from a small local model to a frontier commercial system.

entry.title: From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Yuxuan Chen, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou

entry.summary: Closes the loop on video reflection removal by physically simulating paired reflected and clean videos in structure space, rendering them with a trained video diffusion renderer, then training a temporally coherent diffusion dereflection model and releasing an evaluation benchmark. Addresses the absence of paired video data that has held this task back relative to single-image reflection removal.

entry.title: Class Activation Mapping in Explainable Computer Vision: A Method-Centered Review of CNN, Transformer, and Foundation-Model-Era Visual Explanations

author.name: AmirHossein Eshghi, Hamid Saadatfar, Seyyed Ali Hoseini, AmirMohsen Eshghi, Siavash Arjomand Bigdel

entry.summary: A method-centered review of class activation mapping approaches spanning gradient-based, gradient-free, high-resolution, weakly supervised, transformer token attribution, causal, and foundation-model-era variants using CLIP, DINO, and SAM. Traces the field from the original 2016 formulation to current practice.

entry.title: Exploring Oversmoothing with Householder Matrices

author.name: Bhaskar Karol

entry.summary: Studies a graph neural network in which aggregated neighborhood messages only determine a reflection direction, and node embeddings are updated by norm-preserving Householder reflectors followed by GroupSort. Proves layerwise norm preservation and related properties as a structural defense against oversmoothing in deep GNNs.

entry.title: Unified Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Complex Graph Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Fali Wang, Ali Al-Lawati, Iliyas Bektas, Jinxuan Fang, Alek Melenski, Tianxiang Zhao, Yao Ma, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: Presents a semi-automatic five-stage framework for generating graph reasoning benchmarks for language models, scaling along graph size, task complexity, description style, graph serialization format and reasoning mode. It enables unified comparison of text-based versus code-based reasoning on controlled, programmatically generated instances.

entry.title: Evaluating AlphaEarth Foundations Embeddings for Wildfire Susceptibility Mapping

author.name: Yuan Zhuang, Sanaa Hobeichi, Peng Shi, Fei Huang

entry.summary: Evaluates whether general-purpose geospatial embeddings from AlphaEarth Foundations can replace hand-assembled physical variables for wildfire susceptibility mapping, using Victoria, Australia from 2017 to 2025. Embedding-based models reconstruct standard predictors accurately and reach ROC-AUC above 0.92 downstream.

entry.title: EgoCITE: Context-Augmented Indexing and Time-Aware Retrieval for Long-Horizon Egocentric Memory

author.name: Le Zhang, Ke Sun

entry.summary: Targets two failures in long-horizon egocentric memory: indices built from context-poor captions and retrieval that ignores the temporal intent of a question. The system rewrites fragmentary captions and transcripts into self-contained atomic memories and organizes them into complementary action, activity, utterance, and conversation records for time-aware retrieval.

entry.title: Scaling Representation Diversity: Modulated Attention and Reconstructive Regularization for Visual Grounding

author.name: Junyi Hu, Tian Bai, Fengyi Wu, Yian Huang, Wei Wen, Zaoli Li, Junli Lin, Xingchen Li, Zhenming Peng, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Revisits referring expression comprehension as unified open-vocabulary grounding and identifies representation degeneration as the barrier to a single generalist model. It combines a modulated attention contrastive head with a text-conditioned predictive auxiliary stream that adds training-time gradient support without inference cost.

entry.title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Wenyu Li, Sidun Liu, Tongrui Hu, Peng Qiao, Yong Dou

entry.summary: Observes that in query-based feed-forward Gaussian splatting the Gaussians decoded from one query often scatter across unrelated scene regions, and fixes this by attaching an explicit 3D anchor with a center and support radius to each query. Anchors are refined across decoder layers to enforce spatial coherence.

entry.title: Bias Mitigation in Face Recognition via Demographic-based Supervised Contrastive Learning

author.name: Yu Linghu, Salman Mohammad, Xinyi Zhang, Manuel G\"unther

entry.summary: Argues that face recognition fairness must be improved in the tail of the non-match score distribution where low false-match operating points live, not just in distribution means. It proposes a demographic-aware supervised contrastive loss aimed specifically at that tail behavior.

entry.title: ContactGuard: Pre-Contact Execution Monitoring with Action-Conditioned Latent World Models

author.name: Gehan Zheng, Matthew Johnson-Roberson, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: ContactGuard monitors robot policy execution before contact is made, predicting the short-horizon latent visual consequence of the policy's planned action chunk and aborting when failure looks likely, trained from unlabelled trajectories without pixel reconstruction. It addresses the problem that contact-rich failures are usually detected only after the robot has already pushed, slipped, or knocked the object. Practical safety layer for visuomotor policies.

entry.title: NestDex: Nested Policy Learning with Copilot Assisted Teleoperation for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: James Zhao, Jinhe Tang, Mingyuan Ba, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: NestDex reduces the burden of collecting dexterous manipulation demonstrations by nesting a learned hand-skill policy inside human teleoperation: the operator commands the arm and toggles hand skills through a single degree-of-freedom clutch instead of specifying full finger trajectories. This copilot-assisted data collection then feeds outer policy learning.

entry.title: A Forced-Structure Reduction and Verifiable Bounds for Conway's 99-Graph

author.name: Aalok Thakkar

entry.summary: Reports an autonomous AI research agent attacking Conway's 99-graph problem, producing verifiable partial results including an exhaustive ceiling on circulant constructions and a forced-structure reduction to a 12-regular graph on 84 vertices. The contributions are machine-checkable rather than a full existence resolution.

entry.title: Harnessing agent memory to build lifelong AI partners for materials scientists

author.name: Siyu Liu, Bo Hu, Beilin Ye, He Cao, David J. Srolovitz, Tongqi Wen

entry.summary: Argues that a lifelong AI partner for materials science should be architected around persistent, portable memory rather than a specific agent implementation, and presents a self-evolving memory framework that stores experience as inspectable facts and executable skills. The aim is reproducibility and transfer of tacit research know-how across agents.

entry.title: Synchronizing Beliefs with Second-Order Theory-of-Mind in Human-Autonomy Teams (Extended Version)

author.name: Jack Mirenzi, Henny Admoni

entry.summary: Recasts preference-based reward learning as active human teaching: because the human knows the objective, they can construct more informative comparisons than learner-generated queries, provided they model what the learner currently believes. Implements second-order theory-of-mind belief synchronization for human-autonomy teams.

entry.title: CORA-Diff: Confidence-Oriented Residual Acceptance for Efficient Diffusion Language Model Inference

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yufeng Zhang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: CORA-Diff accelerates diffusion language model decoding by keeping the original transfer rule intact and applying confidence-and-persistence gating only to positions the rule leaves unresolved, letting blocks terminate early. It is training-free and avoids learned filters or cache-specific machinery.

entry.title: Glance, Scrutinize, and Think: Advancing Video Anomaly Detection from Training-Free to Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Shibo Gao, Peipei Yang, Xu-Yao Zhang, Linlin Huang

entry.summary: Tackles the split between DNN methods that localize when anomalies occur and LLM methods that explain what happened by introducing a human-inspired global-to-local paradigm: glance to form temporal hypotheses, scrutinize suspicious segments, then iteratively rethink. Includes a training-free variant and an agentic reasoning extension for video anomaly detection.

entry.title: Social Chain of Thought: A Multi-Agent Architecture Grounded in Medical Differential Diagnosis Methodology

author.name: Del Coburn, Scott Sanner, Dan Silver

entry.summary: Social Chain of Thought structures multi-round LLM interaction around clinical differential-diagnosis methodology, aiming to make specialist reasoning explicit and transparent for complex cases. The paper asks when multi-agent structure is actually needed and where it beats monolithic inference rather than assuming it helps.

entry.title: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications

author.name: Linqiang Guo (Peter), Li Gu (Peter), Zihuan Jiang (Peter), Zhixiang Chi (Peter), Siobhan Reid (Peter), Ziqiang Wang (Peter), Yuanhao Yu (Peter), Wei Liu (Peter), Yang Wang (Peter), Tse-Hsun (Peter), Chen

entry.summary: CoAdapt-GUI performs test-time adaptation for mobile GUI agents facing unseen apps without target demonstrations, jointly updating a structured workflow context and a LoRA policy from the agent's own rollouts and rewards. The workflow context deliberately keeps transferable procedures and verification rules while excluding source-app-specific interface details.

entry.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Sen Xu, Wei Wang, Shixi Liu, Jixin Min, Yingwei Dai, Zhibin Yin, Yirong Chen, Junlin Zhang

entry.summary: CLR reallocates test-time compute from sampling more solutions toward targeted verification, condensing each reasoning trace into a compact set of decision-critical claims and attempting semantic falsification of those claims. It exploits the asymmetry that refuting a specific claim is easier than constructing a fully correct solution, and requires no training.

entry.title: CTBench: Evaluating Troubleshooting Capabilities of AI Agents in Realistic Telecom Network Operations

author.name: Xingyu Yan, Tingting Dai, Antonio De Domenico, Mohamed Sana, Nicola Piovesan, Changchang Li, Bowen Liu, Kun Jiang, Mengjie Zhang, Dingcheng Shan, Jing-Cheng Pang, Chenwei Wu, Sijie Wu, Lianying Chao, Haoran Cai, Jiantao Ye, Xubin Li, Simon Mark Lucas, Xin Chen
