entry.summary: CTBench is an expert-constructed public benchmark for telecom network troubleshooting agents, focused on root cause analysis and path restoration in partially observable multi-vendor environments with diverse devices, protocols, and interfaces. Tasks carry rich metadata including golden reference procedures.

entry.title: Backtrader-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Algorithmic Trading with Self-Generated MCQs

author.name: Ruoxi Zhao, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: Builds a contamination-resistant benchmark for LLM coding agents in algorithmic trading by auto-generating multiple-choice questions from executable backtest configurations, plus a generator-solver loop that keeps only questions unanswerable without running code. Addresses the difficulty of grading agents whose outputs are numerical backtest results.

entry.title: Advancing MLLM-based UAV Image Understanding and Reasoning: A Benchmark and a Training-Free Multi-Agent System

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Shuoxun Zhang, Peng Ye, Lin Zhang, Jiakang Yuan, Shenghong Yi, Yuening Wang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark of 1500 human-annotated question-answer pairs from thirteen public drone datasets spanning six capability dimensions and sixteen tasks, then proposes a training-free multi-agent system to handle extreme scale variation, arbitrary camera orientation, and dense objects in aerial imagery. Provides the first unified assessment of aerial understanding and reasoning for multimodal models.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Probabilistic Constrained Clustering from Entangled Pairwise Supervision

author.name: Shaojie Zhang, Ke Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes constrained clustering when pairwise supervision is real-valued and entangles intrinsic ambiguity, annotator judgment, and noise, defining an aleatoric target and analyzing its identifiability. Introduces an angular pairwise objective and an estimator-corrector-integrator pipeline.

entry.title: A Neighborhood Attention Transformer Network for Enhanced 3D Segmentation of the Left Anterior Descending Artery

author.name: Rafi Ibn Sultan, Chengyin Li, Yiannos Demetriou, Ahmed I. Ghanem, Joshua P. Kim, Justine Cunningham, Hassan Bagher-Ebadian, Dongxiao Zhu, Kundan S. Thind

entry.summary: NA-UNETR uses neighborhood and dilated neighborhood attention with uncertainty-guided optimization to segment the left anterior descending artery in non-contrast free-breathing CT, a very small low-contrast structure with poor inter-observer agreement. Motivated by cardiac dose sparing in thoracic radiotherapy.

entry.title: Represent, Then Generate: Multimodal-Conditioned Time-Series Generation under Irregular Missingness

author.name: Haochen Zhang, Jiaheng Guo, Yu-Chao Huang, Nicholas Knoz, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: ReCoGen is a two-stage framework that first learns per-modality masked-autoencoder representations of heterogeneous clinical conditions and then generates missing physiological time series from them. It targets the realistic case of irregular missingness across signals and static covariates in patient monitoring.

entry.title: Novel Knowledge-Guided Generative Methods for Synthetic Transcriptomic Data

author.name: Francesca Pia Panaccione, Sofia Mongardi, Marco Masseroli, Pietro Pinoli

entry.summary: Compares generative models for synthetic transcriptomic data and introduces GAN variants that encode prior biology through gene interaction graphs, including a multi-kernel graph-neural-network generator. The aim is synthetic gene-expression data that preserves biologically real patterns for downstream tasks.

entry.title: Virtual Temperature Sensors in Power Transformers Using Neural Ordinary Differential Equations

author.name: Berk Hadzhamolla, Alexander Johannes Stasik, Signe Riemer-S{\o}rensen

entry.summary: Uses neural ordinary differential equations as virtual temperature sensors for power transformers, aiming for the fidelity of physics simulation without the cost of finite-element or fluid-dynamics modeling and without transformer-specific thermal constants. It targets real-time asset monitoring where geometry is unknown.

entry.title: Concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Retraining of Malware Classification Models

author.name: Christofer Washington Berruz Chungata, Martin Jurecek, Katerina Potika, William B. Andreopoulos, Mark Stamp

entry.summary: Compares one-class SVM and minibatch k-means approaches to automatic concept drift detection for malware classifiers, benchmarked against maximum mean discrepancy, and studies adaptive retraining triggered by detected drift. Malware classifiers are especially exposed to drift because attackers continuously mutate samples.

entry.title: Are Large Language Models Reliable Reviewers? A Benchmark for Error Detection in Financial Documents

author.name: Ying He, Zhouhong Gu, Zhecheng Hu, Yubo Zhou, Hao Shen, Jiaqing Liang, Zhaoqian Dai, Shuguang Ma, Fei Yu, Yanghua Xiao, Zhixu Li

entry.summary: Introduces FinED-Bench, a benchmark of over 900 recent financial documents across nine scenarios designed to test whether language models can detect errors rather than just answer questions about financial data. The task is stratified across three levels of cognitive complexity.

entry.title: Evaluation Resolution Confounds Learning-Rule Comparisons in Model-Brain RSA of Early Visual Cortex

author.name: Nils Leutenegger

entry.summary: Shows that conclusions about which learning rules produce brain-like visual representations depend heavily on the image resolution used at evaluation, since biologically plausible rules are only trainable on small images. The reported advantage of untrained or locally trained networks over backpropagation in early visual cortex largely disappears or reverses across resolutions.

entry.title: SSPO: Structure-Aware Similarity-Weighted Preference Optimization for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Yuanyu Li, Jintao Xu, Zijiang Liu, Yongzhi Qi, Ningxuan Kang, Jianshen Zhang, Wei Qi, Chen Xie, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: SSPO improves training of neural combinatorial optimization solvers by scoring all sampled solutions in a group with a dissimilarity-weighted scheme, rather than anchoring only on the best solution or weighting peers uniformly. The paper names two failure modes, gradient signal polarization and baseline redundancy, and targets both.

entry.title: DYSANOS Generative Dynamic Smooth Arbitrage-free Non-parametric Option Surfaces

author.name: Hans Buehler, Blanka Horvath, Anastasis Kratsios

entry.summary: Presents a generative market model that produces full future paths of spot and option prices with smooth implied volatility surfaces free of static arbitrage across all strikes and expiries. A simple autoregressive hidden-state baseline is trained on index option data from 2020 to 2025 and compared to implied-volatility PCA.

entry.title: DonorRank: Donor Language Selection for Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Speech Recognition

author.name: Akriti Dhasmana, Aarohi Srivastava, David Chiang

entry.summary: Proposes a learning-to-rank framework that predicts which higher-resource donor languages will transfer best for zero-shot speech recognition in under-resourced Indic and African languages. It outperforms common heuristics such as genetic relatedness or simply picking a high-resource language.

entry.title: AWARe: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting via Activation-Weighted Adaptive REtention

author.name: Juncheng Liao, Jinfan Lv, Guoming Wang, Jupeng Zheng, Ling Xiao, Siliang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a fine-tuning method for multimodal LLMs that scores parameter importance from activation patterns and throttles updates to parameters critical for prior knowledge, reducing catastrophic forgetting. It targets the practical problem of downstream adaptation degrading general capabilities.

entry.title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels

author.name: Vsevolod Skorokhodov

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why score distillation sampling in latent space produces noisy or artifact-laden pixels: the optimized image can drift along pixel directions that the VAE encoder barely constrains, so the latent looks clean while the rendered image degrades. Controlled 2D experiments and VAE-only optimization support the analysis. Useful conceptual clarification for text-to-3D and distillation-based generation.

entry.title: Topology-Unified 2D Pose Estimation across Intact, Residual and Prosthetic Limbs

author.name: Tianye Qi, Tengyue Zhang, Jiaying Ying, Tianqing Zhu, Xin Yu

entry.summary: ProPose is a benchmark and annotation protocol for human pose estimation that unifies representations of intact limbs, residual limbs, and diverse prostheses including running blades within one topology. It addresses severe representation bias in mainstream pose datasets that almost exclusively feature able-bodied subjects. Important for accessibility, sports analytics, and clinical applications of vision models.

entry.title: CoverPrune: Coverage-Driven Token Pruning for 3D VLMs via Optimal Transport

author.name: Peng Ling, Yingda Yin, Lingting Zhu, Weikai Chen, Shengju Qian, Zeyu Hu, Xin Wang, Wenming Yang

entry.summary: CoverPrune reduces the large visual token counts that slow 3D vision-language model inference, arguing that standard diversity-maximizing pruning discards representative tokens in favor of outliers and breaks multi-view geometric consistency. It reframes pruning as an optimal-transport coverage problem and is training-free. A useful efficiency lever for spatial reasoning models.

entry.title: SCULPT: Subtractive Composition for 3D Part Generation

author.name: Sikuang Li, Chen Yang, Jiemin Fang, Jiazhong Cen, Yuhe Wei, Jichen Pang, Wei Shen, Qi Tian

entry.summary: SCULPT generates part-aware 3D assets by subtractive composition, carving parts out within the native generation loop, rather than segmenting a finished shape or additively assembling parts from predefined layouts. This aims to avoid gaps, interpenetrations, and material discontinuities at shared part boundaries while still exposing editable structure. Relevant to production 3D asset pipelines.

entry.title: H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models

author.name: Dingyi Rong, Yue Shi, Chaofan Ma, Jiezhang Cao, Zongrui Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Yao Mu, Guangtao Zhai, Ning Liu

entry.summary: H2R-Bench evaluates whether video world models can turn egocentric human manipulation demonstrations into robot-centric videos, a cross-embodiment translation that would let abundant human video substitute for expensive robot data. It systematically probes a transfer capability that recent world models claim but that has gone largely unmeasured. Relevant to scaling robot learning data.

entry.title: How Organizations Use AI: Evidence from ChatGPT

author.name: Aaron Chatterji, David Holtz, Neel Rakholia, Prasanna Tambe, Gawesha Weeratunga

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Links ChatGPT Enterprise account records to usage logs, worker roles, task classifications, and public-company financials through March 2026, analyzing over 17 million messages across more than 1,500 organizations at the six-month adoption horizon. Documents rapid growth from both new adopters and rising intensity, and shows adoption concentrated among larger, more valuable US public companies.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations for Improved Myocardial Perfusion MRI Quantification

author.name: Christos Tsepas, Chang Yan, Maximilian Fuetterer, Sebastian Kozerke, Cian M Scannell

entry.summary: Extends physics-informed neural networks with spatiotemporal implicit neural representations to fit tracer-kinetic models to dynamic contrast MRI, improving robustness of myocardial perfusion parameter estimation. Targets a noise-sensitive inverse problem in cardiac imaging.

entry.title: Learning from Multimodal Pseudo-Labels for Robust Open-Vocabulary Instance and Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Duy Tran Thanh, Yeejin Lee, Byeongkeun Kang

entry.summary: Combines vision-language pseudo-mask generation, CLIP-guided synonym filtering, and LLM-based caption reconstruction to train open-vocabulary instance and open-set panoptic segmentation without exhaustive annotation. Targets noisy pseudo-masks, weak grounding, and out-of-vocabulary or synonymous class names.

entry.title: User-Assisted Collaborative Distributed Inference for Efficient QoS-Aware Autoscaling

author.name: Alfreds Lapkovskis, Ali Beikmohammadi, Sindri Magn\'usson, Praveen Kumar Donta

entry.summary: Proposes serving AI inference by combining dedicated infrastructure with compute volunteered by service users, modeled through a high-dimensional generative Markov process with temporal factorization to support scheduling and autoscaling under QoS constraints. Aims to break the link between demand growth and centralized capacity cost.

entry.title: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement

author.name: Karim Aly, Alexei Sharpanskykh, Jacco Hoekstra

entry.summary: TailBooster augments rare extreme events in mixed-type air transport records by combining a generative model with two anomaly-detection layers that enforce operational feasibility, avoiding physically impossible synthetic flights. Targets tail under-representation that hampers delay and disruption prediction.

entry.title: HAMP-LIC: Hessian-Aware Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Yuefeng Zhang

entry.summary: HAMP-LIC applies Hessian-trace-based sensitivity estimation to assign mixed bit widths across blocks of pretrained learned image compression models, using a four-stage post-training quantization pipeline. Aims to enable low-bit deployment without the quality collapse of uniform quantization and to reduce encoder-decoder mismatch across hardware.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Dynamic Threat Analysis for Attacker-Reachable Software Weaknesses in Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Md Wasiul Haque, Sagar Dasgupta, Mizanur Rahman, Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: Uses compiler-precise static analysis across 185 packages of the Autoware autonomous driving stack to identify reachable software weaknesses, then tests whether local open-weight LLMs can generate executable artifacts that dynamically confirm exploitability at 740 sampled sites. It provides a weakness taxonomy grounded in input-to-safety-output flows.

entry.title: When the Knowledge Base Becomes the Gold Standard: Measuring Resource-Shared Evaluation Loops in Entity-Level Machine Translation

author.name: Jinhyung Bae, Dain Kil, Seongmin Oh, Seungmin Lee

entry.summary: Shows that when a knowledge base is both injected into a translation system and used as the evaluation gold standard, scores measure instruction compliance rather than translation quality. Using independent expert annotations for Korean historical person names, the authors quantify this self-referential evaluation loop.

entry.title: PatchGen: Learning Soft Intra-Image Predictive Subsets for Visual Generalization

author.name: Zhaorui Tan, Weimiao Yu, Xi Yang

entry.summary: Hypothesizes that each image contains a sample-adaptive subset of patches sufficient for prediction, proves that restricting to this oracle subset preserves achievable risk while tightening complexity bounds, and learns soft patch subsets accordingly. The goal is robustness to data and label distribution shifts.

entry.title: Erase but Preserve: Controllable Removal of Copyrighted Animation Characters via Optimized Semantic Anchors

author.name: Qiao Li, Xiaomeng Fu, Wangjia Yu, Runze He, Baisen Wang, Jiao Dai, Jizhong Han

entry.summary: Proposes erasing copyrighted animation characters from text-to-image diffusion models by optimizing an anchor embedding in the continuous text representation space, giving finer control than prompt steering and avoiding brittle anchor selection in weight editing. The method aims to remove the character while preserving overall image fidelity.

entry.title: Structured Local Differential Modeling for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Jiazhen Yang, Ruijin Jin, Junjun Zheng, Xiangheng Kong, Zunlei Feng, Jie Lei

entry.summary: Argues from an information-theoretic angle that generated-image detectors are dominated during training by high signal-to-noise semantic content, drowning out subtle low-level forensic traces. The proposed detector suppresses semantic dominance and amplifies low-level statistical responses.

entry.title: NaviDC-OCR: Navigating Document Parsing Across Digital and Camera-Captured Documents

author.name: Peng Cai, Zhaofan Zou, Shifa Liu, Yikun Wang, Jiawei Tang, Kaicheng Yang, Meng Tong, Zhongjiang He, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Presents a unified document parsing framework meant to work on both clean digital documents and camera-captured pages, avoiding the cascading errors that geometric distortion causes in layout-first pipelines while curbing the redundant generation and hallucination of end-to-end approaches. Document parsing is a high-volume commercial workload for vision-language models.

entry.title: NARU: A Benchmark for NARrative Evolution and Cultural Nuance Understanding in Japanese Extreme Long Video

author.name: Yuheng Huang, Jianlang Chen, Jiayang Song, Hua Qi, Aza Kai, Vincent Markert, Edison Marrese-Taylor, Jianjun Zhao, Lei Ma

entry.summary: NARU is a benchmark of nearly 1,500 questions over 155 Japanese long-form videos totaling almost 147 hours, testing whether models can track evolving narratives and interpret implicit cultural and social meaning. It is built with a hierarchical memory-based annotation pipeline and targets a non-English, high-context media setting rarely covered by existing suites. Useful for probing cultural competence in video LLMs.

entry.title: Attention from Action, for Action: Emergent Visual Bottlenecks for Policy Learning

author.name: Zheyu Zhuang, Ruiyu Wang, Nick Heppert, Johannes Fabian Hahn, Abhinav Valada, Florian T. Pokorny, Danica Kragic

entry.summary: Argues that label-free visual bottlenecks for visuomotor policies currently rely on hand-set heuristics (gripper-centered crops, fixed scales, event timing) that misalign when task-relevant evidence sits away from the end effector. Proposes deriving regions of interest from action signals themselves so attention emerges rather than being hard coded.

entry.title: High-resolution Calibrated Probabilistic Hourly Precipitation from a Deterministic Forecast

author.name: Thomas M Hamill

entry.summary: An attention residual U-Net converts a single deterministic convection-permitting precipitation forecast into calibrated probabilistic hourly rainfall, predicting a no-rain probability plus a two-component Gamma mixture for positive amounts, trained against radar-and-gauge analyses. Represents operationally oriented postprocessing rather than a full generative weather model.

entry.title: Poor Man's Agentic Modeling: Simulating Large LLM-Agent Societies on a Laptop

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: Proposes replacing each LLM agent in a large social simulation with a cheap low-parameter surrogate fitted from a few thousand queries, enabling laptop-scale simulation of large agent societies. An interaction-order by memory taxonomy predicts in advance whether surrogate fidelity will hold as agent count grows.

entry.title: Towards Query-Agnostic RAG Evaluation via Query Coverage and Claim Verifiability

author.name: Jeonghwan Choi, Taewon Yun, Minjeong Ban, Gyeonghun Sun, Jae-Gil Lee, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Q-CARE is a reference-free RAG evaluation framework that decomposes queries into sub-queries and answers into atomic claims, unifying assessment around query coverage and claim verifiability. It yields coverage-aware retriever metrics and claim-level generator metrics that work across closed and open-ended queries.

entry.title: RecSys Factory: Bounding LLM Agent Autonomy to Decision Points in the Industrial Recommender Lifecycle

author.name: Dongyang Ao, Kaixiang Fang, Shijie Xu

entry.summary: Describes a production LLM-agent platform deployed for 78 days across three Tencent recommender business lines, organized around the principle of granting autonomy at discrete decision points rather than over whole pipelines. Frames an autonomy-determinism-efficiency trilemma and resolves each vertex with a separate architectural decomposition.

entry.title: The Off-Support Barrier: Why Semantic Safety Constraints Are Not Learning-Problem Invariants, and What Follows for Prior Design, Containment, and Verification

author.name: Yoshinori Watanabe

entry.summary: Argues from singular learning theory that semantic safety constraints such as not escaping a sandbox are off-support objects, not measurable with respect to the model and data distribution, unlike learning-theoretic quantities like the real log-canonical threshold. Derives reward hacking, the weakness of prior-based or penalty-based safety encoding, and implications for containment and verification as corollaries.

entry.title: From Prompting to Behavioral Alignment: Personalized LLM Judges for Recommendation Evaluation

author.name: Alireza S. Ziabari, Kat Ellis, Colleen Chan, Ding Tong

entry.summary: Identifies bidirectional rationalization, where zero-shot LLMs convincingly justify both positive and negative engagement predictions for the same item and evidence, undermining their use as offline recommendation evaluators. Fixes it with a sequential behavioral alignment pipeline pairing fine-tuning with preference optimization to align judges to real user behavior.

entry.title: Learning from Online User Feedback for Shopping Agents

author.name: Haobo Zhang, Kelong Mao, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: LOFA converts heterogeneous, sparse, and noisy conversational feedback from real e-commerce shopping-agent logs into reliable training signal, rather than relying on offline interaction data or synthetic preferences. Targets the gap where deployed agents generate rich natural-language feedback that current pipelines discard.

entry.title: The Sleeping Agent: What Gist-Based Context Compression Loses and Why

author.name: Nicholas E. Kyrkewood

entry.summary: Uses a sleep-inspired salience-weighted consolidation scheme as a diagnostic probe to characterize what gist-based context compression loses in long-horizon agents, evaluated across all ten LoCoMo conversations with about 1,500 matched questions. Finds compression helps some retrieval types while degrading others rather than being uniformly beneficial.

entry.title: TRACE Bench: Task-driven Roleplay Agentic Checklist Evaluation

author.name: Jiahui Zhang, Ziwei Zhang, Yipeng Wang, Yibo Liu, Haozhou Pang, Yikai Hu, Hongyan Ren, Lan Zhou, Qi Gan, Kai Sheng

entry.summary: Presents a roleplay evaluation framework that decomposes each character profile into a fixed checklist, then has a user agent converse while privately tracking which requirements were satisfied, so scores trace back to specific dialogue evidence. Cross-validates coverage against released transcripts from an existing commercial roleplay benchmark.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning based DBMS Buffer Pool Auto-Tuning for Optimal Memory Utilization

author.name: Yifan Wang, Patrick Royer, Rapha\"el F\'eraud, David Delande

entry.summary: Describes MicroTune, an online reinforcement learning controller that continuously resizes DBMS buffer pools to cut wasted RAM while holding service-level latency targets. Compares several RL algorithms on traces combining external and internal database metrics.

entry.title: SegPAR: Class-Centric Decision-Based Sparse Attack for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Dongsu Song, DaeYun GO, Boseung Seo, Jay Hoon Jung

entry.summary: Adapts decision-based sparse black-box attacks from image classification to semantic segmentation and proposes a class-centric exploration strategy that greatly reduces query waste compared to pixel-accumulating baselines. Establishes a benchmark for a threat model that had been largely ignored in segmentation.

entry.title: FM-LLM: A frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for adapting LLMs to time series forecasting

author.name: Rentao Gu, Yihang Ding, Junjie Li, Yi Ding, Weijing Sang, Xiaoli Huo, Xin Qin, Yuefeng Ji

entry.summary: Adapts frozen LLMs to time-series forecasting without textual prompts by injecting Fourier-analysis-based spectral tokens and routing through an asymmetric mixture of experts. Argues that prompt-based modality alignment wastes compute and ignores the spectral structure of time series.

entry.title: Beyond Memory: A Transactional Continuity Kernel for Long-Lived AI Agents

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: Argues that long-lived agents need an explicit control plane rather than more memory, and proposes a transactional kernel where untrusted components propose typed state changes against an exact predecessor head and a short atomic transaction revalidates before activation. Targets stale overwrites, unaudited exposure, and self-authorizing privilege escalation in persistent agent state.

entry.title: HYDRA: Hyperbolic Dynamic Representation Architecture for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Zhao Su, Yuxin Xia, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Qi Zhu, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong

entry.summary: HYDRA reduces the parameter redundancy of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks by mapping inputs into the Poincare ball, performing spline updates in tangent space, and sharing functional transformations through a low-rank prototype block. Targets KAN scalability and efficiency.

entry.title: EGRL: Edge generation-guided relation-aware learning for RNA-protein interaction prediction

author.name: Danyu Li, Ling Zhou, Rubing Huang, Xian Zhong, Bin Zou, Kui Jiang

entry.summary: EGRL predicts RNA-protein interactions with a graph neural network that learns implicit meta-paths and generates candidate edges, aiming to handle data sparsity and cold-start molecules that predefined heterogeneous-graph schemas miss. It offers a cheaper computational alternative to wet-lab interaction assays.

entry.title: Exponential Convex Calibration Dimension for the Multi-Label Jaccard Measure

author.name: Mingyuan Zhang

entry.summary: A theoretical study of the per-instance Jaccard (IoU) loss in multi-label classification, proving that the loss matrix is nonsingular and that exact calibration requires a surrogate output dimension exponential in the number of labels. The proof combines MinHash Gram representations with Boolean Moebius inversion.

entry.title: A Local-Linearly Convergent Algorithm for Nonconvex Equality-Constrained Optimization

author.name: Frank E. Curtis, Lingjun Guo, Daniel P. Robinson

entry.summary: Extends the analysis of a recent gradient-eigenstep method for nonconvex equality-constrained optimization, proving local linear convergence near strong second-order stationary points under suitable step-size and penalty parameter choices. It clarifies when the method reduces to gradient descent on Fletcher's augmented Lagrangian.

entry.title: Easper: An Accessible ASR Pipeline for Language Documentation

author.name: Aso Mahmudi, Ting Dang, Ekaterina Vylomova, Nick Thieberger

entry.summary: Presents an open-source no-code workflow that lets field linguists fine-tune speech recognition models from their existing annotation software using cloud compute. It also studies which recordings to transcribe first to bootstrap a usable model, testing prioritization strategies on three Vanuatu languages.

entry.title: Structuring the Space of Perspectives

author.name: Agnese Daffara, Sebastian Pad\'o, Tanise Ceron

entry.summary: A conceptual review that maps how NLP notions such as stance, sentiment, framing, and argumentation relate to one another, proposing properties that distinguish perspective-related concepts. The aim is to give perspective research a clearer theoretical scaffolding.

entry.title: VOS-Agent: The 1st Place Solution for the 8th LSVOS Challenge (MOSEv2 Track)

author.name: Canyang Wu, Jinrong Zhang, Xusheng He, Ce Bian, Xianjing Han, Jianlong Wu

entry.summary: Reports a competition-winning video object segmentation system that keeps a strong promptable segmentation backbone as the shared dense module and routes sequences to specialized agents for tiny targets or semantically defined identities. Conditional activation avoids forcing a single inference path for all difficulty types.

entry.title: QuISE: Defense against Typographic Attacks on VLMs via Query-Irrelevant Semantic Editing

author.name: Shubin Lu, Jiaqi Yin, Yihao Huang

entry.summary: QuISE defends vision-language models against typographic attacks, where misleading text pasted into an image hijacks the model's answer, by locating query-relevant text regions and replacing them with semantically irrelevant substitutes. It is training-free, model-agnostic, and works on closed-source APIs without internal access. Practical mitigation for a cheap and effective real-world attack class.

entry.title: When Is a Task Vector Enough? An Empirical Theory of Implicit Multimodal ICL

author.name: Jiaqian Li

entry.summary: Proposes a Selection-Realization hypothesis to explain when a simple static task vector suffices for implicit multimodal in-context learning versus when query-conditioned transformations or attention routing are needed. Demonstrations are viewed as inducing a compact family of internal edits from which the query selects, with model computation constraining implementation. Offers a organizing theory for a fragmented set of activation-steering methods.

entry.title: Edit2TikZ: A Comprehensive and Challenging Benchmark for Scientific Figure Editing with TikZ

author.name: Zongyun Zhang, Jiacheng Ruan, Xian Gao, Ruizhu Zhou, Lingcheng Meng, Lining Hu, Ting Liu, Yuzhuo Fu

entry.summary: Edit2TikZ is a benchmark of over 1,500 samples for instruction-guided editing of scientific figures via LaTeX TikZ code, requiring models to recover visual structure, ground the requested change, emit compilable code, and leave everything else untouched. Existing TikZ benchmarks mostly test generation or reconstruction rather than surgical edits. A useful stress test for multimodal code agents.

entry.title: Evaluation of Clinically Steerable Retinal Image Generation from Foundation Model Latent Spaces

author.name: Zuzanna A. Wakefield-Sk\'orniewska, Bart{\l}omiej W. Papie\.z

entry.summary: Evaluates whether retinal foundation models can drive clinically steerable image synthesis, finding that generated representations and images retain demographic and clinical phenotype information when judged by classifiers from the same foundation model, but those gains largely vanish under independent evaluators. This suggests self-referential evaluation inflates apparent controllability. A cautionary result for synthetic medical data pipelines.

entry.title: FUSE: Active Functional Affordance Grounding through Adaptive Semantic-Geometric Evidence Acquisition

author.name: Zhou Chen, Sathyanarayanan N. Aakur

entry.summary: Defines active functional affordance grounding, where an embodied agent must move to gather views that reveal what an object can be used for rather than what it is, and proposes FUSE, which couples uncertainty-driven exploration with a learned amortized planner over semantic and geometric evidence. It addresses the fixed-viewpoint assumption of prior affordance methods. Relevant to embodied search and manipulation.

entry.title: Dion3: Full-Stack Orthogonal Updates

author.name: Noah Amsel, Jack Zhang, Kwangjun Ahn, Ali Naeimi, Austin Feng, Berlin Chen, Tri Dao, John Langford

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Attacks the orthogonalization and communication overhead that limits the Muon optimizer, introducing a cheaper Gram-based Newton-Schulz variant, symmetry-exploiting GPU kernels, and a megabatching strategy for sharded weights. Also proposes orthogonalizing only a fraction of momentum rows per step, improving on prior distributed Muon variants.

entry.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL

author.name: Simon Yu, Nicholas Tomlin, Marwa Abdulhai, Ximing Lu, Derek Chong, Abe Hou, Dilara Soylu, Sergey Levine, Christopher D. Manning, Weiyan Shi

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Identifies simulator collapse: because a single LLM user-simulator is mode-collapsed, policies trained against it overfit to exploiting that dominant mode and transfer poorly to other simulators and real users. Proposes a verbalized-sampling inference-time fix that broadens simulator behavior and a complementary training-time solution, with theoretical formalization.

entry.title: Generative Semantic Segmentation via an Observable Semantic-Image Interface and Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment

author.name: Weize Cai, Yongqi Dong, Zhida Shao, Zixin Fu

entry.summary: Presents a generative semantic segmentation framework where a diffusion-distilled one-step generator renders a semantic RGB image and distances to a fixed class color codebook form an explicit probabilistic interface, avoiding color drift and boundary mixing. Adds hierarchical alignment of multi-level generator features with a zero-initialized projection for deterministic inference.

entry.title: A 12-CNOT Double Qubit Excitation Gate

author.name: Irfansha Shaik

entry.summary: Reports a twelve-CNOT decomposition of the double qubit excitation operator, one gate below the previous best, with reduced CNOT depth and total circuit depth at the cost of two extra single-qubit gates. Relevant to compiling variational quantum chemistry circuits on noisy hardware.

entry.title: HSTGFormer: Hyper Spatial-Temporal Graph Transformer for 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Ruochen Li, Shuang Chen, Wenke E, Farshad Arvin, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei

entry.summary: HSTGFormer reformulates monocular 3D human pose estimation as localized coupled graph aggregation over joint-time nodes, replacing the common design of separate spatial then temporal stages. The hyper spatial-temporal graph gives each joint-time node a local receptive field spanning both dimensions.

entry.title: Keep, Customize, or Exit: Default Design and Token Pricing in LLM Reasoning Services

author.name: Ahmet Bugra Gundogan, Yigit Turkmen, Melih Bastopcu

entry.summary: Models an LLM reasoning service as a Stackelberg game where the provider sets per-token price and a default reasoning-token budget while users accept, customize or leave. It derives the user's optimal allocation in closed form, characterizes optimal defaults via a three-regime rule, and proves equilibrium existence.

entry.title: Wasserstein Filtering: A Sample Selection Method for Robust Distribution Learning

author.name: Yikai Xu, Zhao Chen, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Wasserstein Filtering selects a subset of samples whose empirical distribution is maximally far in Wasserstein distance from the fully contaminated empirical distribution, thereby isolating geometrically influential outliers before distribution estimation. Three tractable algorithms are proposed, including a marginal screening scheme and joint optimization variants.

entry.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges

author.name: Yuchao Wu, Junqin Li, XingCheng Liang, Yongjie Chen, Yinghao Liang, Linyuan Mo, Guanxian Li

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval architecture that indexes documents as events paired with their entities, forming implicit hyperedges queried through SQL at inference rather than building a global knowledge graph offline. It targets structured constraints and multi-hop questions that dense retrieval handles poorly, while keeping incremental updates cheap.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Tier Infant-Centered Audio Understanding with Whisper via Structured Speaker Conditioning

author.name: Xulin Fan, Jialu Li, Mohammad Nur Hossain Khan, Kexin Hu, Bashima Islam, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson, Nancy L. McElwain

entry.summary: Adapts a speech foundation encoder with low-rank fine-tuning plus a target-speaker-aware transformer for multi-tier tagging of naturalistic infant-centered home recordings. A factorized speaker-token design with family-specific offsets improves robustness to household domain shift.

entry.title: Quantifying the Relationship Between Clinical Safety and Environmental Impact in Therapeutic LLMs

author.name: Alireza A. Safaei, Laura M. Vowels, Matthew J. Vowels, Apoorv Jha, Shekoufeh Rahimi

entry.summary: Combines clinical safety scores on a mental health benchmark with life-cycle environmental estimates across 47 model configurations, reporting that the last few points of safety improvement come with roughly sixty times the estimated energy per million output tokens. It frames a nonlinear safety versus sustainability tradeoff for therapeutic deployments.

entry.title: Class Geometry as Supervision for Sample-Efficient Open-World Detection

author.name: Akash Rao, Zhou Chen, Revanth Reddy Palem, Udhav Ramachandran, Ruth Scimeca, Sathyanarayanan N. Aakur

entry.summary: Adds a supervision signal that forces prototype spaces in open-world detectors to preserve estimated visual or semantic dissimilarities between classes, instead of treating each prototype as an independent anchor. The approach targets scarce-data scientific and biomedical imaging with fine-grained categories.

entry.title: Towards Sparsely Annotated Open-World Object Detection

author.name: HeeJu Han, AJeong Kim, Jinsun Park

entry.summary: Defines a new task combining sparse annotation with open-world detection, where an unlabeled region may be either a missed known object or a genuinely novel category. The proposed framework separates known-target recovery from unknown discovery with two complementary mechanisms.

entry.title: Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge

author.name: Arda Uzunoglu, Benjamin Van Durme, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Argues for an Information Abundance Paradox: when training contexts contain plentiful relevant evidence, models have less incentive to internalize knowledge in weights and instead lean on retrieval from context. Pretraining with longer documents is shown to shift models toward contextualization and away from parametric memorization.

entry.title: MaSRead: Content-Addressed Reading of Replicated Latent Stores

author.name: Carlos Baquero, Lu\'is Brito, Jo\~ao Resende

entry.summary: MaSRead lets independent latent-reasoning agents share key-value cache fragments merged by a conflict-free replicated data type, then solves the resulting read problem via opaque keyed tag sets and hard attention masks so a later unknown query can address the right fragments. Multi-hop queries are served by a graph walk over lexically connected fragments.

entry.title: Geometry-aware Incremental Neural Operator for Long-Horizon PDE prediction

author.name: Jiaquan Zhang, Shuxu Chen, Haifan Meng, Yi Lu, Zhihan Lyu, Fan Mo, Wei Dong, Yang Yang, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: GeoIncNO improves long-horizon autoregressive PDE rollouts by explicitly structuring the repeatedly applied latent transition increment with geometry-aware low-rank projections, targeting spectral inconsistency, phase misalignment, and mean drift. It addresses error accumulation that persists even with better backbones.

entry.title: EvoGraph-Mem: Failure-Aware Editable Graph Memory for Long-Term Language Agents

author.name: Yuxi Qian, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: EvoGraph-Mem maintains long-term agent memory as an editable insight graph where each node tracks positive and negative evidence plus an activation state, so stale or over-generalized insights can be deactivated instead of accumulating as memory pollution. The focus is maintenance rather than storage and retrieval.

entry.title: AgonAlpha: Autonomous Alpha Discovery via Prompt Economy and Scalable Agentic Search

author.name: Weicheng Ye, Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Shunyao Yu, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: AgonAlpha is an agentic system for quantitative trading factor discovery that searches over frozen research artifacts including hypotheses, executable expressions, and review status rather than formulas alone, with an adversarial reviewer holding veto power and budget allocation that accounts for pending evaluations. Reports top-graded alphas from independent deployments on the WorldQuant BRAIN platform.

entry.title: CLAIM: Leading Open-domain Active Clarification of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Measurement

author.name: Kuangzhao Yang, Ziliang Zhao, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: CLAIM uses uncertainty measurement to decide when an LLM should ask a clarifying question and which aspect of an ambiguous query to clarify, avoiding reliance on manual annotation or preference alignment. Targets open-domain interaction where answering ambiguous queries directly yields overgeneralized or wrong responses.

entry.title: ExRole: From Team Trajectories to Executable Roles in Multi-Agent Language Models

author.name: Zhou Liu, Chaoyang Han, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: ExRole turns agent roles from hand-written prompt labels into learned executable control variables by extracting future-aware role prototypes from team trajectory prefixes, rendering them as instructions and token-aligned markers, and routing shared LoRA rank slots with turn-level credit. Evaluated on multi-hop QA datasets.

entry.title: Graph-Structured Rubrics: Compiling Rubrics into Typed Evaluation Graphs for LLM Judges

author.name: Xi Chen, Jie Mu, Mo Xuan, Qun Shao

entry.summary: Graph-Structured Rubrics compiles a rubric into a response-independent typed evaluation graph before any response is seen, with criterion nodes plus transformation, reduction, and gating operators composed through typed ports and a readout mapping to a score or preference. Malformed or type-incompatible graphs are rejected at compile time.

entry.title: Do Influence Tactics Matter? Investigating Prompt Framing Effects in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Alex Deaconu, Anubhav Gupta, Manaal Basha, Nicholas Haydu, Gema Rodr\'iguez-P\'erez

entry.summary: Operationalizes eight psychology-derived influence tactics, such as rational persuasion and ingratiation, into reproducible prompt templates and measures their effect on LLM code generation quality. Tests whether human persuasion strategies transfer to prompting practice.

entry.title: High-dimensional Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Learned Variable Interactions

author.name: Hongyan Wang, Jiayu Huang, Haotian Zheng, Xin Gao, Chi Ding, Ying Liu, Xia Wang, Qing Xu, Keqiang Li

entry.summary: Scales multi-objective Bayesian optimization to high-dimensional decision spaces by first learning which decision variables interact, then decomposing the space and running local Bayesian optimization in the resulting subspaces. Aims to break the exponential sampling complexity that confines most such methods to low dimensions.

entry.title: CoQui: A Coordinate-Conditioned Quantum Implicit Generative Adversarial Network for End-to-End Image Generation

author.name: Xue Yang, Rigui Zhou, ShiZheng Jia, Dax Enshan Koh, Siong Thye Goh, Young-Wook Cho, YaoChong Li, Xuezhi Ma, Hongyu Chen, Xin Wang

entry.summary: Reformulates quantum image generation as coordinate-conditioned implicit function learning so that quantum resources no longer scale with image resolution and pixels can be controlled individually. Addresses probability competition in amplitude-encoded quantum GANs.

entry.title: M-Net: Integrating Spectral Features and Physical Field Operators into Deep Learning for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Jing Zhu, Ye Wang, Fumin Wang

entry.summary: M-Net adds explicit mathematical inductive biases to U-Net for medical image segmentation, including spectral features from local pixel-matrix condition numbers and discrete divergence and curl-like field operators. Tests whether such priors improve over purely data-driven learning.

entry.title: Efficient Hessian-Free Methods for Multi-Objective Bilevel Optimization with Nonconvex Lower Level

author.name: Yicong Jiang, Feihu Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Hessian-free algorithms for multi-objective bilevel optimization that handle nonconvex lower-level problems by using a Moreau envelope reformulation into a single-level multi-objective problem. This targets meta-learning and automated learning settings where prior methods assumed convex inner problems.

entry.title: Sinkhorn Linearization and the Spectral Proxy: Unifying the Statistical and Algorithmic Theory of Feature-Parameterized Inverse Optimal Transport via a Single Spectral Sandwich

author.name: Han Dong, Jiaming Li, Yongqiang Gong, Ruixi Li, Yin Liu

entry.summary: Develops statistical and algorithmic theory for inverse optimal transport with feature-parameterized costs, centered on the sensitivity of the entropic transport plan to cost perturbations and a spectrally exact proxy. A single spectral sandwich bound yields identifiability, estimation rates and algorithmic guarantees.

entry.title: Principal Trait Analysis: Towards Deriving "Skills" in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Hunter McNichols, Kai Du, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: Introduces a data-driven method to derive latent prompting traits that predict success in human-AI collaboration, aiming to replace static top-down guidelines that go stale as model capabilities change. The goal is to inform workforce and education recommendations about AI collaboration skills.

entry.title: PseudoMapLabeler: Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Label Generation for Semi-Supervised Online Mapping

author.name: Chikao Tsuchiya, Dhaval Bhanderi, David Ilstrup, Hsinmin Cheng, Christopher Ostafew

entry.summary: Proposes a teacher-student semi-supervised framework for online high-definition map construction that uses distribution-based confidence maps to keep partially reliable map elements rather than discarding them wholesale. Spatial clipping preserves the high-confidence portions of otherwise noisy predictions.

entry.title: RGB-D Video Generation for Improving Human-to-Robot Object Handover Prediction

author.name: Tianyu Sun, Zhoujie Fu, Zihui Gao, Bang Zhang, Guosheng Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Hand2Bot, an RGB-D dataset of human-to-robot object handovers including body posture and facial cues, plus PassGen, a video diffusion pipeline with an intention-aware temporal face encoder for synthesizing handover sequences. A depth-editing strategy is used to narrow the simulation-to-reality gap. Aims to unblock handover prediction, a common bottleneck in human-robot collaboration.

entry.title: Less Annotation, More Interpretation: Prior-Guided Concept Bottleneck Models for Interpretable Cancer Imaging Diagnosis

author.name: Baoqiang Ma, Kenneth Gilhuijs

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid concept bottleneck model for cancer imaging that needs far fewer instance-level concept annotations, combining limited labels with class-conditional distribution matching on unlabeled cases and prior initialization of the concept-to-diagnosis head. Evaluated on mammography and lung nodule datasets across annotation budgets from zero to full. Makes interpretable-by-design clinical models more practical.

entry.title: Splat-based Metal Artifact Reduction in Cone-Beam CT via Polychromatic Modeling

author.name: Kiseok Choi, Inchul Kim, Jaemin Cho, Hyeongjun Cho, Min H. Kim

entry.summary: A physics-inspired, self-calibrating method for reducing metal and beam-hardening artifacts in cone-beam CT by embedding a polychromatic X-ray model into an efficient splat-based reconstruction. It targets the compute cost that makes recent neural-representation reconstructions impractical clinically. Directly useful for dental and interventional imaging workflows.

entry.title: GeoCache: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View Texture Diffusion via Geometric Delta Transport

author.name: Haotang Li, Zhenyu Qi, Shaohan Henry Wang, Kebin Peng, Yutong Zhao, Zi Wang, Bo Liu, Huanrui Yang, Sen He

entry.summary: GeoCache accelerates geometry-conditioned multi-view texture diffusion by exploiting a new redundancy source: geometrically corresponding surface points across views have transferable evolution in their predicted clean signals, so computation can be transported across views instead of skipping denoising steps. Skipping steps would destroy the cross-view alignment that keeps textures consistent. Training-free speedup for 3D asset texturing.

entry.title: SNM-VFI: Symmetric Nonlinear Motion-Guided Generative Video Frame Interpolation

author.name: Jisoo Jeong, Hong Cai, Jamie Menjay Lin, Hanno Ackermann, Hyeonjun Sim, Yinhao Zhu, Yunxiao Shi, Fatih Porikli

entry.summary: SNM-VFI interpolates video frames by initializing and steering a pretrained video diffusion model with correspondence-aware intermediate frames built from optical flow under a symmetric nonlinear motion model, instead of denoising from pure noise. It is training-free and offers motion controllability. Qualcomm-affiliated work relevant to on-device video enhancement.

entry.title: Semantic Radiance Fields as Simulators for Spatial Reasoning in Real-World Scenes

author.name: Nico Heider, Micha{\l} Jan W{\l}odarczyk, Katarzyna Wasielewska-Michniewska, Przemys{\l}aw Ho{\l}da, Martin Schieck, Marcin Paprzycki, Maria Ganzha, Bogdan Franczyk

entry.summary: Proposes using semantic radiance fields, built by lifting 2D segmentations from pretrained vision models into a 3D field that jointly encodes geometry, appearance, and per-class semantics, as simulators for training and evaluating spatial reasoning agents. This gets the photorealism of real-world reconstructions plus the queryable ground-truth semantics of synthetic simulators. Useful infrastructure for embodied evaluation.

entry.title: RoboSynChallenge: Mastering Real-World Dexterity via Generalizing Synthesized Manipulation Skills

author.name: Runyi Zhao, Ruixin Wu, Chengkun Li, Hongrui Zhang, Ang Li, Ruixing Jin, Yueci Deng, Yingying Guo, Lihe Ding, Shaocong Dong, Tianfan Xue, Yanjun Gao, Yudong Luo, Pascal Poupart, Simo Wu, Kui Jia, Wei-shi Zheng, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: A competition report on generalizable robotic manipulation that pairs large-scale synthetic data generation with standardized real-robot evaluation across tasks, environments, and difficulty tiers. The setup tests whether synthesized state-action trials can substitute for scarce real demonstrations when final scoring happens on hardware. Useful community infrastructure for measuring sim-to-real generalization.

entry.title: SAP-Nav: Spatial Semantic Representation Meets Active Perception for Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation

author.name: Xuetong Pei, Jian Liu, Vidura Munasinghe, Bo Miao, U-Xuan Tan, Wenrui Ding, Na Zhao

entry.summary: SAP-Nav is a zero-shot, fully online framework for open-vocabulary object navigation where instructions may reference scene, room, region, or instance level cues, building a queryable spatial-semantic map from actively chosen room views. Active perception serves both persistent spatial grounding and acquiring clear discriminative views for target verification. Relevant to language-instructed household robots.

entry.title: TangPoetryBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark and Rubric-Conditioned Evaluator for Poetry-to-Image Generation

author.name: Haoqi Hu, Tongji Luo, Li Zhang, Boning Zhou

entry.summary: Creates a multi-dimensional benchmark of over a thousand images for evaluating how well text-to-image models illustrate classical Chinese poetry, plus a rubric-conditioned evaluator. Argues that similarity metrics like CLIPScore reward literal correspondence and cannot judge implicit imagery or emotion, or even separate strong from weak models.

entry.title: Multi-AUV Ad-hoc network-based Target Tracking: A Value Gradient Guidance Multi-Agent Diffusion Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Jiaao Ma, Chuan Lin, Guangjie Han, Shengchao Zhu, Qian Zhu, Ying Liu, Zhenyu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a value-gradient-guided multi-agent diffusion RL algorithm plus a hierarchical diffusion control architecture for cooperative target tracking by networked autonomous underwater vehicles under constrained acoustic communication and ocean disturbances. Aims to stabilize training in high-dimensional joint state-action spaces.

entry.title: CW-BASS v2: Saturation-Aware Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Segmentation under Foundation-Model Teachers

author.name: Ebenezer Tarubinga

entry.summary: Argues that pseudo-label selection rules designed for weak, under-confident teachers can hurt when the teacher is a self-supervised foundation encoder whose confidence saturates. The proposed method calibrates on held-out data, estimates per-class noise, and applies a self-adaptive confidence floor that provably keeps retention below one.

entry.title: Chance-constrained selection of sequential intervention strategies from counterfactual estimates

author.name: Minkyoung Kim, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: Addresses selecting among sequences of interventions under a cumulative budget by bounding the tail probability of cost overrun rather than only the expected cost, using counterfactual estimates identified from observational data. It extends prior two-step policy learning architectures that constrained means at a single decision point.

entry.title: Inference-Time Orthogonal Seeding Enables Geometry-Aligned 3D Organ Segmentation for Slice-Propagation Methods

author.name: Md Rakibul Haque, Tushar Kataria, Shireen Y. Elhabian

entry.summary: Shows that single-slice label propagation for 3D organ segmentation accumulates error because it ignores coronal and sagittal evidence, and studies multi-axis registration and orthogonal seed placements at inference. Better seeding improves geometric consistency without extra dense annotation.

entry.title: Dual-Stream Cross-Anchor Correction Grounding Long-Form Captions and the Domain Limits of Object-Level Anchors

author.name: LingKai Bu

entry.summary: Tackles object hallucination in long, detail-rich captions by injecting object-level visual anchors into the language model during fine-tuning rather than only intervening at decoding time. The authors report that existing training-free remedies help mainly for short captions while fine-tuned models still name absent objects in over forty percent of long captions.

entry.title: Contextual Quality-Diversity Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control in Tropical Commercial Buildings

author.name: Tran Le Vu

entry.summary: Applies quality-diversity evolutionary reinforcement learning to chiller plant and air-side HVAC supervisory control, maintaining an archive of policies indexed by weather and load context rather than one scalarized policy, with a deterministic safety shield on every action. Trained on a reduced-order model of a tropical commercial building.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding for Clinical Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Md Maklachur Rahman, Tracy Hammond

entry.summary: Adds frequency-domain conditioning to text-guided medical image segmentation, using discrete cosine transform band statistics modulated by text-derived parameters alongside conventional spatial cross-attention. Targets boundary and texture fidelity in pulmonary infection segmentation, which spatial-only language guidance tends to miss.

entry.title: Ready Cohorts: Bounding GPU Opportunity and Avoiding Host Round Trips in LLM-Agent Control

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes when the small deterministic control transitions between model and tool calls in LLM-agent services expose enough concurrent work to justify GPU execution, defining offline-optimal and online achievable batching shares and computing the optimum via dynamic programming. Evaluated on a replayed multi-session public agent trace.

entry.title: Dual Spatial-Temporal Attribution: Architecture-Aligned Post-Hoc Explainability for Recurrent Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Iyad Assaad Nekka, Hamida Seba, Khaled Walid Hidouci, Karima Amrouche

entry.summary: Builds a strictly post-hoc explainability framework for AddGraph, a GCN plus GRU dynamic-graph anomaly detector, using a dual spatial-temporal attribution mechanism whose components mirror the detector's architecture. Motivated by auditability requirements when flagged edges come with scores but no reasons.

entry.title: Black-Box Knowledge Transfer across Distinct Feature Sets

author.name: Oh-Ran Kwon, Daeyoung Ham

entry.summary: Proposes transferring predictive knowledge from a black-box model into a new input space with different features, by decomposing the target function into a transferable part informed by the black box and a non-transferable residual. Estimation uses abundant unlabeled paired features plus limited labeled data.

entry.title: From Visual Widgets to UI Code: Efficient Tool-Grounded Generation

author.name: Houston H. Zhang, Tao Zhang, Li Gu, Linfeng Ye, Yuanhao Yu, Xinxin Zuo, Yang Wang, Zhixiang Chi

entry.summary: WidgetGen studies whether lightweight tool grounding, extracting observable text and color evidence plus high-level layout reasoning, improves the fidelity and efficiency of direct screenshot-to-UI-code generation. It positions itself between hallucination-prone end-to-end multimodal generation and rigid structured pipelines.

entry.title: ReconSpan: Reconstruction-Guided Adaptive Latent Tokenization

author.name: Lixing Li

entry.summary: ReconSpan forms variable-length text chunks whose content a backward decoder can reconstruct from a single prefix code, keeping that code as an adaptive latent token. One trained autoencoder yields average chunk lengths from about 6.5 to 12.2 tokens, with topic information preserved better than exact details.

entry.title: Distribution Steering via Sliced Optimal Transport Control

author.name: Kaito Ito, Anqi Dong

entry.summary: Develops a finite-horizon feedback control framework for driving a system's state distribution to a target using sliced optimal transport, avoiding full-dimensional transport map construction. Projected one-dimensional maps supply directional terminal conditions that are converted into minimum-energy realizable feedback laws.

entry.title: FSGR: Mitigating Token Frequency Bias for Fair SID-Based Generative Recommendation

author.name: Yuchen Zheng, Sihan Xu, Jingwen Yang, Xiangrui Cai, Haiwei Zhang, Xiaojie Yuan

entry.summary: Identifies token frequency bias in semantic-ID generative recommenders, where frequent codebook tokens are systematically over-predicted due to imbalanced codebooks, popularity bias and maximum likelihood training. The proposed method targets fairer exposure across item categories.

entry.title: TraVEL: Trajectory-Guided Video Embedding Learning for Driving-Video Retrieval

author.name: Yi-Chung Chen, Philip Jacobson, Tom Lampo, Yiren Lu, Jin Yao, David I. Inouye, Jing Gao, Danhua Guo, Burhan Yaman

entry.summary: TraVEL adapts a general-purpose multimodal embedding model for driving-video retrieval by supervising with trajectory information, so that a single searchable vector distinguishes motion-centric events like turning direction or acceleration. It targets scalable log curation without expert rules or multi-stage perception pipelines.

entry.title: Poly-Dialectal Neural Machine Translation System for Bangla Regional Dialects

author.name: Rakib Ullah, Ruhul Islam Rahul, Tanbir Ahmed

entry.summary: Builds a unified translation system covering twelve Bangla regional dialects with multi-directional translation that does not route through standard Bangla. It targets severe degradation of mainstream models on dialectal variation for a language with hundreds of millions of speakers.

entry.title: Surface-to-Skeleton 3D Cephalometry: Estimating Hidden Skeletal Landmarks from CT-Derived External Soft-Tissue Surfaces

author.name: Tomoki Abe, Taiki Kanaya, Kazuki Saita, Mao Noda, Chie Tachiki, Yasushi Nishii, Hideo Saito

entry.summary: Studies whether internal skeletal landmarks can be inferred from external soft-tissue surfaces derived from the same CT acquisition, using 240 clinical scans from two hospitals under a locked retrospective protocol. A hierarchical point-cloud model reaches about three millimeters mean radial error on skeletal landmarks.

entry.title: Dual-Manifold Geometry Guided Representation Learning: Adaptive Coupling between Kernel and Data Spaces

author.name: Wencong Zhang, Yue Zhang, Meiyan Huang, Wei Yang, Qianjin Feng

entry.summary: Argues that convolutional filters and intermediate features form two coupled geometric spaces sharing a channel dimension, and derives a lightweight transform that uses the kernel Gram matrix to guide feature evolution. The claim is that parameter geometry carries structural information usually ignored by representation learning.

entry.title: TennisVAR: A Stroke-Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Large Language Model for Tactical Reasoning in Tennis Videos

author.name: Yifan Mei, Qingling Shi, Changli Wu, Jiayuan Rao, Jiayi Ji, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Defines a rally-level tennis task requiring a model to answer an open-ended tactical question, assign a hierarchical tactic label, and ground its explanation in an ordered chain of specific strokes anchored to racket-ball contact frames. It targets the gap between recognizing individual actions and explaining how they shape a point.

entry.title: Learning Unified Video and Image Representation for Video Face Forgery Detection

author.name: Haotian Liu, Yang Liu, Guoying Zhao, Xiaobai Li

entry.summary: UVIF tackles detection of partially manipulated videos, where only some frames are forged, by jointly training on annotated images and videos through a shared encoder and multi-task objective. Most prior video deepfake detectors assume every frame is fake, which fails on realistic partial edits. Relevant as generative face manipulation tools proliferate.

entry.title: RbFT-Net: Rectify-Before-Fuse Temporal Radar Anchors for 4D Radar-Camera Depth Completion

author.name: Wentao Zhao, Shouxuan Wu, Yongtao Cen, Tianchen Deng, Yuyang Zhang, Jingchuan Wang

entry.summary: RbFT-Net completes dense metric depth maps from cameras plus 4D millimeter-wave radar by explicitly treating accumulated multi-frame radar returns as noisy and rectifying them before fusion, rather than trusting them. This avoids propagating clutter, multipath, and temporal misalignment errors into large depth regions. Aimed at cost-effective autonomous driving sensing without lidar.

entry.title: Reliability analysis for BraTS-GoAT segmentation: a controlled robustness study of deep-ensemble uncertainty

author.name: Riya Deepak Shet, Le Zhang

entry.summary: A controlled robustness study asking not just how accurately brain tumor segmentation models perform but whether their uncertainty estimates flag their own errors, comparing a cross-validated nnU-Net baseline against a small deep ensemble under distribution shift. Calibration improves modestly in-distribution, with the more informative test being out-of-distribution error detection. Directly relevant to safe clinical deployment.

entry.title: MapRoute++: Surrogate-Guided Semantic Routing for Visual Concept Unlearning

author.name: Ashok Urlana, L. D. M. S. Sai Teja, Vivek Hruday Kavuri, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru

entry.summary: MapRoute++ is a challenge submission for erasing specific visual concepts from a text-to-image model, adding task-specific objectives, richer concept representations, and semantic routing to select concept-specific mappers. It reports about 12 percent average improvement over the prior state of the art on an erasure-retention-robustness metric for Stable Diffusion. Relevant to content safety and copyright compliance in generative models.

entry.title: AirForesight: Current-to-Future Spatial Map Imagination with Cross-Space Planning Consistency for UAV-VLN

author.name: Yutong Liu, Xiaojie Li, Mingzhu Xu, Jianlong Wu

entry.summary: AirForesight adds explicit spatial imagination to drone vision-language navigation: it learns a structured current-map representation from sparse multi-view observations, supervised jointly by map reconstruction and future-trajectory prediction, so the representation encodes future-aware structure rather than mapping vision and language straight to actions. Aims at consistency between map space and planning. Relevant to outdoor aerial instruction following.

entry.title: S2-HWM: Sparse Event-Structured Hierarchical World Model for Long-Horizon Surgical Robot Manipulation

author.name: Shuzhe Zhang, Xin Zhu, Yinling Qian, Qiong Wang

entry.summary: S2-HWM is a hierarchical world model for long-horizon surgical robot tasks that learns sparse event evidence from latent trajectories to decide when a high-level manager should update goals, rather than imagining uniformly at primitive-step resolution or relying on hand-specified stages. This aligns temporal abstraction with actual state-dependent interaction transitions under sparse rewards. Targets a safety-critical, long-horizon domain.

entry.title: Don't Cut Corners: How Training Outside the Prior Makes Simulation-Based Inference More Robust

author.name: Chaipat Tirapongprasert, Matthew Ho

entry.summary: Points out that uniform-box priors used to generate simulation training sets create sharp edges where neural posterior estimators degrade, and proposes Tailed-Uniform proposals that pad the box with decaying tails. Networks trained this way produce better calibrated posteriors near and beyond prior boundaries in astrophysical inference tasks.

entry.title: Huber-Wasserstein barycenters for robust distribution-valued data

author.name: Carlos Cardoso-Perell\'o, Alberto Gonz\'alez-Sanz

entry.summary: Defines a robust barycenter for distribution-valued data by inserting a Huber loss into the optimal transport cost itself, acting on individual displacements rather than on the Wasserstein distance after optimization. The paper proves regularity and uniqueness of dual potentials and positions the estimator as interpolating between Wasserstein means and medians.

entry.title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Chaofan Zhai, Yicheng Song, Ravi Bapna, Junyao Ye

entry.summary: Introduces an RL-based AI tutor that jointly optimizes short-term learning, by balancing new knowledge against spaced reinforcement grounded in cognitive theory, and long-term outcomes by modeling engagement and dropout risk. Targets the low retention that plagues online education platforms.

entry.title: Local verification cannot detect non-transportability: a cohomological theory of context preservation in agentic reasoning

author.name: Suyash Mishra

entry.summary: Proves that step-by-step local verification of agentic reasoning cannot detect when a conclusion fails to transport across contexts, modeling evidence as a cochain over a nerve of context space so that path-dependence equals the holonomy of a Cech cohomology class. A Hodge decomposition separates evidence conflict into a gradient part and an irreducibly non-transportable part.

entry.title: Can Frontier LLMs Match Natively Multimodal Embeddings? A Comparison on Hard-Negative Text-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Archan Dutta, Vyanktesh Kanungo

entry.summary: Compares Google's natively multimodal Gemini Embedding 2, an embedding model available since March 2026, against frontier LLMs used as zero-shot visual rerankers on hard-negative text-to-image retrieval. Asks whether general-purpose LLM reasoning can substitute for dedicated contrastive dual-encoder retrieval.

entry.title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces

author.name: Mengyu Chen, Feiyu Lu, Chun-Fu Chen, Lucas Vinh Tran, Jay Katukuri

entry.summary: Proposes an inverse theory-of-mind pipeline for recommendation that reasons backward from observed interactions to infer beliefs, preferences, and decision traits, rather than treating clicks as direct preference signals. Motivated by generative interfaces and extended reality where the system must decide where, when, and how prominently to present content.

entry.title: HUGIN: Enhancing Vision-Language Planning for Autonomous Logistics Sorting

author.name: Xikai Sun, Cangtian Zhou, Kebin Liu, Ke Ma, Xu Wang, Zaishu Chen, Haotian Wang, Li Liu, Yunhao Liu

entry.summary: HUGIN improves vision-language planning for autonomous logistics sorting, formulated as joint multi-scene understanding over spatially disjoint camera views. It combats scarce cross-scene supervision with endogenous data augmentation that recombines verified atomic facts, plus a global context mechanism to counter attention dispersion over long visual inputs.

entry.title: Every pooling rule has its world: matching probability combination rules to situations and stakes

author.name: Tanel Tammet, Priit J\"arv, Dirk Draheim

entry.summary: Derives the assumptions under which different probability-pooling rules, such as averaging versus multiplying odds, are correct, and validates the analysis with Monte Carlo experiments over controlled generative mechanisms. Aims to help systems pick a combination rule matched to source dependence and decision stakes.

entry.title: Personalized Scorer Modeling: A Learning-Based Framework for Deriving Robust Sleep Stage Labels from Multiple Experts

author.name: Seyyed Ali Hoseini, Javad Baseri, Hamid Saadatfar, Edris Hoseini Gol, AmirHossein Eshghi

entry.summary: Constructs more reliable sleep-stage reference labels from multiple expert scorers by modeling each scorer's stage-specific behavior with confusion matrices derived from machine learning models, producing a learning-based hypnogram. Uses public multi-scored EEG and chin EMG datasets with hand-crafted spectral features.

entry.title: Foundations of Independent Component Analysis

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: A self-contained measure-theoretic exposition of linear independent component analysis, developing characteristic function theory and then a graded sequence of identifiability results under progressively stronger source assumptions. It culminates in identifiability up to translation, permutation and scaling for Gaussian-free sources.

entry.title: Who Would You Vote For? Auditing Political Alignment in LLMs: An Italian Case-Study

author.name: Simone Mungari

entry.summary: Audits how multiple LLMs evaluate Italian political parties and leaders across nine criteria using a reproducible prompting framework. The focus is on measuring expressed preferences rather than inferring any hidden ideology of the model.

entry.title: Structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D Plant Modeling

author.name: Meng-Yu Jennifer Kuo, Ryo Kawahara

entry.summary: A framework for reconstructing continuous plant growth in 4D from sparse time-lapse scans, modeling morphogenesis as a procedural process on a structure-aware Riemannian growth field rather than relying on dense registration. It jointly handles topology changes such as new organs appearing and geometric deformation. Relevant to agricultural phenotyping and scientific imaging.

entry.title: SketchSense: Learning to Interpret Imperfect Sketch Guidance for Image Inpainting

author.name: Zian Yang

entry.summary: SketchSense handles sketch-guided inpainting when user strokes are messy, displaced, or incomplete, by simultaneously denoising interacting RGB and structure streams with bidirectional attention rather than either freezing the sketch as a hard condition or cleaning it up first. This lets appearance context help resolve ambiguous strokes. Improves usability of sketch-based editing tools.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Action Recognition with Cross-Attentive Latent Sparse Experts

author.name: Imtiaz Ul Hassan, Tasweer Ahmad, Nik Bessis, Ardhendu Behera

entry.summary: FineX recognizes fine-grained actions by factorizing cues into RGB appearance, pose heatmap geometry, and skeletal graph topology, exchanging information via pairwise cross-attention and routing each stream through a sparse mixture-of-experts with load balancing. It reports state-of-the-art on fine-grained action benchmarks. Applies MoE routing to multimodal video recognition.

entry.title: Learning to Persuade Exposes How Easily LLMs Abandon Correct Beliefs

author.name: Nimet Beyza Bozdag, Emre Can Acikgoz, Gokhan Tur, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Already covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Trains persuader agents with adversarial reinforcement learning to flip a target model's answer in a single interaction, showing that one targeted argument can collapse accuracy to near zero even when the argument is factually false. Frames resistance to harmful persuasion as an unmet reliability requirement for models that debate, advise, and collaborate.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Noisy-Label Time-Series Classification via Dynamic Time Warping Based Granular Ball Computing

author.name: Ziqiang Li, Yun Liu, Gouhei Tanaka

entry.summary: Groups temporally similar training series into granular balls under dynamic time warping and classifies at granule level, aiming to blunt the effect of mislabeled samples while cutting the number of expensive warping computations at inference. Tested on four benchmark datasets with symmetric label noise.

entry.title: Non-Degenerate Risk Certification for Automated Security Decisions: A Decision-Contract Theory with ATT\&CK-Aligned Triage as a Worked Instance

author.name: Zhenpeng Li

entry.summary: Argues that risk certificates for automated security decisions are vacuous unless tied to an explicit decision contract, since a system that abstains from acting trivially satisfies any risk bound. It develops an error-conservation law across harmful automation, human deferral and semantic masking, with an ATT and CK-aligned triage instance.

entry.title: Fine-tuned Normalizing Flows for ALICE Zero Degree Calorimeter Fast Simulation

author.name: Emilia Majerz, Jacek Otwinowski, Witold Dzwinel, Jacek Kitowski

entry.summary: Builds a normalizing-flow surrogate for expensive Monte Carlo simulation of the ALICE zero degree calorimeter response at the LHC, using pretraining on imbalanced data then per-particle fine-tuning with gradual unfreezing. It also proposes conditional metrics that better capture physics-relevant input-output dependence than Wasserstein distance alone.

entry.title: Can Vision-Language Models Assess Proxemic Risk from Egocentric Robot Images?

author.name: Vladyslava Rudas, Dmytro Kuzmenko

entry.summary: Tests whether open-source vision-language models can rate how dangerous a robot's proximity to people is from egocentric images, comparing prompting strategies and light fine-tuning against a random baseline. Zero-shot performance is near chance and fine-tuning helps only modestly, though one model reaches better recall on high-danger cases.

entry.title: Attribute-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization for Controllable Fashion Retrieval

author.name: Najmeh Forouzandehmehr, Topojoy Biswas, Evren Korpeoglu, Kannan Achan

entry.summary: Factorizes fashion image and text embeddings into four named attribute slots, each with its own learned gate balancing visual versus textual evidence, so retrieval can be steered per attribute. Color and pattern lean on image evidence while taxonomy-like attributes lean on text.

entry.title: Mind the Context: Continual Learning of Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via Environmental-Social Disentanglement

author.name: Rafal Robert Karpinski, Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Nikhil Churamani, Yiming Luo, Maartje M. A. de Graaf, Davide Dell'Anna, Hatice Gunes

entry.summary: Studies domain-incremental continual learning for socially appropriate robot behavior, where a robot meets new contexts (living room, office, hallway) over time and must disentangle environmental factors from social ones. The aim is adaptation to new social norms without forgetting prior context knowledge.

entry.title: LLMs in Process Diagram Engineering: From Optimal PFDs to Validated P&IDs

author.name: Timur Zakarin, Sergei Voitov, Sergei Shumilin, Evgeny Burnaev

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline that synthesizes chemical process flow diagrams and then converts them into validated piping and instrumentation diagrams, comparing four methods and favoring a hybrid of genetic algorithms with LLM components. Targets a workflow that is still almost entirely manual in process engineering.

entry.title: From Numbers to Judgment: Specialist LLM Agents and Reinforcement Learning for European Listed Real Estate

author.name: Pardis Taghavi, Santosh Bhavani

entry.summary: Tests whether decomposing financial analysis into eight lens-aligned specialist LLM agents beats monolithic prompting on European listed real estate, holding model, evidence, instructions, schema, and scoring fixed. Decomposition improves numerical tasks by about 16 points but does not reliably help, and can hurt, integrative judgment tasks.

entry.title: CLEAR: Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling for Long-Tailed Classification

author.name: Gawon Lim

entry.summary: Proposes a long-tailed classification ensemble that creates diverse experts through threshold-based structured sampling and then weights them per class using smoothed class-wise precision as a trust score. Aims to fix the gap where multi-expert methods rarely decide which expert to believe for a given class.

entry.title: Towards Model-based Run-time Cybersecurity: On Control-Flow Anomaly Detection, Attack Identification, and Hardware Monitoring

author.name: Martin Sachenbacher, Martin Leucker, Alexander Weiss, Aliyu Tanko Ali

entry.summary: Outlines a model-based architecture that combines software-level control-flow observation with hardware tracing to make intrusion detection and attack-tree identification robust to attackers who camouflage their control flow. Position-style systems security work rather than a machine learning contribution.

entry.title: Few-Shot Ordinal Learning for Day-Wise Freshness Estimation with Hyperspectral Fish Images

author.name: Kazi Nabiul Alam, Pooneh Bagheri Zadeh, Akbar Sheikh-Akbari

entry.summary: Introduces a few-shot episodic framework for day-wise fish freshness estimation from hyperspectral images, treating each fillet as a task and using a CORAL-style ordinal head to respect label ordering. Motivated by scarce per-product annotations that make full supervision impractical.

entry.title: Demand Transfer Estimation at Scale via Restricted Logit Modeling

author.name: Lakshya Garg, Deep Narayan Mishra, Swapnil Yadav, Haoan Wang, Sujal Alugubelli, Karthik Kumaran, Anupriya Sharma

entry.summary: Presents a restricted logit choice model for estimating demand transfer between substitutable items at retail scale, adjusting independent item forecasts for assortment effects instead of re-forecasting every candidate assortment. It targets the computational blow-up of assortment optimization over large item universes.

entry.title: On the global feature importance for interpretable and trustworthy heat demand forecasting

author.name: Milan Zdravkovi\'c
