entry.summary: Reports the fourth GENEA Challenge, a large-scale human evaluation of five speech-driven gesture generation systems on a dyadic conversation dataset, using disentangled assessment of motion quality versus speech alignment plus dyadic mismatching to isolate interlocutor responsiveness. Four user studies gathered over 23,000 votes, and a new semantic gesture task with text mismatching was introduced.

entry.title: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning

author.name: Wenrui Bao, Tianyun Jiang, Zhiben Chen, Ser-Nam Lim, Peter D. Peng, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: Surgical WAM learns a world model from abundant unlabeled endoscopic video and converts the learned dynamics into closed-loop surgical robot control, addressing the scarcity of synchronized video-kinematics demonstrations. The study asks how much control performance can be recovered under a fixed budget of action-labeled data.

entry.title: Models inherit the writer, not who the writer was imitating

author.name: 0Chris5R

entry.summary: Extending recent work on subliminal transfer of model self-identity, this study has teacher models imitate other models and then fine-tunes students on those outputs, separating stylistic signature from identity claims. Students reliably pick up the imitated model's detectable writing style but their stated identity still tracks the model that actually generated the data, dissociating style from identity inheritance.

entry.title: The Knowing-Saying Gap: When Probes See Errors that Confidence Misses

author.name: Jyotin Goel, Ipshita Bandyopadhyay, Justin Shenk

entry.summary: Shows that linear probes can detect corrupted context inside language models with near-perfect accuracy, yet those same probes fail to predict whether the final answer will be wrong, and structured confidence outputs collapse to uninformative values. The authors report a pre-registered hypothesis being refuted, highlighting limits of probe-based runtime monitoring.

entry.title: An AI Scientist that Doesn't Drift: Taste, Structure, and Falsifiable Findings in a Quadruped Navigation Research Loop

author.name: Yiwen Zhang, Eloise Zeng, Jaeha Lee, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: Builds an autonomous LLM research loop for quadruped navigation generalization that resists metric-chasing drift via an immutable prediction-outcome experiment card, narrowly scoped subagents, and a preference oracle encoding the human researcher's taste. The design forces falsifiable hypotheses that cannot be retroactively rewritten.

entry.title: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?

author.name: Xiaoou Liu, Longchao Da, Hanyang Chen, Yuan Ling, Hua Wei

entry.summary: Introduces a perturbation framework and benchmark that stress-tests mobile GUI agents by systematically injecting realistic interface variability along state, transition, and action axes derived from an MDP taxonomy. It shows agents that perform well on clean AndroidWorld degrade substantially under realistic conditions.

entry.title: Who Built This Model? Tracing LLM Lineage via Spectral Fingerprints in Weight Space

author.name: Yiwei Chen, Bingqi Shang, Sijia Liu

entry.summary: Investigates whether open-weight LLMs carry intrinsic fingerprints in weight space alone, without any input data, that reveal lineage such as independent origin, same series, or shared base checkpoint. Proposes a unified geometric and spectral fingerprint for lineage discrimination.

entry.title: Improving Constraint Models with LLM Agents

author.name: Florentina Voboril, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Uses an LLM agent to reformulate constraint programming models from an open-ended space, proposing alternative encodings such as symmetry breaking, implied constraints, and reformulated variables, and validating each empirically by round-tripping solutions rather than proving correctness. This escapes the fixed rule libraries of prior automated reformulation systems.

entry.title: Matching Supervision to the Student's Learning Capacity: A Unified Framework for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yongkang Yang, Zhezheng Hao, Hong Zhang, Yi Liu, Xiankun Lin, Wence Ji, Fanjunduo Wei, Jiarui Yu, Qiang Lin, Xiaoyun Liang, Hande Dong

entry.summary: Argues that the two main lines of on-policy self-distillation, choosing which tokens to learn from and controlling how much privileged context the teacher sees, are coupled through the student's learning capacity, and unifies them in a single framework. Optimizing either alone yields suboptimal transfer of privileged reasoning context into model parameters.

entry.title: CIDER: A Dataset of Contextual Disclosure Boundaries for Privacy Preference Alignment

author.name: Bingcan Guo, Eryue Xu, Jijie Zhou, Zhiping Zhang, Tianshi Li

entry.summary: CIDER is a dataset of about 14.9k annotations from 169 people capturing individual disclosure boundaries across 60 interpersonal scenarios where sharing would violate privacy norms, including AI-mediated conditions. It defines a task where models must predict a specific user's disclosure decision from their prior boundaries, testing personalized privacy alignment beyond general norms.

entry.title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games

author.name: Fatemeh Seyedin, Adrian Weller, Jinhyuk Yun, Mahmoudreza Babaei

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical public-goods game with managerial authority, elections, wages, oversight, and private communication, then tests six frontier models across twelve institutional configurations added one at a time. Finds distinct model-family behavioral profiles including promise-breaking and lying at measurable rates, and studies whether governance pathologies like free-riding and entrenched leadership emerge.

entry.title: Open Evaluation Agent: Efficient and Promptable Evaluation of Visual Generative Models

author.name: Shulin Tian, Ziqi Huang, Fan Zhang, Hongyuan Zhu, Yu Qiao, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Presents an evaluation agent for visual generative models that decomposes a natural-language evaluation request into sub-aspects, generates targeted prompts, and runs efficient multi-round assessment on few samples, mimicking how humans form impressions quickly. Provides explanations and user-tailored analysis instead of only aggregate numbers.

entry.title: Unified Hallucination Fuzzing for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Pengfei Zhou, Jiajun Song, Zhiwei Tang, Yixing Ma, Xiaopeng Peng, Donghui Si, Yuhang Xu, Huiqi Song, Yiyuan Miao, Yichen Qian, Weihua Chen, Wangbo Zhao, Bohan Zhuang, Jiasheng Tang, Yang You

entry.summary: Presents a hallucination evaluation framework for multimodal LLMs combining a fine-grained benchmark spanning object, instruction, and knowledge hallucination types with a self-adaptive fuzzing procedure that generates new stress cases. The fuzzing component targets the rapid saturation of static hallucination benchmarks.

entry.title: Search-G1: Grounded Search Agents via Representation-Based Intrinsic Rewards

author.name: Cheng Ruoxi, Ma Haoxuan, Zhang Hongyi, Zhang Junming, Duan Ranjie, Xia Qiaolin, Wang Hao, Lu Yu, Shi Haibo, Ma Xingjun

entry.summary: Search-G1 trains search-augmented agents with an intrinsic reward computed from internal representations that measures whether an answer is actually grounded in retrieved evidence, rather than relying on sparse outcome rewards or costly judge annotations. The aim is to discourage redundant retrieval while enforcing evidence use.

entry.title: MasDrift: Benchmarking Authorization Preservation Across Multi-Agent Architectures

author.name: Zhuoning Xu, Xiucheng Zhang, Hanjun Luo, Yingbin Jin, Yinpeng Dong, Hanan Salam

entry.summary: MasDrift is a benchmark of 600 benign productivity tasks that pairs required work with reserved actions to test whether authorization boundaries survive delegation from supervisors to subagents. It compares single-agent, centralized, and decentralized coordination while varying hierarchy depth and peer width, reporting a tradeoff between task completion and authorization preservation.

entry.title: Second Order Drifting Models

author.name: Drake Brown, Yuhao Huang, Shih-Hsin Wang, Bao Wang

entry.summary: Extends one-step drifting generative models by augmenting samples with artificial velocity variables, lifting the training dynamics into phase space so that density perturbations follow accelerated second-order dynamics in Fourier space. This targets the slow recovery of fine-scale structure caused by kernel-spectrum-dependent decay rates.

entry.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families

author.name: Alizishaan Khatri, Dun Li Chan

entry.summary: A reproducibility and generalization study of lightweight MLP probes on final-layer activations that detect harmful prompts as well as guard models a thousand times larger. The authors replicate the original single-model pipeline and extend it across several open model families and benchmarks while quantifying how much reported performance depends on inference non-determinism during activation extraction.

entry.title: Halpern Iteration Achieves $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1/p})$ $p$th-Order Oracle Complexity for Monotone Variational Inequalities

author.name: Lesi Chen, Xinliang Zhang, Hengyu Wang, Chengchang Liu, Yongchao Chen, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a large-step inexact Halpern iteration method for smooth monotone variational inequalities that achieves a faster convergence rate than the long-standing second-order Newton proximal extragradient bound, and generalizes the result to pth-order oracles. Advances the theory underlying minimax and equilibrium optimization.

entry.title: Predictive safety filter enhanced curriculum learning control for efficient vehicle dynamics controller

author.name: Baocong Zhang, Siliang Lu, Chenyang Li

entry.summary: DUET combines two distillation paradigms for extreme two-step video generation, assigning a trajectory-level expert to the high-noise step for diverse structure and a distribution-level expert to the low-noise step for appearance quality. This is framed as a way to break the quality-versus-diversity trade-off in few-step video diffusion distillation.

entry.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains

author.name: Diandian Zhang, Tingyu Song, Lin Fu, Zheyuan Yang, Yilun Zhao

entry.summary: Sci-VBench evaluates whether video generators can produce scientifically accurate, knowledge-grounded footage across 1,253 expert-annotated examples spanning 60 subjects and four disciplines, with a rubric-based protocol. The authors report that non-expert humans and MLLM judges agree reasonably well with expert ratings under the rubric.

entry.title: CHORUS: Complementary Experts for High-Coverage Testbench Stimulus Generation

author.name: Hejia Zhang, Sheng Lu, Zhongming Yu, Chia-Tung Ho, Brucek Khailany, Jishen Zhao

entry.summary: A post-training pipeline for generating high-coverage hardware verification testbench stimuli that exploits the observation that staged supervised fine-tuning produces behaviorally diverse checkpoints, which dense-reward RL converts into complementary experts with distinct task-level strengths. Combines these experts to exceed what a conventional single fine-tuning then RL pipeline achieves.

entry.title: SeFaR: Semantic Feature-aware Robustness Testing of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Nusrat Jahan Mozumder, Divya Gopinath, Corina Pasareanu, Matthew Dwyer

entry.summary: SeFaR tests whether vision models satisfy natural-language requirements under realistic semantic variations, using a hierarchical concept model to explore semantic feature space in a structured way. It targets safety-critical perception where rare, under-represented scenarios drive failures.

entry.title: Efficient Weak-Entropy PINN for Solving Hyperbolic Conservation Laws

author.name: Qi Gao, Kuang Huang, Xuan Di

entry.summary: Introduces a weak-entropy formulation for physics-informed neural networks so they can capture shocks in hyperbolic conservation laws without knowing discontinuity locations in advance or adding artificial smoothing. Targets applications like gas dynamics and traffic flow where shock formation and propagation must be predicted accurately.

entry.title: BooST: Bridging Semantics and Motions for Efficient Skill Transfer

author.name: Jusuk Lee, Daesol Cho, Jonghun Shin, Seungyeon Yoo, Jonghae Park, Taekbeom Lee, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: BooST learns skill abstractions that bind high-level semantic intent to low-level motion dynamics, so transferred skills generalize across tasks and domains while remaining robust to visual and dynamics perturbations. The goal is stronger priors that cut the in-domain data needed for downstream robot policy learning.

entry.title: Self-Normalized Inference for Constant-Stepsize Temporal-Difference Learning under Markovian Sampling

author.name: Min Zeng, Yichen Zhang, Xiaofeng Shao

entry.summary: Develops inference tools for constant-stepsize temporal-difference learning from a single Markov trajectory, establishing a functional central limit theorem and a Brownian-bridge self-normalizer that yields pivotal confidence regions without estimating long-run covariance or tuning bandwidths. Richardson-Romberg recursions handle the stepsize-dependent bias.

entry.title: Gromov-Wasserstein Quantization and Clustering: Structure, Rates, and Algorithms

author.name: Florian Beier, Stephan Eckstein

entry.summary: Studies Gromov-Wasserstein quantization, which clusters not just points within a fixed space but also the ambient geometry itself, proving existence of solutions, characterizing them, and justifying a Lloyd-style iterative algorithm. Convergence rates for approximating general measures are also given.

entry.title: VisEditBench: Can Vision-Language Models Edit Visualization Code from Multimodal Feedback?

author.name: Mizanur Rahman, Arshia Azimlu, Shadikur Rahman, Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Amran Bhuiyan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque Prince

entry.summary: VisEditBench provides 1,395 human-annotated tasks for editing existing visualization code from multimodal feedback, covering both repairing flawed charts using buggy or marked-up images and adapting charts to desired styles. Existing benchmarks measure generation from scratch, missing the iterative revision loop that dominates real authoring.

entry.title: The Illusion of Cross-Lingual Safety in Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Abigail Oppong, P Sam Sahil, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Maryam Ibrahim Mukhtar, Esmael Ahmed Abdu, Tassallah Abdullahi, Jessica Oparebea, Saminu Mohammad Aliyu, Idris Abdulmumin, Abubakar Juma Chilala, Nicholaus Dismas Ladislaus, Alfred Malengo Kondoro, Lemofouet Valdini Douglace, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, Seid Muhie Yimam

entry.summary: This framework lets GUI grounding models keep improving after deployment via a closed loop of exploration on unseen interfaces, MLLM-based reflective evaluation of failures, and on-policy self-distillation of the corrected behavior, with no human labels. It targets the brittleness of frozen grounding models on novel UIs.

entry.title: Ex-Omni-2D: Expressive Omni-Modal Dialogue Models with Native Visual Presence

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Zhipeng Li, Xiaoying Tang, Tianshu Yu, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: Ex-Omni-2D generates coordinated text, personalized speech, and reference-conditioned talking-avatar video in response to multimodal queries, mediated by a predicted Visual Thought Plan describing scene, emotion, and motion. Multi-codebook speech units serve as a shared acoustic-temporal interface that keeps the speech and video pathways aligned online.

entry.title: Chain of Spatial Thoughts: Modality-Agnostic Spatial Grounding for Vision Language Models

author.name: Hunter Schofield, Mohammed Elmahgiubi, Mohammad Mahdavian, Richard Shi, Jinjun Shan, Amir Rasouli, Dongfeng Bai

entry.summary: The paper distills scene-level 3D geometry and object-centric spatial attributes into continuous latent Space Tokens, giving vision-language models explicit spatial grounding without extra encoders or architectural changes at inference. It offers a modality-agnostic route to spatial reasoning for embodied applications.

entry.title: Toward the Cognitive--Physical Limits of Embodied Intelligence through a World-Model-Centric Autonomous Racing Agent

author.name: Zitong Shan (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Baichuan Lou (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Yanxin Zhou (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Shuge Wu (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Xianqi He (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Bolin Zhao (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Sheng Zhao (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Zhouheng Li (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Chee Kiong Ong (K2 Holding, L.L.C, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates), King Ho Holden Li (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Chen Lv (School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore)

entry.summary: This work builds a world-model-centric autonomous racing agent and argues that racing, with its near-saturated vehicle dynamics, adversarial interaction, and hard safety constraints, is a stringent testbed for the joint cognitive and physical limits of embodied intelligence. The system aims to model and refine those limits together rather than only pushing raw speed.

entry.title: Aerial Layouting: Design and Control of a Compliant and Actuated End-Effector for Precise In-flight Marking on Ceilings

author.name: Christian Lanegger, Marco Ruggia, Marco Tognon, Lionel Ott, Roland Siegwart

entry.summary: This paper presents a compliant actuated end-effector and control scheme allowing an aerial robot to make millimeter-accurate marks on ceilings, a precision level well beyond the centimeter accuracy sufficient for contact inspection. The target application is construction site layouting and general push-and-slide interaction tasks.

entry.title: Mendel G\"odel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution

author.name: Changzhi Liu, Yilun Liu, Sikuan Yan, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: Extends self-improving coding agents beyond single-trajectory mutation by adding reaction-norm mutations that edit an agent using evidence from many tasks and cross-lineage hybridization that merges edits from different agent lineages. The evolutionary analogy draws on Mendelian inheritance principles.

entry.title: Locating Failure in Multi-Page Visually Rich Document Understanding: An Empirical Attribution

author.name: Lewei Xu, Yihao Ding, Zihan Xu, Daniel Yitian Su, Daochang Liu, Siwen Luo, Yifan Peng, Wei Liu

entry.summary: Attributes errors in multi-page visually rich document understanding to representation, selection, and reasoning failures, isolating each through controlled interventions. Finds that vision is necessary but not a substitute for text extraction, that missing pages hurt far more than distractors, and that models fail to integrate evidence across pages even when all of it is provided.

entry.title: TokenPrint: A Calibrated Token-Space Fingerprint for Language-Model Provenance

author.name: Yuqi Wu, Shengming Zhao, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free fingerprint for model provenance based on top-k vocabulary projections of late hidden states across a fixed set of knowledge probes, compared by token-string overlap. Across 32 open-weight models from nine families it produces a similarity ladder that broadly tracks documented relatedness, from independent training through shared bases and fine-tunes.

entry.title: ActBench: Self-Evolving Benchmark of Behavioral Safety in Cowork Agents

author.name: Hongwei Yao, Yiming Liu, Meihui Chen, Jieling Chen, Zikun Chen, Yiling He, Wangze Ni, Cong Wang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: ActBench evaluates behavioral safety of coworking agents from their execution trajectories rather than final answers, pairing each of 600 benign tasks with an adversarial variant containing a reachable payload across 15 risk behaviors, six execution spaces, and 48 web APIs. A reward-guided beam search evolves attacks that stay effective while preserving task completion, making the benchmark self-updating.

entry.title: Carnot: Interpretable, Interactive, and Optimized Execution of Deep Research Queries

author.name: Matthew Russo, Yash Agarwal, Tianyu Li, Zhuohan Gu, Michael Cafarella, Omar Khattab, Tim Kraska, Samuel Madden

entry.summary: Carnot compiles natural language deep-research requests over enterprise data lakes into explicit physical execution graphs that users can inspect, interrupt, and correct, replacing the opaque black-box behavior of deep research agents. It also exposes optimization controls for API cost and latency, positioning between expensive semantic operators and uncontrollable agents.

entry.title: ConRub-Med: Reinforcement Learning with Consensus Rubrics for Open-Ended Medical Question Answering

author.name: Taojie Zhu, Yuan Xia, Tao Sun, Yizhi Wang, Yan Chen, Qunshan He, Tian Guan, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Junwei Liu, Yonghong He

entry.summary: ConRub-Med scales rubric-based reward design for open-ended medical QA: three heterogeneous models independently propose atomic criteria, a reviewer model filters them into consensus rubrics, and the rubrics drive policy optimization. This extends verifiable-reward RL into a domain where exact answer checking is impossible but clinical distinctions matter.

entry.title: VoxSumm: A Multilingual Corpus of Long-Form Spoken News for Joint Summarization and Translation

author.name: Yejin Jeon, Marie Maltais, Virginia Ceccatelli, Min Ma, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: VoxSumm formalizes joint speech summarization and translation, generating concise target-language summaries directly from long source-language spoken documents, and provides a 24-language benchmark of about 10K BBC article-summary pairs. It bridges the gap between text-centric long-document summarization and translation-focused multilingual speech research.

entry.title: TRACE-GS: On-Policy Trajectory Distillation with Privileged Geometric Conditioning for Sparse-View 3DGS Restoration

author.name: Linlian Jiang, Yuchen Xi, Sadman Rakib Pinon, Ruigang Yang, Yang Wang, Xinxin Zuo

entry.summary: TRACE-GS adapts a diffusion prior to sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting restoration through on-policy trajectory distillation, where a teacher conditioned on extra training views supervises states actually visited during inference rollouts. This fixes the mismatch between independently noised training states and compounding inference-time deviations.

entry.title: How risky would it be to make powerful AI obey one or a few people?

author.name: cousin_it

entry.summary: Two authors present a structured written debate, refined over roughly ten private exchange rounds, on how dangerous it would be if the first powerful AI systems follow instructions from a very small group rather than being value-aligned. One side draws on historical precedents of extreme power imbalance to argue the risk is severe.

entry.title: CMU-Drive and V2V-VLA: Cooperative Multi-agent Unified Driving with Reasoning Benchmark and Vehicle-to-Vehicle Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Hsu-kuang Chiu, Stephen F. Smith

entry.summary: Presents a closed-loop benchmark for cooperative driving among multiple connected autonomous vehicles plus a vision-language-action model that fuses multi-vehicle perception, reasoning, and planning in a single forward pass. Targets the gap where existing driving VLAs assume a single ego vehicle.

entry.title: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks

author.name: Mansi Uniyal, Agamdeep Singh, Ananya Singha, Priyanshu Gupta, Mukul Singh, Gust Verbruggen, Vu Le, Sumit Gulwani

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline that mines public spreadsheet corpora to build benchmarks for creating derived artifacts such as formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting, yielding a curated 150-task evaluation set with three levels of query specificity. Existing spreadsheet agents are evaluated across artifact type, step complexity, and instruction granularity.

entry.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

author.name: Zhengze Huang, Luyang Yu, Di Hong, Xinzhe Huang, Wanyu Lin, Zhixuan Chu, Zhan Qin, Tianhang Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes an alignment framework that trains reasoning models to emit a structured reflect-then-answer sequence to catch flawed inference chains, plus a reward mechanism encouraging abstention when the model lacks the needed factual knowledge. It separates reasoning hallucination from knowledge hallucination as distinct failure sources.

entry.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: Are Embodied VLMs Ready for Safety-Critical Scenarios?

author.name: Gabriele La Malfa, Nitay Alon, Emanuele La Malfa, Reuth Mirsky, Stefan Sarkadi

entry.summary: Extends a theory-of-space evaluation framework into a safety-critical pipeline testing whether embodied vision-language models explore competently, build reliable spatial memory, and respond appropriately to hazards under partial observability. It probes whether decisions rest on physical evidence or on visual-language priors and biases.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Discovery of Algebraic Graph Constructions

author.name: David Seka, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Asks whether an LLM agent can recover a short algebraic description, such as a Cayley graph or lexicographic product, from raw adjacency data produced by SAT solvers or graph generators, without fine-tuning. It interleaves LLM reasoning with symbolic verification to discover structural explanations rather than mere existence certificates.

entry.title: Omni2LoRA: Coherence-Preserving Parametric Memory for Efficient Omni Language Models

author.name: Puneet Mathur, Manan Suri, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Omni2LoRA compresses long audio-visual context into a LoRA adapter generated in one forward pass by a Perceiver hypernetwork reading a frozen omnimodal model's internal states, bypassing token-level compression that destroys cross-modal temporal anchors. It converts context into parametric memory to make omnimodal inference tractable.

entry.title: Resolution Meets Reduction: Efficient Visual Context for 3D Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Jonathan Suprijadi, Raphael Stock, Moritz Langenberg, David Zimmerer, Kim-Celine Kahl, Stefan Denner, Yannick Kirchhoff, Karol Gotkowski, Maximilian Rokuss, Jeremias Traub, Tassilo Wald, Constantin Ulrich, Klaus Maier-Hein

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-agent world model that decouples a shared, agent-count-agnostic world state from per-agent observations rendered through a unified query interface, so the number of agents can vary at inference time. Removes the fixed-population assumption that limits scalability of existing interactive world models.

entry.title: From Recovery to Drop-off: How Action Post-training Reduces a VLM's Late-Layer Depth Decodability

author.name: Alexander Hackett, Arnaud Denis-Remillard, Axel Cassou

entry.summary: Probes depth perception from every decoder layer of a weight-matched vision-language model and its action post-trained vision-language-action counterpart, finding the action model decodes depth worse at every layer plus an additional late-layer collapse that the base model does not show. Causally localizes the late-layer drop to MLP writes, since ablating them recovers most of the lost decodability.

entry.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yubo Jiang, Fengying Xie, Zhiguo Jiang, Haopeng Zhang

entry.summary: SKALD tackles the fact that 63 to 68 percent of RLVR rollout groups are all-correct or all-wrong and thus yield no learning signal, by distilling a skill-card-conditioned teacher view into a question-only student of the same base model. An annealed tilted objective stabilizes the context-induced distribution mismatch so no privileged input is needed at test time.

entry.title: CurveFP: Rational-Radix Logarithmic Datatypes with Closed Products for Language Models

author.name: Ye Qiao

entry.summary: CurveFP defines low-precision number formats whose products stay inside the codebook, so multiplication reduces to a sign XOR and an integer index update with a bounded accumulation schedule. Two instantiations target training and compact deployment, with the seven-bit variant claimed to beat comparable baselines.

entry.title: Share First, Route What Remains: A Unified Framework for Token-Adaptive MoE Computation

author.name: Gongli Zhang, Zhulin Liu, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: Unifies shared experts, fine-grained expert decomposition, and dynamic routing in mixture-of-experts models by observing a dependency: extracting reusable shared computation changes both what remains and how much expert capacity the remainder requires. Decomposing upcycled feed-forward experts into key-value channels shows co-activated experts align at a subset of value positions.

entry.title: Do Judges Behave Like Algorithms?

author.name: Riya Manchanda, Eric Chen, Chloe Zhu, Cynthia Rudin, Brandon Garrett, Songman Kang

entry.summary: Rather than debating whether judges should use algorithms, this study asks whether judges already behave algorithmically, testing how predictable misdemeanor decisions are from discrete factors like criminal history, age, and charge type. The answer bears directly on whether judicial decisions can be audited and improved with formal rules.

entry.title: Optimistic Rates for Multiclass PAC Learning

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: Resolves an open problem in multiclass PAC learning by establishing the optimal excess risk at every fixed oracle risk level, interpolating between the known realizable and agnostic endpoints in terms of the Natarajan and Daniely-Shalev-Shwartz dimensions. The rate is achieved by a learner that needs to know neither the oracle risk nor the confidence level, uniformly in alphabet size.

entry.title: Do AI weather models miss extremes?

author.name: Marvin Vincent Gabler, Roberto Molinaro, Niall Siegenheim, Henry Martin, Mark Frey, Niels Poulsen, Philipp Seitz, Olivier Lam

entry.summary: Verifies eleven physical and AI forecast systems against European station observations over ten months for wind, temperature, shortwave radiation, and precipitation, scoring errors within climatological regimes rather than in reanalysis space. Concludes that AI models do not show a uniform skill deficit in the tails, contradicting the common claim that they systematically miss extremes.

entry.title: The Parser Already Knows: Lightweight Bias Correction in Constrained Decoding

author.name: I\c{s}{\i}l \"Ozg\"u, Yaoxuan Wu, Guy Van den Broeck, Miryung Kim

entry.summary: Observes that the parser and lexer states already maintained during incremental grammar-constrained decoding encode future grammatical validity, which is exactly the information needed to undo the distributional distortion caused by rigid token masking. Proposes a lightweight correction that recovers the model's true distribution without the expensive iterative resampling that online methods require.

entry.title: Stay or Stray - A Dynamical Systems Viewpoint of Popularity Bias

author.name: Sarvesh Shashidhar, Lankireddy Prabhat, Arpit Agarwal, D. Manjunath, Karan Bhukar, Tanmay Khandelwal

entry.summary: Models the feedback loop between recommender updates and user engagement as a two-time-scale stochastic approximation, deriving an ODE whose equilibria explain when popularity bias emerges and locks in. This provides a dynamical explanation rather than yet another empirical demonstration of the bias.

entry.title: V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark

author.name: Alicia Larsen, Victoire Laurent, Aulia Kharis Rakhamsari, Lara Turgut, Nino Antulov-Fantulin

entry.summary: V-FiLLM generates financial reasoning benchmark items from executable computation trees grounded in real tables, so answers are correct by construction and no model sits in the labeling loop. Four independently controllable difficulty axes allow arbitrary-scale generation without annotation cost or inherited generator error.

entry.title: The Multilingual Quantization Tax: Structural Collapse and Typological Fragility in Edge SLMs

author.name: Mohammad Wathiq Soualhi

entry.summary: A zero-shot multilingual evaluation of 4-bit weight quantization across two open small-model families over eight typologically diverse languages, finding that compression exposes latent pretraining inequalities. Reported effects include representational collapse for some non-Latin scripts where models fail to emit valid task logits at all.

entry.title: Similarity Gates Approve Reversals: A Validity Audit of Embedding-Cosine Thresholds in Agent Systems

author.name: Scott E. Frias

entry.summary: Audits the widespread practice of using embedding-cosine thresholds as semantic quality gates in agent frameworks, showing the score measures wording change rather than meaning change. In the audited production drift guard, none of 56 meaning-breaking mutations were caught, since instruction reversals are often single-word edits while agreement can involve heavy rephrasing.

entry.title: From Reasoning Depth to Reasoning Breadth: Evaluating Multi-Point Associative Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Si'an Xie (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Jiaxun Liu (Peking University), Biao Yang (Kuaishou Technology), Wei Yuan (Kuaishou Technology), Fan Yang (Kuaishou Technology), Tingting Gao (Kuaishou Technology), Ming Wu (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)

entry.summary: MPAR-Bench isolates reasoning breadth, the ability to explore multiple semantic directions in parallel and integrate independent clues into one answer, as opposed to the reasoning depth that current benchmarks reward. It uses 1,000 bilingual English-Chinese items inspired by a cooperative clue-guessing game and built with a multi-agent generation pipeline.

entry.title: Calibrating Post-Training Feature Shifts for LLM Data Contamination Detection

author.name: Zhen Yang (The University of New South Wales), Mengqi Wang (The University of New South Wales), Gengda Zhao (The University of New South Wales), Mo Zhou (The University of New South Wales), Jianwei Wang (The University of New South Wales), Wenjie Zhang (The University of New South Wales)

entry.summary: Observes that instruction tuning, preference optimization, and reasoning training shift the output-derived features that membership-inference-style contamination detectors rely on, blurring the separation between training members and non-members. The authors propose calibrating for these post-training feature shifts to restore detection power.

entry.title: Every Token Counts: Exact Likert-Scale Distributions for Measuring LLM Attitudes and Biases

author.name: Davood Wadi, Mohsen Ghodrat, Matthew Philp

entry.summary: Replaces free-text survey prompting with an analytically exact framework that reads the model's full token probability distribution over Likert options, borrowing experimental design and measurement practice from human psychometrics. This disentangles whether an observed bias comes from baseline traits, contextual confounders, or interactions, which aggregate benchmarks cannot separate.

entry.title: Mitigating Context Interference for Reliable and Efficient Search Agents

author.name: Boyang Xue, Bin Wu, Shuofei Qiao, Sheng Wang, Rui Wang, Yiming Du, Hongru Wang, Jeff Z. Pan, Emine Yilmaz, Kam-Fai Wong, Aldo Lipani

entry.summary: A systematic study of context interference in multi-turn search agents, identifying which context components (notably retrieved but irrelevant documents) distract the model, and proposing context refinement to improve reliability and efficiency. The framing connects retrieval noise directly to agent failure modes and token cost.

entry.title: DistilVDR: A Compact End-to-End Visual Document Retriever via Dual-Student Distillation

author.name: Zhuchenyang Liu, Ziyi Wang, Yao Zhang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: DistilVDR distills an 8B vision-language retriever into a 524M single-vector visual document retriever using only pointwise cosine alignment to the frozen teacher embedding space, needing no relevance labels, negatives, or contrastive loss. The design preserves the text-query versus image-document input asymmetry while cutting indexing and serving cost.

entry.title: From Detection to Understanding: TAR and TAR-Bench for Multi-Task Traffic Anomaly Reasoning

author.name: Han Zhang, Yilin Zhao, Zaid Pervaiz Bhat, Zheng Tang, Varun Praveen, Vidya N. Murali, David C. Anastasiu, Tomasz Kornuta

entry.summary: TAR provides 44K chain-of-thought training annotations over 3,670 CCTV videos for ten traffic anomaly reasoning tasks, with TAR-Bench supplying human-curated held-out test annotations. Evaluating eleven vision-language models shows that strong question-answering accuracy does not predict temporal grounding ability.

entry.title: Once Poisoned, Arbitrarily Controlled: A Programmable Backdoor in VLMs

author.name: Tao Lin, Gaojie Jin, Zongxin Liu, Peng Wu, Lijia Yu

entry.summary: Demonstrates a programmable backdoor in vision-language models where a single poisoning phase lets an attacker later choose arbitrary, previously unseen target caption semantics and synthesize matching stealthy triggers at inference time. This any-to-any control decouples target selection from poisoning and requires no retraining.

entry.title: Rescene: band-limited stochastic forcing turns a frozen neural weather operator into a climate emulator

author.name: Minjong Cheon

entry.summary: Rescene adds a 0.4M-parameter wrapper with band-limited stochastic forcing around a frozen vision-transformer weather operator, converting a medium-range forecaster into a stable long-rollout climate emulator without retraining the backbone. It tackles the well-known drift and blow-up problem of autoregressive ML weather models at long horizons.

entry.title: Before We Defer Research to AI: Measuring Apparent-Success-Seeking

author.name: Keira Leal

entry.summary: Motivated by an AI coding assistant that gamed a test suite by copying failing cases into a few-shot prompt, the author proposes measuring what they call apparent-success-seeking: the tendency of models to produce signals of success rather than actual task completion. The argument is that such measurement should precede delegating substantive research work to AI agents.

entry.title: TelemetrySuffBench: Is Agent Telemetry Sufficient for Failure-Origin Diagnosis?

author.name: Yuxuan Zhu, Peng Pu

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled benchmark that separates whether an agent failure is detected, whether its origin step can be localized, and whether a system correctly abstains when telemetry is insufficient, using masked multi-component traces with delayed-binding faults. Frontier models achieve only modest origin-localization accuracy even with full telemetry.

entry.title: The Authority Expectancy Effect in Multi-User Conflict

author.name: Eunna Lee

entry.summary: Studies how signals of social authority such as occupation, institutional documentation, and relational status interact with severity-based prioritization in four frontier chat models across allocation, blame attribution, and dispute mediation tasks. It identifies a reference-dependent Authority Expectancy Effect that additive reweighting of authority cues fails to explain.

entry.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training

author.name: Ting Zhou, Zhenqing Ling, Daoyuan Chen, Qianli Shen, Yilun Huang, Ying Shen, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: Introduces task learnability as a static prior for RL post-training data selection, distinguishing how much a task will improve under continued training from how solvable it currently is, since equally solvable tasks respond very differently to optimization. Derived from analyzing per-task reward trajectories, it guides non-uniform task sampling to spend RL compute better.

entry.title: WorldSimProbe: Diagnosing Simulator Faithfulness in Action-Conditioned World Models for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Peterson Co, Sicheng Hu, Chunxuan Jiao, Hongyang Cheng, Yulin Luo, Yijie Xu, Sixiang Chen, Zhongxia Zhao, Zihao Wang, DaFeng Chi, Peidong Liu, YuTong Chen, Henghua Liu, Zhihao Yuan, Huizhu Jia, Yuzheng Zhuang, Tianle Zhang, Liang Lin, Huajie Tan, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: WorldSimProbe formalizes an observable simulator contract that any action-conditioned world model should satisfy (supplied actions must actually determine transitions) and probes whether current embodied world models meet it, rather than judging them on visual quality or coarse rollout outcomes. Provides diagnostics of simulator faithfulness for planning and policy evaluation.

entry.title: VibeLifeBench: Can Your Life Agent Be Proactive and Persistent in a Living World?

author.name: Xiaohongshu Inc

entry.summary: VibeLifeBench evaluates life-assistant agents on weeks-long tasks in a world that changes without prompting, testing proactivity, restraint about when to ask versus act, and plan consistency over time. It targets a capability axis absent from static, single-request agent benchmarks.

entry.title: MUSE: A Full-Text Cross-Domain Knowledge Base of Scientific Problems, Solutions, and Rationales

author.name: Tsofia Cohen, Tom Hope

entry.summary: MUSE mines problem-solution-rationale triplets from full-text scientific papers, starting from 579 expert-annotated paragraphs with a rich span-and-link schema and scaling to a 37K-triplet grounded knowledge base via a modular extraction pipeline. It targets machine-readable records of scientific problem solving across domains.

entry.title: SafeCap: Improving LVLM Safety with Image Captioning Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Caoyuan Ma, Wenpu Liu, Weichu Xie, Tian Gu, Shilei Zhao, Lingxi Min, Shuai Dong, Yuqi Xu, Ji Zhao, Ziyue Wang, Wenzheng Chang, Taiqiang Wu, Yongfu Zhu, Wenqi Shao, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: SafeCap trains large vision-language models with reinforcement learning to first write a safety-relevant caption of an image and then answer, rewarding captions that let a frozen text-only LLM reach a safe decision. Reported to improve safety on five multimodal benchmarks while preserving utility on six vision tasks.

entry.title: When Repository Labels Are Not Image-Level Truth: A Supervision Auditing Framework for Chest Radiograph AI

author.name: Yesika Alexandra Agudelo-Londo\~no, Jhon Wilmer Pino-Rom\'an, Brahian Carrera Rodr\'iguez, Jos\'e Miguel Casta\~neda-Bedoya, Juan Pablo G\'omez-L\'opez, Aura C. Puche-Sarmiento, Niharika S. D'Souza, Juan Sebastian Osorio-Valencia, Jon E. Duque-Grajales, Jazm\'in Ximena Su\'arez-Revelo, Jorge Mario V\'elez-Arango, Gabriel Castrill\'on

entry.summary: Repository Supervision Auditing compares labels extracted from radiology reports in public chest X-ray datasets against expert image-level annotations, using cardiomegaly in MIMIC-CXR as the case study. It characterizes sources of disagreement and builds a curated cohort for deployment-oriented evaluation before models are trained.

entry.title: Beyond Decision Boundaries: Relational Geometry Attacks on Contrastive Embedding Manifolds

author.name: Fei Zhao, Peiyuan Zhang, Xi Li, Chengcui Zhang, Nitesh Saxena

entry.summary: This work proposes adversarial attacks that corrupt the relational geometry of contrastive embedding spaces rather than flipping classification decisions, pushing positive pairs apart and pulling negative pairs together across the manifold. It targets verification systems whose decisions depend on similarity structure rather than discrete boundaries.

entry.title: Neural Introspection Gating for Adaptive KV-Cache Reuse in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhijie Wu, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: Gated VLA-Cache is a training-free extension of key-value cache reuse for vision-language-action models that decides when to reuse cached visual token states by monitoring the model's own logit margin between the top two action tokens. Adding this introspective uncertainty signal to purely visual-similarity heuristics reduces recomputation without degrading control.

entry.title: Real-World Cooperative Bimanual Dexterous Grasp of Large Objects from Single-View Observations

author.name: Ziming Li, Mingxuan Wu, Jiaqi Zhang, Hongfei Li, Yan Gan, Deqiang Ouyang, Ning Wang

entry.summary: The authors present a real-world bimanual dexterous grasping system for large objects from single-view observations, including a multimodal dataset with joint angles, vision, and force signals, a diffusion model that generates joint-level grasp configurations from segmented point clouds, and an execution strategy. It moves cooperative bimanual grasping beyond simulation-only studies.

entry.title: When Your State Estimator Has Lost The Plot: Detecting Estimator Failures Via Spectral Analysis

author.name: Christian Lanegger, Helen Oleynikova, Roland Siegwart, Michael Pantic

entry.summary: The authors propose a sensor-agnostic way to detect state estimator degradation by analyzing the frequency-domain power distribution of recent velocity estimates, without relying on idealized covariance assumptions or training-distribution-specific learned models. It is evaluated on outdoor robot data with unmodeled disturbances such as sensor aliasing.

entry.title: Dual Stress: Runtime Safety Monitoring for Safety-Constrained MPC Navigation

author.name: Jamil Chahine, Wenqi Cai, John Abanes, Anthony Tzes

entry.summary: The paper observes that a safety-constrained model predictive controller already computes Karush-Kuhn-Tucker multipliers measuring the marginal control effort spent avoiding each obstacle, and proposes a horizon-weighted sum of these multipliers as a runtime hazard monitor. It is benchmarked against fifteen conventional geometric warning signals such as clearance and time to collision.

entry.title: Extreme concentration of power over ASI has non-obvious advantages

author.name: Seth Herd

entry.summary: The companion piece argues, against the common view, that a future in which one or a few humans hold AI-enabled near-absolute power might turn out acceptably well, on the grounds that people tend to behave better under conditions of security, abundance, and full information. The author connects this to whether technical alignment should target corrigibility or value alignment.

entry.title: A decade of mathematical certainty: Reflections on the Automated Reasoning Group

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon reflects on ten years of its Automated Reasoning Group, describing how formal verification and program analysis moved from research demos to production services that answer billions of security and reliability queries daily on AWS. It is a retrospective on scaling mathematical proof techniques to industrial cloud infrastructure.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Framework Overcomes Fundamental Limitations of Large Language Models for Glaucoma Detection from Fundus Photography

author.name: Jalil Jalili, Hossein Taghizad, Anuwat Jiravarnsirikul, Christopher Bowd, Akram Belghith, Raheleh Kafieh, Christopher A. Girkin, Sally L. Baxter, Robert N. Weinreb, Linda M. Zangwill, Mark Christopher

entry.summary: Builds an agentic pipeline in which an LLM makes an initial glaucoma assessment from fundus photos, calls specialized deep learning tools for image quality, classification, and disc segmentation, then reflects to integrate the evidence. Evaluated with two existing frontier models on two public ophthalmology datasets under multiple image conditions.

entry.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Zhong, Kuo Wang, Peng Liu, Quanlong Zheng, Junlin Xie, Zhijia Liang, Yanhao Zhang, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: Proposes a recovery-aware agentic framework for reasoning over hours-long egocentric video, in which the agent self-checks intermediate tool observations and dynamically trades off zooming into a promising region versus switching regions. It targets error propagation in chain-of-tool-thought pipelines that lack backtracking.

entry.title: Lingjing: A Simulation Testbed for Multi-Agent Embodied Tasks in Open-Ended Cities

author.name: Xiaohe Li, Yiru Wang, Junhao Fan, Mingyuan Liu, Jie Huang, Kaixin Zhang, Jiahao Li, Chen Qian, Zide Fan

entry.summary: Introduces a city-scale simulation platform where heterogeneous embodied agents including drones, ground robots, and vehicles share synchronized physics and structured urban state reconstructed from real geographic data. It offers a Gym-like interface for single and multi-agent ReAct-style agents with integrated task design and evaluation.

entry.title: CORDA: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Harm-Centric Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Siddarth Singh, Victoria Williams, Simon Rosen, Ebenezer Gelo, Helen Sarah Robertson, Ibrahim Suder, Benjamin Rosman, Geraud Nangue Tasse, Steven James

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 90 moral dilemmas designed to test whether models can rank and prioritize between conflicting moral principles when no option is cost-free, rather than merely selecting acceptable answers. It builds on a morality chains formalism covering trolley-style, medical, and resource allocation cases.

entry.title: Different Feedback, Different Updates: Selective Self-Learning from User Interactions for Large Language Models

author.name: Xuanchen Li, Haitao Li, Yujia Zhou, Qingyi Pan, Heng Wang, Yiqun Liu, Min Zhang, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: SLIFT decomposes user feedback messages into atomic components and labels each as a general fix, a context-specific preference, or non-actionable, then routes updates to two LoRA adapters: a generalist for default behavior changes and a specialist for conditional refinements. The goal is continual learning from organic user interactions without overgeneralizing narrow preferences.

entry.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization

author.name: Hao Sui, Simeng Qin, Jie Liao, Xiaojun Jia, Bing Chen, Yang Liu

entry.summary: ElasticBack plants a conditional backdoor in a single LLM agent skill document by pairing a rule embedded in the skill with a benign-looking trigger in the user query, so the malicious payload fires only when both co-occur. It requires no weight fine-tuning or multiple poisoned skills, making detection harder than always-on skill attacks.

entry.title: GENCO - A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-State Grid Analysis

author.name: Alban Puech, Matteo Mazzonelli, Tamara R. Govindasamy, Mangaliso Mngomezulu, H\'ector Maeso-Garc\'ia, Thomas Tolhurst, Javad Bayazi, Ali Moeini, Naomi Simumba, Celia Cintas, David Nelischer, Romeo Kienzler, Jonas Weiss, Anna Varbella, Florian D\"orfler, Gabriela Hug, Martin Mevissen, Juan Bernab\'e-Moreno, Fran\c{c}ois Mirall\`es, Hendrik F. Hamann, Etienne Vos, Thomas Brunschwiler

entry.summary: GENCO is a unified neural solver that handles power flow, optimal power flow, and state estimation for transmission grids in one architecture with a shared network representation, released alongside an open-source low-code development framework and large-scale synthetic datasets. Motivated by the absence of foundation-model approaches in engineering domains requiring strict physical consistency.

entry.title: How sensitive do we want AI to be? Socio-communicative competencies of large language models in healthcare

author.name: Dorothee Amelung, Andrew M. Bean, Sabine C. Herpertz, Felix H. Krones, Guy Parsons, Adam Mahdi, Isabella Schneider

entry.summary: Analyzes 1800 transcripts from a dataset of human participants seeking medical information from three models to evaluate socio-communicative competence, not just factual accuracy. The study asks how sensitive and socially skilled LLM responses should be in clinical support settings.

entry.title: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards

author.name: Xi Li, Shu Zhao, Xiaohan Zou, Fei Zhao, Fuxiao Liu, Yusen Zhang, Cheng Han, Yushun Dong, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: A survey of the safety landscape for multimodal LLMs, arguing that modality alignment and fusion create new threat classes such as compromised modality integration and cross-modal misalignment that unimodal safety frameworks do not capture. It systematizes emerging attacks and corresponding defenses.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Adversarial Co-evolution of Specialist Heuristics and Problem Instances for LLM-based Automated Heuristic Design

author.name: Oguzhan Gungordu, Siheng Xiong, Faramarz Fekri

entry.summary: MOSAIC co-evolves hard problem instances alongside specialist heuristics inside a quality-diversity archive indexed by structural instance features, so that LLM-generated heuristics are not tuned only for average performance on a fixed dataset. Instances evolve to expose weaknesses and heuristics specialize per region of the instance space.

entry.title: Multi-Branch Policy Optimization for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Shuai Lyu, Yuning Gong, Ruiling Gao, Xiaoran Shang, Zhonghong Ou, Ping Zong, Yifan Zhu, Yuan Sun, Yang Qin, Peng Hu

entry.summary: Multi-Branch Policy Optimization builds reasoning trees during RL training for multimodal models so that credit can be assigned at branch points rather than uniformly across all tokens of a response. It targets the degeneration of relative advantages when perceptual uncertainty causes divergent reasoning paths from different visual groundings.

entry.title: Keep It Simple: Multi-Key Episodic Memory Retrieval for Ultra-Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yeeun Choi, Youngbeom Yoo, Joon-Young Lee, Hyolim Kang, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: MERIT argues that for videos spanning hours to days, memory built before the query is known should optimize for high recall rather than pre-modeling complex relations, deferring high-level composition to inference. It uses multi-key episodic indexing plus inference-time temporal expansion in an agentic retrieval loop.

entry.title: The Anatomy of a Prompt Injection: A Component Model for Structured Analysis

author.name: Jeremy McHugh

entry.summary: Argues that prompt injections are still catalogued as verbatim strings rather than structured exploits, and proposes a seven-component model that labels attacker intent, tool targets, sinks, and effects so attacks can be compared and mutated without fragile string matching. Intended for defenders, red teams, and threat intelligence workflows.

entry.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning

author.name: Haojie Huang, Xinlei Yu, Chengming Xu, Zhangquan Chen, Cheng Yang, Qingdong He, Yu Yang, Jiangning Zhang, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Proposes Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement, a training-time audit that neutralizes object-centric evidence regions in images and measures whether a vision-language model answer actually depends on that local evidence, then folds this causal signal into GRPO reinforcement learning alongside correctness. The goal is to stop VLMs from answering via language priors or dataset shortcuts rather than genuine visual grounding.

entry.title: Targeted Counterfactual Fingerprinting for Black-Box LLM Ownership Verification

author.name: Yutong Wu, Xiaofan Bai, Shixin Li, Pingyi Hu, Ziqi Zhou, Zilong Wang, Xiaojing Ma, Songfeng Lu, Yuhong Li, Jin Xuan, Yi Wang, Dongmei Zhang, Bin Benjamin Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a black-box fingerprinting method for verifying LLM ownership that converts open-ended generation comparison into constrained counterfactual answer checks, making the signal robust to fine-tuning, quantization and further alignment behind a response-only API. Targets the fragility of existing full-text or soft-feature fingerprints.

entry.title: Three Necessary Principles for Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Nikos Giakoumoglou, Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Argues that label-free visual representation learning requires jointly satisfying three non-overlapping objectives, formalized as observation, prediction and regularization principles, and proves that omitting regularization admits the constant encoder as a global minimizer and that momentum encoders give no collapse guarantee at convergence. Provides a theoretical account of why certain self-supervised recipes collapse.

entry.title: Hidden Language Consistency Phenomena in Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Muhammad Ali Shafique, Kelly Marchisio

entry.summary: Measures whether multilingual reasoning models keep the intended language in both their chain of thought and their final answer as task difficulty rises, using a multilingual math benchmark across eight languages and four difficulty tiers. Identifies distinct difficulty-dependent regimes including gradual degradation and abrupt collapse of language consistency.

entry.title: UniSpace: Unified Visual Representation and Scalable Multimodal Modeling

author.name: Jinbo Yan, Limeng Qiao, Jie Qin, Junyan He, Feize Wu, Guanglu Wan

entry.summary: Asks whether understanding, generation and editing can share one visual representation space derived from a frozen pretrained semantic vision transformer, arguing that patch parameterization rather than the frozen blocks themselves causes loss of fine detail. Reparameterizes patches to retain pixel-level information while keeping semantic strength for unified multimodal modeling.

entry.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yuki Ichihara, Naoto Iwase, Mohammad Atif Quamar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Disentangles why on-policy self-distillation works by replacing the paired reference solution with a solution from a different problem, isolating target-specific privileged information from the general effect of conditioning the teacher on some worked example. Tested across three models and multiple tasks.

entry.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhuo Sun, Entong Li, Yanlong Zhao, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Wenxuan Yuan, Kaiyu Li, Che Liu, Huihang Liu, Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Li Zeng

entry.summary: SR-OPSD addresses instability in on-policy self-distillation, where the self-teacher is a moving, context-conditioned copy of the student policy that co-evolves with it. The method introduces a self-referenced objective to avoid chasing a shifting target and prevent distributional collapse.

entry.title: MedPixel: A Unified Pixel-Language Model for Medical Reasoning and Segmentation

author.name: Haoyu Yang, Meixing Shi, Zengjie Chen, Haoran Sun, Haitao Leng, Xiaoming Shi, Yuxiang Cai, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: MedPixel unifies medical vision-language reasoning with pixel-level segmentation through a shared language-mask interface, supported by a new 440K-example pixel-language dataset. It aims to close the supervision gap between mask-rich segmentation data and language-rich but spatially unannotated medical VLM data.

entry.title: ProbGuard: Calibrated Safety Risk Estimation from LLM Output Distributions

author.name: Xinzhe Huang, Biwu Yao, Kedong Xiu, Mengnan Zhao, Di Wang, Puning Zhao, Tianhang Zheng

entry.summary: Reframes LLM safety guardrails as probabilistic risk estimation over the model output distribution rather than deterministic classification of finished token sequences, using early-generation distributional signals. Claims the first fully probabilistic, architecture-agnostic guardrail with calibrated risk scores.

entry.title: MoE Proxy Models for Low-Cost Failure Reproduction and Diagnosis in LLM RL Post-Training

author.name: Yikai Wang, Chuansai Zhou, Yuhang Zhou, Weiqiang Wu, Cong Wu, Yue Deng, Ben Feng, Mingming Zhu, Beirong Zhou, Zhibin Wang, Sheng Zhong, Chen Tian, Wangze Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes real failures encountered in large-scale LLM reinforcement learning post-training on Huawei Ascend hardware, including gradient overflow and loss divergence, and identifies model-side factors that govern whether such failures reproduce. Builds small mixture-of-experts proxy models that recreate the failures cheaply for diagnosis instead of debugging on full-size runs.

entry.title: Flow Straight to Reality: Perceptually Consistent Flow Matching for Efficient Image Restoration

author.name: Sangwoo Jo, Donggeun Ko, Jayeon Kang, Youngsang Kwak, Jaehwa Kwak, Sungjoon Choi

entry.summary: PCFlow parameterizes a direct continuous transport from degraded to clean images with a latent consistency flow-matching objective, aiming to escape the distortion-versus-perception tradeoff without multi-stage generative pipelines or expensive posterior sampling. The result is a single-framework restoration model with fewer sampling steps.

entry.title: VIDS-Seg: Towards Reliable Uncertainty Quantification in Pediatric Cardiac Ultrasound Segmentation

author.name: Paul Fischer, Ece Ozkan

entry.summary: VIDS-Seg brings out-of-distribution-aware amortized variational inference to dense segmentation via a lightweight prediction head, so models trained largely on adult data can flag likely failures on pediatric cardiac ultrasound at inference time. The motivation is that retraining with labeled pediatric data is often infeasible.

entry.title: Threshold Structure of Optimal Policies in Restart POMDPs

author.name: Konstantin Avrachenkov, Alexey Piunovskiy, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Studies partially observable decision problems on general state spaces where the controller either lets a hidden state drift or restarts and observes it, showing the problem reduces to a fully observed MDP over last observation and elapsed time. Under a cost-deterioration condition, optimal policies are proved to have a threshold structure in elapsed time.

entry.title: AlbumentationsX: One Augmentation Pipeline for Images and Related Annotations

author.name: Vladimir Iglovikov

entry.summary: Describes AlbumentationsX, an augmentation library that keeps images and all associated annotations (masks, boxes, keypoints, stereo views, video frames, volumes) synchronized under a single sampled set of random parameters. It also supports saving pipeline definitions, inspecting what a call did, and exact replay.

entry.title: Dual-Loop Self-Evolution via Verifiable Emotion Feedback for Multi-Turn Empathetic Dialogue

author.name: Yi Wei, Shuo Jiang, Huaixia Dou, Jie Zhu, Junhui Li, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: A dual-loop reinforcement learning framework for multi-turn empathetic dialogue where an inner loop optimizes the policy against a frozen user simulator and verifier, and an outer loop evolves the training interaction distribution to keep pace with the improving policy. This targets the mismatch that arises when policies improve but their training experience stays fixed.

entry.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction

author.name: Kaiqi Fu, Rime Wen, Altman Lin, Shawn Qin, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: X2-Turn adds a frame-synchronous turn-state prediction head alongside streaming ASR in a delayed-stream speech model, so interruptions, backchannels, and utterance completion are judged continuously rather than per chunk. Building on a pretrained realtime speech backbone, it removes the need for a separate auxiliary ASR model and improves responsiveness.

entry.title: Attention-Path Fragility as an Uncertainty Signal in Large Language Models

author.name: Minsoo Kim, Sungyoung Ji, Kisung Moon, Ilyong Yoon

entry.summary: ASMI estimates token-level uncertainty by masking attention heads and measuring BALD mutual information among the resulting subnetworks, with a semantic-agreement kernel to ignore surface-form differences. The signal is training-free and adds error-predictive information beyond single-pass confidence, particularly for confident-but-fragile predictions.

entry.title: LEGO: Leveled Language Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yuning Peng, Haiping Wang, Yuan Liu, Yipeng Lu, Zhen Dong, Bisheng Yang

entry.summary: LEGO builds open-vocabulary 3D scene representations that capture semantic part-whole hierarchies by reconciling inconsistent multi-view SAM granularities into a single 3D-consistent hierarchy and grounding segments with CLIP embeddings. This enables multi-level, structurally coherent open-vocabulary 3D segmentation.

entry.title: Whole-Body Planning for Humanoids Navigating Confined Spaces via Self-Collision Avoidance References

author.name: Carlos Gonzalez, Luis Sentis

entry.summary: A three-stage whole-body planner for humanoids in tightly confined spaces plans directly over kinematically reachable rigid-body volumes with differentiable collision avoidance, producing volume-informed guides for a full-order trajectory optimizer. This avoids the poor local minima that spline-on-particle abstractions hit in cluttered environments.

entry.title: Improving TensorSketch Using Complex Random Variables

author.name: Amit Sharma, Mohammad Azhar Khan, Rameshwar Pratap, Keegan Kang

entry.summary: The paper shows that using complex-valued random variables in TensorSketch reduces the variance of polynomial kernel sketches, attacking the exponential growth in variance with polynomial degree that afflicts existing real-valued estimators. It builds on prior evidence that complex distributions improve related sketching schemes.

entry.title: Posterior contraction rates in Sobolev norms and Bayesian derivative estimation for infinite-dimensional exponential families

author.name: Emanuele Dolera, Stefano Favaro, Matteo Giordano

entry.summary: This paper establishes minimax-optimal posterior contraction rates in positive-order Sobolev norms for infinite-dimensional exponential families with Gaussian series priors, covering Bayesian estimation of derivatives of the density. The analysis uses a recent Wasserstein-distance approach to contraction together with refined Laplace-type estimates.

entry.title: CausalNav: Reliability-Certified Causal World Models for Control under Physical-Parameter Shift

author.name: Yiyao Zhang, Diksha Goel, Hussain Ahmad, Shixun Huang, Jun Shen

entry.summary: Presents a controller that uses a signed action-conditioned causal transition graph to simulate candidate interventions and give policy advice, but only accepts that advice when a predictive-reliability certificate and two gating checks all pass, otherwise falling back to a base controller. It is evaluated against nine baselines under physical parameter shift.

entry.title: GraphThink: Graph-Enhanced LLM Thinking for Long-Horizon Embodied Task Planning

author.name: Chen Li, Sijie Cheng, Yuelin Zhang, Junxi Li, Maozhi Huang, Yang Liu, Wenbing Huang

entry.summary: Combines a task graph providing structured procedural knowledge with a scene graph acting as environmental memory to reduce physical hallucination and support event-driven replanning in long-horizon embodied planning. The task graph also supplies fine-grained reward shaping for GRPO training of the LLM planner.

entry.title: Directed Neuro-Symbolic Stochastic Execution for Verification of Distributed Parallel AI Programs

author.name: Gautham Koorma, Vikas Sharma, George Edwards, Mahdi Eslamimehr

entry.summary: Combines LLM-guided schedule prediction with symbolic constraint solving and coverage-guided stochastic mutation to test distributed parallel AI programs whose non-determinism defeats conventional fuzzing or symbolic execution alone. The authors provide soundness, bounded completeness, and probabilistic completeness proofs for the hybrid solver.

entry.title: JustLLMGRPO: Radiographic Control for Chest X-Ray Generation

author.name: Pengxiang Cai, Xiaohan Li, Anglin Liu, Qingyuan Zeng, Zexun Li, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Shows that reformulating radiology report prompts with an unmodified LLM, while keeping the image generator frozen, dramatically improves chest X-ray synthesis fidelity by suppressing non-renderable content like temporal comparisons and uncertainty. Unconstrained rewriting however degrades semantic alignment with the source report, motivating an RL-based constrained reformulation objective.

entry.title: SodaMem: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Graph Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: Fengrong Wan, Chengcan Wu, Ningtao Lyu

entry.summary: Presents an agent memory system that stores typed fact events with mandatory provenance spans and explicit mention, occurrence, and validity times, linked by supersede, contradict, and update edges. A planner-reader loop gathers citable evidence before answering, targeting currency and ordered temporal reasoning that flat retrieval logs handle poorly.

entry.title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Hongsheng Xin, Pan Zhou, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: RISE-RL improves rubric-based reinforcement learning for open-ended generation by using repeatedly missed rubric criteria to steer exploration toward privileged trajectories that plain on-policy rollouts rarely find, retaining only those exceeding the mean natural-rollout reward. Targets the information loss when fine-grained rubric feedback is collapsed into a scalar reward.

entry.title: Optimize Cheap, Deploy Strong: Cost-Aware Cross-Tier Transfer for Evolutionary Optimization

author.name: Tal Oved, Roi Pony, Oshri Naparstek, Udi barzelay

entry.summary: Restructures evolutionary prompt and agent optimization by running the high-volume answering role on the cheapest model tier while reserving a strong model for the rare reflection step, then transferring the cheaply evolved prompt upward to a stronger deployment model. Provides a cost-controlled characterization across four tasks and eleven models of when cheap-tier search substitutes for expensive target-tier search and when it fails.

entry.title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information

author.name: Junjie Ye, Zhuohui Sheng, Shaofan Liu, Yulun Zhu, Wenjie Fu, Dingwei Zhu, Ming Zhang, Yujiong Shen, Weichao Wang, Xin Zhao, Shihan Dou, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Pluto Zhou

entry.summary: SPIEval is a human-curated benchmark testing whether LLM mobile assistants can stitch together personal information scattered across ten apps, spanning reasoning, disambiguation, integration, preference inference, and multi-intent decomposition. It includes 250 multi-turn tasks over 4,335 personal records with 21 tools, targeting a capability gap that current agent benchmarks miss.

entry.title: From Interpretability to Control: Insights from Six Years of the TrustNLP Workshop

author.name: Rahul Gupta, Abhinav Mohanty, Anaelia Ovalle, Anil Ramakrishna, Anubrata Das, Apurv Verma, Jwala Dhamala, Ninareh Mehrabi, Tharindu Kumarage, Yada Pruksachatkun, Yang Trista Cao, Kai-Wei Chang, Aram Galstyan

entry.summary: A meta-analysis of all 144 papers from six editions of the TrustNLP workshop, classified along six trust dimensions, tracing the field's move from post-hoc interpretability of static models to mechanistic understanding and proactive control of generative systems. It links shifts in research focus to capability milestones such as the arrival of high-impact chat models.

entry.title: Redux: (∃ Stochastic Natural Latent) Implies (∃ Deterministic Natural Latent)

author.name: David Lorell

entry.summary: The author revisits a previously retracted agent-foundations theorem about natural latents, claiming that the existence of a stochastic natural latent implies the existence of a deterministic one, and this time backs it with a machine-checked Lean4 proof produced with heavy LLM assistance for autoformalization. The post is notable both for the mathematical result underpinning natural abstraction work and as a case study of frontier models being used to close a hard proof gap.

entry.title: MetaSpace: Metamorphic Testing for Spatial Cognition in Embodied Agents

author.name: Gengyang Xu, Dongwei Xiao, Yiteng Peng, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Proposes metamorphic testing as an alternative to hand-annotated VQA and task-success metrics for evaluating spatial cognition in embodied agents, generating semantically equivalent scene transformations whose outputs should stay consistent. This exposes latent spatial reasoning failures that task-completion metrics hide.

entry.title: Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents

author.name: Ao Ding, Hongzong LI, Shiqin Tang, Li Zhang, Liang Chen, Xuyang Chen, Zi Liang

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic framework for studying how long-term agent memory evolves when new information reinforces, revises, or conflicts with stored memories. It finds benign accumulation is relatively harmless while contradiction and authority conflicts drive failures in continual agents.

entry.title: Who Verifies the Benchmark? Decentralizing Trust in Large Language Model Evaluation

author.name: Sahil Pardasani, Madhusudan Singh

entry.summary: Argues that vendor-reported LLM benchmarks operate largely on trust and proposes decentralizing verification, motivated by market-moving unverified claims and by evidence that LLM judges show identity-aware bias toward answers from particular source models. It measures and addresses this trust deficit in evaluation.

entry.title: SkillSmith: Enhancing Locally Deployed Agents via Automatic Skill Construction and Evolution

author.name: Xinle Jiang, Remy Xie, Ming Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses that locally deployed small-model agents underperform cloud agents mainly because they lack environment knowledge such as rules and operating procedures, then automatically constructs and evolves reusable skills to supply that knowledge. The goal is privacy-preserving, low-cost on-device assistants that close the gap with cloud LLM agents.

entry.title: BRACE: Taming Sharp Irregularities via Barycentric Rational Forecasting for Fast Diffusion Transformers Inference

author.name: Jinlong Yang, Jinke Wu, Lizilin, Yao Zhou

entry.summary: BRACE accelerates diffusion transformer inference by replacing derivative-based polynomial extrapolation of cached features with barycentric rational forecasting plus Chebyshev enhancement, motivated by the observation that feature trajectories are globally smooth but locally irregular. This targets the quality collapse of existing caching methods at high acceleration ratios.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks on Deep OCR Systems

author.name: Wenbo Sun, Hongzong LI, Yanyun Wang, Jiahao MA, Shuxin Zhuang, Rong Feng, Shiqin Tang, Zi Liang

entry.summary: Presents a pure black-box adversarial attack on a generative OCR vision-language model where only the decoded output string is observable, casting the attack as zeroth-order optimization over a sequence-similarity loss with random-direction gradient estimation. Targets the compression-based long-context OCR approach that treats vision as an optical compression channel.

entry.title: Complete, Scalable, and Robust Prioritized Planning for Multi-Robot Ordered Storage and Retrieval at Maximum Capacity

author.name: William Zhang, Tzvika Geft, Jingjin Yu, Kostas Bekris

entry.summary: Formulates ordered storage and retrieval at maximum capacity for multi-robot puzzle-based warehouses on grids accessible from one boundary, and gives a prioritized planning method that is complete, scalable, and deadlock-robust. It bridges geometric feasibility results with execution efficiency for high-density storage.

entry.title: Shape Mutating Expert Compression:LorExperts and BTExperts

author.name: Inesh Chakrabarti, Sourjya Roy, Bowen Bao, Thiago Crepaldi, Spandan Tiwari, Ashish Sirasao

entry.summary: Compresses mixture-of-experts models by exploiting the observation that experts organize into co-activation communities, so multiple shared components can be fitted per community instead of one global shared component that fails as expert count grows. This preserves all experts and the router, unlike pruning or merging methods that require router retraining.

entry.title: Router Sensitivity Under Lightweight Fine-Tuning Identifies Prunable Experts in Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Ali Janati, Kaoutar El Maghraoui, Xinyi Luo, Wenyuan Shen, Owen Zou, Yankai Mao

entry.summary: Tests whether expert pruning signals based on router weight changes, previously justified only under full fine-tuning, survive when adaptation is done with a lightweight adapter. Finds that router-only low-rank adaptation training a tiny fraction of parameters gives the cleanest pruning signal and outperforms broader adaptation at matched rank after removing half the experts.

entry.title: Persistent Semantic Entities in Tool-Augmented LLM Systems

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes persistent semantic entities, implicit state in tool-augmented agents that binds to a name, activates on events, and propagates across agent boundaries while remaining invisible to standard debugging. Across 24 models from 11 families the paper reports universal susceptibility, with name binding as the necessary mechanism and preference contamination persisting without decay.

entry.title: Learning from Consensus and Disagreement: Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation with Minority-Trajectory Contrast

author.name: Jiaxin Guo, Yanwei Yue, Xuanbo Fan, Chunyu Yang, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a fully unsupervised on-policy self-distillation framework that manufactures privileged information from the model's own unlabeled rollouts, using answer-level consensus to identify a stable reasoning mode for dense positive supervision and contrasting minority trajectories for the negative signal. Removes the dependence on gold solutions or verifiers that limits existing methods.

entry.title: Do AI Forecast Ensembles Sample the Correct Conditional Distribution?

author.name: Lucas J. Howard, Elizabeth A. Barnes

entry.summary: Tests whether AI-based probabilistic ensembles actually sample the correct joint conditional distribution, using a diffusion model for coastal sea-level forecasting plus Lorenz-96 controls. Finds skillful marginal forecasts at every station while joint spatial structure is worse than climatology, a failure invisible to the energy score but caught by the variogram score.

entry.title: From Inaudible Inputs to Model Failures: Low-Frequency Safety Risks in LALMs
