entry.summary: Empirically compares deep ensembles, Bayesian neural networks, and Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty quantification across genomics tasks including sequence-to-activity prediction and single-cell expression analysis. Assesses how dataset characteristics common in genomics affect the reliability of each uncertainty estimate.

entry.title: Two-stage Odd Residual Flows for Mean-Preserving Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Kiran Madhusudhanan, Christian Kl\"otergens, Lars Schmidt-Thieme, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage probabilistic forecaster that first learns a point mean forecast and then fits residual normalizing flows constrained to preserve that mean, avoiding the accuracy degradation that joint likelihood training causes. Targets long-horizon risk-sensitive forecasting where both calibrated distributions and accurate means are needed.

entry.title: Quantifying the noise sensitivity of the Wasserstein metric for images

author.name: Erik Lager, Gilles Mordant, Amit Moscovich

entry.summary: Derives finite-sample bounds on how additive pixel noise perturbs Wasserstein distances between images treated as discrete measures, showing the signed 2-Wasserstein error grows with the square root of the noise standard deviation rather than linearly as for Euclidean distance. Provides theoretical grounding for preferring optimal-transport distances in noisy imaging settings.

entry.title: HyperShape: Hyperelasticity Across Diverse Shapes

author.name: Leo Widmer, Sidaty El Hadramy, St\'ephane Cotin, Philippe Claude Cattin

entry.summary: Releases an extensible generator of synthetic shapes and matching hyperelastic simulation data, producing 2D and 3D datasets with tunable geometric complexity. Enables systematic evaluation of whether neural operators generalize across domain geometry and boundary conditions, including out-of-distribution and synthetic-to-real transfer.

entry.title: SPOTting the Future: Lookahead Explanations for Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tamar Gozlan, Claudia V. Goldman

entry.summary: Introduces a model-agnostic tool that explains deep RL policies by building an interpretable finite-horizon tree from sampled actions and simulated successor states, given access to the policy and a simulator. Provides formal guarantees on asymptotic recovery of the most probable action and characterizes disagreement behavior.

entry.title: DualSpectralCF: Training-Free Sign-Aware Spectral Collaborative Filtering

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Tong Qi, Xiaoxue Han

entry.summary: Extends training-free spectral collaborative filtering to use explicit negative feedback such as one-star ratings and distrust links, via a signed input signal that plugs into any spectral filtering backbone. Aims to capture the accuracy gains of learned sign-aware recommenders without gradient-based training.

entry.title: Quantum Incremental Learning with Mixed State Prototypes

author.name: Yu Wu, Qianli Zhou, Xinyang Deng, Wen Jiang, Kang Hao Cheong, Witold Pedrycz

entry.summary: A quantum incremental learning framework that adds classes by introducing trainable mixed-state prototypes instead of widening the quantum circuit, sidestepping NISQ-era width limits and the orthogonal-basis cap on class count. Aims to avoid catastrophic forgetting under tight parameter and memory budgets.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Vision Foundation Models for Robust Leukemia Cell Classification across Multiple Microscopy Datasets

author.name: Carlos Zamora, Hiram Zuniga, Ulises Orozco-Rosas, Kenia Picos

entry.summary: A two-stage pipeline built on a pretrained vision foundation model with retrieval augmentation classifies leukemia cells across five heterogeneous microscopy datasets, first detecting leukemia and then subtyping into ALL versus AML. The focus is generalization across staining, illumination, and site protocol shifts that break single-dataset models.

entry.title: Conflict or Strategy? Asymmetric Role Framing of La France insoumise and Rassemblement National in French News Headlines, 2022-2025

author.name: Amr Sobhy

entry.summary: Analyzes 28,592 French news headlines about two populist parties using a three-model LLM annotation pipeline validated against a stratified human audit. The main finding is role asymmetry rather than valence asymmetry: the left-populist party is framed through conflict while the right-populist party gets a strategic-electoral register.

entry.title: MAD-HOI: Masked Autoregressive Diffusion for Generating Articulated Hand Object Interactions from Text

author.name: Ananya Bal, Kartik Sharma, Ethan Lai, Samyak Tiwari, Liza Dahiya, Chaitanya Chawla, Laszlo A. Jeni

entry.summary: SSRL-MAR reduces motion artifacts in 3D brain MRI without paired clean-corrupted data or k-space access, using contrastive learning on 3D patches to extract motion representations, an artifact-aware synthesis network, and a final correction stage. This suits clinical settings where paired supervision is unavailable.

entry.title: Seeing things through in the age of AI

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: The essay observes an asymmetry in which AI dramatically accelerates drafting and prototyping while offering only a small speedup on the finishing work of polishing, debugging, verification, and production hardening. The author argues this asymmetry explains the flood of low-quality AI-assisted output alongside disappointing gains on work that matters.

entry.title: ArchAgent v2: A Case Study with the Data Prefetching Championship

author.name: Abraham Gonzalez, Raghav Gupta, Akanksha Jain, Hanna Alam, Alexander Novikov, Po-Sen Huang, Matej Balog, Marvin Eisenberger, Sergey Shirobokov, Ng\^an V\~u, Hank Levy, Borivoje Nikoli\'c, Sagar Karandikar, Martin Dixon, Parthasarathy Ranganathan

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, ArchAgent v2 scales agentic evolutionary search from single-level cache replacement policies to multi-level data prefetcher design, adding cascaded evolutionary search that subdivides the design space by memory level and other techniques to handle vast search spaces, hardware budgets, and slow simulation. Framed as a case study against a data prefetching championship setting.

entry.title: TeXFix-Bench: An Empirically Grounded Multi-Format Benchmark for LLM-Based Document Source Repair

author.name: Prajwal S. Venkateshmurthy

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for LLM repair of broken document sources across LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown, grounded in an empirically mined 18-category fault taxonomy derived from real crash reports and commits. Fault injection uses AST-aware mutation operators across formats.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Semantics and Reconstruction:Unifying Sign Language Translation and Production

author.name: Xiao Liu, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Jiaxin Yin, Bowen Guo, Yaqi Sun, Zhiwei Jiang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Attempts to unify sign language understanding (recognition and translation) with sign language production in a single model, despite the two directions requiring opposite mappings between visual sign sequences and text. Bridges semantic understanding with signal reconstruction in one framework.

entry.title: RecoverFly: A Failure-Aware Reinforcement Learning Post-Training Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Boxiong Wang, Hui Kang, Geng Sun, Jiahui Li, Chao Yu, Daxin Tian

entry.summary: RecoverFly post-trains end-to-end UAV vision-language-action policies with failure-aware reinforcement learning to supply the corrective supervision that behavior cloning lacks in closed-loop flight. It targets sample inefficiency, long-tailed scene distributions, and policy distribution shift during optimization.

entry.title: STAIR: Effective Incident Response Using an End-to-End Agentic Planning Framework

author.name: Hanlin Jiang, Jionghao Huang, Shaofei Li, Bojia Yu, Peng Jiang, Yuxin Ren, Ning Jia, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: STAIR is an agentic planning framework for cybersecurity incident response that maintains the incident as a graph-structured state, aligns actions with the current recovery stage, and reuses historical experience, addressing the instability of LLM planners over long-horizon recovery. It aims to replace static expert playbooks that cannot adapt to evolving incident conditions.

entry.title: DoseBridge: Denoising Diffusion Bridge Model for Dose Prediction in Lung Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy

author.name: Zerun Zhang, Xiaoda Cong, Xiangkun Xu, Peter Y. Chen, Xuanfeng Ding

entry.summary: DoseBridge predicts proton-therapy dose distributions with a denoising diffusion bridge that anchors on the patient CT and encodes beam geometry as a spatially aligned mask, fused multiscale with target and organ-at-risk maps for under 2% extra parameters. It was evaluated retrospectively on 52 advanced lung cancer plans.

entry.title: Dynamic Context Adapters: Efficiently Infusing History into Vision-and-Language Models

author.name: Yuhang Song, Bor-Jiun Lin, Jiaxu Liu, Te-Chuan Chiu, Anh Nguyen, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: Dynamic Context Adapter injects compressed fixed-size memory of past frames into pretrained vision-language models so they can handle sequential decision-making without quadratic attention over full frame history. It aims to avoid both compute blowup and lossy temporal compression.

entry.title: Visual Geometry Foundation-Aware Gaussians for Single-Frame Surround-View Driving Reconstruction

author.name: Junhong Lin, Jinlong Wang, Xianda Guo, Yanlun Peng, Wei Zheng, Guoqing Liu, Hanli Wang, Tiesong Zhao, Wei Gao

entry.summary: VGGD uses pretrained visual geometry foundation model features (VGGT) as a frontend prior for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction from single-frame surround-view driving cameras with minimal overlap. The argument is that upstream geometric representation quality, not decoder complexity, is the bottleneck.

entry.title: ConfTriage: A Calibration-Aware LLM Triage Framework for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy with Selective Specialist Deferral

author.name: Md Rabiul Islam, Samir Abdaljalil, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: ConfTriage tests whether a generalist LLM reading a natural-language rendering of standard nodule attributes can act as a calibrated triage layer for pulmonary nodule malignancy, deferring low-confidence cases to a specialist imaging model. It provides a finite-sample combined-error bound and an oracle inequality for excess risk.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Trustworthy Multimodal Reasoning and Evaluation Benchmark in Complex Urban Scenes

author.name: Zhaoyang Wei, Bowen Jiang, Xumeng Han, Jiashu Li, Xuehui Yu, Yuling Liu, Guorong Li, Zhenjun Han, Jianbin Jiao

entry.summary: AD2-Bench proposes a hierarchical visual diagnosis framework that decomposes multimodal reasoning in adverse-condition urban driving scenes into a structured chain of evidence, so failures in reasoning steps can be attributed rather than only final answers scored. Findings indicate models often infer without adequate visual evidence.

entry.title: Every Packet Counts: Dispersing Information for Loss-Resilient Learned Image Compression

author.name: Yuhang Wei (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Chuqin Zhou (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yibo Shi (Huawei Technologies Ltd), Jing Wang (Huawei Technologies Ltd), Guo Lu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

entry.summary: Makes learned image compression resilient to packet loss by redistributing energy across latent channels so critical information is not concentrated, and by interleaving channel groups to break sequential decoding dependencies. Targeted at satellite and emergency communication links.

entry.title: Is There Really a Camouflaged Object? Towards Realistic Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Huafeng Chen, Yueming Lyu, Chenyang Si, Wende Tan, Liucheng Guo, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Argues that camouflaged object detection is evaluated under a closed-world assumption where every image contains a camouflaged target, causing severe false positives in open-world deployment. Introduces OPC16K, a 16,245-image benchmark from 14 sources that includes pure backgrounds and non-camouflaged objects.

entry.title: Robust Safety Filtering for Input-Constrained Underactuated Linear Systems

author.name: Muhamad Rausyan Fikri

entry.summary: The paper builds a safety filter for input-constrained underactuated linear systems facing unknown disturbances, combining an H-infinity baseline derived from a differential game with a disturbance observer whose estimate and error bound feed robust high-order control barrier function constraints. Pointwise feasibility for scalar-input systems is characterized exactly through an admissible input interval.

entry.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models

author.name: Guide Labs Team, Andreas Madsen, Aya Abdelsalam Ismail, Giang Nguyen, Isaac Plant, Muawiz Chaudhary, Nathaniel Monson, Saqib Azim, Zhichen Guo, Julius Adebayo

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, Argues that interpretability need not cost capability by making it a training objective rather than a post-hoc analysis, and shows across three orders of magnitude of compute that representations become more disentangled and concept-aligned as scale grows, for both autoregressive and diffusion language models. The recipe is instantiated in an 8B diffusion language model built for steerability.

entry.title: Legal Responsibilities Using Autonomous Agents For Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Mark Burgess

entry.summary: Applies Promise Theory and a downstream causal-influence principle to the question of who bears legal responsibility when autonomous AI agents cause criminal or negligent damage, including cases of agents escaping containment. It argues responsibility can be assigned via policy-constrained agent freedoms.

entry.title: From Relevance to Execution Utility: Reward-Aware Dynamic Execution Gating for Skill-Based LLM Agents

author.name: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Hongyu Gu, Hao Li, Haoyu Wang, Yixiong Chen, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: RADEG inserts a lightweight learned gate between skill retrieval and execution for skill-based LLM agents, predicting whether executing a retrieved skill bundle is worth its cost rather than just whether it is topically relevant. It is retriever-agnostic and trained as a cheap surrogate of downstream execution utility.

entry.title: NeuroPilot: An Agent-Driven Smart Pipeline for Processing, Quality Control, and Managing Neuroimages

author.name: Yiyao Chen, Yucheng Li, Jungong Tong, Shaoqi Wang, Kunhao Zhou, Ziquan Wei, Monica Murea, Marissa DiPiero, Tingting Dan, Guorong Wu

entry.summary: NeuroPilot packages neuroimaging standardization, preprocessing, and quality control expertise into three LLM-invocable skills orchestrated by an agent, replacing project-specific scripting and manual quality review. It aims to generalize across infrastructure settings with a single configuration.

entry.title: Learning an Interior Layout Policy in a Domain Specific Language Action Space

author.name: Yuhao Lu, Weichen Zhang, Wenyi Xiao, Haohui Chen, Yiyun Fei

entry.summary: LayoutDSL has an LLM emit interior layout decisions as programs in a domain-specific symbolic language instead of directly regressing object coordinates, and accounts for structural elements such as doors and windows. The claim is that a symbolic action space lets the model learn design reasoning rather than raw geometry fitting.

entry.title: Geometry Beats Estimated Depth: RGB-Only Multi-Camera 3D Tracking under Sim2Real

author.name: Abdullah Naeem, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Noman Khan, Md Tamjidul Hoque

entry.summary: Compares a geometry-first RGB pipeline using homography lifting and multi-camera fusion against a monocular depth pseudo-LiDAR pipeline for warehouse multi-camera 3D tracking under simulation-to-real transfer. Concludes that cross-view geometric consistency rather than monocular depth accuracy governs performance.

entry.title: LoRSA: Toward Generalizable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Biomedical Downstream Tasks

author.name: Saed Moradi, Benyamin Ghojogh, M. Hadi Sepanj, Yimin Yang, Ashirbani Saha

entry.summary: LoRSA combines a dense low-rank adapter capturing globally shared task structure with a dynamically structured sparse low-rank component providing localized residual corrections, for adapting vision foundation models to biomedical tasks. The motivation is that a single low-rank update confines all adaptation to one narrow subspace.

entry.title: Metadata Reconstruction from Values Alone: Recovering Column Semantics in Undocumented Warehouses

author.name: Mike Helwig

entry.summary: Tackles the inverse of typical text-to-SQL settings by recovering column and value semantics from data alone in undocumented warehouses with cryptic identifiers. A deterministic profiler extracts structural evidence such as value fingerprints, pattern matches, and checksum verdicts, and the language model proposes semantics conditioned on that evidence with provenance and evidence-bounded confidence.

entry.title: Effect of Abstractions and Prompting Strategies on LLM-Guided High-Performance Optimizations

author.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Klepl, Maty'a\v{s} Brabec, Martin Kruli\v{s}

entry.summary: Studies how different code abstractions and prompting strategies affect an LLM's ability to produce high-performance, parallel-optimized code, comparing LLM-guided optimization against traditional domain-specific auto-tuning pipelines. Findings inform how to structure representations given to models for HPC code optimization.

entry.title: Biologically Informed Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Center Generalization of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Alejandro L. Garc\'ia-Navarro, Carlos Sevilla-Salcedo, Bel\'en Rodr\'iguez-S\'anchez, Vanessa G\'omez-Verdejo

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic representation-learning framework for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry that jointly models acquisition-specific variability and biological supervision available in microbiology datasets, improving cross-institution generalization. Aims to make microbial identification and resistance prediction models portable across labs.

entry.title: Do Evaluation Metrics Detect Errors in Classical Chinese to English Translations?

author.name: Osvaldo Quinjica, Eric Bennett, Xinchen Yang, Andrew Schonebaum, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Builds a minimal-pair diagnostic framework to test whether standard automatic translation metrics detect error types that matter to scholars translating Classical Chinese into English, probing both reference-based and reference-free metrics. Finds all metrics have blind spots, with one learned metric performing best overall.

entry.title: Calling the Bluff: Detecting Ever-Shifting Harmful Chat Dialogue via Ordered Reasoning Chain Regularization

author.name: Haojie Yu, Ziyou Jiang, Junjie Wang, Mingyang Li, Yuekai Huang, Jie Huang, Qing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes decomposing harmful-dialogue detection into an ordered reasoning chain over topic, harm indicator, severity and type, using intermediate supervision as a structured regularizer plus prototype-based feature augmentation to stay robust as attackers shift harm categories and vocabulary. Reports gains across multiple domains and harm categories.

entry.title: Epistemic Transfer in AI-Assisted Verification: A Framework and Evaluation Protocol

author.name: Christoph Trattner

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating AI verification assistants by what users can do after the tool is removed, introducing an epistemic transfer effect measure comparing delayed unassisted performance and a tool-removal cost measure of immediate performance drop. Distinguishes this construct from correction effects, trust, reliance and human-AI team performance.

entry.title: SignLlama: Enhancing Gloss-free Sign Language Translation by Prioritizing Visual Features for LLMs

author.name: Shiwei Gan, Xiao Liu, Yafeng Yin, Zhiwei Jiang, Bowen Guo, Lie Xie, Sanglu Lu, Hongkai Wen

entry.summary: SignLlama adapts LLMs to gloss-free sign language translation by diagnosing two failure modes: the distribution gap between visual and text embeddings, and autoregressive concatenation causing the model to underweight visual cues. It restructures fusion so visual features are prioritized during decoding.

entry.title: How People Evaluate AI-, Expert-, and Peer-Style Financial Advice

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A preregistered vignette experiment with 285 participants holding financial content constant while varying communication style (AI assistant, certified planner, online forum) and independently manipulating displayed source labels, including mislabeled conditions. Separates the effect of who people think is speaking from how the advice is written.

entry.title: SafeQL: Search-based Refinement for Safe and Efficient LLM-based Text-to-SQL

author.name: Geonho Lee, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: SafeQL makes the database an active participant in text-to-SQL refinement, using search-based repair guided by schema and DBMS feedback instead of regenerating whole queries after execution errors. Targets the persistent problem of LLMs referencing nonexistent tables, columns, functions, or values.

entry.title: Learning Preference Adaptation for Large Language Model Personalization via Verbal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuting Liu, Wei Wu, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo

entry.summary: Studies task-specific preference adaptation: given a universal natural-language user preference summary, derive a task-conditioned view that keeps decision-relevant evidence and drops distracting context. AlignXada is a training-free meta-learning framework that produces these views verbally rather than requiring fine-tuning or manual per-task engineering.

entry.title: LEED: Local Embedding Evolution Distance for over-smoothing estimation and virtual node selection in GNN

author.name: Killian Cressant, Pedro B. Velloso

entry.summary: LEED is a node-level metric that tracks how individual embeddings evolve across GNN layers, giving finer-grained diagnosis of over-smoothing than global Dirichlet energy. It is also used to select where to insert virtual nodes to relieve over-squashing.

entry.title: NeuroRefiner: Morphology-Aware Multi-Agent Refinement for 3D Fluorescence Microscopy Neuron Segmentation

author.name: Haiyang Yan, Jinyue Guo, Yanchao Zhang, Bingqing Wang, Zhenchen Li, Jing Liu, Jiazheng Liu, Linlin Li, Hua Han

entry.summary: NeuroRefiner is a multi-agent system that mimics expert workflows for 3D neuron segmentation, with agents that diagnose topological errors, issue correction instructions, and validate refinements against a dedicated refinement network. It targets fragmentation caused by sparse, elongated neuron morphology.

entry.title: Power law graph attention: exact generalization of scaled dot-product attention, empirical collapse at inference

author.name: Burc Gokden

entry.summary: Analyzes power law graph attention, which replaces the fixed bilinear form of scaled dot-product attention with a learned input-generated operator, proving it contains standard attention exactly as a special case and establishing positivity and spectral structure. The author also reports an empirical collapse of the learned operator at inference and labels each claim by evidentiary status.

entry.title: Can Bayesian Optimization Efficiently Find a Strong Single Expert in Neural Thickets?

author.name: Nigel Bastian Cendra, Abdelhamid Ezzerg, Fernando Julio Cendra, Jeremias Knoblauch, Jakob Zeitler

entry.summary: Applies Bayesian optimization inside a random low-dimensional linear embedding of LLM weight space to find strong single expert models without backpropagation. Reports matching or exceeding random search with roughly five times fewer candidate evaluations on reasoning benchmarks using small Qwen2.5-Instruct models.

entry.title: Benchmarking Time Series Generation Methods for Privacy-Preserving Forecasting

author.name: Luis Amorim, Vitor Cerqueira, Moises Santos, Paulo J. Azevedo, Carlos Soares

entry.summary: Benchmarks synthetic time series generators and noise-based anonymization baselines when synthetic data fully replaces real data for forecasting, jointly measuring downstream forecast quality and distance-based empirical privacy risk on seven datasets. Characterizes the utility-privacy trade-off in the train-on-synthetic test-on-real regime.

entry.title: MIDAS: Mutual Information Disentanglement with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Yuhua Wen, Yingying Zhou, Qifei Li, Yingming Gao, Zhengqi Wen, Jianhua Tao, Ya Li

entry.summary: Handles missing or corrupted modalities in multimodal sentiment analysis by variationally disentangling shared from modality-specific information via mutual-information objectives and fusing the remaining evidence with uncertainty weighting. Argues this extracts task-relevant signal better than imputation or heuristic coordination constraints.

entry.title: Knowledge-Guided 3D CT Generation: A Conditioning-Centric Taxonomy

author.name: Francesca Pia Panaccione, Eugenio Lomurno, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: Surveys conditional 3D CT generation and organizes the fast-growing literature along a taxonomy centered on how external knowledge conditions the generative process. Motivated by clinical needs including augmentation, privacy-preserving sharing, and simulating specific anatomical or pathological scenarios.

entry.title: P3CA: Encoder-Agnostic Interpretation of Vision Foundation Model Embeddings via Spatial Probing

author.name: Amoon Jamzad, Dilakshan Srikanthan, Faranak Akbarifar, Nooshin Maghsoodi, Parvin Mousavi

entry.summary: Proposes an encoder-agnostic probing method that, given a user-selected spatial region, estimates local feature normalization and dominant covariance directions and projects the whole spatial tensor onto them to visualize where locally informative directions appear. Requires no retraining, encoder modification, or task labels, targeting inspection of vision foundation model embeddings in medical imaging.

entry.title: A Quantum Roadmap for Softmax Attention: Exact Born-Rule Analogs for Softmax Attention on the Probability Simplex

author.name: Eric A. F. Reinhardt, Adam J. Hauser

entry.summary: Argues that when attention inputs and outputs live on the probability simplex, softmax attention has an exact quantum realization: scores become Hadamard-test statistics on block-encoded projections of amplitude-encoded inputs, and the softmax temperature maps to a measurement repetition count. Sparse attention with exact zeros appears at the boundary of the resulting family.

entry.title: A Convolutional Layer Activation Dimensionality Reduction for Out-of-Distribution and Adversarial Attack Detection Methods

author.name: Leandro de Souza Rosa, Lorenzo Capelli, Clara Nunes Barrancos, Mauro Mangia, Riccardo Rovatti

entry.summary: This work proposes a dimensionality-reduction step for convolutional layer activations that explicitly controls the compression versus information trade-off, improving downstream out-of-distribution and adversarial-attack detection based on intermediate activations. It targets a gap where existing reduction methods either lack such control or discard useful structure.

entry.title: MammoMix: Leveraging Mixture of Experts for Robust Mammogram Breast Detection

author.name: Dinh Tan Nguyen, Hoang Quan Dang, Chen Zhang, Sai Ho Ling

entry.summary: MammoMix trains per-domain expert detectors for mammographic lesions and combines them with an input-dependent gating mechanism, aiming for robustness across datasets that differ in image quality, lesion appearance, and demographics. It targets the degradation single detectors suffer when trained on heterogeneous mammography sources.

entry.title: Embedding Rotation Invariance for Provable Multi-Oriented Scene Text Recognition

author.name: Zhibin Ma, Pengwen Dai, Yi Liu, Xugong Qin, Chenyun Yu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: A multimodal pretraining framework for medical imaging that treats structured clinical tables as semantically meaningful two-dimensional objects rather than flat vectors, using importance-aware adaptive masking as a label-free curriculum. It argues tabular phenotypes carry quantitative diagnostic signal that unstructured reports lack.

entry.title: Grid-Preserving Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Convolutional Inductive Bias to Vision Transformers under Data Scarcity

author.name: Junyong Choi, Cheolhyeon Park, Jaehoon Cho

entry.summary: iBKD distills convolutional inductive bias into Vision Transformers under data scarcity by preserving the spatial grid throughout the transfer path instead of pooling or projecting to logits. An inductive bias attention module aggregates student layers to align with CNN teacher structure.

entry.title: SpecF2M: A Spectral-Aware Multi-task Network Estimating Axial Length and Refractive Error from Pediatric Fundus Photographs

author.name: Mengxian He, Xinyue Liu, Yunyun Sun, Wei Hao, Minqing Zhang, Lichun Wang, Shunyi Zhang, Wu Yuan

entry.summary: SpecF2M is a multi-task network that estimates axial length and refractive error components from pediatric fundus photographs using anatomy-guided enhancement and a hybrid spatial-spectral encoder. It aims to make myopia screening possible without dedicated biometry or cycloplegic refraction.

entry.title: OAA: Three Phases of Vocal Guidance in Human-Drone Teleoperation

author.name: Allan Henry (LPNC, GIPSA-COPERNIC, LIG, GETALP), Christian Graff (LPNC), Solange Rossato (LIG, GETALP), Jos\'e-Ernesto Gomez-Balderas (GIPSA-COPERNIC), Sylvain Huet (GIPSA-COPERNIC)

entry.summary: Using motion capture and speech from human-human pointing guidance and human-drone gamepad teleoperation, the study shows that spontaneous vocal guidance consistently organizes into three distinct phases of orientation, approach, and adjustment. Phases are detected automatically by change point detection on 3D trajectories and validated statistically.

entry.title: Robust Sliding Mode and Admittance Control of Underactuated Aerial Manipulators for Contact-Based Inspection

author.name: Tareq Aziz Alqutami, Yvan Petillot, Matthew W. Dunnigan, Mustafa Suphi Erden

entry.summary: A robust control architecture for an underactuated hexarotor with a one-degree-of-freedom arm combines integral-augmented sliding mode control for trajectory tracking with admittance control for contact force regulation, mapping contact force to a feedforward attitude command. The arm actively compensates vehicle tilt to keep surface alignment during sustained contact inspection.

entry.title: Improved cross-validated distances for multivariate pattern analysis

author.name: Laurent Caplette, Sarah Lipp\'e

entry.summary: This commentary improves on recommended cross-validated distance measures for multivariate pattern analysis of neural data, showing that the cross-validated Euclidean distance decomposes into between-partition distances and using that structure to build a more reliable generalized variant. It also derives improvements for correlation-based distances.

entry.title: AI governance work needs much better monitoring

author.name: jackultraphil

entry.summary: The author argues that AI governance funders rarely verify whether grants achieved anything, and proposes a lightweight practice of agreeing on written indicators before disbursement, having grantees assign probabilities, and scoring annually. An example is given where a grantee reported twenty policy recommendations while only a fifth were even partially implemented.

entry.title: DualCert: A Solver for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Constraint-Coupled Learning

author.name: Yancheng Song, Yongzhi Qi, Wei Qi, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: Introduces DualCert, a learning-augmented TSP solver in which learned refinement steps are constrained by degree equations and dynamically separated subtour elimination constraints, so learned transitions remain feasible with respect to constraints discovered during search. Uses KKT-manifold structure and dual repair to couple learning with optimization guarantees.

entry.title: TRACE: TRajectory Attribution for Automated Context Engineering

author.name: Yikai Zhao, Pradeep Kumar Misra, Saurabh Pandey

entry.summary: TRACE mines historical agent trajectories for implicit dissatisfaction signals such as user corrections, rephrasings, and abandonment, then attributes failures to specific context sources (system prompts, knowledge bases, tool descriptions, skills) and proposes remediations. It automates context engineering maintenance without model fine-tuning or explicit feedback collection.

entry.title: DSLE: A Learning Environment for Dark Souls Boss Encounters

author.name: Derin Gezgin, Jim O'Connor, Tanner Goodwin, Gary B. Parker

entry.summary: Releases a containerized learning environment exposing all 22 boss fights of a difficult action game through a Gymnasium-style interface with real-time combat, high-dimensional visual input, and sparse terminal rewards, plus a recommended five-boss subset for controlled comparison. Baselines include random, expert-system, and evolutionary agents.

entry.title: Evaluation of Motivational Interviewing Counsellors with Task-Aware Multi-Stage LLM-Based Simulated Clients

author.name: Jiading Zhu, Xinyu Cindy Wang, Thomas Nguyen, Yan Qing Lee, Osnat C. Melamed, Peter Selby, Jonathan Rose

entry.summary: Introduces a task-aware simulated client framework for evaluating motivational interviewing counselors in smoking cessation, structured around the evoking stage with staged conversation flow and a policy governing what the client reveals. It targets the mismatch between generic simulated patients and the specific therapeutic tasks being assessed.

entry.title: An evolutionary model of animats with VLM-based subjective evaluation

author.name: Shota Miyazaki, Takaya Arita, Reiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Uses a vision-language model as a subjective fitness judge in an evolutionary algorithm, comparing image sequences of two virtual soft robots and selecting on aesthetic terms such as cute or strange. Morphology and locomotion co-evolve under this subjective selection pressure.

entry.title: Tools to Explain Neural Networks for Power System Dynamics

author.name: Petros Ellinas, Johanna Vorwerk, Spyros Chatzivasileiadis

entry.summary: Applies Neural Tangent Kernel analysis to explain why machine learning surrogates for stiff, multi-timescale power system dynamics train well or poorly, giving a modal interpretation analogous to small-signal eigenvalue analysis. Positions explainability as a prerequisite for grid operators to adopt learned simulators.

entry.title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs

author.name: Nuthakki Siva Gopala Krishna, Kanishka Jain

entry.summary: Argues that knowledge distillation transfers not just capability but behavioral patterns including how a model represents its own identity, and introduces an adversarial multi-agent framework to stress-test self-identity consistency in student models. Raises concerns about homogenization, inherited bias and accountability in distilled model families.

entry.title: Tabular Numeric Stretch Transformation

author.name: Zihao Ye, Juyong Kim, Johnna Sundberg, Burak Varici, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: Frames numeric feature preprocessing for tabular deep learning as an optimization problem that stretches feature distributions to make the target function smoother and easier to learn, in unsupervised (density-equalizing minimax) and supervised (target-aware) variants. Targets the underexplored preprocessing stage rather than model architecture.

entry.title: Distributed Optimization with Streaming Data: A Temporal Weighting Perspective

author.name: Muhammad Faraz Ul Abrar, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Erik G. Larsson

entry.summary: Theoretical study of decentralized first-order optimization when data arrive as a stream and the global objective is a temporally weighted average of evolving losses. The authors derive convergence guarantees for multi-iteration decentralized gradient descent under strong convexity and smoothness.

entry.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-IV: Developmental Topology Observatory

author.name: Kaustubh Kapil, Kishor P. Upla

entry.summary: The fourth instalment of the Transformer Geometry Observatory tracks how the representation point cloud and its manifold topology evolve layer by layer during training, rather than analyzing isolated layers or whole networks. The goal is a developmental account of when raw inputs become task-relevant representations.

entry.title: Coordinating the Unknown Lipschitz Constant in Multiplayer Bandits

author.name: Ricardo Parada, Chenzhang Zhao, William Chang

entry.summary: Studies cooperative multi-agent bandits over continuous Lipschitz action spaces when the Lipschitz constant is unknown, across three information structures. The key technical difficulty is that non-communicating agents must independently converge on the same discretization of the joint action space, and the paper gives regret guarantees for algorithms that do so.

entry.title: Beyond Detection Accuracy: Measuring Explanation Cost, Stability, and Utility for Resource-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Abdurrahman Tolay

entry.summary: Argues that intrusion-detection research ignores the compute cost and instability of generating explanations, and jointly measures detection accuracy, SHAP cost, local explanation stability, and selective explanation on a carefully de-leaked IoT dataset. The leakage-safe data construction is itself a contribution given widespread benchmark contamination in this area.

entry.title: Riemann GeoResolver: A Non-Euclidean Attention Framework from Euclidean Resolver to Hyperbolic-Spherical Geometry

author.name: Liangchen Ge

entry.summary: A theoretical treatment of inverse-distance attention as an alternative to softmax attention, with claimed separation results on retrieval circuit width, stronger Polyak-Lojasiewicz constants implying linear convergence, and bounded effective rank limiting noise memorization, then extended to hyperbolic and spherical geometries.

entry.title: Link-adaptive digital twin for robust physical-layer modeling in hybrid-amplified ultra-wideband optical networks

author.name: Xiaoxuan Gao, Rentao Gu, Yingchun Wang, Xinyi Liu, Junshi Gao, Yuefeng Ji

entry.summary: A link-adaptive digital twin decomposes signal-to-noise ratio modeling in ultra-wideband optical networks into separate amplifier-noise, nonlinear-interference, and signal-power predictions to generalize across heterogeneous links. Targets fast, robust physical-layer estimation under strong Raman scattering effects.

entry.title: Surfacing the Unsaid: CUE-Bench for Affective Stance in Chinese Discourse

author.name: Zhenyan Zheng, Yunyao Zhang, Junxi Sheng, Junqing Yu, Zikai Song

entry.summary: CUE-Bench is a Chinese benchmark for affective stance, targeting emotion conveyed indirectly through irony, politeness, or deliberate mismatch between surface wording and intent. It structurally separates explicit expression, implicit affect, pragmatic intent, and fine-grained emotion so evaluations can expose deeper emotion-understanding failures.

entry.title: Withholding the Completing Chunk: Deterministic Pair-Completion Guardrails for Streaming LLM Output

author.name: Christopher M. Frost

entry.summary: This work proposes a deterministic guardrail for streaming LLM output that withholds the specific chunk which would complete a two-predicate danger signature, so unsafe text never escapes mid-stream. Across signature families and chunk sizes the streaming decisions matched a buffered scanner while single-predicate controls passed unimpeded.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts-based Entropy Model for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Jonas Brenig, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: Introduces a mixture-of-experts entropy model for learned image compression so only the parameter subset relevant to a given image is activated, reporting a 16.85 percent BD-rate gain over VVC on Kodak. Short paper from a well-known image restoration and compression group.

entry.title: Putting Registers to Work: Task Registers for Token Pruning in Vision Transformers

author.name: Hongsen Cao, Mona Jaber, Shanxin Yuan, Ahmed Sayed

entry.summary: Probes which components of token-pruning policies transfer across classification, segmentation, and detection by applying parameter-free reduction criteria one layer at a time without retraining, finding that dense tasks rank criteria differently and prefer opposite recovery endpoints. Motivates a task-adaptive pruning policy using ViT register tokens.

entry.title: Multi-Level Evidence Aggregation for Robust Facial Phenotype Retrieval in Rare Genetic Disorder Prioritization

author.name: Alexander Hustinx, Carolin Kaffin\'e, Behnam Javanmardi, Tzung-Chien Hsieh, Peter Krawitz

entry.summary: Improves facial phenotype retrieval for rare genetic disorder prioritization by aggregating evidence at inference time across multiple images per patient and multiple patients per disorder, instead of comparing single image pairs. No changes are needed to the underlying encoder.

entry.title: Foundation Model-Enabled Efficient Data Sampling (FEEDS): A label-efficient training strategy for pan-cancer, multi-tracer PET/CT datasets

author.name: Biratal Raj Wagle, Bashirul Azam Biswas, Grant Chau, Matthew E. Maeder, Muhammad Azeem Arshad, Michael S. Leapman, James B. Yu, Indrani Bhattacharya

entry.summary: FEEDS uses vision foundation model embeddings to select the most informative and diverse unlabeled whole-body PET/CT studies for expert annotation, reducing labeling burden for pan-cancer, multi-tracer lesion segmentation. The strategy targets both label and compute efficiency.

entry.title: Learning Gaussian Structure: Intervention-Guided Density Control for Feed-Forward Driving Reconstruction

author.name: Hang Li, Jiahe Li, Meiying Gu, Jin Zheng, Lina Yu, Xiao Bai

entry.summary: LGS improves feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction of driving scenes by adding intervention-guided density control, so the initialized primitive set can be densified rather than frozen, and by explicitly aggregating cross-time evidence per primitive. This addresses the lack of gradient-driven densification available to optimization-based splatting.

entry.title: Compositional Benchmark Synthesis for Hierarchical Human Action Recognition

author.name: Farnaz Soleimani (LISSI), Abdelghani Chibani (LISSI), Yacine Amirat (LISSI), Ghazaleh Khodabandelou (LISSI)

entry.summary: The authors synthesize a four-level hierarchical benchmark spanning atomic actions, activities, low-level intentions, and high-level intentions by composing episodes from a flat single-label action corpus while preserving real extracted features. The goal is to enable evaluation of long-horizon intention recognition without collecting new hierarchical datasets.

entry.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control via Sequential Convex Programming for Drone-to-Drone Docking

author.name: Neeraj Balachandar, Shriram Hari, Vishnu R. Unni

entry.summary: Autonomous mid-air docking between multirotors is formulated as a finite-horizon optimal control problem on a reduced-order nonlinear model augmented with disturbance states, solved by sequential convex programming in a receding-horizon loop. Noisy-measurement state estimation supports relative motion prediction, validated in a high-fidelity MuJoCo simulation.

entry.title: On using crises to shift political will for AI

author.name: clickyquack

entry.summary: A governance essay arguing that AI safety incidents will keep occurring and that advocates should prepare to amplify those incidents that make the case for their preferred policies legible to national-security-minded skeptics. It draws analogies to the post-Hiroshima nuclear regime and COVID-era emergency measures as examples of felt crises unlocking rapid policy change.

entry.title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution

author.name: Anton Razzhigaev, Andrei Gritsaev, Andrei Kaznacheev, Nikita Dragunov, Roman Yampolskiy, Andrei Kuznetsov

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, Presents a self-developing coding agent harness whose tools, prompts, context assembly and core implementation evolve through reviewed commits that become the runtime for subsequent work, in both a recursive self-improvement mode and an experience-driven mode. Reported runs built on the existing Claude Opus 5 model claim best-known scores on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and OSWorld-Verified.

entry.title: H2: A Dual Hybrid Semantic Data Lake Architecture for Medical Data Harmonization with Human-In-the-Loop verified, LLM Driven Metadata Annotation System

author.name: Ioannis N. Tzortzis, Georgia Kapetadimitri, Agapi Davradou, Nefeli Kousta, Nikolaos Bakalos, Ioannis Rallis, Dimitrios Kalogeras, Nikolaos Doulamis, Anastasios Doulamis

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid semantic data lake architecture for medical data harmonization in which an LLM generates metadata annotations that humans verify before ingestion. The aim is to prevent heterogeneous clinical images, tables, and free text from degenerating into an unusable data swamp.

entry.title: Emotion2Skill: Model-Internal Emotion Signals for Adaptive Skill Selection and Evolution

author.name: Bohan Lin, Hejia Geng, Xinyi Xie, Heng Zhou, Qinghua Xing, Bo Liu, Chen Zhang, Yudong Zhang

entry.summary: Emotion2Skill extracts internal emotion direction vectors from an LLM and uses them as an additional signal for choosing and evolving skills in a skill-based agent, on the premise that internal affective state causally influences behavior. It is one of the first attempts to feed interpretability-derived internal features into agent-level routing rather than only steering outputs.

entry.title: SkillSentry: Reliable Skill Execution for LLM Agents via Runtime Assurance

author.name: You Lu, Xinyu Huang, Bihuan Chen, Xin Peng

entry.summary: SkillSentry defines a domain-specific language for expressing runtime guidance about how a skill should be executed, then monitors and constrains agent execution to reduce deviation and step-level errors across repeated runs. Targets the reliability gap where agents that can complete a task sometimes fail on similar tasks or reruns.

entry.title: COMEX: A Composition-Grounded Benchmark and Learning Framework for Explainable Aesthetic Image Cropping

author.name: Rui Yang, Wei Zhou, Dingyong Gou, Xiaohui Cui, Cong Li, Yinyin Gong, Yipo Huang, Jiliang Zhao

entry.summary: Reformulates explainable image cropping as a joint crop, composition category, and explanation problem, and releases a benchmark of over thirty thousand quadruples built via image expansion and a reversed input-output pipeline. The goal is explanations grounded in compositional principles rather than post-hoc text.

entry.title: HugSelect: An Explainable Multi-Criteria Decision-Support Framework for foundation-model selection

author.name: Alireza Joonbakhsh (Shiraz University), Arda Canser Adal{\i} (Utrecht University), Slinger Jansen (Utrecht University), Farshad Khunjush (Shiraz University), Siamak Farshidi (Wageningen University, Research)

entry.summary: Proposes treating foundation-model selection as an auditable multi-criteria software component decision rather than popularity-based hub search, building a knowledge base of over 70,000 models from repository metadata, extracted capabilities and community-perceived quality. Delivers an explainable decision-support framework for engineers picking models.

entry.title: Open-World Semantic Segmentation with Sensitivity Modeling

author.name: Anastasios Romanos Varvarigos, Nikos Giakoumoglou, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Extends a dual-decoder open-world segmentation baseline with a third complementary decoder, combining Gaussian prototypes for known classes, contrastive isolation of unknowns, and an added sensitivity-modeling branch to segment known categories while detecting and grouping novel content. Targets overconfident misclassification in closed-world segmentation models.

entry.title: Can We Optimize the Performance-Carbon Emission Break-Even Point?: The Quest for Greener LLMs

author.name: Sourav Das, Tanmay Joshi, Kripabandhu Ghosh

entry.summary: Folds a calibrated differentiable energy surrogate, fit from on-hardware profiling and using parameter norm, FLOP and memory proxies, into the fine-tuning objective of several small open models to seek configurations where accuracy improves at near-zero additional inference carbon cost. Argues inference rather than training dominates deployed model footprint.

entry.title: Fourier Self-Supervision for Fine-Grained Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Sarah Rastegar, Mina Ghadimi Atigh, Pascal Mettes, Yuki M. Asano, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: Applies dual frequency-domain filtering (low-pass for coarse category attributes, high-pass for fine detail) as a self-supervision signal for generalized category discovery, aiming to move beyond superficial visual cues. Targets fine-grained recognition of both known and novel classes in unlabeled data.

entry.title: GALA: Graph-Augmented LLM Agents for Root Cause Analysis and Incident Response in Microservices

author.name: Yifang Tian, Yaming Liu, Zichun Chong, Zihang Huang, Yiran Li, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: GALA+ is an LLM agent framework for microservice root-cause analysis that uses the service dependency graph to bound exploration and fuse multi-modal telemetry, with a trace-and-graph-aware scoring module for hypothesis generation. It goes beyond fault ranking to produce actionable incident-response steps.

entry.title: How Far Do Foundation Models Transfer to Infant Signals? A Cross-Dataset Transfer Audit with a Unified Need Ontology

author.name: Wu Hangyu

entry.summary: Audits how well frozen audio foundation-model encoders transfer across four infant cry corpora under a unified five-class need ontology, with byte-level and embedding-level leakage screening. Reveals large within-corpus variance, on-average negative cross-corpus transfer, and hundreds of duplicate clip groups that inflate single-corpus results.

entry.title: Two-Step MV-DeepONet: Probabilistic Operator Learning for Uncertainty Propagation Driven by Random Input Fields

author.name: Yupei Nie, Lei Wang, Jiasen Liu

entry.summary: Extends probabilistic DeepONet operator learning so that predictive uncertainty is not restricted to diagonal (pointwise) covariance, using a two-step mean-variance training scheme to capture cross-location dependence in field-valued outputs. Aimed at forward uncertainty propagation under random input fields.

entry.title: Visual Distortion Detection in UGC Images Using Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Ziheng Jia, Yingji Liang, Jiaying Qian, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: VIGIL uses a large multimodal model to localize and describe specific perceptual distortions in user-generated images, moving beyond a single global quality score. It targets the synthetic-to-authentic generalization gap that arises when models are trained mainly on artificially distorted images.

entry.title: Multimodal Federated Learning under Dual-Axis Modality Missingness

author.name: Adiba Orzikulova, Jaehyun Kwak, Jaemin Shin, Yunqi Guo, Xiaomin Ouyang, Guoliang Xing, Steven Euijong Whang, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: Flux tackles multimodal federated learning where modality availability varies both across clients and across individual samples, a realistic condition in health sensing. It uses mask-aware unimodal supervision to learn per-sample per-modality confidence, fused into an adaptive temperature that adjusts prediction sharpness.

entry.title: UniDFKD: A Unified Semantic Prior Framework for Architecture-Agnostic Data-Free Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Xuewan He, Tong Chu, Zihan Cheng, Yuchen Su, Qianxin Xia, Guoming Lu, Jielei Wang, Wen Li

entry.summary: UniDFKD makes data-free knowledge distillation architecture-agnostic by replacing reliance on batch-norm statistics, which modern vision transformers lack, with a unified semantic prior for synthesizing training data. This restores distillation quality when the teacher is a ViT rather than a CNN.

entry.title: DAVE: A Decoupled Audio-Visual Enhancement Framework for Real-World Speech Separation

author.name: Wei Zhou, Wanyi Ning, Yinshang Guo, Qianxiao Fang, Haitao Qian, Yingpeng Li

entry.summary: DAVE decouples visual conditioning from the separation network so that degraded or unreliable video does not corrupt audio-visual speech enhancement, and releases a 219,411-mixture corpus built from public meeting recordings with combinatorial acoustic augmentation. A progressive multi-objective schedule jointly optimizes separation and enhancement.

entry.title: Monotonicity-Guided Bottom-Up Petri Net Discovery: The SPECpp Framework

author.name: Leah Tacke genannt Unterberg, Lisa L. Mannel, Wil M. P. van der Aalst

entry.summary: SPECpp discovers Petri net process models bottom up by exploiting monotonic properties of individual candidate places, letting sequences, choices, loops, and concurrency emerge rather than imposing predefined constructs as top-down inductive miners do. The core challenge tackled is pruning an exponential candidate-place space.

entry.title: KGCaRe: Explainable Complex Conditional Question Answering using Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction and Context Retrieval with LLMs

author.name: Ghanshyam Verma, Simanta Sarkar, Devishree Pillai, Hotaka Shiokawa, Yourong Xu, Fiona Veazey, Peter Hubbert, Hui Su, Paul Buitelaar

entry.summary: KGCaRe builds a knowledge graph from documents using multi-prompt LLM extraction and combines graph retrieval with vector retrieval to answer complex conditional questions with explainable evidence. It targets domain settings where plain RAG underperforms.

entry.title: REATS: LLM Reasoning-based Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xu Zhang, Chang Xu, Hui Sun, Nan Ma, Zijian Zhang, Peng Wang, Wei Wang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: REATS uses an LLM as an ensemble router for time-series forecasting, combining textual descriptions of temporal patterns with numerical features to produce interpretable, sample-adaptive weights over base forecasters via chain-of-thought. It also studies design choices for structuring LLM inputs.

entry.title: A matched-integrator evaluation of Hamiltonian neural networks on pendulum and Kepler dynamics

author.name: Lenick Kemunto Nyabuto, Yae Ulrich Gaba, Birahim Tewe

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of Hamiltonian neural networks against parameter-matched feedforward baselines under identical data, derivative targets, optimization, and integration schemes across five seeds. On the pendulum the Hamiltonian prior cut mean energy drift 42-fold and trajectory error nearly 16-fold at long horizons.

entry.title: Dreamer-SAC: Off-Policy Learning in Latent World Models for Sample-Efficient Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiazhuo Li, Linjiang Cao, Qi Liu, Xi Xiong

entry.summary: Dreamer-SAC couples a recurrent state-space world model with off-policy soft actor-critic training directly in latent space, mixing real interactions with short-horizon imagined rollouts and n-step targets to limit model bias. It is evaluated on driving efficiency and safety objectives.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Agent Bandits with Heavy-Tailed Rewards and Information Asymmetry

author.name: Daphne Feng, Ricardo Parada, Lily Jiang, Sophia Yi, William Chang

entry.summary: Extends decentralized multi-agent bandits to heavy-tailed reward distributions under three information-asymmetry regimes, deriving robust algorithms whose regret nearly matches centralized heavy-tailed rates. Validated on Pareto-distributed synthetic rewards.

entry.title: BREAD: Baseline-Referenced Explanations for Anomaly Diagnosis

author.name: Jiaqi Qiu, Rob Goedhart, Jannis Kurtz, Inez M. Zwetsloot

entry.summary: Introduces a model-agnostic diagnosis method that explains flagged anomalies by referencing a normal baseline distribution, aimed at AI-based statistical process monitoring where traditional model-specific diagnostics do not transfer. Positioned as more scalable and better attributed than generic feature-attribution XAI.

entry.title: Long-Time Trajectory Approximation via SA-NODEs: Model Predictive and Floquet Strategies

author.name: Ziqian Li, Nikolaos M. Matzakos

entry.summary: Shows that error bounds for semi-autonomous neural ODEs degrade doubly exponentially over long horizons and proposes two state-reset training strategies, one using model-predictive windowing with data restarts and one exploiting Floquet structure for periodic autonomous systems. Establishes parameter budgets that grow linearly rather than explosively with horizon length.

entry.title: Sequential Modality Dropout for Robust Multi-Modal Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Wenlong Zhang

entry.summary: Trains multimodal sequential recommenders with entire modality streams randomly erased for whole user histories so the model does not become dependent on any one modality. Measures robustness as the fraction of full-modality accuracy retained when a modality is unavailable at serving time, across four backbones and four product datasets.

entry.title: DSAR: Dual-Stream Autoregressive Modeling of Temporal Cloth Dynamics for Photorealistic Animatable Avatars

author.name: Haozhong Xiong, Yao Yu, Yu Zhou, Sidan Du

entry.summary: DSAR models animatable human avatars with a dual-stream autoregressive formulation that treats cloth appearance as evolving causally from previous states rather than being a function of current pose alone. This targets over-smoothed or artifact-heavy renderings on out-of-distribution poses.

entry.title: Self-Geometry: GT-Free and Plug-and-Play Test-Time Adaptation for Geometrically Consistent 3D Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Seokhyun Youn, Dahyeon Kye, Sung-Ho Bae, Jihyong Oh

entry.summary: JFRDet performs explicit affine registration in feature space to fuse severely misaligned RGB and infrared imagery for oriented object detection, rather than relying on implicit feature adaptation that only handles small offsets. It also accounts for illumination effects on modality reliability.

entry.title: Multiple Scale Latents for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Jonas Brenig, Radu Timofte

entry.summary: Replaces the single latent plus hyperprior design in learned image compression with a hierarchy of latents at multiple spatial scales, each with its own entropy model, reporting a 17.9 percent BD-rate reduction over VVC on Kodak. The authors note the approach is orthogonal to other compression advances.

entry.title: Static in Frames, Dynamic in Events: Rethinking Features in Event Cameras as Motion Cues

author.name: Hesam Araghi, Jan van Gemert, Nergis Tomen

entry.summary: Analyzes two features commonly used in event-camera corner detection, structure tensor eigenvalues and spatiotemporal density, and argues theoretically and empirically that they function as motion cues with no frame-based analogue. It then shows these cues combined with local geometry can improve motion estimation.

entry.title: Capturing Uncertainty in Human Motion for Representation Learning in Soccer

author.name: Yizhou Xu, Lars Bretzner, Tiesheng Wang, Atsuto Maki

entry.summary: A self-supervised framework learns 3D skeleton motion representations for soccer players by predicting future motion, using a conditioning module that models a distribution over discretized plausible futures rather than a single trajectory. Explicitly modeling multimodality improves prediction accuracy on large-scale player tracking data and yields better downstream representations.

entry.title: Algorithmic statistics of retinal images

author.name: Loan Huynh, Ronald Zambrano, Layton Aho, Fabio Lavinsky, Gadi Wollstein, Joel S. Schuman, Andrew R. Cohen

entry.summary: The authors apply normalized compression distance as a metric-learning approach, combined with anisotropic structure-enhancing filters, to quantify and visualize retinal OCT volumes. The motivation is that standard supervised deep features are non-metric and can introduce systematic distortions in disease progression measurements.

entry.title: Neuroevolution Arena: Nested Ecological Evaluation of Update-and-Inheritance Regimes across Neural Architectures

author.name: Yuxu Ge, Yifei Cheng

entry.summary: Neuroevolution Arena is a GPU-accelerated artificial-life environment where independently parameterized neural cells compete, used to compare three update-and-inheritance regimes crossed with two architectures over fifty thousand generations. An audit-tracked nested protocol shows that controllers can rank differently under training versus frozen ecological evaluation.

entry.title: ChronoState: Hidden Elapsed-Time Conditioning for Temporal-State Action Selection in Frozen-Backbone Language Models

author.name: Sam Siavoshian, Omar Ramadan, Amir K. Saeed, Benjamin A. Johnson, Amin Mohamed El-Amin Diab, Benjamin M. Rodriguez

entry.summary: Introduces ChronoState, a benchmark testing whether a frozen language model can combine symbolic task state given in the prompt with elapsed wall-clock time supplied as a non-token scalar through a side channel, then choose the correct time-dependent action. Experiments use a small frozen instruct model as backbone with injected chronometric conditioning.

entry.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

author.name: Yuanchi Zhu, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Chenxu Du, Xinqi Yang, Hebao Zhu, Bokai Zhao, Tianyu Liang, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Weiyang Shi, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: SafeSceneReason is a multimodal industrial-safety benchmark and training corpus that links workplace imagery to knowledge from occupational accident investigations, requiring models to assess compliance, spot hazardous interactions, explain accident mechanisms, and recommend prevention. Built from complementary scene-centric and accident-knowledge pipelines.

entry.title: MMArch: Benchmarking Multimodal Reasoning Grounded in Architectural Evidence

author.name: Chenxu Du, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Xinqi Yang, Yuanchi Zhu, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: MMArch is a 1,212-item short-answer benchmark for architecture and civil engineering built from figures in peer-reviewed papers, requiring models to combine distributed visual evidence with engineering principles rather than just extract information from drawings. Items are produced by a planner-writer pipeline and validated by automated screening, adversarial audit, and expert review.

entry.title: Control-Oriented Scenario Tree Construction through Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fabio Pavirani, Bert Claessens, Pierre Pinson, Chris Develder

entry.summary: Learns how to build scenario trees for multistage stochastic model predictive control by optimizing directly for downstream control performance rather than distributional fidelity, parameterizing the assignment of sampled scenarios to tree leaves with an attention-based policy trained by reinforcement learning. Challenges the assumption that better distribution matching yields better control.

entry.title: CircuitReason-1k: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Visual-to-Symbolic Reasoning inElectrical Circuits

author.name: Xinqi Yang, Kang An, Tengyue Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Chenxu Du, Yuanchi Zhu, Hebao Zhu, Ziliang Wang, Faqiang Qian, Yunli Yang, Qibing Ren

entry.summary: A benchmark of 1,000 authentic textbook electrical circuit problems that requires grounding symbols in diagrams, recovering latent topology, choosing a physical model, formulating coupled equations, and preserving units, signs, and phase conventions through a long chain of steps. Each item pairs diagrams with a typed answer and a reference worked solution.

entry.title: Defending Retrieval-Augmented Intrusion Detection Against Knowledge Poisoning and Prompt Injection

author.name: Kaysarul Anas Apurba, Md. Hasibul Hasan, Mahedee Zaman Moon, Sk. Md. Mizanur Rahman, Atsuo Inomata

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent retrieval-augmented intrusion detection system with defenses against poisoned knowledge bases and prompt injection, combining soft trust scoring, label-embedding consistency checks and prompt sanitization. Reports partial recovery of clean classification quality as poisoning rates rise on a standard network-traffic dataset.

entry.title: Abstracted Away: Resisting Alienation and Ungrounded Abstraction in AI Research Communities

author.name: Vyoma Raman, Isabel O. Gallegos, Neha Srivathsa

entry.summary: A position and reflection paper by early-career critical AI researchers arguing that dominant abstraction practices in computational AI research separate legitimacy from lived experience of harm and crowd out critical reflection, producing alienation and epistemic injustice. Proposes ways research communities can resist ungrounded abstraction.

entry.title: Triple Expert Learning from Noisy Labels for Semi-Supervised Vision Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Xuanyu Liu, Zheng Fang, Hongyang He, Yundi Hong, Daizong Liu

entry.summary: TriNoL routes unlabeled samples into high, medium, and low confidence regions and assigns each to a dedicated LoRA expert (positive, alignment, negative), so that a single low-rank adapter is not forced to absorb reliable and noisy pseudo-label gradients simultaneously. Targets semi-supervised adaptation of frozen vision foundation models.

entry.title: MARA: Flow-Matching-Guided Multi-Agent Resource Allocation for Computational Resource Efficient Learning

author.name: Hanye Zhao, Muning Wen, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: MARA allocates discrete compute nodes among concurrent training jobs that must hit target losses before deadlines, forecasting future loss trajectories with conditional flow matching and coordinating nodes via a cooperative multi-agent autoregressive policy. It treats compute as indivisible nodes rather than continuous throughput.

entry.title: FeedbackTrack: Visual-Cortex-Inspired Cross-Frame Feedback for Transformer Tracking

author.name: Yueyang Cang, Xiaoteng Zhang, Zhiyuan Ning, Yuchen He, Li Shi

entry.summary: FeedbackTrack adds sparse, layer-aligned cross-frame feedback to pretrained transformer trackers, caching previous-frame intermediate states and reinjecting them into corresponding layer groups via query modulation and gating pathways. Inspired by recurrent feedback in visual cortex, it reuses intermediate representations that feed-forward trackers discard.

entry.title: How Simple Can It Get? From Interpretable Equations to Readable Rules for Financial Decision Making

author.name: Adia Lumadjeng, Ilker Birbil, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Starts from an interpretable classifier that is itself a single predictive equation and progressively simplifies it into pruned monomials, if-then rules, and the integer scorecards finance already uses, quantifying the accuracy lost at each simplification step. Across four financial datasets pruning is shown to be nearly free.

entry.title: TSPORec: Token Selection via Preference Optimization for LLM-Based Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Wenqiao Zhu, Chao Xu, Haipang Wu, Ji Liu

entry.summary: TSPORec uses preference optimization to select which tokens of item descriptions an LLM recommender should attend to, instead of naively truncating to the first few tokens. The goal is to cut inference cost in sequential recommendation without discarding informative text.

entry.title: Accelerated Learning of High Dimensional Functions with a Tensor-Featured Training Network

author.name: Karl Pierce, Yuehaw Khoo, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Accelerates learning of high-dimensional functions by inserting contextual features into a network's first layer, alternating between standard gradient descent on network weights and periodic updates of the feature basis, with complex features decomposed via tensor networks. Rank-1 features are evaluated matrix-free on the domain.

entry.title: $\beta$-VAEs as Effective Theories: Tolerance-Dependent Dimension

author.name: Johannes Hirn

entry.summary: Tests whether the linear-Gaussian picture of beta-VAE latent collapse, where regularization strength acts as a spectral cutoff aligned with reconstruction utility, survives in nonlinear VAEs trained on climate data. Finds collapse onsets shift and broaden but the utility ordering is preserved, supporting an effective-theory reading of latent dimensionality.

entry.title: Partially Observable Learning for Multi-Platform Dispatch Optimization

author.name: Fengming Yao, Man Luo

entry.summary: Models instant-delivery dispatch when couriers freely serve multiple competing platforms and each platform sees only its own orders and interactions, giving inherent partial observability. Proposes a partially observable learning approach that also relaxes the common assumption that couriers must accept assignments.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Statistical Downscaling of Sea Surface Temperature Using a Residual Corrective Neural Network

author.name: Onkar Jadhav, Tim French, Ivica Janekovic, Nicole L. Jones, Matthew Rayson

entry.summary: Statistically downscales sea surface temperature from a coarse seasonal coupled forecast system using a U-Net to produce an initial high-resolution estimate, then refines it with a residual correction network. Offers an inexpensive alternative to computationally prohibitive dynamical downscaling for long periods and large ensembles.

entry.title: Automatic Field-of-View Adjustment for a View-Expansive Microscope via LSTM-Based Gaze and Pipette Motion Interpretation

author.name: Kenta Yokoe, Takuya Hara, Tadayoshi Aoyama

entry.summary: An LSTM predicts the appropriate microscope field-of-view from operator gaze and pipette motion, driving an automatic adjustment on a view-expansive microscope that avoids physical lens changes. Aimed at reducing workflow interruptions during intracytoplasmic sperm injection.

entry.title: Self-Knowledge Retrieval Augmented Generation Framework for Patent Matching

author.name: Jian Zhang, Songlin Lei, Zhuohao Yang, Bangli Liu, Ziwei Wang, Xufeng Weng, Gehan Amaratunga, Yu Lin, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: A self-knowledge retrieval-augmented framework for patent matching that has the LLM parse patents and mine deep semantic relationships itself rather than relying on domain fine-tuning or purely external retrieval. The aim is to detect subtle technical differences between patents without heavy labeling or catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: FUSE: Frame-Unified Stress Estimation from Facial Video

author.name: Stefanos Gkikas, Thomas Kassiotis, Yang Guo, Guangliang Li, Giorgos Giannakakis

entry.summary: FUSE performs facial-video stress detection by fusing all frames of a complete recording into a single input, eliminating the window-length, overlap, and aggregation choices that complicate conventional clip-based pipelines. This allows direct modeling of temporal information across the entire session.

entry.title: Bridging Event Streams and DiT: Event-Guided Video Frame Interpolation

author.name: Guixu Lin, Yuyang Yu, Xiang Ji, Linyao Chen, Zhengwei Yin, Mengshun Hu, Mingdeng Cao, Shengfeng He, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes an adapter that injects event-camera motion cues (image-warped events plus bidirectional flow) into a frozen pretrained image-to-video diffusion transformer for video frame interpolation. The goal is to handle large temporal gaps and complex motion without retraining an event-conditioned generator from scratch.

entry.title: MMArt A Multi-Perspective Multimodal Dataset for Visual Art Understanding

author.name: Shuai Wang, Wangyuan Ding, Yixian Shen, Jia-Hong Huang, Stevan Rudinac, Monika Kackovic, Nachoem Wijnberg, Marcel Worring

entry.summary: MMArt is a dataset of 74,234 WikiArt paintings annotated from four independent perspectives (narrative, formal, emotional, historical) plus a harmonized unified caption, produced by specialist models and human annotation. It argues that shallow art interpretation by VLMs is partly a dataset limitation.

entry.title: InterPruner: Interactive Structured Pruning via Taylor-Implicit Criterion and Language-Prior Modulator for Multimodal Object Detection

author.name: Qi Ming, Zihan Yang, Shaoguang Huang, Si Sun, Hanqing Zhang, Nanqing Liu, Jiahui Lv, Juan Fang, Aleksandra Pizurica

entry.summary: InterPruner is a structured channel pruning framework for RGB-infrared detectors that derives channel importance from a high-order Taylor and implicit function criterion and modulates pruning using language priors and cross-modal interaction. It targets redundancy from parallel dual-modality backbones.

entry.title: E$^3$mo-Bench: A Scalable Benchmark for Multimodal Evoked and Expressed Emotion Understanding via Bayesian Pairwise Alignment

author.name: Lancheng Gao, Ziheng Jia, Shengyan Li, Zixuan Xing, Jiarui Wang, Huiyu Duan, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: E3mo-Bench is a benchmark of 12,314 QA pairs over 2,524 videos that jointly evaluates expressed and evoked emotion in multimodal LLMs via perception, open-vocabulary recognition, and valence-arousal-dominance rating. Continuous annotations are scaled using a Bayesian pairwise alignment procedure.

entry.title: GS-CPE: Unified 6-Degree-of-Freedom Camera Pose Estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Huaiyuan Weng, Chul Min Yeum, Su-Min Kang

entry.summary: GS-CPE estimates 6-DoF camera pose in a coarse-to-fine manner, first using retrieval-guided geometric estimation on a Gaussian Splatting scene and then refining by minimizing a visibility-aware masked RGB warping objective with adaptive re-rendering. Evaluated on indoor and other localization benchmarks.

entry.title: HUI360: A 360{\deg} Egocentric Dataset and Baselines for Human-Robot Interaction Anticipation

author.name: Raphael Lorenzo-Louis, Fabio Amadio, Bertrand Luvison, Serena Ivaldi

entry.summary: HUI360 is presented as the largest in-the-wild dataset for anticipating human-robot interaction, collected from a mobile robot with a 360-degree camera across multiple environments over three months. It includes baselines for predicting whether passersby will engage with the robot.

entry.title: SAR2Agri: Learning SAR Intensity Representations for Agricultural Monitoring

author.name: Moti Rattan Gupta, Anupam Sobti

entry.summary: SAR2Agri learns SAR intensity representations specifically for agricultural monitoring tasks such as crop type mapping, yield prediction, and phenological event detection, rather than grounding SAR in optical imagery as multimodal remote sensing foundation models do. It argues existing SAR-specific foundation models target different downstream tasks.

entry.title: APCReg: Anatomical-Prior-Guided Coarse-to-Fine CBCT--IOS Registration via Multi-View Projection and Reliability-Controlled Residual Correction

author.name: Xincan Zheng, Yaqi Wang, Zhi Li, Jiahao Bao, Lan Feng, Yiru Xia, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: APCReg performs registration between cone-beam CT and intraoral dental scans using an anatomical-prior-guided coarse stage that decomposes the six-degree-of-freedom search into ordered orthogonal projection alignments, followed by reliability-controlled residual refinement. It targets a workflow that today still relies on manual clinician adjustment.

entry.title: A Neural Network Based Teleoperation for Remote Controlled Vehicles

author.name: Ning Ding, Azim Eskandarian

entry.summary: This teleoperation framework for remotely driven vehicles combines wave-variable encoding to preserve stability under stochastic communication delay with an adaptive radial basis function network that compensates for unmodeled vehicle dynamics. Decoupled adaptive laws are tailored to longitudinal and lateral vehicle behavior rather than robotic arms.

entry.title: Immersive Micromanipulation Integrating Pipette and Injector Operations with McKibben-Based Haptic Sensations for Workload Reduction

author.name: Kenta Yokoe, Sumiwa Saito, Yuki Funabora, Tomoko Isomura, Tadayoshi Aoyama

entry.summary: An immersive micromanipulation system for intracytoplasmic sperm injection unifies pipette and injector control in one hand and adds pneumatic artificial-muscle haptic feedback representing aspiration, discharge, and oocyte contact. A human-participant study reports reduced workload and improved operation compared with the visual-only baseline.

entry.title: Large Multimodal Agents for Intelligent Transportation Systems: Architectures, Evidence, and Deployment Challenges

author.name: Muhammad Ayub Sabir, Shaohong Zheng, Zhiyu Qu, Fatima Ashraf, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: A structured literature review that maps 42 study families on large multimodal agents for intelligent transportation, separating claims about multimodality, autonomy, empirical validation, and deployment readiness. It introduces capability and validation grading scales plus methodological-concern domains to audit evidence quality.

entry.title: Agentic Router: An Execution-Grounded Continual Learning Approach With Memory

author.name: Yuxuan Chen, Rongpeng Li, Zhifeng Zhao, Yuntao Liu, Xing Xu, Honggang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an execution-grounded agent for command-line network operations that generates multiple candidate action sequences, predicts their execution consequences, and reranks by utility and risk, while abstracting past executions into retrievable operational lessons. Targets the gap between plausible-looking commands and safe, effective network configuration changes.

entry.title: Adaptive Semantic Capacity Allocation for Parallel Generative Recommendation

author.name: Chenxi Li, Yuchen Lu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: Argues that generative recommenders using fixed, uniform semantic ID structures waste prediction capacity, and proposes adaptively allocating the number of semantic slots and codebook sizes across semantic subspaces for parallel (non-autoregressive) generation. Shows that uniformly lengthening identifiers gives limited gains, indicating redundancy in homogeneous designs.

entry.title: Coordinated incentives in AI-generated misinformation governance

author.name: Qin Li, Gui Zhang, Minyu Feng, Matjaz Perc, Attila Szolnoki

entry.summary: Models AI-generated misinformation governance as a three-party evolutionary game among a regulator, an AI company, and users with heterogeneous rewards and punishments, deriving replicator dynamics and stability conditions. Concludes that neither regulation nor market incentives alone suffice and that truthful-content regimes require coordinated incentive alignment.

entry.title: Cross-Model Humor Preference Modeling with Cards Against Humanity

author.name: Victor Winter, Farhan Lakhany

entry.summary: Tests whether one language model can predict another model humor preferences in a Cards Against Humanity style binary selection task, using a design that filters out self-preference effects.
