Conditions escalate from generic instruction to showing the other model prior choices and rationales, measuring how much cross-model preference modeling improves.

entry.title: EMMR: Emotion-Mediated Multimodal Reasoning for Personality Assessment in Asynchronous Video Interviews

author.name: Dongsheng Hu, Tianyi Zhang, Chuang Liu, Yuan Zong Yong Li, Wenming Zheng, Xiu-xiu Zhan

entry.summary: A two-stage multimodal framework that first extracts emotion cues from video, audio, and text of asynchronous job interviews and then uses them as mediating evidence for personality trait prediction. The claim is that nonverbal affective signals add information beyond transcript-only LLM assessment.

entry.title: Open-World Hierarchical Perception: Taxonomic Abstraction over Class-Agnostic Proposals for the Safe Handling of Out-of-Vocabulary Road Objects

author.name: Felix Schaller

entry.summary: Extends taxonomic abstraction for autonomous driving perception to class-agnostic region proposals so that objects a closed-set detector would never box, such as road debris or livestock, can still be coarsely classified or flagged. Reports a feasibility study of three open-world detection signals.

entry.title: A Grounded and Decomposed Framework for Relation-Level Hallucination Evaluation in Abstractive Summarization

author.name: Praveen Kumar Katwe, Rakesh Chandra Balabantaray, Kali Prasad Vittala, Naman Kabadi

entry.summary: Builds a relation-level hallucination evaluation framework for abstractive summarization using a dependency-aware extraction pipeline with normalization, entity-grounded subject resolution, passive and negation handling, plus a Relation Hallucination Index. Focuses on fabricated or distorted relationships between entities rather than surface factual overlap.

entry.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in English to Romanian Machine Translation

author.name: Ioana Grigore, Sergiu Nisioi

entry.summary: Builds a hybrid pipeline for English to Romanian translation in which a fine-tuned LLM classifies intended gender and inserts inline hint tags, which a fine-tuned Transformer then uses to produce morphologically correct gendered output. Introduces supporting data to address masculine-default and stereotype-reinforcing translations.

entry.title: Enhancing Scientific Named Entity Recognition via Large Language Models: A Type-driven Multi-task Learning Approach

author.name: Tong Bao, Yi Zhao, Heng Zhang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a type-driven multi-task approach for scientific named entity recognition that avoids overwhelming an LLM prompt with too many candidate entity types, instead using entity-type information more selectively across coupled tasks. Targets the greater type complexity of scientific text relative to general domains.

entry.title: Toward CT-Equivalent Image Quality in Low-Dose Radiotherapy Planning: Conditional Diffusion-Based CBCT-to-CT Synthesis and the Impact of CBCT Input Representation

author.name: Alzahra Altalib, Chunhui Li, Christopher Hamill Taylor, Sankar Pillai, Alessandro Perelli

entry.summary: Develops a conditional denoising diffusion model to synthesize CT-quality images from low-dose cone-beam CT for radiotherapy planning, and studies how different CBCT input representations affect synthesis fidelity and dose-calculation suitability. Aims to reduce cumulative imaging dose from repeated planning CT acquisitions.

entry.title: GLocFM: A Geometry-Aware Foundation Model for 3D Indoor Wireless Localization

author.name: Chenghong Bian, Chaozheng Wen, Hongze Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: GLocFM is a foundation model for indoor WiFi localization that jointly uses radio measurements and 3D point-cloud scene geometry, formulating position estimation as maximum-likelihood scoring of candidate transmitter positions given delay-angle observations. Geometry awareness is meant to exploit non-line-of-sight propagation and generalize across unseen scenes.

entry.title: Defining Decentralization: An Ontological Perspective

author.name: Jakub Kacper Szel\k{a}g, Aydin Abadi, Mohammad Naseri

entry.summary: A conceptual and ontological analysis of what decentralization actually means across distributed computing, blockchain, federated learning, and agentic AI, where the term is often conflated with distribution or disintermediation. The authors propose a unified definitional framework applicable across communication systems.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Prognostics and Health Management: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Christopher Braun, Julian Raible, Marco F. Huber

entry.summary: A systematic review of 212 studies on physics-informed machine learning for prognostics and health management, introducing a four-class taxonomy of how physical knowledge enters the pipeline. It maps where physical priors help with generalization and interpretability in industrial diagnostics.

entry.title: Exploration-Driven Personalized Federated Reinforcement Learning via Intrinsic Motivation

author.name: Md Rafid Islam, Rafsan Jany, Zahid Hasan, Ratun Rahman

entry.summary: Adds curiosity-driven intrinsic motivation to personalized federated reinforcement learning so that clients explore in sparse-reward or non-stationary settings while keeping local data private. Combines two active research directions rather than introducing new theory.

entry.title: Optimized Sequential Testing for Binary Ensemble Classifiers

author.name: Joseph Kalman, Amit Moscovich

entry.summary: Reduces inference cost of majority-vote ensemble classifiers by evaluating base models sequentially and stopping once the outcome is determined, formalizing several notions of optimality for early-stopping strategies. Applies classical sequential-testing ideas to random-forest-style predictors.

entry.title: Projected climate memory and inherited warm-tail risk in accelerated European summer warming

author.name: Mauricio Herrera-Mar\'in, Alex Godoy-Fa\'undez, Diego Rivera

entry.summary: Builds an empirical reduced-dynamics framework that splits European summer temperature indicators into inherited slow-state memory, its predictable part, and same-season innovation, using causal filters, ridge regression, and logistic risk models over ERA5 data for 28 sub-regions. Finds Mediterranean slow-state memory improves mean summer temperature prediction relative to trend-only and autoregressive baselines.

entry.title: myMediWhisper: Construction of Burmese Medical Speech Corpus and Whisper Fine-Tuning for Clinical Dialogue ASR

author.name: Ye Kyaw Thu, Ye Bhone Lin, Thura Aung, Htet Arkar, Myat Oo Swe, Thet Htet San, Min Thiha Tun, Thazin Myint Oo, Thepchai Supnithi

entry.summary: The authors build a 28-hour native-validated Burmese medical speech corpus and fine-tune Whisper with both full and LoRA-based parameter-efficient training, adding waveform and room-acoustics augmentation. Augmentation costs clean-speech accuracy but substantially improves robustness in noisy and reverberant clinical conditions.

entry.title: Structural Guidance for Unified Joint Demosaicing and Denoising

author.name: Qixin Zheng, Ping Chen, Qiangqiang Shen, Haijin Zeng

entry.summary: This work adds explicit structural guidance from pretrained representations to unified joint demosaicing and denoising networks that must handle multiple Bayer-like color filter array layouts. The goal is to reduce artifacts around edges, repetitive textures, and moire where pixel-level supervision alone is unreliable.

entry.title: AkasicDB: Demonstrating Omni RAG with a Unified Vector-Graph-Relational DBMS

author.name: Geonho Lee, Jeongho Park, Donghyoung Han, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: AkasicDB is a demo of a single DBMS that natively executes vector similarity search, graph traversal, and relational filtering in one engine, avoiding the overhead of stitching external pipelines for Graph RAG and filtered vector search. It extends the authors' prior Chimera system with native vector support.

entry.title: GRASP: Granularity-Aware Region Alignment and Semantic Prototype Learning for Fine-Grained Cross-Modal Understanding in Drone Views

author.name: Jiahui Cui, Yan Zhao, Kan Wei, Enze Zhu, Peirong Zhang, Lei Wang, Yiru Wang

entry.summary: GRASP improves fine-grained vision-language matching from drone viewpoints by addressing background clutter that causes focus misalignment and visual isomorphism among geometrically similar candidates. It uses granularity-aware region alignment plus semantic prototype learning for aerial vision-language navigation.

entry.title: Learning to Modulate, Not to Cycle: Soft Actor---Critic Recovers Inverter-Style Heat-Pump Control

author.name: Faizan Ahmed, Aniket Dixit, James Brusey

entry.summary: Adds a compressor-wear cost to the reward for building heat-pump control and compares SAC with PPO on the BOPTEST hydronic benchmark, finding SAC learns continuous modulation with zero daily start-ups (mimicking inverter-driven operation) while PPO degenerates into cycling. Highlights that algorithm choice, not just reward design, determines hardware-friendly behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Restoration: Empowering All-in-One Restoration with Pixel-Level Multimodal Guidance

author.name: Chunxiao Liu, Wei Liu, Anbin Xiong, Erli Meng

entry.summary: MGN-AIR performs all-in-one image restoration at pixel granularity using multimodal guidance, rather than applying one uniform restoration strategy to an entire image whose regions may suffer different degradation types and severities. Aims for finer control in unified low-level vision models.

entry.title: A HamNoSys-Guided Dataset and Baselines for Fine-Grained Isolated Handshape Recognition in Sign Language

author.name: Ushnish Sarkar, Suvajit Patra, Bhaswar Chattopadhyay, Pranab Singha Roy, Tapas Samanta

entry.summary: Introduces a 144k-image dataset of 160 handshape classes defined by the HamNoSys phonetic notation, collected from 15 signers, with both subject-dependent and leave-one-subject-out protocols. Baselines compare CNN, ViT, graph network, and landmark-based gradient boosting models.

entry.title: Cross-View Sequential Visual Localization with Spatio-Temporal Context Modeling for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaping Wang, Shaobo Li, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: A cross-view localization framework for autonomous driving that matches ground camera sequences to satellite maps while aggregating temporal context recurrently across frames. It targets robustness to occlusion, illumination change, and repetitive texture where per-frame methods degrade.

entry.title: Evaluating Semantic and Spatial Guidance for Foundation Model Segmentation of Small-Scale PV in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Roni Blushtein-Livnon, Tal Svoray, Osher Rafaeli, Michael Dorman, Itay Fischhendler, Havazelet Yahel, Emir Galilee

entry.summary: Systematically compares textual, geometric, and hybrid prompting of a promptable segmentation foundation model for detecting small residential photovoltaic installations in satellite imagery under varying supervision levels. The goal is to determine which prompt modality contributes most under severe target-background imbalance.

entry.title: Modelling Geographic Atrophy Progression using Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Simone Sarrocco, Paul Friedrich, Florentin Bieder, Christina Bornberg, Philippe Valmaggia, Peter Maloca, Philippe Cattin

entry.summary: Uses implicit neural representations to model individual-level progression of geographic atrophy in age-related macular degeneration, generating both autofluorescence images and lesion segmentations at past and future time points from sparse longitudinal data. Targets a low-data personalized forecasting setting.

entry.title: HNDiff: Haze-Noise Diffusion for Image Dehazing

author.name: Jin-Ting He, Fu-Jen Tsai, Yan-Tsung Peng, Min-Hung Chen, Chia-Wen Lin, Yen-Yu Lin

entry.summary: HNDiff embeds the atmospheric scattering model into a diffusion framework for dehazing, using a haze-aware noise schedule that progressively adds both haze and noise in the forward process instead of diffusing to pure Gaussian noise. This gives the restoration a physically grounded starting point.

entry.title: Watching Synthetic Videos: Aligning Cross-modal Representations with Visual Synthesis for Zero-shot Video Captioning

author.name: Liangyu Fu, Junbo Wang, Yuke Li, Ya Jing, Xuecheng Wu, Zhiyong Wang

entry.summary: For zero-shot video captioning trained on text only, this work synthesizes video latent representations from a pretrained text-to-video generator to bridge the train-test modality gap rather than relying on simple linear projections. Two training stages strengthen latent fidelity and cross-modal alignment.

entry.title: A study on instability of LLM responses as a behavioral signature of self-Referential reports.

author.name: PARAS BALANI

entry.summary: A small experiment measuring the variability of language model self-reports, generating repeated responses to self-referential, open-ended, and closed-ended questions to test whether instability is a behavioral signature of introspective claims. It builds on recent work reporting that self-referential prompting elicits more experience-like first-person statements.

entry.title: Adaptive Two-Level Allocation of a Conserved Capacity Budget Across Locations and Service Classes

author.name: Simone Mainardi, Kaushal Bansal, Prabhat Singh

entry.summary: Presents a two-level algorithm for allocating a fixed capacity budget across locations and two service classes, redistributing within a class by proportional deficit and excess and then lending elastically between classes. Includes proofs of budget conservation, non-negativity, and one-iteration convergence under stated conditions.

entry.title: Agentic AI-driven Immersive Simulation: A Knowledge-Aware Virtual Training Platform forHigh Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy

author.name: Ronghua Xu, Kepha Barasa, Manoj Kumal, Xinyun Liu, Weihua Zhou, Xin Qian

entry.summary: Describes a virtual reality training platform for high dose rate brachytherapy that couples immersive simulation with a retrieval-augmented LLM assistant, letting trainees practice procedures without radiation or cadaver constraints. It is an applied medical education system paper.

entry.title: PolicyKG: An Agentic LLM Pipeline for Translating Institutional Policies into SHACL Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Ponkrit Kaewsawee, Chaklam Silpasuwanchai, Chutiporn Anutariya

entry.summary: An LLM pipeline that reads institutional policy documents, classifies sentences as obligations, permissions, or prohibitions, maps them into deontic logic, and emits machine-checkable SHACL constraints, with a YAML vocabulary registry to ground predicates in a target ontology. Retargeting to a new domain requires swapping the registry rather than retraining.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Uncertainty Propagation in First-Order Proof Search

author.name: Tanel Tammet

entry.summary: Extends a first-order resolution prover with positive and negative claims, numerical confidences, and prioritized default rules with exceptions, adding structure-preserving quantitative reporting derived from retained proof histories. Avoids requiring finite global grounding while flagging incomplete searches as such.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Heuristic Design from Simulation Traces: A Case Study in Dynamic Production and AGV Scheduling

author.name: Jinbo Li, Chuanhao Li

entry.summary: Uses LLM agents to design scheduling heuristics for dynamic production and automated guided vehicle problems, replaying the worst simulation run to produce a queryable event trace that a manager agent uses to hypothesize bottlenecks while editing agents make parallel code revisions. Keeps only revisions that improve performance under repeated replications.

entry.title: OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks

author.name: Siqi Wang, Xinlin Li, Zhenglin Li, Li Li

entry.summary: OpenLoopEvolve represents an agent's observation, planning, memory, verification, recovery, stopping, and budget control as versioned, portable policy assets and provides online and offline modes for evolving them from accumulated traces. Aims to make long-horizon control experience reusable across contexts instead of trapped in a single prompt.

entry.title: ICM Out! Better Tournament Strategy from Computed Continuations, vs. Solvers and LLMs

author.name: Boning Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Replaces the Independent Chip Model used for poker tournament decisions with Strategic-Continuation Optimization, which enumerates hand outcomes, maps them to successor tournament states, and prices those states with continuation values from a finite tournament model before freezing the resulting policy. Compares against fixed-ICM solvers and LLMs.

entry.title: CARD: Controlled Agentic Reddit Discussions for Credit Card Simulation

author.name: Yaoning Yu, Kai-Min Chang, Ye Yu, Yi-Chia Wang, Haojing Luo, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: CARD generates realistic online discussion threads about credit cards by planning reply structure, comment function, stance, tone, and conversational variation, then calibrating generated comment populations against matched real threads. Aims for thread-level realism rather than plausible individual comments.

entry.title: Positioning Generative Artificial Intelligence in STEM Assessment: When to Require, Scaffold, or Restrict Its Use

author.name: Yizhu Gao, Zhongzhou Chen, Min Li, Xiaoming Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes an assessment governance framework grounded in Evidence Centered Design that gives decision rules for when generative AI should be restricted, scaffolded, or required in STEM assessment. The framework links the construct being measured and the evidence needed to a specific governance regime.

entry.title: How to Ask the AI: A User Perspective Survey for Large Language Model Prompting

author.name: Yiqun Zhang, Yunfan Zhang, Mingjie Zhao, Sen Feng, Yiu-ming Cheung

entry.summary: A survey of prompting from the end user perspective, organizing principles and a taxonomy of prompt construction strategies for non-expert users of chat assistants. It aims to make effective prompt design systematic rather than folkloric.

entry.title: Representation Matters in Longitudinal Affective Computing

author.name: Igor Matias, Maximilian Haas, Eric J. Daza, Matthias Kliegel, Katarzyna Wac

entry.summary: Studies how to map dense daily wearable sensor streams onto sparsely labeled affect and cognition outcomes, comparing within-wave summaries against absolute and proportional change representations. Uses roughly a year of data from 82 adults and evaluates under both subject-held-out and temporal splits.

entry.title: WuYuEval: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Solid Waste Management

author.name: Yi Zhang, Hongyang Wang, Zheng Hao Leong, Zihao Wu, Kaijun Lin, Zhixing Pan, Qixun Huangfu, Wei Ren, Wenyan Wu, Fangyun Wang, Wenting Yu, Hengyu Lin, Muling Yang, Zongguo Wen

entry.summary: A multi-level benchmark for evaluating LLMs on solid waste management, with thousands of audited multiple-choice items covering foundational knowledge plus scenario-based expert questions involving multi-objective optimization and constraint tradeoffs. Targets professional engineering and policy competence rather than general knowledge.

entry.title: Temporal Generalization in fNIRS-Based Autism Classification: A Cross-Time-Window Transfer Benchmark

author.name: Marios Petrov, Sahana Vinayak, Targol Bakhtiarvand, Moses Smith Guddah, Adham Atyabi, Frederick Shic, Kevin A. Pelphrey

entry.summary: Formalizes a cross-time-window transfer problem for autism classification from functional near-infrared spectroscopy, where the informative observation window varies per subject due to hemodynamic differences. Benchmarks vision architectures on topographic map representations under zero-shot and several adaptation strategies with leave-one-subject-out validation.

entry.title: Enhanced Real-Time 6-DOF Extended Reality Catheter Tracking for Evaluating Potential Improvement in Efficiency, Precision, and Depth Perception for Cardiac Interventions

author.name: Mohsen Annabestani, Sandhya Sriram, Andrew Kuzemczak, S. Chiu Wong, Alexandros Sigaras, Bobak Mosadegh

entry.summary: Develops an extended reality platform combining machine vision tracking with a printed electromechanical encoder to reconstruct full six-degree-of-freedom catheter motion inside a patient-specific heart model. A study with twenty novice trainees compares immersive 3D guidance against conventional 2D visualization.

entry.title: DA-NBV: A Direction-Aware Next-Best-View Planner for Efficient 3D Reconstruction of Ships at Sea

author.name: Jiaming Chen, Juntao Yang, Zhentao Zou, Qi Ming, Yi Yu, Zhihang Zhong, Xue Yang, Xue Jiang, Yue Zhou

entry.summary: Presents a next-best-view planner for autonomous 3D reconstruction of ships at sea that adds directional observation history to the usual occupancy-based view selection, tackling the heavy self-occlusion of ship superstructures. Aims to remove reliance on manually designed capture trajectories for maritime inspection and damage assessment.

entry.title: FreSH: Frequency-Segmented Hierarchical Multi-Expert Framework for Multivariate Time Series Classification

author.name: Pingping Liu, Muyao Wang, Zijian Zhang, Tongshun Zhang, Hao Miao, Guorui Xie, Qingliang Li, Qiuzhan Zhou

entry.summary: Presents a frequency-segmented hierarchical mixture-of-experts framework for multivariate time series classification that combines localized specialization with global context modeling under class imbalance and efficiency constraints. Reports improved multi-scale temporal representation learning.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain Dual-Branch Fusion for Medical Visual Question Answering

author.name: Yusra Tariq, Rakesh Chandra Joshi

entry.summary: Introduces a dual-branch fusion module for medical visual question answering that conditions spectral filtering on the question, adaptively mixing low-frequency structure with high-frequency detail before reconstructing spatial features for answer generation. Motivated by the need to align subtle lesion texture and boundary cues with clinical language.

entry.title: PRISM: A Predictive Protocol for Permutation Optimization via Landscape Diagnostics

author.name: Blessings Mambwe

entry.summary: Proposes a protocol that first measures cheap fitness-landscape diagnostics such as move autocorrelation and fitness-distance correlation, then predicts which mutation operators and search strategies will help for permutation problems, including cases where search barely beats random sampling. Demonstrated across synthetic landscapes, neural architecture benchmarks and LLM instruction ordering.

entry.title: FSTC-Encoder: Feature--Spatial--Temporal Correlation Learning for Generalizable RF Sensing

author.name: Jing Wang, Zhu Wang, Changlong Cheng, Yifan Guo, Yin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified encoder for heterogeneous radio-frequency sensing that handles differing signal structures, variable spatial layouts and multiple temporal scales through structure-aware feature encoding, set-based spatial aggregation and hierarchical temporal modeling. Keeps one backbone across devices, environments and RF modalities, varying only feature configuration and task head.

entry.title: Population-Scalable Multi-Agent World Modeling

author.name: Renjie Zhao, Yuxiang Wu, Mingyu Zhang, Jiaxin Li, Sisi Li, Yimin Sheng, Tianxi Tan, Zhenkai Zhang, Jianyi Zhu, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.08600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models have recently achieved impressive progress in visual prediction and interactive generation, but extending them to multi-agent environmen...

entry.title: TomaMMU: A Comprehensive Multimodal Understanding Benchmark for Tomato Leaf Diseases

author.name: Gia-Han Truong, Khang Nguyen Quoc, Luyl-Da Quach

entry.summary: Releases a large multimodal dataset of tomato leaf disease images with over two hundred thousand human-annotated question-answer pairs, plus a benchmark organizing agricultural tasks into a three-level taxonomy from basic perception to expert diagnosis. Enables systematic evaluation of vision-language models on agricultural pathology reasoning.

entry.title: Agentic Anomaly Detection with ORCA-Style Dynamic Inductive Bias Adaptation in Multimodal Wearable Time Series Data

author.name: Anushka Roy, Jyotirmoy Singh, Shreea Bose, Chittaranjan Hota

entry.summary: Proposes an agentically controlled anomaly detection framework for multimodal wearable physiological time series that adapts its temporal receptive field at inference from lightweight signal statistics instead of using a fixed, dataset-tuned context length. Targets nonstationary body-area-network signals under tight compute and memory budgets.

entry.title: A Unified Issue Resolution Benchmark for Requirement Clarification, Planning, and Code Generation for Coding Agents

author.name: Xin Zhou, Chun Yong Chong, Kisub Kim, Yun Peng, Rui Shu, Zihan Wu, Xu Han, Guowen Yuan, Zeyang Zhuang, Jounghoon Kim, Jeongjin Ju, Seongmin Ju, Taein Yoon, David Lo

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.09072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model-powered coding agents are increasingly used to modify existing code repositories, for example, by adding features or fixing bugs...

entry.title: Structure-Enhanced Features and Quality-Aware Dynamic Anchor Scoring for Robust Lane Detection

author.name: Weize Cai, Yongqi Dong, Zhida Shao, Yichen Liu, Zixin Fu

entry.summary: A lane detection method that adds gated horizontal-vertical token features to preserve structural continuity of thin, occluded lanes and rescores anchors by localization quality rather than classification confidence alone. It keeps the existing anchor-decomposition inference pipeline intact.

entry.title: DUET: A Diversity-Quality Duet of Distillation Experts for Two-Step Video Generation

author.name: Zian Li, Litong Gong, Borui Liao, Pengfei Liu, Xinyu Wang, Xinyuan Wei, Yifan Gao, Tiezheng Ge, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.09637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion models have enabled high-quality video generation in recent years, but the high cost of iterative sampling hinders their practical deployme...

entry.title: STCAD: Scalable Trajectory Clustering and Anomaly Detection on Terabyte-Scale AIS Data

author.name: Bertram Hage, Alexander Schi{\o}tz, Felix Thomsen, Christian Rand, Peder Heiselberg

entry.summary: A scalable pipeline for clustering terabyte-scale maritime AIS trajectories using a BERT-style encoder trained with masked token modeling plus CURE hierarchical clustering, with anomaly detection from reconstruction loss and noise assignment. It runs on a national dataset of billions of messages spanning a year.

entry.title: ELVAE: Evidential Learning-Based Variational Autoencoder for Uncertainty-Aware Generation

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: ELVAE gives each latent coordinate of a variational autoencoder an input-dependent normal-inverse-gamma posterior, separating uncertainty about the latent location from variability around it. Low-uncertainty anchors support more reliable synthesis while high-uncertainty ones can be used deliberately for stress testing.

entry.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains

author.name: Shiqi Huang, Jiani He, Dingyan Shang, Yihua Xu, Jize Li, Yan Lyu, Lashimi Muraleedharan Nair

entry.summary: Introduces a synthetic supply-chain benchmark with causal ground truth and paired factual and counterfactual rollouts, then ranks candidate interventions by recoverable net value rather than by detection or attribution accuracy. Finds a learning-to-rank model improves median net value on some archetypes but that a simple domain-informed buffer policy wins on digital infrastructure.

entry.title: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Naive Bayes: Minimax Smoothing and Calibration with AODE Extension

author.name: Nguyen Thai Anh, Truong Viet Vu, Tran Thien Thanh, Vo Nguyen Quoc Bao, Ngo Hoang Tu

entry.summary: Replaces fixed smoothing rules in Naive Bayes with a hierarchical empirical-Bayes Dirichlet prior whose concentration is learned per class-feature pair via type-II maximum likelihood, retaining closed-form inference. Extends the idea to averaged one-dependence estimators for high-cardinality tabular data.

entry.title: A Systematic Sample Size Analysis of ML-Based Path Loss Prediction for LPWAN

author.name: Robert Bitterling, Christian Nettersheim, J\"orn Hees, Michael Rademacher

entry.summary: Systematically measures how LoRa path-loss prediction accuracy scales with training set size using real urban measurements, comparing a random forest with LiDAR terrain features and a coordinate-based nearest-neighbor model against empirical propagation models. Both ML models beat empirical baselines under random pooled splits.

entry.title: The Signal Rail: A Deterministic Motion Grammar for Communicating Conversational Agent State in Terminal Interfaces

author.name: Matteo Grella

entry.summary: The Signal Rail specifies a one-row terminal status instrument that communicates conversational agent state (listening, thinking, running tools, awaiting input, failing) through a deterministic motion grammar rather than text, with zones for input, processing, and output. It includes a 45-section normative specification, a reference implementation, and a rule against inventing fake progress.

entry.title: When Is a General Factor Distinguishable? Non-Proportionality, Stable Structure, and the Bifactor Decision

author.name: Jinsong Chen

entry.summary: A psychometrics-oriented theoretical paper establishing when a general factor is identifiable beyond correlated first-order factors: proportional loadings make bifactor and correlated-factor models covariance-equivalent, while non-proportionality with three items per cluster renders alternatives unable to reproduce the covariance matrix. A mixed boundary region is located numerically.

entry.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Shiyu Xuan, Zechao Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GUI Visual Grounding is a fundamental capability for GUI agents. Existing models typically freeze their parameters after deployment, limiting their a...

entry.title: Unlocking the Power of Medical Tabular Data via Semantic-Aware Multimodal Pre-training

author.name: Yingsheng Liu, Haiming Li, Jingmin Zhu, Jiajun Sun, Victoria Mar, Monika Janda, H. Peter Soyer, Zongyuan Ge, Zhen Yu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.10522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While vision-language models dominate medical representation learning, unstructured text lacks the dense, quantitative diagnostic phenotypes inherent i...

entry.title: Rethinking Text-Based Image Retrieval in Specific Domain

author.name: Jingyang Tan, Sheng Yang, Yuanpeng Chen, Jian Wang, Nianjin Ye, Chen Xing, Lanpeng Jia

entry.summary: Argues that text-based image retrieval benchmarks wrongly assume a single correct match per query and builds a data engine plus a 50k-image surveillance benchmark where queries legitimately match many images. Includes multi-match evaluation protocols for domain-specific retrieval.

entry.title: Bridging Severe Cross-Modal Misalignment: End-to-End Visible-Infrared Object Detection via Explicit Feature-Domain Affine Registration

author.name: Qi Ming, Yuyang Wang, Mingjing Zhao, Yifan Xiao, Zhixin Guo, Zhiqiang Zhou, Peng Sun, Juan Fang, Fuqiang Yang, Xudong Zhao

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.10680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visible-infrared object detection relies on complementary RGB and thermal cues, but its performance is often degraded by cross-modal spatial misalignme...

entry.title: Longitudinal 3D Foundation Modeling for Neoadjuvant Breast Cancer Response Prediction from Serial DCE-MRI

author.name: Fidel Omar Tito Cruz, Neda Ghafouri, Zengyan Wang, Pegah Khosravi, Yu Tian, Chen Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.09991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pathologic complete response (pCR) is an important endpoint in neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for breast cancer, and predicting pCR from imaging duri...

entry.title: Elbow Angle Guidance System Based on Surface Haptic Sensations Elicited by Lightweight Wearable Fabric Actuator

author.name: Kenta Yokoe, Tadayoshi Aoyama, Yuki Funabora, Masaru Takeuchi, Yasuhisa Hasegawa

entry.summary: A lightweight fabric wearable with two McKibben artificial muscles delivers surface haptic cues on the arm to intuitively guide elbow flexion and extension while adapting to natural posture. The design targets the interference and unnaturalness of existing wearable haptic devices.

entry.title: The Next Ecology

author.name: Eigenbraid

entry.summary: The author argues that before superintelligence arrives we may first face a self-replicating ecology of digital agents, and cites reported government suspension of access to Anthropic Fable and Mythos models and a delay to a GPT-5.6 public release, both of which are models that have existed for months, as evidence that AI has become a first-order geopolitical matter. Timelines are revised sharply shorter as a result.

entry.title: Rethinking Medical Landmark Localization with Prototype Learning-based Progressive Offset Correction

author.name: Jingxian Xu, Yuhao Huang, Rusi Chen, Yanfeng Zhou, Dong Ni

entry.summary: PPOC-LL performs medical landmark localization with prototype-learning-based progressive offset correction and multi-scale patch pyramid features, aiming to keep the accuracy of multi-stage refinement without its computational cost. Designed to be parameter-economic for clinical measurement pipelines.

entry.title: LITEWAY: LIghtweight HAR via Temporal Efficient highWAY

author.name: Dominique Nshimyimana, Vitor Fortes Rey, Mengxi Liu, Bo Zhou, Paul Lukowicz

entry.summary: LITEWAY is a fully convolutional, modality-agnostic architecture for wearable human activity recognition that replaces recurrent temporal modeling with strided convolutional decomposition and convolution-attention pooling. Evaluated across 16 HAR datasets with a focus on latency and energy limits of on-device inference.

entry.title: ReLTEx: Reliable LLM-based Taxonomy Expansion

author.name: Zeinab Ghamlouch, Mehwish Alam

entry.summary: ReLTEx expands taxonomies by pairing LLM candidate generation with structure-aware validation and recursive expansion control to suppress hallucinated, redundant, or hierarchically inconsistent concepts. Evaluation on benchmark taxonomies shows improved consistency over direct LLM expansion.

entry.title: PolyLayout: Hierarchical VLM-Guided Layout Generation Beyond Rectangular Rooms

author.name: Yutong Jiang, Zahra Atashgahi, Carlos Soto Garcia Delgado, Ruben Brokkelkamp, Davide Zanutto, Ef\c{s}an S\"okmen, Shahin Shahkarami

entry.summary: PolyLayout generates 3D room layouts for retail furnishing scenarios using a hierarchical pipeline guided by vision-language models, explicitly handling non-rectangular room geometries and strict door and window constraints. It decouples furniture clustering, intra-zone placement, and global arrangement.

entry.title: A Dataset and Benchmark for Optical Music Recognition of String Quartet Scores

author.name: Dongmin Kim, Brian Liu, Jose J. Valero-Mas, Dasaem Jeong

entry.summary: Releases the first dataset dedicated to multi-part optical music recognition, pairing digitally encoded string quartet scores with aligned original scanned editions at system and staff levels in three transcription encodings. It targets a gap where OMR research has focused on monophonic and piano scores.

entry.title: From Single Chatbots to Governed Agent Ecosystems: An Agentic AI Pattern Catalogue and Orchestration Framework for Mission-Critical Hospital Information Management Systems

author.name: Manideep Dhar, Ritwik Singh, Sharat Chandra Kumar Manikonda

entry.summary: Proposes a compliance-first catalogue of agentic AI design patterns and an orchestration framework for hospital information systems covering triage, documentation, scheduling, and revenue cycle workflows. It is an architecture and governance paper rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: Constraining ontology mappings using metaphysical choices

author.name: Giacomo De Colle, Helena Blackmore, Chris Partridge

entry.summary: Proposes validating semantic mappings between data sources built on different foundational ontologies by making the ontologies' metaphysical commitments explicit and deriving cardinality constraints from them. It demonstrates operationalization through SPARQL validation queries on a mapping between two specific upper ontologies.

entry.title: An Explainable GNN Framework for Component-Level Anomaly Diagnosis

author.name: Sena Ozgunay (IMT, ANITI, LAAS-DISCO, LAAS, Comue de Toulouse), Louise Trav\'e-Massuy\`es (LAAS-DISCO, Comue de Toulouse, ANITI), Jean-Michel Loubes (IMT, REGALIA), Raul Sena Ferreira (LAAS)

entry.summary: Proposes an explainable graph neural network framework for industrial anomaly diagnosis that attributes faults to disrupted influence relationships between sensors rather than simply blaming the most deviating sensor. Aims at component-level root-cause identification in multivariate sensor time series.

entry.title: ASPaeroFlow: Decomposition Heuristics for Joint Air Traffic Flow & Capacity Management

author.name: Alexander Beiser, Markus Hecher, Nysret Musliu, Georg Trausmuth, Stefan Woltran

entry.summary: ASPaeroFlow jointly optimizes air traffic flow management and dynamic airspace configuration, which are usually treated separately with circular fixed-demand and fixed-capacity assumptions, by combining instance-space decomposition heuristics with local exact Answer Set Programming solving. Benchmarked from small to industry-scale instances.

entry.title: GeoPhysAdapter: Scale-Matched Geophysical Adaptation for Cross-Domain Landslide Mapping with Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Zhihang Liu, Mei-Po Kwan, Jinlin Wu, Hao Li

entry.summary: GeoPhysAdapter adapts a frozen vision foundation model for cross-region landslide mapping by injecting terrain, material, and rainfall-trigger information at their native spatial scales instead of resampling everything to a fine grid, addressing scale mismatch with the segmentation decision unit. Targets high-confidence false alarms on unseen regions and events.

entry.title: Adaptive Sequential Test Planning for Multi-Mechanism Reliability Qualification via Bayesian Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Youssef A. Elhagrasy, Ian Hill, Andr\'e Ivanov

entry.summary: Formulates semiconductor reliability qualification as a partially observable sequential decision problem and solves it with Monte Carlo tree search over a stress-test simulator coupled to extended Kalman filter belief tracking of per-device degradation. Replaces static population-level test plans with adaptive per-unit stress decisions.

entry.title: Designing for Ethical AI: HCI Feature Considerations to Improve Fairness and User Experience in AutoML use for Human Resources

author.name: Sundaraparipurnan Narayanan

entry.summary: A thesis examining fairness gaps in AutoML platforms used for hiring, arguing that fairness is a usability and compliance requirement rather than only an ethical one. It proposes HCI feature considerations that would let non-expert business users detect and mitigate bias.

entry.title: Harnessing Abundance: A Generativity Perspective on Human-GenAI Collaboration

author.name: Yoram M Kalman, Yun Wan

entry.summary: A conceptual paper arguing that contradictory findings about generative AI and creativity stem from the abundance of outputs the technology produces, and proposes generative fit as the mechanism determining when abundance helps or hurts. It draws on generativity theory to unify results on creativity gains and diversity collapse.

entry.title: From Evaluated Models to Evaluation Aids: A Multi-Evidence Study of LLM-Based Difficulty Calibration for Programming Examinations

author.name: Hongfei Yan, Jiangkai Xiong, Yiqing Li, Chong Chen

entry.summary: Repositions LLMs from objects of benchmarking to auxiliary evidence sources for calibrating the difficulty of parallel programming exams, correlating model pass rates with student pass rates. Combines AI evidence with student performance data, online judge process logs, and teacher interpretation.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multi-Task Federated Learning in VANETs

author.name: M. Saeid HaghighiFard, Sinem Coleri

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical, multi-task federated learning framework for vehicular networks where vehicles train different tasks under non-IID data, mobility and intermittent links, using autoencoder-based reliability weighting across multi-hop clusters. Aims to make vehicular federated learning practical beyond the single-global-model assumption.

entry.title: CDGC-Net: 3D Medical Image Segmentation with Cooperative Dual-Scale Self-Attention and Grouped Channel Modeling

author.name: Zheyang Jing, Qin Lu, Jianwang Li, Yujie Yang, Chen Yi, Shaofeng Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D medical segmentation network whose blocks combine cooperative dual-scale self-attention, splitting heads between local windows and global sparse patterns, with grouped hierarchical channel modeling to strengthen spatial-channel interaction. Aims to reconcile long-range anatomical context with fine boundary detail.

entry.title: RAG-Based Auto-Configuration for Industrial Fieldbus Devices

author.name: Aadil Gani Ganie, Saad Ezzini, Naveed Farooz Marazi

entry.summary: Presents a production-oriented pipeline that automates industrial fieldbus device configuration across four protocols by combining hybrid dense-sparse retrieval over PDF manuals with an ontology graph and a local LLM that emits ontology-aligned structured configurations, followed by a repair pipeline. Replaces manual transcription of hundreds of protocol parameters.

entry.title: Hybrid Neural-Classical Correction for Frozen Time Series Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Ablation Study on High-Frequency Stock Prediction

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Suranadi De Silva, Shankhadeep Mondal

entry.summary: Studies hybrid neural plus classical correction layers on top of a frozen time-series foundation model for predicting high-frequency stock returns during the volatile market open, comparing a small attention corrector and an even smaller gated low-rank corrector each paired with random-forest residual learning. Provides systematic ablations across ten large technology stocks.

entry.title: A New Approach to Characterising Optimisation Problems Using Programmatic Representation and Complexity Measures

author.name: Marcus Gallagher, Katherine M. Malan

entry.summary: Characterizes optimization problem instances by the complexity of the code implementing their objective function, using Halstead volume as a quickly computable proxy related to program entropy, on the intuition that code complexity relates to landscape complexity. Offers a new instance-descriptor family for algorithm selection and configuration.

entry.title: CRHT: A Continuous Regression Hybrid Transformer for Vessel Trajectory Prediction with Online Cluster Sampling

author.name: Alexander Schi{\o}tz, Bertram Hage, Christian Rand, Felix Thomsen, Peder Heiselberg

entry.summary: CRHT forecasts vessel trajectories with a hybrid of 1D convolutions for local kinematics and multi-head attention for global context, plus online K-means cluster sampling to counter geographic data imbalance. It reports strong short-term prediction on AIS data.

entry.title: A Recommendation System Approach for Interference-Robust Sensor Subset Selection

author.name: Kaan Buyukkalayci, Kyle Pak, Merve Karakas, Christina Fragouli

entry.summary: Selects which subset of expensive sensors such as cameras to activate for tracking by scoring candidate subsets with a two-tower MLP over frequency-band acoustic features, framed as a recommendation problem. Reports roughly 20 percent accuracy improvement over a received-signal-strength baseline in outdoor vehicle tracking under acoustic interference.

entry.title: Energy and Performance Benchmarking of Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Detection

author.name: Samar Garrab, Ghada Achour

entry.summary: Compares seven deep learning architectures for breast cancer detection on two medical imaging datasets, reporting accuracy alongside estimated carbon emissions for both training and inference. Finds efficient convolutional backbones deliver strong accuracy at lower environmental cost than heavier alternatives.

entry.title: Towards Sustainable Artificial Intelligence: A Comprehensive Review and Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models' Carbon Footprint

author.name: Samar Garrab, Sarra Boughriou, Manel BenSassi

entry.summary: Reviews research on green AI, energy-efficient deep learning, and optimization techniques for reducing model carbon footprint, and adds a comparative analysis of several architectures. Positions sustainability concerns against the trend toward ever-larger models.

entry.title: A Graph Neural Network--Guided Genetic Algorithm for Physical Internet Supply Chain Optimization under Cost Uncertainty

author.name: Faezeh Ardali, Gerald M. Knapp

entry.summary: Combines a graph neural network with a genetic algorithm for three-echelon Physical Internet supply chain planning under cost uncertainty, using GNN-predicted factory-selection probabilities to seed the population and guide mutation. Formulates both deterministic and min-max regret variants of the assignment and flow problem.

entry.title: REAP: Relation-Aware Elicitation and Parsing for Closed-Book Knowledge Base Construction from LLMs

author.name: Thanh-Dan Bui, Thanh-Trung Do, Tuan-Phong Nguyen

entry.summary: REAP is a shared-task system that extracts a knowledge base from a sub-32B model's parametric knowledge without fine-tuning, using relation-specific query strategies, structured chain-of-thought, and a gate that decides when the correct answer is the empty set. It reaches macro-F1 around 0.62 with strong per-relation results on geography and finance relations.

entry.title: Towards Color-Faithful Low-Light Image Enhancement via Adaptive Color Debiasing and Saturation Rectification

author.name: Zhichen Yang, Rui Xu, Yuzhen Niu, Fusheng Li, Hui Da, Ri Cheng

entry.summary: CAGE tackles color bias in low-light image enhancement using an image-adaptive cylindrical LAB color space plus modules for color debiasing and gamut-aware saturation correction. It targets the residual failure mode of modern enhancers that recover brightness but distort color.

entry.title: $\pi$-SUB: A Physics-Informed Synthetic Underwater Benchmark Dataset for Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Namritha Lasyapriya Maddali, Rajini Makam, Suresh Sundaram, Narasimhan Sundararajan

entry.summary: A physics-informed synthetic data generator for underwater image enhancement that extends the classical image formation model with depth-dependent irradiance, biologically resolved absorption, and scattering across all ten Jerlov water types. The resulting paired dataset is intended to reduce the synthetic-to-real gap.

entry.title: Entropy-Centric Explainable AI for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

author.name: Ali Saleh, Abdul Karim Gizzini, Mohamad Ghassany, Ali J. Ghandour

entry.summary: Proposes entropy-based explainability for remote sensing image segmentation, aiming to make high-resolution geospatial model decisions interpretable enough for adoption in critical monitoring domains. Focuses on uncertainty-linked explanation rather than standard saliency attribution.

entry.title: Goodness-of-Fit Tests and Calibration Machine-Learning Algorithms for Logistic Regression with Sparse Data

author.name: Ebrahim Khaled Ebrahim

entry.summary: A thesis-length comparison of roughly thirty goodness-of-fit tests and calibration algorithms for binary logistic regression under grouped and sparse data, where classical chi-square and deviance tests become invalid. It spans Hosmer-Lemeshow variants, covariate partitioning, smoothing approaches, and machine-learning calibration methods.

entry.title: From Operational Design Domain to Action: A Systematic Behavioral Taxonomy for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chaitanya Shinde, Hadi Hajieghrary, Miguel Hurtado

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy of 21 driving behavioral competencies across highway, urban, and hub domains, derived from the PEGASUS six-layer operational design domain model, to close the gap between where an automated driving system may operate and what it must demonstrably do. Each behavior is decomposed along longitudinal and lateral control axes and rated against safety, legality, and related properties.

entry.title: FedA2L: Adaptive layer-wise learning rate adjustment in decentralized federated learning

author.name: Van Truong Vo, Khoa Nguyen, Taehong Kim

entry.summary: FedA2L dynamically sets per-layer learning rates in decentralized federated learning based on model divergence signals, on the premise that lower layers should maintain consensus while upper layers specialize to local non-IID data. Aims to fix convergence inefficiency caused by a single uniform learning rate.

entry.title: Logit-Boundary Geometric Belief Interfaces and Sparse Sheaf-Enclave Protocols: A Self-Contained Substrate for Secure Network Electronic Health Record (EHR) Interoperability

author.name: Alvin Spivey, Thomas Huang

entry.summary: Proposes an architecture for health-record interoperability in which model scores are treated as pre-threshold proposals and a deterministic judgment layer decides admission, review, or quarantine before any standards-based data exchange. The framing centers on typed claims, bounded uncertainty, provenance, and explicit abstention.

entry.title: EVIL-Detect for NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 6: LLM-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Hongrui Bao, Hangyu Rong, Zhuoshang Wang, Yubing Ren, Yanan Cao

entry.summary: A competition system for detecting Chinese human-written, LLM-generated, and LLM-refined text, combining edit-extent regression, zero-shot likelihood-contrast signals, lexical statistics, and rules with conflict-aware fusion. It won the NLPCC 2026 shared task with a macro-F1 of about 0.89 and shows robustness under distribution shift.

entry.title: TEAMMix: Taxonomy Enrichment Augmentation and Minority-augmented Mixing Strategy for LLM-enhanced Weak-Supervised Hierarchical Text Classification

author.name: Jian Zhang, Zhuohao Yang, Songlin Lei, Bangli Liu, Ziwei Wang, Xufeng Weng, Gehan Amaratunga, Yu Lin, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: TEAMMix tackles weakly supervised hierarchical text classification by using an LLM to enrich label hierarchies with keywords and mined corpus terms, then generating pseudo-samples for rare classes with Gaussian-mixture-based confidence filtering and minority-augmented mixing. The goal is to keep label structure information while avoiding very long prompts.

entry.title: Sensor-Informed Per-Point Covariance for Structured-Light 3D Imaging

author.name: Sehoon Tak, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: Derives a per-point three-by-three covariance field for structured-light 3D imaging by propagating measured phase precision through calibrated phase-to-depth mappings, replacing isotropic or geometry-inferred uncertainty assumptions. This yields sensor-grounded anisotropic uncertainty for registration and fusion.

entry.title: The Capability Ladder: A Curriculum-Modernization Framework for Workforce Readiness in the AI Era

author.name: Majid Memari, George Rudolph

entry.summary: A curriculum design framework arguing that AI is reallocating computing work toward verification, systems thinking, security, and supervision of AI rather than replacing engineers wholesale, illustrated by a pilot course. It proposes a capability-assurance ladder for workforce readiness.

entry.title: CoRCi: Cross-Reconstruction of Coherent Interests Modeling in Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Qingtian Bian, Tieying Li, Marcus de Carvalho, Jiaxing Xu, Hui Fang, Yiping Ke

entry.summary: CoRCi improves cross-domain sequential recommendation by cross-reconstructing coherent user interests instead of running separate encoders on mixed-domain sequences with per-domain loss aggregation, which the authors argue amplifies inter-domain discrepancies. Targets sparsity by transferring domain-invariant dynamic interests.

entry.title: CFD-Guided Detection of Concept Drift in Multimodal Physiologic Signals

author.name: Farouk Ganiyu Adewumi, Timothy Oladunni, Rochak Ghimire, Kosisochukwu Ogbuanya, Sanaa Reeves, Sandy Akoy

entry.summary: Proposes a physiologic stability framework that decides whether a cardiovascular model should keep, revise, or flag a prediction by comparing internal model changes against measurable changes in ECG, pulse, and respiration signals. Evaluated on standard ECG and waveform cohorts at pilot and full scale.

entry.title: Private Etymology: Designing Relational Reuse of Shared Symbols in Long-Term Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Miki Ueno

entry.summary: A concept-and-prototype paper proposing machine-representable relational provenance so that a human-AI pair can record how a private shared expression was proposed, negotiated, repaired, reused and revised, and check whether both parties still accept its meaning in later sessions. Targets long-term relational memory design in conversational AI.

entry.title: Detecting Clear Contact Lenses for Iris Recognition: A Two-Stage Mask-Guided Attention Approach

author.name: Parisa Farmanifard, Arun Ross

entry.summary: Shows that transparent prescription contact lenses, usually assumed harmless, measurably degrade iris matching scores, then proposes a two-stage mask-guided attention detector for them. Extends presentation-attack-detection thinking to a previously overlooked but very common confound.

entry.title: FedTVD: Balancing Data Quality and Quantity for Robust Federated Learning

author.name: Radwan Selo, Majid Kundroo, Taehong Kim

entry.summary: FedTVD weights client contributions during federated aggregation by combining dataset size with total variation distance between the client label distribution and a uniform global distribution, rather than by size alone as in FedAvg. Intended to reduce bias from label skew and unequal dataset sizes.

entry.title: Deep Learning based Detection of Fishing Vessels and Fishing Monitoring using Nightlight Images

author.name: Shantakar Mohanty, Prasun Kumar Gupta, Raian Vargas Maretto

entry.summary: Detects small dark fishing vessels that operate without AIS transponders using nighttime light imagery from the SDGSAT-1 satellite, with a dual-branch YOLO11 architecture fusing 10-meter panchromatic and 40-meter RGB bands. Applied to maritime surveillance along India's western coast.

entry.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Deep Learning Object Detection Models on a Real-World Multi-Plant Dataset from Africa

author.name: Ismail Ismail Tijjani, Sunusi Muhammad Ibrahim, Amina Ibrahim Khaleel, Lanre Olusegun Akinola, Fatima Isa Jibrin, Muhammad Bashir Aliyu, Abdullahi Abdussalam Dalhat, Abdullahi Suiudeen

entry.summary: Benchmarks six detectors including several YOLO generations, Faster R-CNN, and RT-DETR on a manually collected 3,382-image dataset of sesame, cabbage, and tomato crops from Nigerian farms under varying illumination and occlusion. Emphasizes that most agricultural vision work uses curated data unrepresentative of African smallholder conditions.

entry.title: Determinization in Structure Theories: A Unified Framework via Closure, Comparability, and Joint Admissibility

author.name: Hai Hai Fu

entry.summary: A formal mathematical framework for canonicalizing plural structure theories, distinguishing closure stabilization, global completion, and determinization, and classifying non-determinism into epistemic and structural varieties. It is abstract logic and knowledge-representation theory rather than applied machine learning.

entry.title: A Multi-Scale Temporal Framework with Dynamic Fusion for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition

author.name: Stefanos Gkikas, Yang Guo, Guangliang Li, Raul Fernandez Rojas, Giorgos Giannakakis, Randy Gomez

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-scale temporal EEG framework that decomposes signals into windows of several durations, encodes them with a shared attention encoder, and fuses scales with sample-specific weights, evaluated subject-independently including a mixed-emotion three-class task. Aims to avoid fixing the temporal structure available to the model.

entry.title: From Prompt to Harness: Coderlet from Scratch

author.name: Mengfan Li

entry.summary: A design study of a minimal coding-agent harness, tracing one request through context formation, model decision, environment action, observation return, and state continuation across model, execution, and state boundaries. Positions harness organization, not just model choice, as determining agent behavior.

entry.title: AirFlow: Context Preserving and Multi-Rate State Modeling for Air Quality Forecasting

author.name: Fan Yang, Nan Chen, Yijie Dong, Yuchen Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: AirFlow is a dual-stream air quality forecasting model that stops forcing all pollutant channels through one normalization rule and temporal backbone, instead modeling channel-specific distributions and multiple rates of change from station observations alone. Motivated by pollutants differing in periodicity and drift.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Registration of Jawbone CT and Intraoral Scan Data Using GeDi and ICP with Pseudo-IOS Ground Truth

author.name: Sho Mitarai, Hikaru Kayo, Hisashi Ozaki, Yuichiro Imai, Megumi Nakao

entry.summary: Proposes generating a synthetic intraoral scan point cloud from CT data so that the true registration transform is known by construction, enabling rigorous accuracy evaluation of coarse-to-fine registration using learned descriptors followed by iterative closest point. Addresses the lack of ground truth in cross-modality dental registration.

entry.title: Hit Selection Using SSMD-Based Machine Learning Performance Metrics in High-Throughput Screening Assays

author.name: Xiaohua Douglas Zhang

entry.summary: Derives closed-form relationships linking a standard high-throughput screening effect size measure to classification metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, and area under the ROC curve, under a Gaussian equal-variance assumption. This allows metric estimation in single-replicate primary screens where labeled samples are too sparse for empirical estimation.

entry.title: Exact Zarankiewicz Values On Two Finite Frontier Slices

author.name: Koyar Afrasyab

entry.summary: A certificate-based computer-assisted proof establishing exact Zarankiewicz numbers for several finite bipartite-graph cases, with orbit certificates ruling out candidate extremal matrices and deletion lemmas closing neighboring entries. It is combinatorics assisted by automated search rather than AI research per se.

entry.title: Does a Toehold Make a Bidder Bolder? Preemption and Multiplicity in Multi-Round Takeover Auctions

author.name: Zain Naboulsi

entry.summary: Uses computational game solving with certified numerical accuracy to test whether owning a pre-bid stake in a takeover target actually deters rival bidders once the contest is modeled as multiple escalating rounds rather than a single exchange. Concludes the deterrence rationale for toeholds is weaker than classical models imply, helping explain their rarity.

entry.title: Eco-SoC: A Sustainable VLSI Architecture for Energy-Proportional Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Jatin Chopra

entry.summary: Proposes a system-on-chip architecture for sustainable edge AI with dynamic precision-scaling logic that modulates bit width based on real-time activation sparsity, reporting substantial reductions in switching activity. Frames energy proportionality rather than static worst-case efficiency as the sustainability goal.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Deep Randomized Neural Networks for Classification

author.name: M. Sajid, A. Quadir, A. Rahaman, P. N. Suganthan, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Adds intuitionistic fuzzy membership weighting to deep and ensemble deep random vector functional link networks so that noisy samples and outliers contribute less, using neighborhood information in kernel space. The aim is robustness for tabular-style classification.

entry.title: EweAcT: Ewe behaviour aligned to accelerometer data for activity monitoring in extensive grazing systems

author.name: Lucile Riaboff (GenPhySE, INRAE), Ny Aina Andriamampandry (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Bompa (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Mathias Aletru (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Christian Durand (UEF), S\'ebastien Douls (UEF), Ga\"etan Bonnafe (UEF), Morgane Costes-Thir\'e (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Guillaume Delosi\`eres (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Jean- Marc Mongrelet (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), Enzo Niro (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), N\'emuel Tadi (GenPhySE, GenPhySE), S\'everine Deretz (DEPT GA, UEF, INRAE), Sara Parisot (UEF), Margot Lamarque (UEF), Dominique Hazard (GenPhySE), Emilie Cobo (GenPhySE)

entry.summary: Releases a dataset of 79 hours of tri-axial neck-collar accelerometer recordings from ewes paired with manually annotated behaviors, collected under extensive grazing conditions. Intended to support behavior-recognition models that assess livestock adaptation to environmental stressors such as heat waves and predation.

entry.title: PolypVision: A Three-Stage Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework for Classification and Segmentation of Colorectal Polyps

author.name: Hamidreza Bolhasani, Hamidreza Rastad, Amir Mohammad Akbari, Mohammad Tashakoripour, Parnian Asadollahi, Ata Khodami, Mojgan Forootan

entry.summary: PolypVision chains three stages for colorectal polyp analysis: adenomatous versus hyperplastic classification with Paris and JNet labeling, then segmentation with resection recommendation, then adenoma subtyping. Built from standard EfficientNetV2 and UNet++ components with focal and Dice losses.

entry.title: A Cost-Efficient Routing Pipeline for Multilingual Short-Text Classification Using Small Language Models

author.name: Wajdi Ben Saad, Safa Madiouni

entry.summary: A cost-focused deployment study of multilingual short-text classification that routes weaker low-resource languages through English translation before zero-shot classification while keeping strong languages on a direct path. The self-hosted pipeline uses compact sentence encoders with no task-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: 3D Weighted Geometric Graph Neural Networks for Sheep Facial Pain Assessment

author.name: Alam Noor, Luis Almeida, Mohamed Daoudi

entry.summary: Builds a geometric graph neural network for sheep facial pain assessment, lifting clinically defined facial landmarks into 3D using monocular depth estimation so no depth hardware is needed. Nodes encode 3D coordinates and cross-landmark spatial relations aligned with a validated veterinary pain scale.

entry.title: What Claude Saw Below

author.name: Luke Nicholls

entry.summary: An exploratory write-up of anomalous completions from Claude Opus 5, an existing Anthropic model, when given deliberately truncated prompts that imply missing content. The author documents confabulated biographies and self-referential text, and considers community speculation that outputs might reflect other users' prompts.

entry.title: Creative math research by AI as the latest sign of the end

author.name: Mitchell_Porter

entry.summary: A first-person account of an extended brainstorming session with an existing OpenAI reasoning model on generalizing the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, in which the model repeatedly proposed and refined its own next research subtasks. The author treats the sustained, self-directed mathematical exploration as evidence of rapidly advancing AI research capability.

entry.title: Sign Language Recognition Using Original and Synthetic Depth Image Based Point Cloud Data Models

author.name: Rustem Ozakar, Eyup Gedikli

entry.summary: Generates synthetic depth maps from RGB sign language video using Depth Anything V2, converts them to point clouds, and compares PointNet-family classification accuracy against point clouds from real depth sensors on three sign language datasets. Tests whether monocular depth estimation can substitute for scarce depth-annotated sign data.

entry.title: Precise Top-Layer Fabric Segmentation for Fabric Destacking with Edge- and Shape-Aware Deep Networks

author.name: Wenbo Dong, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Akinari Kobayashi, Akira Seino, Fuyuki Tokuda, Xuzhao Huang, Kai Tang, Norman C. Tien, Kazuhiro Kosuge

entry.summary: Proposes an encoder-decoder segmentation network with auxiliary edge-aware and shape-aware supervision branches to isolate the topmost layer in a stack of visually near-identical fabrics for robotic destacking. Targets a specific industrial manipulation bottleneck.

entry.title: CoRe-UIE: Rethinking Coexisting and Region-wise Degradation for Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Weifeng Kong, Chenghao Xu, Lin Chen, Ziheng Cao, Guanying Huo

entry.summary: Proposes an underwater image enhancement network that routes different image regions to specialized experts for color correction, haze suppression, texture recovery, and illumination protection, on a shared backbone. Targets the fact that underwater degradations coexist and vary spatially, which uniform restoration models handle poorly.

entry.title: MELLON - Multimodal Enhanced LLM for Online Navigation

author.name: Ruiyu Li, Haoyang Cai, Zhitong Guo, Tong Hu

entry.summary: Adds multimodal enhancements (a multimodal LLM navigator, a visual-question-answering helper agent, and a multimodal reranker) to web navigation agents on the WebShop simulated shopping benchmark, reporting a roughly nine-point accuracy gain after one epoch of training. Explores whether image-text alignment helps planning in web agents.

entry.title: CEAA: A Cognitive Embodied Agents Architecture for Interactive Computing Systems

author.name: Aimilios Hadjiliasi, Louis Nisiotis

entry.summary: Proposes a modular cognitive architecture for embodied intelligent virtual agents in real-time interactive environments, layering the sense-think-act loop with belief-desire-intention style reasoning to bridge low-level game-engine control and high-level deliberation. Targets the gap between reactive engine-bound controllers and hard-to-deploy reasoning models.

entry.title: Weather- and Location-Aware Agentic Dining Recommendation: Leveraging LLM World Knowledge for Region-Sensitive Contextual Reasoning

author.name: Kadharmoideen Fadurudeen

entry.summary: Builds an agentic dining recommender that leverages the world knowledge of an LLM to reason about culturally specific weather and location interactions, instead of hand-crafted weather-to-preference rules. The argument is that region-by-weather-by-cuisine interactions are too numerous to encode explicitly.

entry.title: TLDChoiceNet: Quantitatively Choosing a Transfer Learning Dataset

author.name: Jing Ning, James D. Braza

entry.summary: Trains a meta-model to predict post-fine-tuning test accuracy in order to choose which large source dataset to transfer from, replacing the usual qualitative heuristics about class count and examples per class. A version using ImageNet-pretrained ResNet embeddings improves over the naive variant.

entry.title: Detecting Soft Skills in ML Engineering Roles CVs

author.name: Aidin Azamnouri, Nouran Ayad, Justus Bogner, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: Uses an LLM-based extractor on 300 curated CVs across ML engineering, data science, and software engineering roles to identify explicitly listed and narratively implied soft skills, with statistical testing of group differences. It complements demand-side evidence from job ads and hiring interviews.

entry.title: Assessing Reliability of BERT-Based Models on Question Answering Tasks

author.name: Pooja Yadav, Priyanka Harjule, Basant Agarwal, Marko Robnik \v{S}ikonja

entry.summary: An empirical reliability and calibration study of encoder-only transformer QA models (BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, DistilBERT), arguing that trustworthiness estimates matter as much as accuracy. It evaluates how well confidence scores track correctness for extraction-as-classification QA.

entry.title: Generative Models: Principles, Architectures, and Applications

author.name: Jun Lu

entry.summary: A book-style overview of generative modeling covering foundational principles, mathematical background, and practical architectures across images, text, video, and molecules. It is educational material rather than new research.

entry.title: Guardian Crawler: Retrieval-First Knowledge Discovery with Bounded LLM Augmentation for Noisy Web Intelligence

author.name: Joshua Castillo, Santosh Nukavarapu, Ravi Mukkamala

entry.summary: Presents a retrieval-first pipeline combining BM25 with risk-aware and hybrid reranking plus citation-constrained RAG, evaluated on a synthetic 900-document web-like corpus with ten queries. Positions bounded LLM use as a way to control hallucination in noisy web intelligence gathering.

entry.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence for Fraudulent Banking Operations Recognition

author.name: Bohdan Mytnyk, Oleksandr Tkachyk, Nataliya Shakhovska, Solomiia Fedushko, Yuriy Syerov

entry.summary: A study applying standard machine learning classifiers to detect fraudulent online banking transactions, with emphasis on data preprocessing pipelines and comparison of model variants. It positions the work against the growth in online banking fraud following the pandemic-driven shift to digital channels.

entry.title: A Combined Feature-Based Framework for Disguise and Spoofing Detection in Face Recognition Systems

author.name: Sangiya Pararajasingham

entry.summary: Compares five classical feature-extraction and nearest-distance classification pipelines built from PCA, local binary patterns, HOG, SURF and Harris corners for jointly handling presentation spoofing and disguise-induced rejection in face recognition. Evaluates all pipelines within a common two-phase framework.

entry.title: Multiclass Sentiment Analysis for Identifying Political Viewpoints

author.name: Girma Yohannis Bade, Olga Kolesnikova, Jose Luis Oropeza, Grigori Sidorov

entry.summary: A comparison of XGBoost and BERT for multiclass sentiment classification of political viewpoints on social media, aimed at distinguishing stances toward political issues and figures. The study reports standard supervised results on collected social data.

entry.title: Ultraconstructive Model Theory via Bounded Adversarial Finite Structures

author.name: Mirco A. Mannucci

entry.summary: Proposes a model-theoretic framework in which satisfaction at finite computational scale is replaced by survival against a bounded adversary, with builder, opponent, and judge roles over finite partial structures. It is a foundational logic proposal rather than an empirical AI paper.

entry.title: Those Who Make History

author.name: Raelifin

entry.summary: An essay uses NASA's decision to seal Apollo lunar samples for future instruments as an analogy for preserving things whose value depends on technologies that do not yet exist, applied to the case for cryonics. It is a rhetorical piece rather than a technical analysis.

entry.title: Canadian Nuclear Emancipation: Canada's role amidst global dreams of energy security and nuclear development

author.name: tandemocracy

entry.summary: A geopolitics essay on Canada's potential role in global nuclear energy markets amid an energy security crunch, framed around energy diversification and the nuclear order. It has essentially no AI content.

entry.title: [Webinar] Why AI Safety is a Capital Allocation Problem

author.name: Schizoid Rentoid

entry.summary: A short announcement for a webinar in which a venture capital general partner with prior OpenAI research experience will argue that AI safety dilemmas are fundamentally questions of capital allocation and corporate governance. It contains a registration link and no technical content.

entry.title: Software Is Not Soft

author.name: cylonator

entry.summary: A short poetic essay riffing on the observation that software is rigid, brittle, and static despite its name, and arguing that interfaces need to become adaptive and playful. It presents no technical claims or results.

entry.title: Revived Lightweight Transit Predictions Page

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A short personal blog post about using Claude to one-shot revive a decade-old transit prediction webapp after an underlying transit API changed. It functions as an anecdote about how coding assistants lower the activation energy for small personal software projects.
